notes: kb/Work PB65 (2026-08-18): ONE screen (DataBinder.ScreenRepositoryIntrinsicName) asked by every declaration funnel — data-name, condition-name, index-name, file-name, paragraph/section name — rejects (COBOLNET1649) a user-defined word spelling an intrinsic-function-name the REPOSITORY identifies (FUNCTION name INTRINSIC, or every catalogued name under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC); LENGTH/RANDOM/SIGN/SUM are reserved words already. subject: Numeric literals
notes: The lexer's FLOAT_BODY (and its DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA twin FLOAT_COMMA_BODY, kb/Work PB98) is exactly the form — a fixed-point literal, the letter E without intervening spaces, a fixed-point exponent; the sign-adjacent twins (function-argument regions, SUBSCRIPT mode) keep -1.5E3 one token (kb/Work R17).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). 'shall include a decimal point' is the lexer's shape (a point-less 1E10 is a user-defined word, §8.3.1.1 — it is diagnosed as an undefined name, which it is); 'from 1 to 36 digits' is checked at the ONE normalizer both funnels share (COBOLNET1661 — a 40-digit significand); a 36-digit significand seeds a floating-point numeric-edited item exactly (the golden's E1).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99), RANGE DETERMINATION REPLACED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-B (kb/Work PB156 + PB195 + PB276). 'a maximum of four digits' - COBOLNET1661 for a fifth (1.0E12345, which used to reach Roslyn as an overflowing C# double literal, CS0594). The IMPLEMENTOR-DEFINED maximum / minimum exponent VALUE is documented in CONFORMANCE.md Sec.7 A.1 item 82 and enforced at compile time, and it is now ONE range for every statement position: the DECIMAL128 range, about 1E-6176 to 9.99E+6144, in EVERY arithmetic mode (ExpressionBinder.CheckLiteral) - so 1.0E+400 evaluates and 1.0E+9999 / 1.0E-9999 are COBOLNET1661. ⛔ THE PER-POSITION SPLIT THIS REPLACED is what the previous note published: a literal in a NATIVE arithmetic expression or statement was screened against binary64 (about 4.9E-324..1.8E+308, so 1.0E+400 was rejected) while the identical program compiled under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. Two rules remain, and they are different rules rather than different positions: a VALUE clause on a FLOAT-* item keeps the RECEIVER's binary form (Sec.13.18.63.3 SR2 - 'permissible values within the range indicated by the PICTURE clause or the USAGE clause', and a FLOAT-* subject has no PICTURE; DataBinder.FitsBinaryFloat, which is that screen's only surviving caller), and a VALUE on a fixed-point or floating-point numeric-edited item has no bound beyond the receiver's PICTURE (PIC 9E+9999 VALUE 1.0E+9999). The two lanes are witnessed SEPARATELY: pb99-floating-literal-range carries only the VALUE-clause entries and pb99-floating-literal-range-statement only the statement ones, because the negative harness asserts that SOME diagnostic contains COBOLNET1661 and a shared file let the VALUE entries satisfy it alone.

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). A zero significand with a nonzero exponent (0.0E+5), a negative zero significand (-0.0E+0) or a negative-signed exponent (0.0E-0) is COBOLNET1661 — in a VALUE clause, a level-88 and a statement alike (the ONE normalizer).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99), COMPLETED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-B (kb/Work PB156 + PB195), and CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (kb/Work PB263 + PB264). D-B's claim recorded here was that the literal's value - significand x 10^exponent - is carried EXACTLY in EVERY position through ONE rendering, NumericRenderer.LiteralNum. THAT CLAIM WAS NOT TRUE OF TWO POSITIONS WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, and this row's five goldens were all VALUE-clause or arithmetic-operand positions, so none of them could have contradicted it. The CALL argument lane and the INVOKE argument lane do not reach LiteralNum at all: they render operand text through the raw EmitText.UnscaledLit helper, which returned the literal's own source text as a binary64 Real NumX for the E-form. The generated C# then handed a double to ManagedPointer<long|Int128>.Cell(...) and did not compile - conforming source rejected by a raw Roslyn CS1503 with no COBOL diagnostic at all (measured both carrier arms). UnscaledLit now honours its own scaled-integer contract for BOTH notations via TryUnscaledParts, taking the (significand, power of ten) pair exactly and never expanding it to text; the CALL lane funnels both of its non-place arms through one carrier build, and the two new goldens pin the four-cell table (two notations x BY CONTENT / BY VALUE, all four displaying the same value) plus the INVOKE arm. The evidence set now covers the argument positions the word EVERY always claimed.

subject: Function-identifier
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB61 — the LENGTH/BYTE-LENGTH folds enumerated from the rule branches; one builder for a runtime-length group; SR6 decided from the definition before binding). SR6 'if a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments' — decided ONCE, from the DEFINITION (the catalog signature, or a REPOSITORY user function's USING formals — SR6 names function-prototype-name-1 too) and BEFORE any argument binds, on every route: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (1:4) drew the §15.3 arity error (the empty list bound first; only RANDOM, MinArgs 0, reached the SR6 arm) and keyword-omitted UPPER-CASE (1:4) under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC died as 'not defined' (the MinArgs guard sent it to the data path). Now COBOLNET1543 (SR6/SR8) on all of them; ResultRefMod no longer carries an SR6 arm. Negatives pb61-sr6-function-keyword-refmod (85+), pb61-sr6-keyword-omitted-refmod and pb61-sr6-udf-prototype-refmod (2002+); FunctionRefModSr6SweepTests sweeps the CATALOG — every argument-permitting row in both forms draws 1543 (never 1504/1639), every zero-argument row (CURRENT-DATE (1:8), the standard's own D.14.3.6 shape) does not.

Pinned twice: (1/3) ** 0 under PROHIBITED is exactly 1.00 (the CA5 sibling - the leak reinstated the pre-CA5 spurious EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION), and (A/B) ** 2 = 1 * (A/B) ** 2 = 11.1111 (the leak made multiplying by one change the value).

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is GR2's four-rank hierarchy (1st unary +/-, 2nd exponentiation, 3rd multiply/divide, 4th add/subtract). The IMPLEMENTATION was already correct and is unchanged: powerExpression puts a full unaryExpression in its base position, so `- 2 ** 2` binds as (-2)**2. What was PARTIAL was the EVIDENCE - rank 1 over rank 2 was pinned NOWHERE, and it is the one rank whose answer differs from every mainstream language, so a regression would have looked like normal behaviour. tests/conformance/2023/pb158_arith_precedence_spine now pins all four ranks in one labelled golden with every expected value derived from GR2/GR3 rather than from a run: R1 `- 2 ** 2` = 4 (rank 1 over 2), R2 `2 ** 3 * 4` = 32 (2 over 3), R3 `2 + 3 * 4` = 14 (3 over 4), R4 `2 ** 3 ** 2` = 64 (GR3 left fold), R7 `8 / 4 / 2` = 1 (GR3 left fold on /), and R5/R6 as the parentheses-vs-precedence discriminator. It also replaces the previous evidence's dependence on pb69 T11, where the precedence fact was INCIDENTAL to a golden about the Int128 carrier and would have vanished silently if that expression were ever rewritten.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "the order of execution of consecutive operations of the same hierarchical level is from left to right"` => OK §8.8.1.2 3). || UPHELD, with my own evidence rather than the adjudicator's. Derived first: every level left-folds, exponentiation included — the standard states no right-associativity exception for `**`, so `2 ** 3 ** 2` = (2**3)**2 = 64, not 512. READ: `ExpressionBinder.BindChain` is `foreach (var child in StatementBinder.Children(node)) { if (child is AddOpContext or MulOpContext) op = child.GetText()[0]; else { var x = BindExprCore(child, context); acc = acc is null ? x : new BoundBinary(acc, op, x); } }` — a strict left fold serving BOTH AdditiveExpressionContext and MultiplicativeExpressionContext; and `ExpressionBinder.BindPower` is `acc = BindExprCore(bases[0], context); for (int i = 1; i < bases.Length; i++) acc = new BoundPower(acc, BindExprCore(bases[i], context));` — the same left fold for rank 2. I ALSO CHECKED THE CHILD ENUMERATOR the adjudicator took on trust: `StatementBinder.Children` is `for (int i = 0; i < node.ChildCount; i++) yield return node.GetChild(i);` — plain index order, no filtering, so no operand can be skipped and no pair re-ordered. `CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith`, the only other walker of this tree, left-folds identically over `node.ChildCount`. || TEST EVIDENCE VERIFIED BY READING BOTH GOLDENS AND THEIR .out FILES, not by trusting the citation: (a) tests/conformance/2014/func_expr_arg.cob header says verbatim '** folds LEFT per 8.8.1.2 r3', its body has `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MAX(2 ** 3 ** 2, 1)` and func_expr_arg.out asserts `POW=00064` — right-folding gives 512, so it discriminates rank 2 and cites this exact rule; (b) tests/conformance/2002/arith_standard.cob has `COMPUTE W1 = 2 / 7 * 7` into PIC 9V9(5) with hand-derived §8.8.1.5 arithmetic in the header, and arith_standard.out asserts `W1=200000` — `2/(7*7)` = 0.0408 would print 004081, so rank 3 left-to-right is pinned, in the SDIDI lane. Both are spec-derived (hand-derived expectations, ISO citations in the headers), neither is a differential, neither is nist:/characterization:/MatchesLegacy. Rank 4 (`A - B - C`) has no golden, but it is the SAME `BindChain` loop already discriminated at rank 3 by (b) — associativity is decided once, in the binder, and no renderer re-associates (I verified `CombineCore` emits self-parenthesized forms only). Rank 1 is prefix-unary, where 'left to right' has no content. || I ALSO CHECKED THE SUBSCRIPT FAST PATH, a second evaluator the adjudicator did not consider: `ReferenceResolver.RenderSegment` splices `+ - * / ( )` into C# text, and C# gives those operators the same precedence and the same left associativity as COBOL, and `**` has no case arm so it routes to the D18 materializer — so rule 3's ORDER holds there too. (That path's VALUE defect — C# integer division — is recorded against GR-8.8.1.2-1; it is not an ordering defect.) The `_outermost` leak recorded against GR-8.8.1.2-1 likewise does not touch associativity. Editions: no Annex E change item for §8.8.1.2 (scanned); batch default.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is Table 3's symbol-adjacency matrix. WHICH CELLS THE GRAMMAR CAN STILL PRODUCE WAS MEASURED, one probe program per cell, parsed through the real compiler rather than reasoned about: ten of the thirteen invalid cells are already hard parse errors ((ident,ident), (binop,binop), (binop,')'), (unary,binop), (unary,')'), ('(',binop), ('(',')'), (')',ident), (')',unary), (')','(')), and two more - (ident,'(') and its sibling - cannot form as an arithmetic PAIR at all because COBOL reads a '(' after an identifier as a subscript or reference-modifier. Exactly ONE cell was producible: (unary, unary). It is now screened by ExpressionFormationPass over the shared frontend rule, covering all THREE evaluating arms (ExpressionBinder.BindExprCore, CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith, and its SoleNumericLiteral reclassification probe, which used to fold `- - 5` to the literal 5). The screen reads TOKEN POSITIONS, not the tree, because SS8.3.3.3.2 rule 2 makes an ADJACENT sign part of the numeric literal - `- -2` is the PERMISSIBLE (unary, literal) pair while `- - 2` is the invalid one, and in the default lexer mode both emit MINUS MINUS INTEGERLIT. A grammar tier would have rejected both, i.e. rejected legal source. The over-rejection guard is pinned positively (golden R10/R11/R12 and three unit cases).

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB136): both defects of the D10 transitional subscript evaluator closed. (1) The splitter's new-segment logic now handles a depth-0 '(' - after ')' or a literal it always opens a NEW subscript; after an IDENTIFIER the split is DECLARATION-INFORMED (a name with no OCCURS cannot be subscripted, so its '(' begins the parenthesized-expression subscript the spec's own NOTE 2 prints, while `DOG (BAKER (I) 3)` keeps BAKER's paren as its own subscript) - the rule-5 restructuring the batch-8 note asked for, threaded as an optional predicate so the intrinsic-argument caller keeps its exact behavior. (2) A quotient-bearing segment routes to the D18 exact evaluator UNCONDITIONALLY: the old token splice was C# integer division over long reads, so an all-integer quotient truncated silently where GR1b evaluates the exact result - (3+4)/2 = 3.5 now raises the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT fatal when checking is on (probed verbatim) and takes the documented lenient truncation otherwise. PB41's scaled-operand routing caught only segments with scaled OPERANDS; the all-integer quotient was exactly the case it could not see.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: CONFORMS as of 2026-08-03 (fix-queue PB28, landed this session). Rule 6 has three parts. r6a (zero base requires exponent > 0) and r6c (negative base requires an integer exponent) are mandatory 'shall' requirements setting EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION, Fatal in Table 14. BEFORE the fix the STANDARD-DECIMAL arm enforced both (CobolDec.Pow) and EVERY NATIVE arm enforced neither, so the same program answered differently depending only on whether an ARITHMETIC clause was present: 0 ** 0 returned 1 (IEEE's convention, not COBOL's) and -2 ** 0.5 returned 0 (Math.Pow yields NaN and the quantizer made it zero), both with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken. CheckPowRule6 now screens every native arm. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY REACHABLE COMBINATION, not sampled: native at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023, and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2023 - all five raise both legs and leave the receiver unmodified per SS14.7.5. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is loudly refused (COBOLNET0806), so that arm is unreachable rather than unverified. r6b ('if the evaluation yields both a positive and a negative real number, the value returned is the positive number') is a SELECTION rule, not a screen, and cannot arise here: both bodies (CobolIntrinsics.PowNativeInt / PowNativeReal and CobolDec.Pow) yield a single value. Checked in the same pass rather than left to be discovered as a fourth leg.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: A 35-digit composite (PIC 9(18) superimposed on PIC 9V9(17)) is legal in COMPUTE under native arithmetic and illegal in ADD — §14.7.7 2) names four verbs in sub-item a) and COMPUTE is not one of them.

subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.2 'Any operand of an arithmetic expression that is not already in SBIDI is converted into SBIDI form'` -> OK (§8.8.1.4.2 rule 1). Expected behavior derived BEFORE reading code: when standard-binary arithmetic is in effect every operand is lifted into an SBIDI (a binary128-equivalent carrier, §8.8.1.4.2 paragraph 3 + NOTE 3: 113-bit significand, exponent range 2**-16494..2**16384), inexact lifts rounding per §11.9.11 (whose rule 2a implies NEAREST-EVEN under this mode). READ: DataBinder.BindDeclarations, DataBinder.cs:318-320 -- `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error('COBOLNET0806', 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature ... and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL')`. READ EditionContext.Error (EditionContext.cs:109): `Diagnostics.Add($'{Prefix()}error {code}: ...')` -- unconditional, no severity policy, no --permissive downgrade path, so the mode is a hard compile failure at EVERY edition and strictness; ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary is produced ONLY by OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf (OptionsBinder.cs:68). CONSEQUENCE: no operand is ever converted to SBIDI because no SBIDI exists -- I grepped src/ for the §8.8.1.4.2 NOTE 3 range constants (16384, 16271, 16382, 16494) and for `SBIDI`: ZERO hits outside comments; the only 128-bit floating carrier named anywhere is Usage.FloatBinary128, itself rejected COBOLNET1564 (PictureAnalyzer.cs:588, Annex A.3 item 17 processor-dependent non-support). The rounding half is unimplemented independently: OptionsModel.IntermediateRounding (OptionsModel.cs:44) defaults UNCONDITIONALLY to CobolRounding.NearestAwayFromZero with the comment citing '§11.9.11 r3' -- the standard-DECIMAL rule -- and there is no ArithmeticMode arm anywhere that supplies §11.9.11.2 rule 2a's NEAREST-EVEN default for standard-binary. Editions derived from the spec, NOT from ConstructRegistry: F.2 item 3 newly designates 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' obsolete in this edition (an element must have been a live facility in the prior edition to be newly designated obsolete), and E.2 item 21 records that the 2002-era 'Standard Arithmetic' mode -- the clause alternative STANDARD-BINARY/-DECIMAL superseded -- is removed at 2023; the OPTIONS paragraph does not exist at 85. Hence 2014,2023. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THE ROW: either an SBIDI carrier (a real or emulated binary128 with §11.9.11.2 r2 rounding) plus a spec-derived golden that shows an inexact decimal operand (0.1) landing as the nearest-even 113-bit approximation, OR an explicit OWNER decision recording documented-non-support under §4.2.6 / A.3 item 2 (see the finding note on GR-8.8.1.4.4-4). Per ground rule 6 the documented-non-support disposition is not mine to award, so the verdict is NOT-IMPLEMENTED. NOT cited as closing evidence: conformance-test:StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported pins the REJECTION (COBOLNET0806 + the word 'obsolete'), i.e. it is a green test holding this gap open, never evidence for this rule's behavior. || UPHELD: verdict, code-location and editions all re-derived independently. (a) I re-read §8.8.1.4.2 in the spec at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:7947-7982 -- rule 1 and NOTE 3 are verbatim as quoted, and NOTE 3's range constants are exactly the four I grepped. (b) My own grep of src/ for `SBIDI` returns ONE hit and it is a comment (CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs:666: 'standard-binary (cap 35) is unreachable (COBOLNET0806 rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY outright; its SBIDI range joins this map if that ever lands)'); my grep for 16384|16494|16382|16271 across src/ returns NOTHING. subject: Standard-decimal arithmetic
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31 (owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB167). r2a-r2d were already exact (binary square-and-multiply over Mul, which for exponents 1-4 performs the printed equivalent expressions digit-for-digit); PB145 had closed every measured wrong answer in the escapes. What remained was r2e's own constraint on the DEVELOPMENT: 'Operands used in the development of that value shall be in SDIDI form. All additions, subtractions, multiplications and divisions performed in the development of the result shall be performed in accordance with the corresponding rules in ISO/IEC 60559:2020' (cite.py --check verified) — and the development went through IEEE binary64 (Math.Pow on the non-integer arm, a Math.Log10 decomposition on the past-loop-bound escape), so it satisfied neither shall and the two arms were two DIFFERENT approximations of the same value. There is now ONE development, exp(operand-2 x ln operand-1), carried entirely on CobolDec Add/Sub/Mul/Div with argument reduction (ln: decimal exponent split + three exact square roots + the atanh series; exp: reduction by n*ln10 so the 10^n factor is an EXACT decimal exponent shift, then the Taylor series), plus one chosen special case: at |operand-2| = 1/2 the equivalent expression is FUNCTION SQRT(operand-1), whose standard-decimal value Sec.15.84.4 r2 fixes EXACTLY, so b ** 0.5 and SQRT(b) agree by construction (they DISAGREED before). CobolDecPowDevelopmentTests scans CobolDec.cs and fails if any binary64 transcendental returns. ⛔ TWO DEFECTS IN THAT FIRST LANDING WERE FOUND BY ITS OWN REVIEW FLEET AND FIXED IN THE SAME WAVE. (1) kb/Work PB267 - the past-loop-bound escape rebuilt the exponent from TryIntegerValue's magnitude, which CLAMPS at long.MaxValue, so every exponent past 2**63-1 was silently replaced by 9223372036854775807: (1 + 10**-33) ** 1.0E+20 answered a flat 1.0000000000000 where 1.0000000000001 is owed, and 0.9999999999999999 ** 1.0E+25 answered a silent 0 where the value is below the decimal128 range entirely. PowMagnitude now carries the exponent OPERAND (an SDIDI holds |operand-2| exactly, so there was never anything to reconstruct), and PowCore screens the ORDER of p x ln b before forming it so an out-of-range product takes Sec.8.8.1.5.2 r2's own two names rather than Mul's clamp, which would say OVERFLOW in both directions. ⚠ The disposition is NOT 'a clamped exponent with |base| != 1 is out of range': the closest SDIDI value to one is 1 +/- 10**-33 and (1 + 10**-33) ** 10**20 is in range, so that screen would be PB145's spurious size error again. (2) kb/Work PB269 - the logarithm's three-square-root argument reduction carries u = m^(1/8) at 34 SIGNIFICANT digits about 1, so Sub(u, One) cancelled away log10(1/delta) of them: measured 17.05 correct digits at the worst point of |m-1| <= 1/4 and EXACTLY ZERO at m = 1 + 10**-33, where the first root rounds back to 1 and ln m came out 0. LnReduced now takes the same atanh series over delta = m - 1 directly inside that band (Sub(m, One) is exact there), which measures 32.74 digits at the same worst point and uses no square root at all. WHAT IS CLAIMED, precisely: an r2e-conforming SDIDI development, NOT 34 correct digits

subject: Standard-decimal arithmetic
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31 (owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB167), CORRECTED THE SAME DAY (kb/Work PB266). r3: 'When operand-2 is less than zero, the result shall be equivalent to the evaluation of the arithmetic expression (1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS (operand-2)))' (cite.py --check verified, both halves). This is an EQUIVALENCE and not implementor latitude - r2's latitude is scoped 'When the value of operand-2 is greater than zero' - and under Sec.8.8.1.5.2's per-operation 34-digit rounding the reciprocal form is a DIFFERENT value from exp(-|p| x ln b): it carries one extra correctly-rounded division and no negated exp argument. ⛔ THE FIRST LANDING'S NOTE CLAIMED THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE CODE DID, in both of its sentences. It said the development 'develops every other negative exponent through the same SDIDI exp/ln core as the positive one, so the r3 identity holds by construction rather than by luck'; measured, it held in 21% of sampled cases, BY LUCK (2 ** -0.25 answered ...4762332146 where 1 / (2 ** 0.25) is ...4762332141). It also said 'the INTEGER arm has honoured it whole since PB145'; the past-loop-bound escape carried the sign INSIDE the exponent, so r3 held below |n| = 500000 and broke above it - a discontinuity at the loop bound. And no pin on the row could see either: pb167's two negative legs and MinusHalfExponent were all -1/2 (the one exponent PowCore short-circuited), pb145's B ** NN and MinusOne_...PastLongRange are base -1 (the |b| = 1 parity shortcut), and HalfPastTheLoopBound uses a POSITIVE exponent. THE CONSTRUCTION NOW: r3's reciprocal is written ONCE, at the top of Pow, over PowMagnitude(b, |operand-2|) - so every arm below it is r3-correct by construction, PowCore needs no -1/2 twin to keep in step, and the divergence is closed at the 34th significant digit where a relation between two SDIDI intermediates and an exact cancellation could both see it (pb167's R3GEN / R3PW7 / R3FAR / R3NEAR / R3DLT legs, and a 10-row unit theory spanning the non-integer, in-bound-integer and past-bound arms). ⚠ ONE VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, pinned: an out-of-range negative exponent now takes its EC name from r3's own expression rather than from where the final value lands, because the operation that leaves the range is the INNER power. 2 ** -600000 reports EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW and 0.5 ** -600000 EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW; before the hoist they answered the other way round (pb145's R3OVER / R3UNDR legs). ⚠ r3 is an IDENTITY requirement, not an accuracy one, and honouring it COSTS accuracy here: the true 34-digit 2**-0.25 is ...4762332149, so the reciprocal form is 8 ulp out where the direct form was 3. That is why the fix is the literal expression and never a tolerance.

notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152), COBOLNET1727. 'Hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal' is a DEFINED TERM and the screen is written to it, not to a paraphrase: 8.3.3.2.2 gives the alphanumeric literal exactly two general formats - format 1 ("..." / '...') and format 2 (X"..." / X'...') - and 'hexadecimal-alphanumeric' names FORMAT 2, so a one-character format-1 literal such as "Z" is NOT admitted however short it is. One byte is exactly two hexadecimal digits (8.3.3.2.3 SR5). Before the screen the decoder took raw[0] for ANY shape, so INITIALIZE ALL TO "AB" silently became 'A'. The 2026-08-30 analysis that scoped this work carried the paraphrase 'a one-character alphanumeric OR one-byte hex literal', which would have shipped an under-reject; the printed page (PDF 307 / folio 277) was rendered and read to settle it. PB151's own golden pb151_options_fill was written with the format-1 spelling and is repaired to X"51" by this landing - 0x51 IS 'Q', so its expected output is unchanged byte for byte.

subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

subject: LOCK MODE clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.5.9.3 SR1 forbids the LOCK MODE clause "for a file that is the subject of an APPLY COMMIT clause". subject: SAME clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.6.4.3 SR11: "A file or record area that is subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause shall not be specified with another file or record area that is not subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause." The SAME clause (§12.4.6.4) is CLAIMED and supported; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause, Annex A.4.3 item 2, refused by name (COBOLNET1709). No accepted program can put a file in an APPLY COMMIT clause, so the rule cannot be violated. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT — the verdict field would speak about SAME, a claimed facility; see the `commit-and-rollback-only` selector, which names this row among its exclusions. Editions 2023: the APPLY COMMIT clause is a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.2 item 2).

subject: SAME clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.6.4.4 GR3: "The file and record area of a file subject to commit and rollback may not be shared with another such file or record area unless it has been closed, a commit or a rollback has been executed and the APPLY COMMIT clause for the file has been deactivated." ⚠ ITS SHAPE IS NOT SR-12.4.6.4.3-11'S and it therefore gets its OWN witness: SR11 forbids mixing a commit-subject file with one that is NOT subject, while GR3 says "another SUCH file" — BOTH files subject to commit and rollback. The SAME clause (§12.4.6.4) is CLAIMED and supported; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause (ISO §12.4.6.3), Annex A.4.3 item 2, refused BY NAME by COBOLNET1709, so no file is ever subject to the facility and the rule cannot be violated. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT: the verdict field would speak about SAME, a claimed facility, and §4.2.7 discharges non-support through user documentation that declines commit and rollback — never SAME. The `commit-and-rollback-only` derived selector names this row among its exclusions for that reason. Editions 2023: the APPLY COMMIT clause is a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.2 item 2).

subject: File description entry
notes: Annex A.4.8 (items 1 FORMAT clause §13.18.24, 2 SELECT WHEN clause §13.18.51) is an OPTIONAL language element (§4.2.7) for which no support is claimed — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 Annex A.4 table, row 'A.4.8 | FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling | Not claimed', which is the WHOLE of the §4.2.7 user documentation for this module (§4's four documented-non-support facilities are MCS, commit/rollback, VALIDATE and screen handling — there is no §4 item for A.4.8, so no §4 reference may be invented). Annex A.4.1 carries the licence from the two named clauses to every associated rule: 'Any associated syntax rules, general rules, other rules, exception conditions, and I-O status values are also optional, even if not explicitly listed.' The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-declined; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-choice-combination; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-no-optional-word. COBOLNET1705 is raised at bind for EVERY occurrence and is an Error, not the COBOLNET1560 accept-inert band, because an inert FORMAT changes which bytes reach the medium (§13.18.24.4 GR1) and an inert SELECT WHEN selects the wrong record description entry (§13.18.51.4 GR1) — a wrong answer, not a missing facility. Measured 2026-09-02: refused at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive.

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3, which already named CLASS a validation clause. Licence: Annex A.4.1, "An implementation shall accept the syntax and provide the functionality for an optional element only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor", and its second sentence carrying the licence to the module's unlisted rules — which is the sentence CLASS needs, because Annex A.4 never LISTS this clause. OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB375, 2026-09-02: the clause is DECLINED WITH VALIDATE, on §13.16.2's own ground — the printed Format-1 validation-clauses group opens with `[ class-clause ]` and maps it to "13.18.11, CLASS clause" (RENDERED, PDF p394 / folio 364) — and §13.18.11.1 leaves it no content outside the module. Refused BY NAME (COBOLNET1708) where it drew a bare "COBOL0307: unexpected 'CLASS'" before. Editions are the DATA-DESCRIPTION clause's band, not the word's: CLASS itself is reserved at all four editions (§12.3.7 SPECIAL-NAMES CLASS clause), so at --std 85 this entry is an ordinary syntax error rather than this decline.

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Licence: Annex A.4.1 and its second sentence. OWNER DECISION kb/Work PB375, 2026-09-02 — the CLASS clause is DECLINED WITH VALIDATE. This rule is the clause's own statement of that confinement: "The CLASS clause takes effect during the content validation stage of the execution of a VALIDATE statement. The CLASS clause is ignored during the execution of any statement other than a VALIDATE statement." With no VALIDATE statement implemented there is no stage for it to take effect in, and the clause is refused by name (COBOLNET1708) rather than accepted and ignored.

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Licence: Annex A.4.1 and its second sentence. OWNER DECISION kb/Work PB375, 2026-09-02. The rule conditions the clause on the item's internal indicator after the FORMAT VALIDATION stage — a per-item state that exists only inside a VALIDATE statement (§14.9.50.4), so nothing of it survives the decline.

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Licence: Annex A.4.1 and its second sentence. subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): alphabet-name-1 shall reference an alphabet defining an ALPHANUMERIC coded character set — a LOCALE alphabet (no coded character set, Table 6) is COBOLNET1669 through the ONE resolver; a FOR NATIONAL alphabet in the slot or an undeclared name is COBOLNET1672/0898; the golden's STANDARD-1 satisfies it.

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): alphabet-name-2 shall reference an alphabet defining a NATIONAL coded character set — the class-mismatch arm (COBOLNET1672) mirrors SR1's; 2002+ (the national half). The same negative's LOCALE arm covers the Table-6 refusal shared with SR1.

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): with record description entries and no SELECT WHEN clauses (none exist in this grammar), one class only (both names → COBOLNET1672); a) every elementary item usage display and signed items SIGN SEPARATE (1672 — probed: a PIC S9 record under CODE-SET draws the SIGN SEPARATE arm); b) the national twin.

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19) — DETERMINATION, documented (CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 27): the sets whose implementor correspondence to the native set is the IDENTITY — NATIVE (§12.3.7.4 GR7 d, by definition), STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 (GR7 c: the correspondence is implementor-defined, and the native set's first 128 characters ARE ISO/IEC 646 IRV), UTF-16 (the D-N1 substrate) — are CLAIMED, their conversion being the identity (the golden's byte-exact round trip); an alphabet whose on-medium representation would differ (a literal-phrase alphabet's remapped ordinals; UTF-8/UCS-4 as variable-width medium encodings) is the DOCUMENTED Annex A §A.3 item 27 non-support — COBOLNET1672, never a silent identity (the negative). Rule --check verified at 13.18.13.4 1).

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): on OPEN the on-medium coded character set is the referenced one — for every CLAIMED set that is the native encoding itself (the identity correspondence), which the golden's write-then-read round trip observes; a non-identity set never reaches OPEN (refused at compile time, GR-13.18.13.4-1's determination).

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: Annex A.4.8 (items 1 FORMAT clause §13.18.24, 2 SELECT WHEN clause §13.18.51) is an OPTIONAL language element (§4.2.7) for which no support is claimed — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 Annex A.4 table, row 'A.4.8 | FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling | Not claimed', which is the WHOLE of the §4.2.7 user documentation for this module (§4's four documented-non-support facilities are MCS, commit/rollback, VALIDATE and screen handling — there is no §4 item for A.4.8, so no §4 reference may be invented). Annex A.4.1 carries the licence from the two named clauses to every associated rule: 'Any associated syntax rules, general rules, other rules, exception conditions, and I-O status values are also optional, even if not explicitly listed.' The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-declined; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-choice-combination; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-no-optional-word. COBOLNET1705 is raised at bind for EVERY occurrence and is an Error, not the COBOLNET1560 accept-inert band, because an inert FORMAT changes which bytes reach the medium (§13.18.24.4 GR1) and an inert SELECT WHEN selects the wrong record description entry (§13.18.51.4 GR1) — a wrong answer, not a missing facility. Measured 2026-09-02: refused at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive.

subject: CODE-SET clause

subject: FORMAT clause
notes: Annex A.4.8 (items 1 FORMAT clause §13.18.24, 2 SELECT WHEN clause §13.18.51) is an OPTIONAL language element (§4.2.7) for which no support is claimed — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 Annex A.4 table, row 'A.4.8 | FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling | Not claimed', which is the WHOLE of the §4.2.7 user documentation for this module (§4's four documented-non-support facilities are MCS, commit/rollback, VALIDATE and screen handling — there is no §4 item for A.4.8, so no §4 reference may be invented). Annex A.4.1 carries the licence from the two named clauses to every associated rule: 'Any associated syntax rules, general rules, other rules, exception conditions, and I-O status values are also optional, even if not explicitly listed.' The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-declined; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-choice-combination; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-no-optional-word. COBOLNET1705 is raised at bind for EVERY occurrence and is an Error, not the COBOLNET1560 accept-inert band, because an inert FORMAT changes which bytes reach the medium (§13.18.24.4 GR1) and an inert SELECT WHEN selects the wrong record description entry (§13.18.51.4 GR1) — a wrong answer, not a missing facility. Measured 2026-09-02: refused at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive.

subject: OCCURS clause
notes: kb/Work PB80 (2026-08-18): GR8a (data-name-1 outside the group) — the sending image is the current-count part and a receiving store touches only it; GR8b (inside) — the maximum length — for EVERY storage shape of the group: a record-struct member and a Tier-B / BASED class-tier window alike (WrapIfOdoGroup wraps both; PlaceRenderer.GroupImage is the ONE image reader over both). A BASED ODO record sent its MAXIMUM before (MOVE BODO TO OUT gave ABcccdddeee for NN = 2), a MOVE into it wrote past the current extent, and a comparison / ref-mod read the maximum. The WORKING-STORAGE twin is the control on every golden row; a REDEFINES-class ODO group cannot be declared (13.18.44 SR forbids redefining a variable-size item), so BASED is the only class-tier shape.

subject: PICTURE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB66). The significand holds 1..36 digit positions: PIC 9(37)E+99 and PIC E+99 are COBOLNET1658 (the negative's BG / BH entries); SR14's 31-position cap is NOT applied to the form (DataBinder's capacity guard excludes IsFloatEdited — Annex A.3 item 1 c/d's 31-digit latitude is unavailable to a processor supporting the standard float usages, so the full 36 is mandatory).

subject: PICTURE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB66). The one sanctioned two-sign form is the significand's fixed +/- beside the exponent's + (NOTE 3): -9.9(5)E+99 and +9(3).9(2)E+999 classify and edit (the golden's E1 / E2); a CR or DB in the significand (9.99CRE+99, 9.99DBE+99) and a floating sign string (+++9.99E+99) are COBOLNET1658; the fixed-point mutual exclusion is Analyze's long-standing check.

subject: PICTURE clause

subject: PICTURE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB66 / D21). (a) the fixed-point numeric-edited definitions are the long-standing Analyze classification (NIST NC-series editing goldens); (b) the floating-point form — 'two parts, separated without any spaces, by the symbol E', the significand a numeric or fixed-point numeric-edited character-string with neither floating insertion nor zero suppression with replacement, the exponent +9 / +99 / +999 / +9999 — is AnalyzeFloatEdited: one E, the exponent shape, and (with §13.18.40.6 Table 10 row E, rendered from the PDF to confirm the OCR) only 9 B 0 / , . and a leading fixed sign before the E; V P S Z * CR DB the currency symbol, a second E, an EDITING phrase and a SIGN clause are each COBOLNET1658 with a per-rule message. Category numeric-edited (PicInfo.IsFloatEdited the discriminator). (b) is a 2002 introduction — COBOLNET0900 below 2002 (registry row pic-external-float-2002, negative pb66-float-edited-at-85).

subject: PICTURE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-17 (with PB60 / AR-15.68.3-3). 'The first occurrence of the currency symbol adds the number of characters in the currency string to the size of the item. Each subsequent occurrence of the currency symbol adds one to the size of the item.' PictureAnalyzer adds the string's extra length to PicInfo.Length once (PIC U9.99 with 'USD' is 7; PIC UUU9 is 6; PIC UUUU is 6), and CobolEdit renders the physical width in every editing case (fixed, floating with the string before the first nonzero digit, the all-floating zero as spaces, BLANK WHEN ZERO). A group image carries the physical width (golden GRP leg: USD5.25X in an X(8)).

subject: REDEFINES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB93). data-name-2 resolves among the PRECEDING same-level siblings only (TakeWhile before the subject, nearest match — NOTE 1) — an entry with a lower level number cannot intervene by construction (it would end the sibling list); a name that resolves to nothing, or only to a LATER sibling, is COBOLNET1654 and the entry binds as an ordinary item (no half-state).

subject: REDEFINES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB93 sweep). A REDEFINES naming an entry that is itself a redefinition is COBOLNET1656 — error strict; under --permissive a warning with the chain semantics (the classifier chases the anchor, SR11) — the documented dialect leniency (GnuCOBOL/IBM accept chains).

subject: REDEFINES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB93). The redefining entries FOLLOW the entries defining the area: the lookup admits preceding siblings only, so `05 A REDEFINES B. 05 B.` is COBOLNET1654 (it used to bind to the later B). The 'without intervening entries that define new storage areas' half is the ClassifyRedefinesClasses layout invariant (a redefiner overlays its target's area wherever it stands among the siblings).

notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB93). data-name-2 / data-name-3 must name an item of the record the level-66 entry follows (FindDescendantOrSelf over the owning record) — a miss is COBOLNET1655 (it used to `continue` silently, leaving a picture-less alias). The 'shall not be the same data-name' half and SR5's level restrictions are not separately diagnosed (recorded on kb/Work PB96's sweep list with the span-composition defect).

subject: RENAMES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB96). The no-THRU alias inherits data-name-2's description and storage: ren.Pic = From.Pic and the resolver forwards to the FROM item's place outright (numeric stays numeric — NC252A's ADD 3500 TO RENAME-12).

subject: RENAMES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB96). The THRU alias is an alphanumeric group item over the record's STORAGE WINDOW from data-name-2's first character to data-name-3's last: the span parts are the record's NON-redefining leaves that intersect the window (a REDEFINES view adds no storage; a redefining FROM / THRU maps to the area it overlays; a boundary inside a leaf is a partial part rendered as the leaf's ref-mod view). Before: every leaf between FROM and THRU was listed, views included (A / B REDEFINES A / C was 6 characters, not 4). The shorter-redefinition-as-data-name-3 case is the CONFORMANCE.md §4 determination (the leftmost-to-rightmost reading).

subject: USAGE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-01 (PB183). SIX phrases - INDEX, MESSAGE-TAG, OBJECT REFERENCE, POINTER, FUNCTION-POINTER, PROGRAM-POINTER - barred from a CONSTANT RECORD entry 'or in any item subordinate to' one; the subtree reach is DataBinder.IsConstantRecordItem, shared with the 13.18.15.3 SR2 receiving guard rather than re-walked. The predicate is written as SR14's five phrases PLUS INDEX so the ONE-phrase difference between SR4 and SR14 is the code's own structure; the drift test asserts Sr4 minus Sr14 == {INDEX} in both directions. MESSAGE-TAG has no Usage member (a 2023 addition, VCR row 32) and FUNCTION-POINTER's PicInfo stays null (staged loud at ParseUsage, the P13 band) - both are covered by the WRITTEN-clause arm and held open by EveryUsageMemberCarriesAnSr14Verdict.

subject: USAGE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-01 (PB183). The rule was verified against the PRINTED page (PDF 535 / folio 505) before implementation - the transcription is character-for-character correct and there is no falsely-restrictive OCR here. ONE screen over DataBinder.ConformanceForest() covers all FOUR usage-acquisition routes (a written clause; 13.18.60.4 GR1 group inheritance; a TYPE clone, verdicted ONCE at the template because the forest prunes clones; a SAME AS copy, which is its own written entry). DETERMINATION: level 77 SATISFIES the 'at level 1' arm - 8.5.1.3.2 puts a 77 entry outside the level system ('no true concept of level') and 13.11.1 declares the level-1 and level-77 spellings ALTERNATIVES for one non-hierarchical data element; GnuCOBOL agrees. Held by ONE named predicate (Sr14PermittedLevel) so the determination is a one-line change. The second arm reads the DECLARATION-side TypedefStrong, not the post-expansion StrongType, so a WEAK typedef's pointer member is rejected at the template rather than once per TYPE use. subject: VALUE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB94). The CLASS half — 'all literals in the VALUE clause shall be numeric' — is COBOLNET1657 for an alphanumeric literal, ALL literal or character figurative on a numeric subject (an ALL FORMATS rule: the item VALUE and the condition-name VALUEs share the funnel); error strict, the representable vendor leniency (a digits-only literal is the number, ALL digits repeat to the digit width, a character figurative is ZERO) is a --permissive warning; a non-numeric content is an error on both axes. The RANGE / exact-representation half was already COBOLNET1625 (ValidateNumericValue); the float legs (a/b) are the float items' own.

subject: VALUE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB97). A NEGATIVE literal requires a signed numeric subject or 'a numeric-edited data item with a representation of a sign' — an editing sign symbol (+ - CR DB; for the floating-point form the significand's own sign, never the exponent's +): PIC ZZ9.99 VALUE -5 and PIC 9.99E+9 VALUE -1.23E+5 are COBOLNET1625, PIC -ZZ9.99 VALUE -5 and PIC S9(5)V99 VALUE -1.5E+3 seed. (A leading + into an unsigned subject is not rejected — no data is lost.)

subject: VALUE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB94). A numeric literal on an alphabetic / alphanumeric / alphanumeric-edited subject is COBOLNET1657 (error strict; the characters as MOVE would store them, with a warning, under --permissive); a national / boolean literal on those subjects is the pre-catalog COBOLNET0898 leg. The alphanumeric-literal SIZE halves ('shall not exceed the size indicated by an explicit PICTURE clause') keep the historical truncating store for alphanumeric receivers (documented on ValidateValueCategory) — the numeric-edited size leg is COBOLNET1570 at 2023 (VCR 34).

subject: VALUE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB97 + PB66). A numeric-edited subject's numeric VALUE literals — in formats 1, 2 AND 4 — convert 'according to the rules for the MOVE statement' through the ONE compose (EditedImageOfNumericValue: fixed → CobolEdit.Format, floating → FormatFloatMove, the same runtime a MOVE uses), so an item VALUE bakes the edited image and a level-88 condition-name compares the EDITED image (before PB97 the raw text '10' was compared to ' 10.00' — never true); 'such that no truncation of digits or sign is required' is ValidateNumericValue on the numeric-edited subject (digit positions at the mask's scale; the floating form's significand digits and exponent range — COBOLNET1625); the FORM rule (fixed-point literals for fixed-point formats, floating-point for floating-point, ZERO / the literal zero for either) is decided once in ValidateValueCategory — COBOLNET1659 in either direction. Numeric-literal VALUEs for numeric-edited items are a 2023 capability (Annex E.3.3 item 43 — the VCR-86 gate below 2023, the ZERO forms at every edition).

subject: Initial and last-used states of data
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152). Action 1 is the consumer point 11.9.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 route to, and its ORDER against action 2 is structural: the fill is a BACKGROUND laid down first and then OVERWRITTEN by VALUE clauses, never a per-item substitute for a missing VALUE. pb152_options_initialize_background pins the ordering with an item that HAS a VALUE beside one that does not. No sequencing code was added - a field initializer is one expression, and only the expression's no-VALUE case changed - so the re-application sites (RecordStructEmitter's field initializers and __ResetStatics, the LOCAL-STORAGE per-activation re-seed, the OO instance cell) inherit it by construction. DETERMINATION recorded in CONFORMANCE.md and COBOLNET_DATA_MODEL_DESIGN D23: 'the storage ... is set to the specified-fill-character' over a typed-native model means CHARACTER-FORMED storage takes the fill, while a NATIVE-NUMERIC carrier and an INDEX cell take their zero - licensed by 13.18.63.4 GR4 c), whose own sentence leaves a VALUE-less item 'undefined and set to a value that may or may not be allowed for that data item or index'. Class object/message-tag/pointer take NULL instead, because that same sentence states it as a positive requirement; USAGE BIT keeps its packed ceil(n/8) zero seed (D19) because its storage is packed bytes rather than character positions.

subject: Exception conditions
notes: kb/Work PB77 + PB75 (2026-08-18): with checking for a fatal exception condition NOT enabled 'the implementor defines whether or not execution will continue, how it will continue, and how any receiving operands are affected'. COBOL.NET's determination for the arithmetic size error condition without a SIZE ERROR phrase (EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION, §14.7.5 no-phrase rule 4; A.1 item 70): execution continues and the resultant identifier receives the LOW-ORDER digits of the result aligned at its scale (CobolNum.Store's high-order truncation), for EVERY value carrier — SDIDI (CobolDec.ToUnscaled, PB74), the native exact family (Rescaled's unchecked arm), a binary64 (ToScaledUnchecked / FromDouble's unchecked form — the exact decimal expansion past the Int128 carrier). A non-finite binary64 landing in a fixed-point receiver stores ZERO. An INTERMEDIATE that cannot be formed at all (a standard-decimal intermediate past decimal128, a native value past the Int128 escape boundary in a value-semantics position, an exponentiation-rule violation, a zero divisor) has no result: execution does NOT continue — the run unit terminates abnormally, exit 1, naming the condition (PB75; it used to be a raw CLR crash, exit 127). Documented on CONFORMANCE.md (the item-70 row).

Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). notes: READ: CorrespondingBinder.CorrMatch (91-151) and CorrEligible (160-165) against Sec.14.7.6's six pair-selection rules, which I re-read in full at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21821-21841. Rule 1 (same data-name and same qualifiers up to but not including D1/D2, FILLER excluded): CorrEligible rejects a nameless (FILLER) entry, and the matcher descends ONLY into name-matched group x group pairs (lines 117-124), so a pair's relative qualification path is identical to D1/D2 by construction. Rule 2 is MOVE-only and is correctly routed to the `verb is CorrVerb.Move` arm (125-130) so it does not apply to ADD. Rule 3 ('In an ADD or SUBTRACT statement, both of the data items are numeric data items') is the `else if (s.Pic?.Category is not PicCategory.Numeric || d.Pic?.Category is not PicCategory.Numeric) continue;` at 134-135 -- a silent non-correspondence, not an error, which is what 'a pair of data items correspond if' requires; pinned by AddCorresponding_Rule3_NonNumericNamesakeIsNotAPair (a PIC 9 / PIC X namesake leaves the target 'A' untouched while the numeric namesake still adds). Rule 4 (OCCURS / REDEFINES / RENAMES, class index): CorrEligible tests IsTable, RedefinesTargetName, Renames and Usage.Index; the class object / pointer / message-tag legs are unmodelled but are unreachable for ADD because rule 3 already requires category numeric on BOTH sides. Rule 5 (nothing subordinate to an ineligible intermediate group) holds because the recursion filters with CorrEligible BEFORE descending, so an OCCURS/REDEFINES group's whole subtree is never visited. Rule 6 is applied SYMMETRICALLY (srcCount at 105-112 as well as cands.Count at 114), which is stricter than the legacy matcher and is what 'the name of each data item ... is unique after application of the implied qualifiers' says. SECOND SENTENCE ('the results are the same as if the user had referred to each pair ... in separate ADD statements'): pairs are emitted in D1 declaration order (the `foreach (var s in src.Children)` walk = Sec.14.7.6's 'the implied statements are executed in the order in which the elements in the group data item immediately following CORRESPONDING are specified'), the one statement rounded-phrase reaches every pair (conformance:2014/corresponding_rounded_mode), the group anchors are hoisted so item identification happens once at statement start (CorrAccess.Hoist), and the statement-level SIZE ERROR aggregation Sec.14.7.6 imposes on top of 'separate statements' is pinned by AddCorresponding_SizeError_AggregatedAcrossPairs (one 'SE' dispatch, the erring receiver unchanged at 5, the later pair still stored at 30, the NOT phrase ignored). A zero-pair group pair is a legal empty implied set (line 78-80). || REFUTED -- CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. THE CLOSING EVIDENCE FOR RULES 4 AND 5 IS A LEGACY-ORACLE TEST. conformance-test:CorrespondingDifferentialTests.AddCorresponding_TableShape_OccursChildExcluded (CorrespondingDifferentialTests.cs:235-236) is `AssertSameAsLegacy(...)`, i.e. `DifferentialGolden.Assert`, whose default mode (`COBOLNET_DIFF_MODE` unset -> 'golden', DifferentialGolden.cs:29-31) asserts only that COBOL.NET still equals a committed .out BAKED FROM A LIVE LEGACY RUN (bake mode, lines 51-62). With it gone, rule 4's OCCURS/REDEFINES leg and rule 5's subtree leg have NO spec-derived test on ADD at all. THREE FURTHER UNVERIFIED EDGES, each read out of the code: (a) Sec.14.7.6's no-phrase aggregation -- 'the level-3 EC-SIZE exception condition for the LAST of the implied statements that raised a size error condition is set to exist after all of the implied statements are completed' -- IS implemented (ArithmeticEmitter.EmitArith:236-247 latches `__sizeEcN` by ASSIGNMENT per failing store, so last-wins, and EcEmitter.EmitSizeHandling runs after the pair loop) but has no test whatsoever; (b) CorrEligible's FILLER leg excludes a nameless entry AND, by `continue`-ing before the descent, its ENTIRE SUBTREE, and the code's own doc-comment (lines 152-158) justifies that with 'the legacy/NIST-proven reading' -- the oracle, not a derivation -- while its stated premise ('a FILLER level contributes no qualifier') is precisely the argument that an item under a FILLER group DOES satisfy rule 1's 'the same data-name and the same qualifiers, if any, up to, but not including, D1 and D2' relative to a same-named item declared directly under D2. That reading is unadjudicated against the spec here and is a live silent-non-correspondence risk; (c) CorrespondingEmitter.Emit runs EVERY pair inside ONE `try` (ArithmeticEmitter.EmitArith:245), so a CobolSizeError raised during a pair's EVALUATION (CobolNum.Widen off an unsigned-wide operand) would ABORT the remaining implied statements, which Sec.14.7.6 forbids ('after all of the implied statements are completed') -- reachability unmeasured, the per-pair composite cap makes it unlikely, but the shape is there. Sec.14.7.6 CORRESPONDING: see GR-14.9.2.4-5. Sec.14.7.7 Arithmetic statements: rule 2 is StatementValidation.CheckComposite, rule 4 + NOTE 3 are the Snapshot/one-initial-evaluation discipline in ArithmeticEmitter. THE FIFTH LEG IS SHORT -- Sec.14.6.13.2 Incompatible data: I re-read it at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21630-21664; rule 2 makes EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE exist whenever the content of a NUMERIC sending item that is not standard-floating-point 'is referenced during the execution of a statement' and would fail a numeric class condition -- an ADD's identifier-1, its Format-2 identifier-2, and (per NOTE 2) its Format-1 identifier-2 read-side all qualify. notes: Rule (--check OK, §14.9.3.3 1): data-name-1 shall be described with the BASED clause. Read `PtrBinder.PtrResolveBased`: it looks the name up and returns it only on `if (item is { IsBased: true }) return item;`, otherwise raising COBOLNET0869 '...shall be a BASED level-01/77 item (ISO §14.9.39 SR18 / §14.9.3 SR1 — rebasing or allocating a non-BASED item is not ISO COBOL)'. `PtrBinder.BindAllocate`'s form-2 arm calls it for drefs[0] and returns BoundNop on failure, so a non-BASED data-name-1 never reaches the emitter. Evidence: conformance:negative/allocate-non-based is exactly this rule's fixture (`01 W PIC X(5).` + `ALLOCATE W RETURNING P.`, reject-at 2002 2014 2023, .err expecting 'the operand shall be a BASED level-01/77 item') and is registered in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json. OBSERVATION, not a downgrade: PtrResolveBased deliberately bypasses the SymbolTable (`dref.ChildCount == 1 && ctx.Data.ByName.TryGetValue(...) ? list[0] : null`, a bypass the class doc flags as a behavior-sensitive follow-up). It rejects a qualified/subscripted operand, which costs nothing here because BASED is a level-01/77 clause and such a name has no higher group to qualify it; and `ByName` is per-program-unit (BinderDriver.cs:383 constructs a DataBinder inside the per-unit loop), so the list[0] pick cannot cross program units. The SR1 predicate itself is exactly the rule. || UPHELD, and the 'no higher group to qualify it' premise is now MEASURED rather than assumed: specs/ISO_COBOL.md:15101 (§13.18.x SR16) reads 'The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section, in the working-storage section, and in the local-storage section. The level number of such data description entries shall be 1 or 77' — so a based entry is never in an FD and has no containing group, and the only legal reference to it is the bare name that `dref.ChildCount == 1` admits. I read PtrBinder.cs:194-203 and confirmed the predicate is `item is { IsBased: true }` with the 0869 error on every other path, and I read the fixture + its .err and confirmed the manifest registration by loading tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json. notes: Rule re-read in context at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 14.9.4.4 1) under the 'FORMATS 1 AND 2' heading; citation validated (`cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "The instance of the program, function, or method that executes the CALL statement is the activating runtime element."` -> OK, General rules 1). It is not maintained across nested activations. Read ProgramTable.CallProgram lines 180-233: for an INITIAL or RECURSIVE unit it does `inst = n.Factory(ParentInstance(n)); n.Instance = inst;` and the `finally` restores ONLY `n.Active--`, the module frame and the EC masks - `n.Instance` is NEVER restored to the outer activation's instance. ProgramTable.ParentInstance reads exactly that field (`_byPath[n.ParentPath].Instance`), and ProgramEmitter.EmitProgramClass emits a contained program's container handle as `private readonly {parent.ClassName} __outer;` assigned once in the constructor, with every inherited GLOBAL item reaching container storage through it (`private ref {type} {b.Field} => ref {b.Path};   // GLOBAL item of a containing program (ISO 13.18.27 GR2)`, BinderDriver.BindUnitData building `__outer.` prefixes). So for a RECURSIVE container R containing C: R#1 calls C -> C is a cached singleton (`inst = n.Instance ??= n.Factory(ParentInstance(n))`) with __outer = inst1; R#1 calls itself -> inst2, `R.Instance = inst2`; inst2 calls C -> the SAME cached C, still bound to inst1, so the callee reads and writes the OUTER activation's storage. The reverse is broken too: after inst2 returns, `R.Instance` still names inst2, so a per-activation callee constructed from inst1's CALL gets a TERMINATED instance as its activating element. Reachable on conforming source: the WORKING-STORAGE composition is loud-staged (DiagnosticCatalog.RecursiveContainedWs, negative fixture tests/conformance/negative/recursive-contained-ws.cob) but LOCAL-STORAGE is not, and 13.18.27.3 SR1b (`cite.py --check 13.18.27.3` -> OK) permits IS GLOBAL on 'A data description entry whose level-number is 1 that is specified in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section' - so `PROGRAM-ID. R RECURSIVE.` + `LOCAL-STORAGE SECTION. 01 LS-G PIC 9(4) GLOBAL.` + a contained C that references LS-G compiles and answers with the wrong activation's automatic data. SECOND, INDEPENDENT HALF: the recursive attribute is not per-containment either - BinderDriver.MakeUnit sets `recursive` ONLY from this unit's own PROGRAM-ID clause plus `if (isFunction) recursive = true`, while 11.10.4 GR4 (`cite.py --check 11.10.4 "The RECURSIVE clause specifies that the program and any programs contained within it are recursive."` -> OK) makes every program contained in a RECURSIVE program recursive, so those containees take the cached-singleton instance model (last-used state) instead of the per-activation instance this rule's 'instance ... is the activating runtime element' requires. What would close the row: an activation STACK of instances per node (push/pop around `inst.Call`) so ParentInstance answers 'the instance that is executing the CALL', __outer rebound per activation for a contained callee, the 11.10.4 GR4 attribute inheritance, plus a golden with a RECURSIVE container, a LOCAL-STORAGE GLOBAL item and a contained callee printing it at two depths. Editions: no Annex E delta touches this rule (E.2's only CALL entry is item 1 bullet 3, the ON OVERFLOW removal), so the batch default applies.

notes: This rule-id carries TWO spec rules: 14.9.4.4 3h) item 3 ('If checking for the exception condition is not enabled, subsequent behavior is as specified in 14.6.13.1, Exception conditions') and the whole of 3i). || UPHELD, including the swallow finding, which I re-derived from the emitted control flow rather than trusting the note. (3i, propagation) EmitPropagationPickup emits the activator-side pickup of a callee-staged GOBACK/EXIT PROGRAM ... RAISING condition, running the 14.9.49 F3 selection over the dynamic name and honoring RESUME (14.6.13.1.3 #6). (3h#3) with no phrase and no enabled name, `!hasPhrase && ecProg.Count == 0` emits the BARE invocation, so the CobolCallException propagates to ProgramTable.RunMain's `catch (CobolCallException cx) { AbnormalTermination(cx.Message) }` - the documented 14.6.13.1.3 #8 implementor choice. UNVERIFIED / DIVERGENT HALVES: (a) a CALL written with ONLY a NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase and no enabled checking SILENTLY SWALLOWS a failure - `hasPhrase = c.OnException is not null || c.NotOnException is not null` is TRUE, so the unfiltered `catch (CobolCallException) { __callErr = true; }` is emitted, `c.OnException` is null so only the `if (!__callErr) { not }` block is written, the NOT-ON body is skipped, and execution falls to the end of the CALL with no diagnostic and no status - while the identical CALL without the NOT ON phrase terminates the run unit loudly. GR3h has no ON EXCEPTION phrase in that source, so item 2 or item 3 governs, and this implementation's item-3 disposition everywhere else is loud termination - so the phrase changes the outcome of a rule it is not a party to. (b) 3i's 'the ON EXCEPTION phrase, if specified, is ignored' is violated for a condition raised INSIDE a successfully-called program that surfaces as a CobolCallException - CobolArgAdapt.Omitted's EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED unwinds past ProgramTable.CallProgram's try/finally into the caller's phrase catch and runs imperative-statement-1. The failure shape to look for is a bare CONTINUE that behaves OBSERVABLY differently from the AFTER-0 spelling under some ambient state. READ: ControlFlowBinder.BindContinue (ControlFlowBinder.cs:57-62) -- `if (cont.arithmeticExpression() is not { } secs) return new BoundNop();` -- and StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundNop) (StatementEmitter.cs:147) returns false emitting nothing, so control simply falls to the next emitted statement. CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION` the AFTER form additionally wraps itself in `ExceptionState.EnterStatement("CONTINUE", loc, ...)` / `ExitStatement` (exception_statement_ambient.g.cs:151-156), but that pair is SAVE-and-RESTORE (ExceptionState.cs:79-88) and nothing raises inside it, so LastStatement/LastLocation are identical afterwards to what a bare CONTINUE leaves -- FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION cannot tell the spellings apart. The claim was that 'COMMIT lexes as a facility IDENTIFIER' so 'APPLY COMMIT ON F' is absorbed by genericClause and silently dropped. It is not: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4 line 436 defines a dedicated token 'COMMIT : 'COMMIT' ;', and genericClause (CobolExpressions.g4) is 'IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER | literal)*' over the IDENTIFIER TOKEN -- not over cobolWord, which is the rule that lists COMMIT as a context-sensitive user word (CobolWords.g4). So in 'ioControlParagraph : I_O_CONTROL DOT (ioControlClause DOT?)*', genericClause consumes only 'APPLY' (no APPLY token exists, so it lexes as IDENTIFIER), the COMMIT token matches no alternative of ioControlClause, the loop exits and COMMIT is left unmatched -> a syntax error. 12.4.6.3.2's format is 'APPLY COMMIT ON [ [ file-name-1 ] [ identifier-1 ] ]...', so the clause is LOUDLY REJECTED, not silently swallowed. subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: UNDER-REJECTION: legal-looking source the standard FORBIDS is accepted and compiled. Rule: 'Identifier-1 shall not reference a data item of class message-tag, object, or pointer.' (cite.py --check 14.9.11.3 OK, rule 1.) READ BindDisplay in full: for each operand child it does exactly one screen -- ExpressionBinder.ScreenIndexNameOperand for a bare INDEX-NAME (13.18.38.3 r7, kb/Work R16, landed) -- and NO class screen. Grepped src/Cobol.Net.Compiler for any class-based exclusion on a DISPLAY operand: the only pointer/object screens in the tree are ConditionBinder's 8.8.4.2.3 SR5 object-relation check, StatementValidation.ContainsNonOrderableLeaf (strongly-typed group ordering), ReferenceResolver.RefModExclusion (8.4.3.3.3 SR1) and DataBinder.Linkage's BY VALUE formal-class check -- none of them on this path. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS to a forbidden operand: FieldOperand binds a BoundFieldOperand, and at emit OperandText.FieldAsString falls through every arm of its final 'p.Item.Pic switch' (Alphanumeric / NumericEdited / National / Boolean / Numeric / float are enumerated; PicCategory.Pointer, PicCategory.ProgramPointer and PicCategory.ObjectReference are not) to the default arm '_ => $"{PlaceRenderer.Read(p)}.ToString()"'. So 'DISPLAY WS-PTR' over '01 WS-PTR USAGE POINTER.' compiles clean and prints ManagedPointer.ToString() -- a value with no COBOL meaning -- and 'DISPLAY WS-OBJ' over an OBJECT REFERENCE item prints the CLR object's ToString(). Both classes are fully modelled here (PicInfo.cs:296/302, carriers 'ManagedPointer' and the object-reference type; DataBinder.Ptr.cs / DataBinder.Oo.cs), so this is reachable from ordinary source, not theoretical. THE THIRD CLASS IS VACUOUS AND SHOULD NOT BE COUNTED AS PASSING: class message-tag has no Usage member at all (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:60-68 states the MCS facility is unmodelled and deliberately gets no dead enum member), so no message-tag operand can be constructed -- the rule's third arm is satisfied by absence, not by a check. FIX SHAPE (structural, per one_rule_one_place): the exclusion is a CLASS-set screen and IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf already computes CobolClass for any BoundOperand including Pointer / Object; the screen belongs beside ScreenIndexNameOperand as a reusable operand-class gate, because the identical 'shall not be of class X' shape recurs across statement operand slots -- sweep for the siblings rather than adding one inline test in BindDisplay. WOULD CLOSE: that screen plus negative fixtures conformance:negative/display-pointer-operand and conformance:negative/display-object-operand. || UPHELD, and WIDENED. I read OperandText.cs end to end and confirmed the fall-through: FieldAsString's terminal switch enumerates { IsUnsignedWideBinary }, { Numeric, IsFloat: false }, { Numeric } (float), and { Alphanumeric or NumericEdited or National or Boolean }, then '_ => $"{PlaceRenderer.Read(p)}.ToString()"'. I also confirmed the PicCategory enum's tail is ObjectReference, Pointer, ProgramPointer (PicInfo.cs:36-47) -- three categories with no matching arm, so all three take the default. WIDENING, with citations I ran myself: 'class pointer' in this standard spans THREE categories, not one -- 8.4.3.11.4 GR1 'Data-address-identifier creates a unique data item of class pointer and category data-pointer', 8.4.3.12.4 GR1 '... of class pointer and category function-pointer' (--check OK), 8.4.3.13.4 GR1 '... of class pointer and category program-pointer' (--check OK), and 8.8.4.2.3 item 11 speaks of 'two operands of class pointer where each operand is of the same category'. So the missing screen must exclude data-pointer, function-pointer AND program-pointer, plus class object -- a four-category set, not the two shapes the note names; a fix that special-cases USAGE POINTER and OBJECT REFERENCE would leave USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER (a modelled category here, PicCategory.ProgramPointer, live since P10 Step 7) still printing a CLR ToString(). That is exactly the feedback_model_the_rule_shape_not_one_case failure the fix must avoid, and it reinforces the adjudicator's CLASS-SET fix shape over an inline per-usage test. Verdict DIVERGES stands.

NO TEST-REF, deliberately: the antecedent is unpopulatable by declaration, so no spec-derived test can exist for this row; it is CONFORMS-but-untestable, not CONFORMS-but-untested. What would change the verdict is the arrival of a device (a printer / reel mnemonic) for which vertical positioning is inapplicable -- at that point GR11 needs real code and this row must be re-adjudicated. || UPHELD with my own reads. I re-located A.3 item 24 in the spec independently (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, Annex A.3 'Processor-dependent language element list' begins at the section-a-3 anchor; item 24 is the DISPLAY positioning row, text verbatim as quoted) and confirmed it is the A.3 counterpart of GR11 rather than of GR9. READ: BindDivide binds `var a = host.Expr.BindExpr(aCtx)` with the comment 'INTO: the divisor; BY: the dividend', then INTO-with-GIVING returns `BoundDivideGiving(dividendX, a, ...)` where dividendX = BindExpr(into.divideIntoOperand()) and BY-with-GIVING returns `BoundDivideGiving(a, divisorX, ...)` where divisorX = BindExpr(byPhrase.divideOperand()); the record is `BoundDivideGiving(BoundExpr Dividend, BoundExpr Divisor, ...)`, so both map correctly. The REMAINDER branch repeats the same mapping through its two conditional expressions (`dividend = intoPhrase ? BindExpr(i.divideIntoOperand()) : a` / `divisor = intoPhrase is not null ? a : BindExpr(b.divideOperand())`) — checked arm by arm, both arms correct. Format 1 (no GIVING) makes each identifier-2 both dividend and receiver: EmitDivide is called with dividend null and reads `num.FieldNum(r.Place)` per receiver — the identifier-2-as-dividend reading. subject: DIVIDE statement
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.12.4 "the remainder is the result of multiplying the subsidiary quotient and the divisor and subtracting the product from the dividend"` -> OK, GR 7). DERIVED FIRST: remainder = dividend - (subsidiary-quotient * divisor), with dividend/divisor as defined in GR2 and the subsidiary quotient as defined in GR6c. READ: EmitDivideRemainder builds `var product = new NumX($"({qt} * {divisor.Expr})", qs + divisor.Scale)` — qt is the GR6c subsidiary quotient at the quotient receiver's scale, and the NumX scale qs + divisor.Scale is the exact scale of the product so the subtraction aligns radix points without loss — then `NumX remainder = num.Combine(dividend, "-", product, rcv)`. That is GR7's expression literally, over the SAME snapshotted dividend/divisor GR2 defines (both materialized by Snapshot(num.FixedLane(...)) before the quotient store, so a quotient receiver aliasing a sender cannot poison it). Both arithmetic lanes are covered by that one Combine: native falls to CombineNative, and STANDARD/STANDARD-DECIMAL to `CobolDec.Sub(..., IntermediateMode)`, i.e. GR7's second sentence. The float lane was the subject of landed kb/Work PB85 (FixedLane) and is not re-reported. (1) The rejected argument was that truncating the subsidiary quotient at the receiver's SCALE rather than its DIGITS 'is exactly equivalent within GR7's reachable domain, because the differing case is the one GR6c's leading condition excludes'. That holds ONLY where the leading condition is implemented — and GR-14.9.12.4-6 records that it is NOT, and that the no-phrase path silently truncates the quotient into identifier-3 while `qt` keeps its full digit count. So the scale-only truncation IS observable: `01 D PIC 9(4) VALUE 1000. 01 V PIC 9 VALUE 3. 01 Q PIC 9. 01 R PIC 9(4).` then `DIVIDE V INTO D GIVING Q REMAINDER R.` (no phrase) stores Q = 3 and R = 1000 - 333*3 = 1, from a subsidiary quotient of 333 that GR6c requires to have Q's ONE digit. The scale-only truncation is a real gap, not a provably-equivalent shortcut; it is filed on the GR-6 row where GR6c defines the subsidiary quotient, and named here because GR7 consumes it. (2) NEW, in this symbol's own expression: the back-multiply is emitted as the raw string `({qt} * {divisor.Expr})` at ArithmeticEmitter.cs:130, bypassing NumericRenderer.CombineNative's `"*" => Checked ? CobolNum.MulChecked(a, b) : ((Int128)(a) * (b))` fork (:417). Every other product in the engine gets the checked form under a SIZE ERROR phrase so an Int128 intermediate overflow becomes the size error condition (14.7.5 case 5 — 'if native arithmetic is in effect and the implementor defines that the range of values allowed for the intermediate data item is to be checked'; validated by reading 14.7.5's case list at spec 21778). This one does not: the unscaled product is (quotient x 10^qs)(divisor x 10^ds), so a deeply scaled quotient receiver and divisor push it past Int128 while the 31-digit composite of operands (14.7.7 rule 2) is still satisfied — e.g. dividend PIC 9(12)V9(9), divisor PIC 9V9(14), quotient PIC 9(12)V9(14) has composite 12+14 = 26 <= 31 yet an unscaled product near 10^40, which wraps silently in C#'s default unchecked Int128 multiply and yields a wrong remainder with no size error.
