subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB330. “An OPEN statement that specifies file-name-1 more than once shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement” (cite.py --check 14.9.27.3 … OK, rule 3). Implemented and correct, including the half a naive implementation misses. CheckCrossStatementBans walks region A (imperative-statement-1 only, matching the rule's scope) and FLATTENS the whole statement — `op.openClause().SelectMany(oc => oc.openFileSpec())` — before grouping, so a duplicate is caught whether it repeats inside ONE mode group or ACROSS two, which is what “specifies file-name-1 more than once” means over a format whose file list is a repeated group. Case-folded with ToUpperInvariant, so the COBOL word's case-insensitivity is honoured. MEASURED (probe/open-p1): xsopen.cob, whose imperative-statement-1 is `OPEN OUTPUT F1 INPUT F1` (the CROSS-group form, which the existing test does not exercise), is rejected COBOLNET1616 at --std 2023. The existing test covers the same-group form (`OPEN INPUT F1 F1`). Editions: 2023 only — Annex E item 19 introduces the facility (“Inline exception processing. The PERFORM statement is enhanced to allow checking for exception conditions inline”), Annex E being the 2014→2023 change list, and the compiler agrees (--std 2014 adds COBOLNET0900 “the Format-3 (exception-checking) PERFORM requires COBOL-2023”), so below 2023 there is no construct for the rule to govern. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED ON THE RULE'S READING, WHICH THE ADJUDICATION NEVER WEIGHED. The mechanism it located is real and I could not break it: EcBinder.ExceptionPerform.cs#CheckCrossStatementBans walks region A = p.statementBlock() (the grammar puts the WHEN/OTHER/COMMON/FINALLY bodies in their own contexts, so region A really is imperative-statement-1), flattens openClause()->openFileSpec() so a repeat is caught across mode groups as well as inside one, and case-folds. 13 probes confirm it: rejected COBOLNET1616 for the cross-group form, a case-different spelling (f1/F1), the OPEN nested in IF/END-IF and in EVALUATE, one instance carrying WITH NO REWIND, three occurrences over three groups, the [WITH] LOCATION head form, and a nested F3 PERFORM's own imp-1; correctly SILENT for two different files, a dup in a WHEN body, in WHEN OTHER, in FINALLY, and in a Format-2 inline PERFORM (not an exception-checking PERFORM). BUT THE ROW IMPLEMENTS ONLY ONE OF TWO READINGS OF 'specifies file-name-1 more than once', and the evidence runs against the one chosen. (a) FAMILY: every sibling imp-1 ban forbids the MULTI-OPERAND form - CLOSE 'specifies more than one file-name' (14.9.6.3 r3), DELETE FILE 'more than one file-name' (14.9.10.3 r4), VALIDATE 'more than one identifier' (14.9.50.3 r6), INITIALIZE 'Identifier-1 shall be specified only once' (14.9.20.3 r2), MERGE/SORT banned outright. On the duplicate reading OPEN is the sole outlier: it would ban a thing that is already erroneous everywhere while permitting exactly the multi-operand form its four siblings forbid. (b) PHRASING: when this standard means 'no duplicates' it says so - 'The same category shall not be repeated' (14.9.20.3 r6, the same clause as r2), 'A given class name', 'A particular user-defined word', 'Any particular screen-attribute'; 8 of the 9 unambiguous duplicate rules carry such an anchor and 14.9.27.3 r3 carries none. (c) PURPOSE: 14.9.27.4 GR25c - an unsuccessful OPEN in imp-1 transfers control to the WHEN phrase, so the file-names after the failing one never open; GR20 defines resumption for that partial execution ONLY on the declarative path ('processing resumes at the next implicit OPEN statement'), and RESUME NEXT STATEMENT is equally legal in a WHEN phrase (14.9.33.3 r1). Banning the multi-file OPEN in imp-1 is what closes that hole; banning a duplicate does not touch it. MEASURED, and this is the whole finding: OPEN OUTPUT F1 F2 F3 inside imperative-statement-1 of a Format-3 PERFORM COMPILES CLEAN and runs at --std 2023, while the same shape written as CLOSE F1 F2 is rejected COBOLNET1612 and VALIDATE N M is rejected COBOLNET1607. The compiler switched readings exactly where the rule text switched from 'more than one X' to the operand tag - and it did so TWICE: INITIALIZE N M in imp-1 also compiles clean (COBOLNET1614 is a duplicate check, 14.9.20.3 r2 is not), the sibling this defect predicts. The honest counter-evidence: 14.9.28.3 r14 does use a bare operand tag for a duplicate rule ('If file-name-1 or file-name-2 is specified in a WHEN phrase, IT shall not be specified more than once...') - but it anchors with 'it' after naming a specific instance, and its 'unless all such instances' tail makes the duplicate sense explicit. 14.9.27.3 r3 has neither. PARTIAL, not DIVERGES: the implemented ban is a strict SUBSET of the wider reading (a duplicate is also two operands), so nothing legal is rejected and the narrow branch is genuinely implemented and pinned by a spec-derived test. What CONFORMS cannot survive is that the row's whole claim rests on a reading the adjudicator did not derive, that the rule's own family, phrasing convention and stated purpose all contradict, and whose wider branch has ZERO enforcement. Settle the reading first; if the wider reading holds, the row is closer to NOT-IMPLEMENTED than to CONFORMS. Editions 2023 upheld (E.2 item 19 checked). One incidental: the cited test's own file carries a broken sibling - PerformFormat3Tests.BareAndFilePairedSameName_Rejected1600 has the body of MultiFileDeleteInImp1_Rejected1613 and asserts COBOLNET1613, so the 14.9.28.3 r15 branch it names is untested.

subject: OPEN statement
notes:
kb/Work PB319. “When file-name-1 is not subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause, then if the sharing phrase is omitted from the OPEN statement and the ALL phrase is specified in the SHARING clause of the file control entry for file-name-1 or if the ALL phrase is specified on the OPEN statement, the LOCK MODE clause shall be specified in the file control entry for file-name-1” (cite.py --check 14.9.27.3 "the LOCK MODE clause shall be specified in the file control entry for file-name-1" → OK, rule 8). The rule is a CONDITIONAL on an OPEN statement with two disjuncts — [phrase omitted AND SELECT says ALL] OR [ALL on the OPEN] — and the compiler enforces it in TWO places, each wrong in a different direction.
DEFECT 1 — THE SELECT-TIME CHECK DROPS THE CONDITIONAL ENTIRELY AND REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE. DataBinder.BindFileControl fires COBOLNET1512 the moment a file control entry says SHARING WITH ALL OTHER without a LOCK MODE clause, with no reference to any OPEN statement at all. §14.9.27.3 is the OPEN statement's syntax rules and SR8's antecedent names the OPEN; the SHARING clause's own clause imposes nothing of the kind — §12.4.5.15.3 has exactly ONE general rule and NO syntax rules (read whole). So a program whose OPEN supplies its own non-ALL sharing phrase satisfies neither disjunct and is legal. MEASURED (probe/open-p1): sr8ovr.cob — `SELECT F1 … SHARING WITH ALL OTHER` with no LOCK MODE, and `OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH NO OTHER F1` — is REJECTED, COBOLNET1512 at the SELECT line 6. Expected: compiles. A program that declares SHARING WITH ALL OTHER and never OPENs the file is the same over-rejection; that one is currently PINNED GREEN by tests/conformance/negative/sharing-all-no-lockmode.cob, whose program has no OPEN statement in it — a green negative golden holding a defect open (feedback/green_test_can_hold_a_gap_open), so the golden has to move with the fix.
DEFECT 2 — THE OPEN-TIME CHECK IS ORDER-DEPENDENT, BECAUSE ITS INPUT LEAKS ACROSS THE FORMAT'S REPEATED GROUP. StatementValidation.CheckOpenSharingAllOther is itself a faithful transcription of the disjunction (`effectiveSharing is AllOther && file.LockMode is null` over `sharing ?? file.Sharing`), but BindOpen computes `sharing` in a variable hoisted OUTSIDE the `foreach (var clause in o.openClause())` loop and never resets it, so one group's phrase is fed to every LATER group's check. MEASURED (probe/open-p1): shrA.cob `OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER F1 OUTPUT F2` is REJECTED (COBOLNET1512 naming F2, which has neither a SHARING clause nor a LOCK MODE clause); shrB.cob writes the SAME two groups in the other order, `OPEN OUTPUT F2 OUTPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER F1`, and COMPILES CLEAN. Two orderings of one repeated group cannot have two verdicts under any reading of SR8 — that is the proof the mechanism is leaked state and not a rule. Both reproduce identically at --std 2002, 2014 and 2023; at --std 85 the construct is correctly gated first (COBOLNET0900).
The rule's leading exemption (“When file-name-1 is not subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause”) is not modelled, which is harmless here only because APPLY COMMIT is a parse error (see SR-14.9.27.3-7) — it becomes live the day A.4.3 is claimed. subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB323. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 OK, 3)): 'If the file associated with file-name-1 is present and insufficient authority exists to open the file, the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, and the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to \'37\''. CODE: FileConnector.Open wraps OpenCore in `catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) { s = FileStatusCode.PermissionDenied; }` (= '37'), which IS correct for the path where the stream constructor itself is refused. BUT every OpenCore decides PRESENCE with `bool exists = File.Exists(HostPath)` (SequentialConnector.cs:210, RelativeConnector.cs:96, IndexedConnector.cs:126), and File.Exists swallows every access error and answers false — so a file that IS present but whose attributes the process may not read classifies as ABSENT and never reaches the '37' mapping. This is the EXACT probe the PB140 sweep already replaced in the DELETE FILE twin: FileRegistry.cs:462-465 carries the comment 'File.Exists swallows every access error and answers false, classifying a PRESENT-but-unobservable file as gone — GR16 requires \'37\' there — so the probe is File.GetAttributes, whose failures DISTINGUISH the two (PB140)'. The OPEN arm of that same sweep was never done (feedback_two_arm_dispatch). PROBE (out-b1/probe/gr3-authority): a present file under a directory whose DACL denies the running user (icacls /deny :(RX)); .NET reports File.Exists = False while File.GetAttributes THROWS. `SELECT FP ASSIGN TO "locked/secret.dat"` → OPEN INPUT gives '35'; `SELECT OPTIONAL FQ` over the same path → OPEN INPUT gives '05' (a SUCCESSFUL open) and the first READ reports AT END '10'. SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: '37' and an unsuccessful open in both cases. The OPTIONAL leg is the silent one — the program is told a file it has no authority to read simply does not exist. No spec-derived test drives an authority failure on OPEN (FileStatusDisciplineTests.DeleteFileFailure_MediumRefusalIs37_OtherIs30 tests only the DELETE FILE twin), so test-ref is empty. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. GR3's explicit '37' sentence is the 2023 clarification (Annex E.2 item 18, 'The OPEN statement may return a file status \'37\' for insufficient authority to open a file'); docs/CONFORMANCE.md §3 determines it is emitted at EVERY edition and not gated, so the rule is adjudicated at all four.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB317. RULE: 'The NO REWIND phrase will be ignored if it does not apply to the storage medium on which the file resides. If the NO REWIND phrase is ignored, the OPEN statement is successful and the I-O status associated with file-name-1 is set to \'07\'.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 11)). WHAT 'does not apply to the storage medium' MEANS is settled by §9.1.13.2 6) — cite.py --check 9.1.13.2 'An OPEN or CLOSE statement is successfully executed but a CLOSE statement with the NO REWIND, REEL/UNIT, or FOR REMOVAL phrase or an OPEN statement with the NO REWIND phrase references a physical file on a non-reel/unit medium.': OK (§9.1.13.2 6)). COBOL.NET's only medium is mass storage (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 rows 31/32/35 claim 'Mass-storage DELETE / I-O open / rewrite'; FileRegistry.CloseReelUnit and CloseNoRewind name it 'a non-reel/unit medium' in their own doc comments), so EVERY OPEN … WITH NO REWIND here is exactly the §9.1.13.2 6) case and must set '07'. CODE: the phrase parses — CobolIO.g4 openFileSpec: 'dataReference (REVERSED | WITH? NO REWIND)?' — and is then DROPPED: BindOpen reads only spec.dataReference() (SequentialIoBinder.cs:37-45), BoundOpen carries no REWIND field, EmitOpen emits a bare FileOpen, and neither FileRegistry.Open nor FileConnector.Open has a no-rewind parameter. There is no OpenNoRewind surface at all, while the CLOSE twin (FileRegistry.CloseNoRewind) DOES set '07' and cites §9.1.13.2 item 6 for it. PROBE (out-b1/probe/norewind/NOREW01.cob, --std default 2023): OPEN INPUT F WITH NO REWIND ⇒ FILE STATUS '00'; OPEN OUTPUT F WITH NO REWIND ⇒ '00'; CLOSE F WITH NO REWIND ⇒ '07'. Spec-derived expected: '07' for both OPENs (GR11 + §9.1.13.2 6)). Observed: '00'. A program that tests FILE STATUS = '07' after an OPEN … WITH NO REWIND — the documented way to learn the phrase was inert — gets the wrong answer. The A.3-item-33 escape does NOT apply: cite.py --check A.3 'The WITH NO REWIND phrase of the OPEN statement is dependent upon a reel or mass storage type of device.': OK (§A.3 33)) — a mass storage device IS present, and the identically-worded CLOSE twin (§A.3 30), OK by --check) is implemented. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row '33–34 … Partial | EXTEND claimed; WITH NO REWIND inert (no reel device)' is therefore itself wrong on A.3 item 33's own words, and neither §4 (documented non-support facilities) nor §5 (A.4 modules) covers it — so this is a defect, not a documented non-support. FINDING: open-no-rewind-07-arm-missing. Test-needed. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB317. RULE: 'If the storage medium for the file permits rewinding, the following rules apply: a) When neither the EXTEND, nor the NO REWIND phrase is specified, execution of the OPEN statement causes the file to be positioned at its beginning. b) When the NO REWIND phrase is specified, execution of the OPEN statement does not cause the file to be repositioned; the file shall be already positioned at its beginning prior to execution of the OPEN statement.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 12)). ARM (a) — VERIFIED. SequentialConnector.OpenCore resets _readOffset/_readOrdinal/_lineByteOffset to 0 and opens INPUT with a fresh StreamReader at offset 0 and OUTPUT with FileMode.Create (truncating); RelativeConnector.OpenCore sets _fpi = 1; IndexedConnector.OpenCore sets _fpiKey = "" with _positioner='O' so the first READ NEXT takes Ordered(-1)[0]. PROBE (out-b1/probe/openbasic/OPBAS01.cob): after writing AAAAAAAAAA then EXTEND-appending BBBBBBBBBB, OPEN INPUT + READ returns AAAAAAAAAA — positioned at the beginning. PROBE (out-b1/probe/openkeyed/OPKEY01.cob, OPKEY02.cob): relative first READ = slot 1, indexed first READ = the lowest prime key. ARM (b) — NOT IMPLEMENTED. The NO REWIND phrase never reaches the bound tree (see GR11), so there is no arm that suppresses repositioning; OPEN OUTPUT … WITH NO REWIND truncates the file exactly as a plain OPEN OUTPUT does. On this mass-storage medium GR11 (not GR12b) is the governing rule — the phrase is ignored and the status must be '07' — but that arm is missing too, so the implementation holds no coherent position on NO REWIND at either rule. PARTIAL, and the harm is recorded under GR11 (finding open-no-rewind-07-arm-missing). Test-needed for arm (a) as well: no spec-derived test asserts the OPEN-positions-at-beginning invariant for any organization. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB328. RULE: 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode. If the file does not support those statements, the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to \'37\' and the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful. The successful execution of an OPEN statement with the I-O phrase sets the open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 to open in the I-O mode.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 16)). TWO halves; both checked. HALF 1 ('37'): FileConnector.Open wraps OpenCore in 'catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) { s = FileStatusCode.PermissionDenied; }'. §9.1.13.6 6) gives ONE status '37' for BOTH sub-case a2 (the I-O phrase is specified but the file will not support the I-O operations) and sub-case b (insufficient authority), so the sub-case distinction is not observable through the FILE STATUS item and the single mapping discharges both. VERIFIED, not deduced — PROBE out-b1/probe/io37/IO3701.cob against a read-only io3701.dat: OPEN I-O ⇒ '37', OPEN EXTEND ⇒ '37' (§9.1.13.6 6a1's twin), OPEN INPUT ⇒ '00'. Spec-derived expected: '37' for the two write-requiring modes, success for INPUT. HALF 2 (open mode set to I-O): FileConnector.Open sets Mode = mode before OpenCore and _openMode on a success-family status; the sequential I-O arm opens the stream FileAccess.ReadWrite so both READ and REWRITE reach it. PROBE out-b1/probe/openkeyed/OPKEY02.cob: after OPEN I-O the READ NEXT succeeds ('00') and the REWRITE succeeds ('00') with the change visible on a re-OPEN INPUT; PROBE out-b1/probe/openkeyed/OPKEY01.cob: a WRITE on an ACCESS SEQUENTIAL file open I-O is '48' — the Table-20 row for sequential access, which does not permit WRITE in the I-O column (that is GR8's rule, outside this part, but it confirms the mode really is I-O and not output). No spec-derived test covers either half — test-needed. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — REFUTED. The rule has two halves; the adjudicator verified half 2 (the open mode is set to I-O) but tested half 1 - the '37' arm - on ONE organization. Half 1 is the project's signature defect shape (a dispatch with several arms and only one right) and it is a WRONG-ANSWER defect with data loss. The rule requires: if the file will not support the input and output statements permitted for its organization in I-O mode, the status is '37' and the OPEN is UNSUCCESSFUL (9.1.13.6 6) a) 2., cite.py --check 9.1.13.6: OK). The compiler's ONLY producer of '37' on OPEN is 'catch (UnauthorizedAccessException)' wrapped around OpenCore at FileConnector.cs:181-183. That catch fires for SEQUENTIAL because SequentialConnector.OpenCore opens a WRITE-capable stream in the I-O arm (SequentialConnector.cs:263). It never fires for RELATIVE or INDEXED, whose I-O arms only call Attach() - a READ of the store (RelativeConnector.cs:127, IndexedConnector.cs:158) - so writability is never probed at OPEN. On the SAME read-only file the compiler answers '37' for sequential and '00' for indexed and relative. Worse, the OPEN's success is believed downstream: READ NEXT is '00', a REWRITE of that record is '00', and the loss surfaces only as '30' at CLOSE on a file that is byte-for-byte unchanged. The compiler CAN detect the condition - OPEN OUTPUT on the same read-only keyed files correctly answers '37', because that arm eagerly calls RecordFraming.WriteStore - so this is a detection-SITE defect, not a platform limit. Corrected verdict DIVERGES, not PARTIAL: this is not an unverified edge, it is a measured wrong answer. SWEEP (rule 4, sibling): the identical omission makes OPEN EXTEND on a read-only indexed/relative file answer '00' where 9.1.13.6 6) a) 1. requires '37'; that belongs to the EXTEND/OUTPUT rule outside this part and should be recorded with the same fix. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023

notes: kb/Work PB322. RULE: 'If the OUTPUT phrase is specified, the successful execution of the OPEN statement creates the file. After the creation of the file, the file contains no records. If physical pages have meaning for the file, the positioning of the output medium with respect to physical page boundaries is implementor-defined following the successful execution of the OPEN statement, whether or not the LINAGE clause is specified in the file description entry of file-name-1.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 18)). TWO halves. HALF 1 (creates the file, no records) — VERIFIED. SequentialConnector.OpenCore's Output arm uses FileMode.Create / StreamWriter(append: false), which creates or TRUNCATES; RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector clear the shared store and RecordFraming.WriteStore(HostPath, []). PROBE (out-b1/probe/openbasic/OPBAS01.cob): a file holding two records, re-OPENed OUTPUT and CLOSEd, then OPEN INPUT + READ ⇒ AT END '10' — the file contains no records. Spec-derived expected: exactly that. HALF 2 (physical page positioning, implementor-defined) — NOT DISCHARGED. cite.py --check A.1 'OPEN statement with OUTPUT phrase (positioning of the output file with regard to physical page boundaries). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor\'s user documentation.': OK (§A.1 130)). A behavior EXISTS (a LINAGE file gets EvaluateLinage() + LinageCounter = 1 at OPEN OUTPUT completion per §13.18.34 GR6b1/GR7d; a non-LINAGE file starts at stream offset 0), but it is nowhere DEFINED in the user documentation: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7's Annex A.1 register does not carry item 130 and its own status block records 163 of the 199 documentation obligations still outstanding, item 130 among them. One half verified, one half outstanding ⇒ PARTIAL. NOT filed as a new finding: the obligation is already carried by the mechanically-derived A.1 register (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 + scripts/audit_annex_a1.py), which is the register that owns it. Test-needed for half 1. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023

subject: OPEN statement
notes: RULE: 'Upon successful execution of the OPEN statement, the current volume pointer is set: a) To point to the first or only reel/unit in the physical file if INPUT or I-O is specified. b) To point to the reel/unit containing the last record in the physical file if EXTEND is specified. c) To point to the newly created reel/unit in the physical file for an unavailable file if EXTEND, I-O, or OUTPUT is specified.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 19)). DERIVATION: §9.1.10 (Current volume pointer) states 'The current volume pointer is a CONCEPTUAL ENTITY used in this document to facilitate exact specification of the current physical volume of a sequential file. The status of the current volume pointer is affected by the CLOSE, OPEN, READ, and WRITE statements.' (cite.py --check 9.1.10: OK) — it is not a programmer-visible register and has no COBOL surface. Its only observable consequences are reel/unit swaps (§14.9.30.4 GR23 READ, §14.9.51.4 GR24 WRITE) and CLOSE unit processing (§14.9.6.4 Table 14). COBOL.NET's storage medium is single-unit mass storage, asserted in code at FileRegistry.CloseReelUnit ('CLOSE … REEL/UNIT on a disk medium: a no-op … the file is on a non-reel/unit medium') and CloseNoRewind, so every physical file has exactly ONE reel/unit and arms a), b) and c) all designate that same and only unit whichever mode is specified. There is nothing the rule can require that a single-unit medium does not already satisfy, and no state a program can observe that would disagree. TEST: unit:FileStatusDisciplineTests.CloseReelUnit_AbsentOptional_NoUnitProcessing is the spec-derived test that pins the single-unit medium model (§14.9.6.4 GR6 / §9.1.13.2 6)) this verdict rests on. ⚠ THE PREMISE IS APPLIED INCONSISTENTLY ELSEWHERE: the same non-reel/unit medium that makes GR19 vacuous is what makes GR11's '07' MANDATORY, and that arm is missing (see GR-14.9.27.4-11 and finding open-no-rewind-07-arm-missing). The medium model is also asserted only in code comments — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 33-34 states the opposite ('no reel device'). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB316. RULE: 'If more than one file-name is specified in an OPEN statement, the result of executing this OPEN statement is the same as if a separate OPEN statement had been written for each file-name in the same order as specified in the OPEN statement. These separate OPEN statements would each have the same open mode specification, the sharing-phrase, retry-phrase, and REWIND phrase as specified in the OPEN statement. If an implicit OPEN statement results in the execution of a declarative procedure that executes a RESUME statement with the NEXT STATEMENT phrase, processing resumes at the next implicit OPEN statement, if any.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 20)). READING: 'as specified in the OPEN statement' is PER FILE-NAME, i.e. per repetition group. §14.9.27.2's general format has an OUTER brace pair with its own trailing ellipsis around the whole '{open-mode} [sharing-phrase] [retry-phrase] {file-name-1 [WITH NO REWIND]}…' group, so one OPEN carries several groups each with its own mode AND its own phrases; §14.9.27.4 GR23 ('The SHARING phrase overrides any SHARING clause in the file control entry of FILE-NAME-1' — cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 23)) and §14.9.27.3 SR8 are both written per file-name-1. The code itself agrees for the MODE (each openClause's mode is attached to its own files) and disagrees for the phrases. DEFECT — the phrases are STATEMENT-scoped, not group-scoped. BindOpen declares 'SharingMode? sharing = null' and 'RetrySpec? retry = null' OUTSIDE the foreach over o.openClause(), assigns them whenever any clause carries the phrase, never resets them, and folds ONE value each into BoundOpen; BoundOpen's own doc comment states the wrong model outright ('Applies to every file in the statement'); EmitOpen computes 'bool shared = o.SharingOverride is not null || o.Retry is not null' ONCE and routes EVERY file through FileOpenShared with that one SharingOverride. REPRO A (rejects legal source) — out-b1/probe/openmulti/OPMUL01.cob: FA has LOCK MODE IS MANUAL, FB has neither a SHARING clause nor a phrase; 'OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH ALL OTHER FA OUTPUT FB.' Expected: compiles (SR8 applies to FA, which HAS the LOCK MODE clause; FB's group carries no sharing phrase so SR8's antecedent is false for it). Observed: 'error COBOLNET1512: OPEN of file FB with SHARING WITH ALL OTHER requires the file to have a LOCK MODE clause (ISO 14.9.27 SR8)' — legal source refused. REPRO B (wrong answer at run time) — out-b1/probe/openmulti/OPMUL03.cob vs the identical OPMUL04.cob control: FB and FC both ASSIGN to opmul03b.dat, FC has LOCK MODE IS MANUAL; 'OPEN OUTPUT SHARING WITH NO OTHER FA OUTPUT FB.' then 'OPEN INPUT FC.'. Expected per GR20 + GR23: FB's group has no sharing phrase, so FB takes the GR23 implementor default (here: not sharing-active) and FC's OPEN is '00' — exactly what the control prints. Observed with the phrase present: FSC = '61' (§9.1.13.9 1 file sharing conflict). FileRegistry.OpenShared also makes FB PERMANENTLY sharing-active for the rest of the run ('if (!_connectorShares.ContainsKey(name)) RegisterSharing(name, FileSharing.AllOther, …)'), changing its OS FileShare posture too. The RETRY phrase leaks identically — same variable, same BoundOpen field, same EmitOpen switch. VERIFIED-CONFORMING HALVES: the per-file decomposition in source order (BindOpen appends one (file, mode) tuple per openFileSpec in order; EmitOpen emits one FileOpen + status store + USE hook per tuple) and the RESUME NEXT STATEMENT sentence — PROBE out-b1/probe/openresume/OPRES01.cob: 'OPEN INPUT F1 OUTPUT F2 OUTPUT F3.' with F1 absent and a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR ON F1 declarative that does RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT prints 'DECLARATIVE HIT:35' once and then 'FS1:35 FS2:00 FS3:00 HITS:1' — processing resumed at the next implicit OPEN, as the rule requires. The REWIND-phrase half of the same sentence is vacuous here only because the phrase is discarded outright (GR11). FINDING: open-phrases-statement-scoped. Test-needed. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023 (the per-file decomposition is 1985+; the sharing-phrase and retry-phrase halves are the COBOL-2002 file-sharing introduction — A.4.7, claimed in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 — and the RESUME NEXT STATEMENT sentence is 2002+, A.4.12)

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB322. 'The SHARING phrase is effective only for files that are shareable.' The predicate 'shareable' is defined by §9.1.15: 'A shared physical file shall reside on a device that allows concurrent access to the file. The implementor shall specify which devices allow concurrent access to a physical file' (cite.py --check 9.1.15 OK). SEARCHED: the string 'shareable' appears nowhere in src or docs, and no device/medium predicate gates OpenShared — the phrase is honoured unconditionally for every connector. That BEHAVIOUR is defensible, because COBOL.NET has exactly one device class (a host file resolved by CobolFile.ResolveHostPath) and host files do allow concurrent access, so 'every file is shareable' makes 'effective only for shareable files' vacuously true. It is PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS because the determination the rule leans on is nowhere stated: Annex A.1 item 76, 'File sharing (which devices allow concurrent access to the file). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation' (cite.py --check A.1 OK, 76)) and its companion item 52 are absent from docs/CONFORMANCE.md — grep for 'concurrent access' there returns nothing, while A.4.7 is listed Claimed in §5. A conforming claim needs the device statement written down; until it is, GR21's antecedent is unverified rather than satisfied. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 / 2014 / 2023 — the SHARING phrase belongs to the file sharing and record locking module (Annex A.4.7, docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 disposition Claimed); the compiler gates it as a 2002 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'file-sharing-clause-2002', VersionConformancePass.cs:1307, negative fixture tests/conformance/negative/sharing_below_2002.cob). Not applicable at 1985.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB321. The rule binds the phrase to ONE file-name-1 ('the level of sharing permitted for the physical file associated with file-name-1') and delegates the operational meaning to §9.1.15. THE LEVEL LANDS ON THE WRONG FILES. §14.9.27.2's general format repeats the whole group `{ open-mode } [ sharing-phrase ] [ retry-phrase ] { file-name-1 [ WITH NO REWIND ] } …` under an outer ellipsis (the transcription's figure note states this explicitly and the grammar matches it: `openClause : openMode (sharingPhrase)? (retryPhrase)? openFileSpec+`), so each repetition carries its OWN phrase. SequentialIoBinder.BindOpen declares `SharingMode? sharing = null` OUTSIDE the `foreach (var clause in o.openClause())` loop and hands a SINGLE `BoundOpen { SharingOverride = sharing }` to the emitter, and EmitOpen applies `o.SharingOverride` to EVERY file in the statement. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-sharing-scope): FA declares SHARING WITH NO OTHER, FB declares SHARING WITH ALL OTHER + LOCK MODE IS MANUAL, both on "shr2.dat"; `OPEN INPUT FA I-O SHARING WITH ALL OTHER FB.` gives FA='00', FB='00'. Control with the phrase removed (`OPEN INPUT FA I-O FB.`) gives FB='61' — so the override written for FB destroyed FA's declared exclusivity. SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: FB='61' in both runs (§9.1.13.9 1) a); Table 19 column 'sharing with no other' is Unsuccessful open in every row). SECOND DIVERGENCE, from §9.1.15 which this rule incorporates: 'The successful opening of a file establishes a file lock for the applicable sharing rules, thereby preventing other run units from opening that file with incompatible sharing rules' (cite.py --check 9.1.15 OK, 3)) — PhysicalFileTable is a field of FileRegistry, i.e. of RunUnit.Current.Files, so the arbitration is IN-PROCESS ONLY and no cross-run-unit file lock exists; worse, a sharing-active connector sets FileConnector.SharedStreams, which opens its streams FileShare.ReadWrite, removing the OS-level exclusion an undeclared connector still gets (proved by the '30' vs '00' contrast between out-b1/probe/open-default-sharing and out-b1/probe/open-noother-vs-plain). Correct halves: the three modes map faithfully onto FileSharing.NoOther/ReadOnly/AllOther, §9.1.15 rule 1's 'record locks are ignored' under no-other is honoured (FileRegistry.LocksEffective), and the single-clause override is exercised by conformance:2002/file_sharing ('EXCL=61' for `OPEN I-O SHARING WITH NO OTHER F-B` while F-A is open). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 / 2014 / 2023 (Annex A.4.7 file sharing and record locking; gated at 2002 by VersionConformancePass.cs:1307). Not applicable at 1985.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB316. THREE SENTENCES, TWO BROKEN. (1) 'The SHARING phrase overrides any SHARING clause in the file control entry of file-name-1' — file-name-1 is the file list of the phrase's OWN openClause. The binder hoists the phrase to statement scope (see GR-14.9.27.4-22), so a SHARING phrase written on the second mode group also overrides the FIRST group's file-control clause. Proved in out-b1/probe/open-sharing-scope: FA's declared SHARING WITH NO OTHER is replaced by FB's clause-2 ALL OTHER override, and the '61' the control run produces becomes '00'. (2) 'If there is no SHARING phrase on the OPEN statement, then file sharing is completely specified in the file control entry' — honoured for a connector that HAS a clause (EmitSharingRegistration emits RegisterSharing only when `file.Sharing != None || file.LockMode is not null`). (3) 'If neither a SHARING phrase on the OPEN statement nor a SHARING clause in the file control entry is specified, the implementor shall define the sharing mode that is established for each file connector' — the definition is MISSING from the user documentation and the code contradicts the only place it is written down. Annex A.1 item 77 ('File sharing (default mode when unspecified). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (9.1.3 ...; 9.1.15 ...; 14.9.27, OPEN statement, General rule 23)') and item 131 ('OPEN statement without the SHARING phrase and no SHARING clause in the file control entry (definition of sharing mode established for each file connector). This item is required ...') both validate with cite.py --check A.1; docs/CONFORMANCE.md — the §4.2 user-documentation face, whose §5 lists A.4.7 as Claimed — has no row for either. docs/PHASE4_RECONCILIATION.md:1523 does state a choice ('our documented choice = default sharing NO OTHER (exclusive, record locks ignored per GR3)'), but the shipped code implements something else: FileSupport.cs's own summary says 'The implementor default for a connector without any SHARING/LOCK-MODE clause is outside the sharing subsystem entirely', and FileRegistry.Open bypasses SharedOpenAttempt for such a connector. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-default-sharing): two plain SELECTs on "shr3.dat" — OPEN INPUT FA '00', OPEN INPUT FB '00' (under the documented NO OTHER default FB must be '61'), and OPEN OUTPUT FB over an open FA gives '30', an OS sharing violation leaking into the I-O status where the documented default requires '61'. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 / 2014 / 2023 (Annex A.4.7; gated at 2002). Not applicable at 1985.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB322. CORRECT HALF: RETRY n TIMES on an OPEN file-sharing conflict re-attempts and, on exhaustion, sets the §9.1.13-appropriate value. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-retry): FA SHARING WITH NO OTHER open INPUT, then `OPEN I-O RETRY 3 TIMES FB` → '61' — exactly §14.7.9.3 GR4's tail ('the statement is unsuccessful, the appropriate value is placed in the I-O status associated with the file connector according to the rules for 9.1.13, I-O status', cite.py --check 14.7.9.3 OK, 4) a)) with §9.1.13.9 item 1 supplying '61'. DIVERGENCE 1 — the phrase is hoisted exactly like SHARING: `RetrySpec? retry = null` is declared outside BindOpen's `foreach (var clause in o.openClause())`, one BoundOpen.Retry reaches the emitter, and EmitOpen renders `o.Retry` for every file, so a RETRY written on one mode group governs the whole statement (the mechanism is byte-identical to the SHARING leak proved in out-b1/probe/open-sharing-scope, and §14.9.27.4 GR20 — sibling part — confirms the per-file reading: the equivalent separate OPENs 'would each have the same open mode specification, the sharing-phrase, retry-phrase, and REWIND phrase as specified in the OPEN statement'). DIVERGENCE 2 — the SECONDS and FOREVER arms answer '52' where the conflict is a FILE SHARING conflict. Same probe: `OPEN I-O RETRY FOREVER FB` → '52' and `OPEN I-O RETRY FOR 2 SECONDS FB` → '52'. RetryLoop re-checks once and returns FileStatusCode.Deadlock. §9.1.13.8 item 2 does license '52' but on terms this build has not met: 'The implementor shall specify under what conditions a deadlock is detected' (cite.py --check 9.1.13.8 OK, 2)) — grep 'deadlock' in docs/CONFORMANCE.md returns nothing, and the status swap also re-routes the raised exception from EC-I-O-FILE-SHARING (first digit '6') to EC-I-O-RECORD-OPERATION (first digit '5') per §9.1.13.1. §14.7.9.3 GR1/GR2's other required determinations (the interval between attempts; m, n and the maximum meaningful timeout; the retry frequency technique) are likewise undocumented. Adjacent but distinct: kb/Work PB142 (open) owns RETRY FOR 0 SECONDS, the DELETE FILE 52-vs-62 misname and the GR1 round-up — none of them this hoist and none of them the OPEN deadlock determination. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 / 2014 / 2023 — the RETRY phrase is §14.7.9, core syntax introduced with the 2002 file sharing / record locking work (docs/COMPLETION_ROADMAP_COUNCIL.md D15 records that RETRY is NOT itself an A.4.7 optional element but is listed in Annex A only as required implementor-defined items); the compiler gates it at 2002 (openClause's `{is2002() || retryPhraseAhead()}?` predicate + the RetryPhrase2002 check). Not applicable at 1985.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. The emitted sequence is exactly the rule's order. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a — the value is placed in the I-O status), then EmitUseHook. Inside the generated __IoCheckEc the body runs: `ExceptionState.SetIo(__ec!, IsFatalIoStatus(__st), ...)` when the name's checking bit is on (b — the level-3 EC-I-O condition associated with the status value, mapped by ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus per §9.1.13.1), then `__EcPerform(__ec!, __f)` consults the installed Format-3 PerformFrame FIRST (c), and only if that returns NoMatch do the F1 file-name / open-mode USE tiers and the outward GLOBAL walk run (d). §14.9.28.4 GR17's 'Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored' is what makes c) exclude d), and the emitter's own comment states it. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-gr25): OPEN INPUT of an absent non-optional file with a `USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION PROCEDURE ON FN` declarative → the declarative runs and reports status 35, and the file is NOT created (a + d, and 'the file is not affected'); the same OPEN inside `PERFORM ... WHEN EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR ... END-PERFORM` → the WHEN body runs and the declarative does NOT (c), after which the run unit terminates abnormally naming EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR — which is §14.9.28.4 GR20's own tail ('If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3'), not a defect. CONFORMS-but-untested: no existing spec-derived test pins the OPEN-specific a-b-c-d ordering (conformance:2023/f3_perform_handler_turn_off_all covers the Format-3 machinery but not through an I-O statement). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, downward to PARTIAL. The rule has a leading requirement and then four ordered actions: 'If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, THE FILE IS NOT AFFECTED and the following actions take place in the following order: a) ... b) ... c) ... d)'. VERIFIED HALF -- the a-b-c-d machinery is right and I could not break it. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a), then EmitUseHook; inside __IoCheckEc the order is SetIo (b), then the F3 PerformFrame via RunTopFrame (c), then, only when no WHEN matched, the F1 file-name and open-mode USE tiers, the F3 __EcDispatch tier and the outward GLOBAL walk (d) -- which is what 14.9.49.4 GR6 requires. I also closed the leg the adjudicator left unexercised: its probe ran a FORMAT 1 USE only, but GR25 d) names 'USE FOR EXCEPTION or USE AFTER EXCEPTION', so I probed a FORMAT 3 declarative (USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR under >>TURN ... CHECKING ON) on an unsuccessful OPEN INPUT: it runs, with FS=35, EXCEPTION-STATUS=EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR and EXCEPTION-FILE=35FN. The 9.1.13.1 status->EC map in ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus matches the standard's list digit for digit. UNVERIFIED-AND-VIOLATED HALF -- 'the file is not affected'. The adjudication tested this in the only direction that cannot lose data (an absent file is not CREATED by a failing OPEN INPUT). I tested the destructive direction and it fails. Connector FA holds po.dat open INPUT under SHARING WITH NO OTHER; connector FB, a plain SELECT on the same physical file, executes OPEN OUTPUT. 9.1.13.9 1) a) and Table 19 (whose 'sharing with no other' existing column is 'Unsuccessful open' in EVERY request row) make that OPEN unsuccessful with status 61, so GR25's own consequent applies and the file shall not be affected. The compiler reports 00 and TRUNCATES po.dat to zero bytes -- the record 'KEEPTHIS01' is gone. That is wrong-answer-with-data-loss on legal source, and it is GR25's own text that is violated, not merely the detection rule's. I checked the counter-hypothesis before charging it: every unsuccessful OPEN the implementation DOES recognise leaves the file intact -- 61 on a sharing-active incoming connector returns before c.Open(mode) is ever called, 41 returns at the top of FileConnector.Open, and 35/37/30 all return before or from the failing stream construction (I confirmed 61 and 41 by probe with the content re-read intact, and the OS-level conflict variant gives 30 with the file intact). So the failure is confined to spec-unsuccessful opens the implementation misclassifies as successful, whose ROOT cause (FileRegistry.Open consults the physical-file table only when the INCOMING connector is sharing-active) is already booked DIVERGES under GR-14.9.27.4-22/-23 -- I am not re-booking that defect, I am recording that GR25's leading clause is therefore unsatisfied and was never measured. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL by the rubric; not DIVERGES, because the four ordered actions that are the substance of the rule are correct and probed. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for sub-rules a) and d); sub-rules b) and c) ride the exception-condition facility and the Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM, 2002 introductions, so they are adjudicated at 2002 / 2014 / 2023.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB324. This rule is a pointer: 'Additional rules affecting the execution of the OPEN statement are given in 12.4.5, File control entry, General rules 3 and 4' (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 OK, 26)). Both referred rules are broken. §12.4.5.3 GR3b (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 OK, 3) b)): 'When the USING phrase of the ASSIGN clause is specified, the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is associated with a physical file identified by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1 in the runtime element that executes the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement.' The grammar parses both USING forms (CobolIO.g4:37-38, `ASSIGN TO? assignTarget (USING dataReference)?` and `ASSIGN USING dataReference`), but DataBinder.BindFileControl reads only `clauses.assignClause()?.assignTarget()`; the `USING dataReference` child is read NOWHERE in src (grep 'assignClause' across the greenfield returns exactly that one site). With the bare `ASSIGN USING data-name` form there is no assignTarget at all, so FileModel.AssignTarget keeps its constructor default — the FILE-NAME. PROBE (out-b1/probe/assign-using): `SELECT FU ASSIGN USING WS-NAME` with `01 WS-NAME PIC X(11) VALUE "target1.dat"` compiles clean, OPEN OUTPUT reports '00', and the records land in **fu.txt**; target1.dat is never created. SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: the connector is associated with target1.dat. This is a silent wrong-FILE defect, not a diagnosed gap. §12.4.5.3 GR3's opening sentence is broken independently: 'The association occurs at the time of execution of an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement that referenced file-name-1' — CobolFile.ResolveHostPath is called from FileRegistry.Register at unit ACTIVATION and its result is stored in the connector's get-only HostPath, so no OPEN ever re-resolves; the standard's own concepts annex underlines the intended timing ('NOTE The MOVE statements only have an effect on the dynamic assignment when a subsequent OPEN statement for the file connector is executed'). GR4's implementor obligations (the meaning and allowable content of data-name-1's value; the consistency rules between it and device-name-1/literal-1) are consequently undefined and undocumented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md. kb/Work A2 (open) already names 'ASSIGN USING' among the proved silently-unenforced class, but as a SYNTAX-rule census item; the defect here is a GENERAL-rule semantic drop and needs its own note. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 — §12.4.5.3 GR3/GR4 govern the ASSIGN clause at every edition; the ASSIGN ... USING form is the later (2002+) addition, and the grammar accepts it at all editions.

subject: READ statement
notes:
kb/Work PB337. RULE: 'The INTO phrase may be specified in a READ statement: a) If no record description entry or only one record description is subordinate to the file description entry, or b) If the data item referenced by identifier-1 and all record-names associated with file-name-1 describe an alphanumeric group item or an elementary item of category alphanumeric or category national.' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.3 OK.)
NO CODE ENFORCES IT, and this is a SEARCH result, not a dossier silence: both READ arms resolve the INTO operand and thread it unexamined -- SequentialIoBinder.BindRead line 152 and KeyedIoBinder.BindRead line 38 are byte-identical (`Place? into = r.readInto()?.dataReference() is { } d ? ctx.Refs.Resolve(d) : null;`) and no caller screens it. `grep -rn 'readInto\|ReadInto' src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/` returns exactly those two lines. A descriptor CBL1704 'READ INTO target must be alphanumeric or group' exists but is declared and used ONLY in the frozen legacy compiler (src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Diagnostics/DiagnosticDescriptors.cs:134 declares it; the only Report site is src/CobolSharp.Compiler/Semantics/Bound/BoundTreeValidator.cs) -- it never runs in the greenfield.
PROBE (out-b1/probe/sr1/into2rec.cob): FD with TWO record descriptions, `01 REC-A / 05 A-1 PIC X(4)` and `01 REC-B / 05 B-1 PIC 9(4) COMP`; `READ SQF INTO WS-NUM` where WS-NUM is PIC 9(4) COMP. SR1(a) fails (two record descriptions); SR1(b) fails twice over (WS-NUM is category numeric USAGE binary, and REC-B is not an alphanumeric group either). Expected from the spec: rejected. Observed: compiles, runs, DISPLAYs `GOT=0000`. Harm is silent under-rejection feeding a garbage implicit MOVE (GR4b).

If it is any other value, the execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to 47.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to 47' -> OK 14.9.30.4 2). notes: Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "the content of any data item, where any part of that data item lies beyond the range of the current record, is undefined" => OK 3)). The rule imposes NO requirement: it declares the content UNDEFINED, and it is registered as such in Annex A.2 item 41 (Undefined language element list — unlike A.1, A.2 carries no documentation obligation). COBOL.NET makes the choice DETERMINATE: FileConnector.Fit pads/truncates the physical record to the record-area width with SPACES, and SequentialIoEmitter.EmitImageInto stores that full-width image into FileModel.AreaRecord (the LARGEST record description, §13.4.2), so every position past the current record reads as a space. A determinate space fill is one admissible realization of 'undefined'. notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE items a-e. cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'The file position indicator is unchanged.' -> OK 14.9.30.4 10) a). SEQUENTIAL ARM CONFORMS: FileRegistry.ReadShared computes the next ordinal (SequentialConnector.NextReadOrdinal) BEFORE the physical read, so on a 51 the connector is never entered -- FPI unchanged (a), status set (b), record area untouched (c, the documented refinement of 'undefined'), READ unsuccessful (e). KEYED ARM DIVERGES on (a) and (d): ReadLockGovern is called AFTER the physical read (its own summary admits the shape), so by the time the 51 is stamped RelativeConnector/IndexedConnector have already set _fpi/_fpiKey/_fpiArrival, _inclusive=false, _positioner='R' and _lastSlot/_lastReadPrime -- (a) violated -- and IndexedConnector.ReadRandom assigns `_refKey = keyIndex` on its THIRD line, before any lookup, so a Format-2 conflicted read also changes the key of reference -- (d) violated. OBSERVED (probe/keyedfpi/KEYEDFPI.cob, two SHARING WITH ALL OTHER + LOCK MODE MANUAL relative connectors over one file seeded AAAAA/BBBBB/CCCCC): A1=00 AAAAA (A reads RRN 1 WITH LOCK); B1=51 RK=0000 (B's READ conflicts); UNLA=00; B2=00 BBBBB RK=0002. EXPECTED FROM SPEC: with the FPI unchanged by the conflict, B's next sequential READ selects the same record -> B2=00 AAAAA RK=0001. RRN 1 is silently skipped and never made available to B. (c) is met on both arms (the emitters store the record area only inside the success branch). (e) is met on both arms. NO EXISTING TEST COVERS THE DIVERGENT ARM: unit:CobolFileLockTests.ReadShared_SequentialOrdinals_Conflict51_AndAdvancingOnLockSkips and conformance:2002/file_sharing_seq exercise ONLY the sequential organization (whose pre-read check is correct), which is why this has stood green -- test-ref left empty deliberately.

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE items a-d. cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'any prior record lock associated with that file connector is released by the execution of the READ statement' -> OK 14.9.30.4 11) a). ITEMS b, c, d CONFORM. ApplyReadLockDiscipline: b -- `else if (meta.Multiple && phrase == WithNoLock) ReleaseSingle(...)`, reached because wantLock is false for WithNoLock, and only at completion of a successful read; c -- the `_ => meta.LockMode == FileLockMode.Automatic` arm auto-locks; d -- `WithLock => true` is the only manual-mode acquisition. LocksEffective correctly suppresses ACQUISITION (never the conflict CHECK) per 12.4.5.9.4 GR1a/b1 and GR3. ITEM a DIVERGES. GR11a ties the release to 'the execution of the READ statement', and 12.4.5.9.4 GR6 is explicit -- 'Execution of any I-O statement except START releases any previously locked record in that file for that file connector' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 <that text> -> OK 12.4.5.9.4 6)). The standard distinguishes deliberately: 11b says 'at the completion of the SUCCESSFUL execution', 11c/d say 'successfully accessed record', 11a says neither. The code gates 11a on success at BOTH call sites: ReadLockGovern early-returns on `statusJustRead[0] != '0'`, and ReadShared calls ApplyReadLockDiscipline only inside `if (ok && ...)`. So an at-end, 46, 47 or 51 READ leaves the prior lock standing. This is a TWO-ARM defect: the governed MUTATING verbs in the same file release unconditionally before the operation (WriteShared and RewriteShared and DeleteShared each call ReleaseAllForConnector / ReleaseAllExcept outside any success test) -- only READ gates it. OBSERVED (probe/gr11a/GR11A.cob, two SHARING ALL OTHER + LOCK MODE MANUAL sequential connectors, single record locking): A1..A3 = 00 with WITH LOCK (A ends holding ordinal 3); A4-ATEND=10; then C walks the file: C1=00, C2=00, C3=51 BBBBB. EXPECTED FROM SPEC: A's at-end READ is an executed I-O statement, so it released A's lock on ordinal 3 -> C3=00 CCCCC. conformance:2002/file_sharing_seq exercises 11a only across SUCCESSFUL reads (its READA3 line), so the divergent path is uncovered -- test-ref left empty.

subject: READ statement
notes: RULE: 'If the IGNORING LOCK phrase is specified on the READ statement, the requested record is made available, even if it is locked.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the requested record is made available, even if it is locked' -> OK 14.9.30.4 12). BOTH ARMS VERIFIED. Sequential: ReadShared guards the whole conflict block with `if (phrase != FileRecordLock.Ignoring && f.ReadEligible)`, so an IGNORING LOCK read falls straight through to f.Read and the locked record is delivered. Keyed: ReadLockGovern wraps only the conflict block in `if (phrase != FileRecordLock.Ignoring)`, and the physical read has already happened, so the record is likewise made available. ApplyReadLockDiscipline maps Ignoring to wantLock=false, so an IGNORING LOCK read neither acquires nor (under multiple locking) releases -- consistent with 14.9.30.3 SR3/SR4, which bar combining IGNORING LOCK with LOCK and bar it entirely under automatic locking. Grammar carries it (recordLockPhrase: IGNORING LOCK | WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK, ordered so WITH NO LOCK is not shadowed) and the 2002 introduction gate fires on the bound phrase (VersionConformancePass.GateStatement -> Constructs.RecordLockPhrase2002). COVERING TEST: conformance:2002/file_sharing_seq line 'READ F-B IGNORING LOCK' -> golden 'IGNB=00 AAAAA' while A holds ordinal 1's lock -- the record IS made available, exactly the rule. Spec-derived (its header derives every line from 9.1.16 / 14.9.30 GR7-GR12).

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE items a-c. cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'any implicit move resulting from the presence of an INTO phrase is executed' -> OK 14.9.30.4 13) (the transcription runs item c flush-left at spec line 26243, so the checker attributes the sentence to 13) b); the sentence is verbatim under GR13). ITEM a: both emitters call EmitStoreFileStatus on every path and the connectors set the FPI inside the success path only. ITEM b: EmitUseHook emits __IoCheck / __IoCheckEc after the status store, consuming the declarative's RESUME action; the AT END imperative is guarded by `if (FileStatus(name)[0] == '1')` so a 3x/4x/5x exception cannot take it. VERIFIED BY PROBE (probe/gr13b/GR13B.cob -- a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON F plus a READ on a closed connector): output 'DECLARATIVE FS=47' then 'AFTER-READ FS=47' -- the declarative ran, AT END did not, and control returned to the end of the READ so the following statement executed, which is GR13b's non-fatal tail exactly. ITEM c: on success the emitters store the record image into the record area (EmitImageInto over FileModel.AreaRecord, the LARGEST record description per 13.4.2), then the INTO move, then NOT AT END / NOT INVALID KEY -- the order GR13c states. 'the AT END phrase or the INVALID KEY phrase is IGNORED': verified by CA15, where a SUCCESSFUL 06 read does not take AT END and delivers the record ('1:ABCDE FS=06'). The keyed emitter's INVALID KEY branch is `if (st[0]=='2')` and its NOT-branch `else if (st[0]=='0')`, so on success only the NOT-phrases run. conformance:2002/file_collating_seq exercises NOT AT END firing on successful keyed reads. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — The adjudicator read item (a) as only 'the connectors set the FPI inside the success path' and never tested its CONDITIONAL half. GR13a is not 'the FPI is set' -- it is 'the I-O status ... is updated AND, IF THE RECORD OPERATION CONFLICT CONDITION DID NOT OCCUR, the file position indicator is set', i.e. under a conflict the FPI must not move (the same requirement GR10a states affirmatively). On the KEYED arm FileRegistry.ReadLockGovern is called AFTER the physical read (its own doc-comment admits the shape: 'the keyed shape is post-read'), so RelativeConnector.ReadSequential / IndexedConnector.ReadSequential have already executed '_fpi = s; _fpiValid = true; _positioner = R' before the 51 is stamped at FileRegistry.cs:585 -- whose comment 'FPI kept (GR10a)' is exactly backwards for this arm, since 'kept' there means 'kept as the read left it', not 'unchanged'. The 53/54 lock-denial return from ApplyReadLockDiscipline is post-read on the same arm and breaks item (a) identically. Items (b) and (c) do hold, and item (a) holds on the sequential arm (ReadShared checks NextReadOrdinal before entering the connector), so this is the classic two-arm defect -- one arm fixed, the sibling never was -- and one arm conforming is not CONFORMS. Verdict DIVERGES rather than PARTIAL because a wrong answer is produced silently: the conflicted record is skipped and never delivered. Same root cause as the adjudicator's own GR10 DIVERGES row (it found the mechanism there and did not carry it back to GR13, which restates the same requirement); one fix -- moving keyed lock governance ahead of the physical read, or snapshotting/restoring the FPI on a conflict -- closes both rows. The cited test-refs do not save it: SequentialFileIoSpecTests.LineSequential_OverLengthRecord..., FileIoDifferentialTests.ReadNotOpen_Status47... and conformance:2002/file_collating_seq all exercise items (b)/(c) or the sequential organization only; none puts a record-operation conflict on a keyed connector, which is why this stood green.

subject: READ statement
notes: RULE: short -> right of the last valid character is undefined; long -> truncated on the right to the maximum size; either way SUCCESSFUL with '04'. cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the record is truncated on the right to the maximum size' -> OK 14.9.30.4 14). SequentialConnector.Read carries two record-sequential legs, both setting shortLong -> FileStatusCode.RecordLengthShortLong and both returning through ReadSucceeded (so the read IS successful and the record IS delivered): the FIXED leg (`if (n < RecordWidth) shortLong = true`, n==0 being EOF) and the RECORD IS VARYING leg (`if (n < VaryMin || n > VaryMax) shortLong = true`). Line sequential is correctly excluded (its short/long conditions are GR15's padding and '06'). BOTH HALVES VERIFIED. Short half: conformance:2002/io_status_04 -- three 5-char records read through a 10-char FD gives S1=00 then S2=04 with the partial record right-padded. Long half (no golden exists, so probed): probe/gr14long/GR14LONG.cob writes a 10-byte record through an FD declared RECORD VARYING 1 TO 10 and reads it through a second FD over the same file declared RECORD VARYING 1 TO 5 -> 'LONG FS=04 REC=[ABCDE] LEN=0010' -- successful, '04', truncated on the right to the maximum size 5. Exactly GR14. FIXED-LEG MINIMUM: the fixed leg treats the record width as BOTH the minimum and the maximum fixed file attribute, which docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3 pins as a behaviour determination ('fixed leg: shorter than the record width; varying leg: outside [VaryMin, VaryMax]') -- legitimate, since 9.1.13.2 item 3 defines '04' against 'the fixed file attributes for that file' and the implementor fixes those. ADJACENT OBSERVATION, NOT THIS ROW: the probe's DEPENDING item received 0010, the PHYSICAL length, after the record was truncated to 5 -- that is 13.18.43 GR15's rule (SequentialIoEmitter.EmitReadLengthStore over FileConnector.LastReadLength), outside this clause; flagged for whoever adjudicates 13.18.43. The 'undefined' right-hand portion is space-filled, which 'undefined' permits.

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB327. RULE has three parts: (1) short record -> the record area right of the last valid character is padded with TRAILING SPACES; (2) that trailing space is the ALPHANUMERIC space for an alphanumeric record area and the NATIONAL space for a national one; (3) long record -> truncated on the right, SUCCESSFUL, '06', and the FPI references the next unread character in the record (NOTE 3: subsequent READs consume the rest). cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'a trailing space is defined to be the national space character' -> OK 14.9.30.4 15). PARTS 1 AND 3 CONFORM. Part 1: the else arm is `LastReadLength = line.Length; image = Fit(line, RecordWidth)` and Fit right-pads with U+0020. Part 3: `_lineRemainder = line[RecordWidth..]; image = line[..RecordWidth]; lineTooLong = true` -> ReadSucceeded(LineRecordTooLong '06'), and the next Read serves _lineRemainder before touching the stream -- the FPI-inside-the-record model NOTE 3 describes; _lastReadLinePartial additionally feeds 14.9.35.4 GR17a's REWRITE '44'. Covered by CA15 ('1:ABCDE FS=06' then '2:FGH   FS=00' then 'E FS=10'), which is spec-derived. PART 2 IS THE MISSING HALF, hence PARTIAL: Fit pads with U+0020 unconditionally and the connector has no national branch at all (its streams are opened with Encoding.Latin1). I could not even exercise the national leg -- probe/natpad/NATPAD.cob (FD record 01 L-REC PIC N(5) on a LINE SEQUENTIAL file) is REJECTED at compile time: 'error COBOLNET0899: national data in a file record ... is recognized but not yet implemented - the record codec is single-byte and the national character is two bytes (Phase 4a residue; ISO 8.1.2 / 13.18.60.4 GR8)'. So the rule's national half is held open by a declared loud residue owned by 8.1.2 / 13.18.60.4, not by this clause -- recorded here, no duplicate finding filed. NOTE for whoever lands the national record codec: in the UTF-16 repertoire the national space IS U+0020, so the pad CHARACTER will be right; what is missing is the two-byte record codec, not the pad choice.

subject: READ statement
notes: RULE: 'Regardless of the method used to overlap access time with processing time, the concept of the READ statement is unchanged; a record is available to the runtime element prior to the execution of imperative-statement-2 or imperative-statement-4, if specified, or prior to the execution of any statement following the READ statement...' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'a record is available to the runtime element prior to the execution of imperative-statement-2' -> OK 14.9.30.4 17). This implementation uses NO overlapped/asynchronous access method: every READ is a synchronous call on the connector, and both emitters place the record-area store FIRST inside the success block -- SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRead emits EmitImageInto(area, tmp) then EmitReadLengthStore then EmitStoreFileStatus then the INTO move then NotAtEnd; KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead emits EmitImageInto then the RRN move-back inside `if (st[0]=='0')`, with the INTO move and NOT AT END / NOT INVALID KEY in the following guarded block. So imperative-statement-2 and imperative-statement-4 and every following statement observe the record already in the record area. Verified as OUTPUT by CA15, whose DISPLAY of REC immediately after each READ shows the record just read ('1:ABCDE', '2:FGH   '), and by every probe in this batch (probe/seqprev, probe/relprev, probe/gr14long) where the DISPLAY after the READ carries the delivered record. The rule imposes nothing further on a non-overlapped implementation.

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE: 'Unless otherwise specified, at the completion of any unsuccessful execution of a READ statement, the content of the associated record area is undefined, the key of reference is undefined for indexed files, and the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid record position has been established.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid record position has been established' -> OK 14.9.30.4 18). RECORD-AREA LEG CONFORMS: both emitters store the image only inside the success branch, so the area is UNCHANGED -- a documented refinement of 'undefined', asserted by conformance-test:FileIoDifferentialTests.ReadNotOpen_Status47_AtEndNotTaken_RecordAreaUnchanged. KEY-OF-REFERENCE LEG CONFORMS vacuously (IndexedConnector._refKey simply survives, which 'undefined' permits). FPI LEG DIVERGES on the lock-denial path. The ordinary unsuccessful paths are right (at-end and '14' set LastReadUnsuccessful and clear _fpiValid; '51' is correctly exempted by GR10a's 'otherwise specified'), but a 53/54 record-lock-limit denial is NOT exempted by any rule and IS unsuccessful per 12.4.5.9.4 GR7 -- 'Any I-O statement that attempts to obtain a record lock that would exceed either limit is unsuccessful and receives an I-O status that indicates that condition' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 <that text> -> OK 12.4.5.9.4 7)). In FileRegistry.ReadShared the denial is discovered AFTER `f.Read(out image)` has already succeeded, which ran FileConnector.ReadSucceeded -- advancing the FPI, setting PrevOpWasSuccessfulRead and CLEARING LastReadUnsuccessful -- and the registry then only overwrites the status; ReadLockGovern's keyed twin is the same shape. OBSERVED (probe/lock54/LOCK54.cob -- one relative connector, ACCESS DYNAMIC, LOCK MODE MANUAL WITH LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS, 20 records, sixteen READ NEXT ... WITH LOCK): READ0015=00 RK=0015, READ0016=54 RK=0015, UNLOCK=00, AFTER54=00 RK=0017. EXPECTED FROM SPEC: the '54' READ is unsuccessful, so GR18 sets the FPI to no-valid-record-position and the next sequential READ is '46' (9.1.13.7 item 6b). OBSERVED HARM: RRN 16 is silently skipped -- it is never made available to the program on any subsequent READ. Same root mechanism as GR10's keyed arm.

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB335. RULE: 'An implicit or explicit NEXT phrase or a PREVIOUS phrase results in a sequential read: otherwise, the read is a random read and the rules for format 2 apply.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'otherwise, the read is a random read and the rules for format 2 apply' -> OK 14.9.30.4 19). The implication is settled by 14.9.30.3 SR8/SR9, so GR19's routing is only as right as they are. TWO INDEPENDENT DIVERGENCES. (1) SR9's TRIGGER SET IS INCOMPLETE. SR9: 'the NEXT phrase is implied if any of the following phrases is specified: ADVANCING, AT END, or NOT AT END' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.3 <that text> -> OK 14.9.30.3). KeyedIoBinder.BindRead's dynamic arm reads `previous ? Previous : next || r.readAtEnd() is not null ? The FPI state it keys on is set only where the rule means it: OpenCore sets OptionalAbsent solely on OPEN INPUT of an absent OPTIONAL file (§14.9.27 GR13); OPEN I-O/EXTEND of an absent optional file CREATES it (GR17) and leaves OptionalAbsent false, so those do not falsely trip GR28. 'execution … is unsuccessful' is realized by LastReadUnsuccessful (the next sequential READ is '46') and by the emitter routing '2x' to the INVALID KEY imperative and never to the NOT INVALID KEY / success arm (KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead: `if (__kst[0]=='2')` … `else if (__kst[0]=='0')`), which is the §9.1.14 transfer contract the rule points at. So under 1985/2002/2014 an OPEN-MODE declarative shall NOT run for GR28's condition when no INVALID KEY phrase is written. COBOL.NET runs it in all four editions. subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text validated (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "sets the file position indicator to the value contained in the data item referenced by the RELATIVE KEY clause" => OK 29)). Both halves verified. Success: KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead emits `FileSetRelativeKey(name, (long)<typed RELATIVE KEY field>)` before the read (the RRN travels through the typed field, never a byte decode), RelativeConnector.SetPendingKey stages it, and ReadRandom does `_slots.TryGetValue(_pendingKey, …)` then `_fpi = _pendingKey; _lastSlot = _pendingKey;` and makes the slot's image available — 'the record whose relative record number equals the file position indicator is made available'. Failure: no such slot (including RRN 0 or negative, which the 1-based SortedDictionary cannot hold) returns '23' and sets LastReadUnsuccessful, and the emitter routes '2x' to the INVALID KEY imperative per §9.1.14, so 'the invalid key condition exists and execution … is unsuccessful' holds. The FPI is not written on the failing path; that is not observable, because LastReadUnsuccessful already makes the next sequential READ '46' (GR21 first paragraph) and REWRITE/DELETE address `_pendingKey`, not `_fpi`. Partial spec-derived coverage of the SUCCESS leg only: conformance:2002/file_sharing ('IGN=ALPHA' — a Format-2 relative READ delivering the record at the staged RRN); the invalid-key leg is covered only by the legacy-baked KeyedIoDifferentialTests, so test-ref is left empty. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Same defect as GR28, and I measured it on GR29's OWN trigger rather than carrying it across: a Format-2 relative READ naming an RRN that does not exist in a PRESENT physical file. GR29's second sentence is 'the invalid key condition exists and execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful. (See 9.1.14, Invalid key condition.)', so the §9.1.14 routing is part of what the rule requires, and Annex E.2 item 19 a) makes the open-mode declarative tier on that condition a 2023 behaviour. COBOL.NET runs it under --std 85/2002/2014 as well, so the record's '1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023' overclaims by three editions. Everything else in the rule is right, and I verified more of it than the adjudication did: the note calls the FPI half unobservable on the failing path, but the SUCCESS half's FPI is directly observable and I observed it - a random read of RRN 2 followed by READ NEXT correctly yields RRN 4 (RRN 3 deleted), and RRN 4 then yields RRN 5, so the FPI really is set from the RELATIVE KEY value and not merely from a last-slot cursor. subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB341. Rule text validated (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "the first record found is the first record in a sequence of duplicates that was released" => OK 32)). Most of the rule is right: ReadRandom slices the key-of-reference value out of the RECORD AREA image the program filled (`KeyOf(Fit(keyedRecordImage), keyIndex)` — the emitter passes FileModel.AreaRecord, the LARGEST record description), compares it with KeyEq under that key's §12.4.5.7 collating sequence (§12.4.5.12.4 GR1, not ordinal), skips SUPPRESS WHEN records (§12.4.5.6.4 GR6), makes the found record available, and returns '23' + the invalid key condition when none matches. WHAT DIVERGES is 'In the case of an alternate key with duplicate values, the first record found is the FIRST RECORD IN A SEQUENCE OF DUPLICATES THAT WAS RELEASED to the operating environment': the tie-break is `rec.Arrival < found.Arrival`, and Arrival is ONE scalar per record shared by every alternate key, which IndexedConnector.Rewrite bumps whenever ANY alternate key changes — so a REWRITE that leaves this key's value alone still moves the record inside THIS key's duplicate sequence, contrary to §14.9.35.4 GR24 a). PROBE (scratchpad/lane3/out-b1/probe/gr32-firstdup/pb3gr32.cob): WRITE 01/AA/PP then 02/AA/PP; `MOVE "PP" TO R-A2, READ F KEY IS R-A2` returned KEY=01 (correct). Then read 01 by prime key, change ONLY R-A1 (AA=>BB), REWRITE, and repeat the same random read: OBSERVED KEY=02; spec-derived expected KEY=01 (R-A2's release sequence is untouched). Same root cause and same fix as GR26 — see finding one-arrival-number-for-all-alternate-keys. No spec-derived test: the citing KeyedIoDifferentialTests case is legacy-baked, and no `READ … KEY IS` exists in the greenfield suites. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 · 2002 · 2014 · 2023

So the predicate actually tested is 'the reference lies somewhere inside an SD record', never 'the reference IS an SD record'. REPRO out-b1/probe/sr1sub/sr1sub.cob: an SD `01 SRT-REC` with `05 SR-KEY PIC X(3), 05 SR-DATA PIC X(5)`; the input procedure executes `RELEASE SR-DATA.` (a 05 item, not a logical record) and then a legitimate `RELEASE SRT-REC.`. EXPECTED per 14.9.32.3 SR1 read with 4.2.2 (`--check 4.2.2 "An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate violations of the general formats and the explicit syntax rules of standard COBOL."` => OK): a compile-time diagnostic naming SR1; there is no correct run-time answer because the source is illegal, and the compiler instead invents an extra sorted record. OBSERVED: compiles clean, prints `RELEASE-OUTSIDE-ACCEPTED-UNDER-TURN-ON`, runs the later SORT and terminates normally; the stranded record is silently discarded by the SORT's `CobolSort.Init` buffer clear. EXPECTED per 14.6.13.1.3 item 7 (`--check 14.6.13.1.3 "If checking for the exception condition is enabled, execution of the run unit is terminated abnormally"` => OK), or item 5's USE dispatch. subject: RELEASE statement
notes: RULE (`--check 14.9.32.4 "The execution of a RELEASE statement causes the record named by record-name-1 to be released to the initial phase of a sort operation."` => OK 14.9.32.4 2). WHAT THE CODE DOES: SortEmitter.EmitRelease renders record-name-1's own character image and calls `CobolSort.Release(sd, image)`, which appends it to that SD's per-file image buffer in release order (CobolSort.cs:77) -- the buffer the SORT's sequence phase then orders and the RETURN phase drains, i.e. exactly the initial phase. The image is a C# string, so the store holds a snapshot: a later mutation of the record area cannot alter an already-released record. THREE LENGTH SHAPES READ AND VERIFIED, all three per 13.18.43.4 GR13 (`--check 13.18.43.4 "During the execution of a RELEASE, REWRITE, or WRITE statement, the number of bytes in the record is determined by the following conditions"` => OK 13.18.43.4 13): (a) fixed SD -- the named record's own width (probe out-b1/probe/base/base.cob returns AAAaaaaa / BBBbbbbb / CCCccccc in key order); (b) RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON -- GR13a's length, emitted as `StrRefMod(image, 1, (int)dep)` (`--check 13.18.43.4 "If data-name-1 is specified, by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1."` => OK 13.18.43.4 13) a)); (c) GR13c, a variable-occurrence record with no DEPENDING ON in the RECORD clause -- probe out-b1/probe/odo/odo.cob generates `CobolSort.Release("RELODO::SRTF", SRT_REC.AsImage().Substring(0, CobolTable.OdoExtentChars(CobolTable.Occ(WS_OCC), 1, 9, 6, 2, 1)))`, i.e. fixed portion 6 + 2 occurrences x 2 = 10 bytes, not the maximum. COVERING TEST is spec-derived (AssertSpec with expectations computed from the standard, not from the legacy oracle) and cites 14.9.32 GR2 in its own section header. EDITIONS: Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32; the rule is edition-neutral in its own text.

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB348. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.4 "The result of the execution of a RELEASE statement with the FROM phrase is equivalent to the execution of the following statements in the order specified"` => OK 14.9.32.4 4): a) MOVE identifier-1 (or literal-1) TO record-name-1 per the MOVE rules, then b) the same RELEASE without FROM. WHAT THE CODE DOES: SortEmitter.EmitRelease:142 emits `move.Emit(new BoundMove(from, [rl.Record]))` FIRST and the `CobolSort.Release` second, and it routes through the SAME MoveEmitter an explicit MOVE uses -- so 'according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement' holds for the GENERAL rules by construction (the MOVE statement's SYNTAX rules are a separate matter and are the subject of SR-14.9.32.3-3, which is NOT-IMPLEMENTED; GR4 itself is about order and equivalence). ORDER AND EQUIVALENCE VERIFIED: probe out-b1/probe/base/base.cob interleaves `RELEASE SRT-REC FROM WS-SEND` and plain `RELEASE SRT-REC` and returns AAAaaaaa / BBBbbbbb / CCCccccc in key order -- each FROM release carries the moved value, and the record area shows the moved value immediately after (`AFTER-REL-SRTREC=[CCCccccc]`). All three operand kinds take the same path: identifier (base probe), literal (`RELEASE SRT-REC FROM "LITERAL1"` in out-b1/probe/fmt/fmt.cob -> `R=[LITERAL1]`), function-identifier (`conformance:2023/pb10_function_identifier_sending` -> `RELEASE-FROM=abcdefgh`). The trailing NOTE (14.6.10 overlapping operands; result undefined if the implicit MOVE's result is undefined) is informative and imposes no additional obligation. COVERING TEST is spec-derived: its expected output is computed from GR4 plus the ascending key order, not from the legacy oracle (the class's AssertSpecPinned helper exists precisely because the oracle is wrong here). EDITIONS: Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32; the rule is edition-neutral in its own text, and the literal-1 operand's own edition gate is recorded on FMT-14.9.32.2. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — GR4 makes RELEASE ... FROM x EXACTLY 'MOVE x TO record-name-1' + the same RELEASE without FROM. It is not. The implicit move is constructed in the EMITTER (SortEmitter.EmitRelease:142 `move.Emit(new BoundMove(from, [rl.Record]))`), so it never passes through MoveBinder.Bind -- which does more than diagnose: it collects CODEGEN-RELEVANT storage facts (`ctx.Data.MarkImageForced(t.Item)` for an alphanumeric-figurative sender into an elementary numeric-DISPLAY receiver, and `MarkRefModStoreImage`), the facts StorageFormPass consumes. A/B PROBE, identical programs per GR4, `SD SRTF / 01 SRT-NUM PIC 9(3)`, SORT ... GIVING (no RETURN, so the RETURN emitter is out of the picture): probe/ref-gr4a/c.cob `MOVE QUOTE TO SRT-NUM. RELEASE SRT-NUM.` at --std 2014 RUNS -- emits `SRT_NUM = new string('\"', 3)` then `CobolSort.Release(...)`, prints AFTER-MOVE=["""] / SORT-DONE, exit 0. probe/ref-gr4a/d.cob `RELEASE SRT-NUM FROM QUOTE.` at --std 2014 ABORTS -- emits `NotImplemented.Run("MOVE of an alphanumeric figurative constant into the numeric item 'SRT-NUM' without image-backed storage")` and dies with an unhandled NotImplementedCobolFeatureException BEFORE the release, so the record never reaches the initial phase and the SORT never completes. Same source, same SD, opposite result. SECOND, INDEPENDENT LEG (edition): at --std 2023 the explicit MOVE is REMOVED and errors COBOLNET0902 (exit 70), while the RELEASE ... FROM QUOTE form compiles with NO diagnostic at all (exit 0) -- 'according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement' is not applied at any edition. THIRD leg (compile hard-failure): with an OUTPUT PROCEDURE instead of GIVING (probe/ref-gr4a/b.cob), the same divergence makes the whole program uncompilable, `error CS0029: Cannot implicitly convert type 'string' to 'long'` in the generated C#. The adjudicator's own summary diagnosed this mechanism ('the BoundMove is first constructed in the EMITTER') but charged it ONLY to the SYNTAX rules SR2/SR3/SR4 and left GR4 CONFORMS on the claim that 'it routes through the SAME MoveEmitter an explicit MOVE uses -- so the MOVE rules hold for the GENERAL rules by construction'. That claim is false: the emitter is the same, but the BINDER's collected facts that the emitter's own output depends on are missing, and the run-time RESULT differs. A wrong result at run time is a GENERAL-rule failure. Note the ordinary shapes DO agree (probe/ref-gr45/ma.cob vs mb.cob: COMP sender, subscripted WS-E(WS-I), ref-modified WS-LONG(3:8) -- all three identical, R=[-0123   ] / [ELEM0002] / [cdefghij]), which is why one probe of the happy path read as CONFORMS.
