NOT VERIFIED (GR13b + 13.18.43.4 GR5a): with no RECORD clause the implicit clause is implementor-defined, and if format 1 is implied its size is 'the record size of the LARGEST record description entry in this file description entry' (cite.py --check 13.18.43.4 => OK 13.18.43.4 5) a)), which is precisely the fixed-length sort file 14.9.40 GR7 presupposes. In that model releasing a SHORT 01 of a multi-01 SD IS GR6's case. This compiler never produces it: SortBinder.BindRelease releases at record-name-1's OWN description size (SortBinder.cs:238-240 + BoundSort.cs:71). MEASURED at probe/ref-gr6/w.cob -- SD with 01 SRT-SHORT PIC X(4) and 01 SRT-LONG PIC X(10), no RECORD clause -- the sort store ends up holding a 4-byte record and a 10-byte record for ONE SD, and SORT ... GIVING writes a 4-character record into an FD whose 01 OUT-REC is PIC X(10) (output file lines '[AAAA]' and '[ZZZZZZZZZZ]'). That may be legitimate implementor latitude (13.18.43.4 GR5 lets the implementor imply FORMAT 2 instead, min=smallest, max=largest, under which 4 bytes is in range and GR6 is vacuous) -- but the implementation nowhere DECLARES that choice, and 13.18.43.4 GR5 is on the implementor-defined list that 'shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation' (docs/rearchitecture/spec-rule-catalog.json:39386). A real clause answering a different question, inherited straight into the GR6 adjudication. CONFORMS asserts conformance in BOTH realizations on evidence from one; PARTIAL is what the evidence supports. Not DIVERGES: nothing measured contradicts GR6 itself -- the release happens, the run continues, and record-name-1's own bytes occupy the leading positions in every over-length case I could build. No test-ref, correctly.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.3 'The AT END phrase and the NOT AT END phrase, when specified, may be written in reversed order.' -> OK, 14.9.34.3 rule 4). Note this is the ONLY 'reversed order' sentence in the whole standard (grep 'reversed order' over specs/ISO_COBOL.md: 1 hit) - every other conditional phrase gets the same effect from 5.2.6.4 choice indicators printed in its own format, whereas the RETURN format (rendered page 738) uses PLAIN brackets, so SR4 is the sole grant. CODE: CobolIO.g4:690 returnAtEndPhrase carries both orders as two alternatives, and SortBinder.BindReturn:269-272 splits them with PhraseBlocks.Split(ae.statementBlock(), PhraseBlocks.StartsWithNot(ae), ...) - one positional swap, total over the NOT-led pair. VERIFIED: conformance-test SortMergeDifferentialTests.Return_ReversedAtEndPhrases_SpecPinned writes 'RETURN SF NOT AT END DISPLAY "R=" S-TXT AT END MOVE "Y" TO WS-EOF END-RETURN.' and asserts the spec-derived 'R=ONE\nR=TWO\nR=THREE' - both branches bind to the right arm (a swap would loop forever or print nothing). AssertSpecPinned, not the legacy differential, so it qualifies. MEASURED, NOT A DEFECT FOUND HERE: the compiler accepts the reversed pair at --std 85 as well (probe p16, exit 0 at both 85 and 2002) with no edition predicate on returnAtEndPhrase. Whether SR4 existed in ANSI X3.23-1985 cannot be re-derived from the 2023 text (the only text available here): Annex E covers 2014->2023 only and names no RETURN change. Recorded as a dossier gap rather than invented as a defect. OVER-ACCEPTANCE NOTE: the NOT-led alternative also admits the NOT-ONLY form (no AT END at all), which the general format forbids - that defect is recorded on FMT-14.9.34.2, not here; SR4's own obligation is fully met.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB349. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.4 'the EC-FLOW-RETURN exception condition is set to exist' -> OK, 14.9.34.4 rule 1). EC-FLOW-RETURN is FATAL (cite.py --find 'EC-FLOW-RETURN | Fatal | RETURN not in range of MERGE or SORT' -> 14.6.13.1.6, Table 13), so with checking enabled 14.6.13.1.3 requires the USE-declarative / abnormal-termination path. DEFAULT-OFF IS CONFORMANT and is NOT the finding: --check 7.3.25.4 'The default TURN directive is \'>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING OFF\'.' -> OK (rule 1) and --check 7.3.25.4 'if checking is not turned on for that exception condition, the results of continuing execution are undefined or defined by the implementor' -> OK (rule 6). Probe p3 (a bare 'RETURN SF AT END ... NOT AT END ...' in MAIN with no SORT/MERGE executing) prints AT END / AFTER and exits 0 - permitted. THE DIVERGENCE IS CHECKING-ON. REPRO (probe p4, out-b1/probe/p4/p4.cob): the same program with '>>TURN EC-FLOW-RETURN CHECKING ON' in column 8 of line 1. EXPECTED from GR1 + Table 13 + 14.6.13.1.3: the exception is set to exist and, being fatal with no handler, the run unit terminates abnormally. OBSERVED: identical output - AT END / AFTER, exit 0. The EC is never set. CODE: ExceptionCatalog.cs:103 registers L3("EC-FLOW-RETURN", EcFatality.Fatal) - a turnable name - but there is no raise site anywhere. CobolSort.cs:34 states it outright: 'The EC-FLOW-RELEASE / EC-FLOW-RETURN / EC-SORT-MERGE-ACTIVE phase tracking ... attaches here when the EC model lands'; the Store has no phase field. EcBinder.EcWrap's QueryFor has no BoundReturn case and EcEmitter.FatalAmbientGates does not list the name, so a RETURN is never wrapped in BoundEcChecked. CONTROL PROBE p5 proves the >>TURN pipeline itself works and the silence is specific to this EC: '>>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON' with an out-of-range subscript prints 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT (fatal): subscript 9 is outside 1..3 (ISO 8.4.2.3.4 GR2)'. THE UNIMPLEMENTED-ELEMENT LICENCE DOES NOT COVER THIS: --check 14.6.13.1.1 'The implementor is not required to raise any exception conditions for level-3 exception-names that are associated with optional language elements or processor-dependent language elements that the implementor has not implemented' -> OK - it is conditioned on OPTIONAL or PROCESSOR-DEPENDENT elements NOT implemented. Sort-merge is neither (it is absent from Annex A.4 and from docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 5's Not-claimed list) and RETURN IS implemented. EDITIONS: GR1's prohibition itself is a 1985 rule; the EC-name half is the 2002 exception-condition facility.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.4 'is undefined at the completion of the execution of the RETURN statement' -> OK, 14.9.34.4 rule 2). This is a PERMISSION, not an obligation: with more than one record description, whatever lies outside the current record's range is undefined, so any deterministic content conforms. CODE (read, not assumed): BindReturn:255-260 deliberately resolves the record area through file.AreaRecord - the LARGEST record's view (13.4.2) - rather than Records[0], so a multi-01 SD is not truncated; EmitReturn:167 calls SequentialIoEmitter.EmitImageInto(rt.RecordArea, tmp), which writes CobolString.Store(image, record.ImageWidth). CobolString.Store(value, width, justifiedRight=false, pad=' ') space-fills, so the bytes outside the returned record are deterministically SPACES - a documented refinement of 'undefined'. The secondary 01s of a multi-01 SD are synthesized REDEFINES over that same area (9.1.2), so they read the same image. Nothing here can contradict a rule whose content is a grant of undefinedness. NO SPEC-DERIVED TEST exercises a multi-01 SD through RETURN (the two spec-pinned sort suites use single-01 SDs), so the row is CONFORMS-but-untested and stays a GAP.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB349. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.4 'the EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN exception condition is set to exist and the results of the execution of the RETURN statement are undefined' -> OK, 14.9.34.4 rule 3). The rule has THREE obligations. (i) NEXT RECORD IN KEY ORDER INTO THE RECORD AREA - CONFORMS. CobolSort.Return:144-156 hands back f.Records[f.Cursor++] from the buffer the Sort/Merge phase left in key order (KeyColumns builds the key columns once; the SORT is stable and the MERGE takes the earliest stream on a tie); EmitReturn stores it through EmitImageInto. Verified spec-derived by MixedUsageRecordImageDifferentialTests.ReleaseReturn_SignedCompLeaves_RoundTripZeroAndMax and by SortMergeDifferentialTests.Return_Into_MovesRecordToReceiver; probe p15 additionally confirms the MERGE arm ('as determined by the keys listed in the SORT or MERGE statement') - MERGE ... USING F1 F2 OUTPUT PROCEDURE with RETURN yields AAA F1-A / AAA F2-A / BBB F2-B / CCC F1-C. (ii) AT END -> imperative-statement-1, then control to the end of the statement, record area undefined - CONFORMS. Return returns false at the cursor end and EmitReturn's else arm runs AtEnd and falls through. The area is left UNCHANGED (probe p1 re-prints the last record), a refinement of 'undefined'. (iii) A RETURN AFTER THE AT END CONDITION SETS EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN - NOT IMPLEMENTED. The name is registered Fatal (ExceptionCatalog.cs:196; cite.py --find 'EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN | Fatal | RETURN executed when at end condition exists' -> 14.6.13.1.6 Table 13) and never raised: the Store carries no at-end latch, EcBinder.EcWrap's QueryFor has no BoundReturn case and EcEmitter.FatalAmbientGates omits the name. REPRO: probe p1 executes RETURN twice past end-of-data and the store silently reports at-end again; adding '>>TURN EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN CHECKING ON' changes nothing (same mechanism proven for the sibling name at GR1 by probes p4/p5). Under the default checking-OFF (7.3.25.4 rules 1 and 6) that silence is a conformant refinement of 'undefined'; under CHECKING ON it diverges, and 14.6.13.1.1's unimplemented-element licence does not apply (sort-merge is neither optional nor processor-dependent, and RETURN is implemented). Two obligations verified, one absent -> PARTIAL.

subject: RETURN statement
notes:
RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.4 'control is transferred to imperative-statement-2, if specified; otherwise, control is transferred to the end of the RETURN statement.' -> OK, 14.9.34.4 rule 4). The rule is an ORDERING: record made available, THEN any implicit INTO move, THEN imperative-statement-2. CODE (read line by line): SortEmitter.EmitReturn:165-176 emits, inside 'if (CobolSort.Return(sd, out tmp))', exactly (1) EmitImageInto(rt.RecordArea, tmp) - the record made available; (2) the 13.18.43 GR15 DEPENDING-length store; (3) 'if (rt.Into is { } into) move.Emit(...)' - the implicit move; (4) 'if (rt.NotAtEnd is { } not) Statements.EmitStatementList(not)'. When NOT AT END is unwritten nothing is emitted and control leaves the if-block - the 'otherwise' arm, observed directly in probe p1 (a phrase-less RETURN falls straight through to the following DISPLAY). VERIFIED: SortMergeDifferentialTests.Return_Into_MovesRecordToReceiver is AssertSpecPinned and its NOT AT END imperative displays BOTH the record area and the INTO receiver, asserting the spec-derived 'AREA=1ONE
INTO=1ONE
AREA=2TWO
INTO=2TWO' - which can only hold if the record was made available and the implicit move executed BEFORE imperative-statement-2 ran. The 'otherwise' arm has no on-disk spec-derived case; it is verified by reading and by probe p1.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB348. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.4 'The implied MOVE statement does not occur if the execution of the RETURN statement was unsuccessful.' -> OK, 14.9.34.4 rule 5 b). GR5 decomposes into six obligations. VERIFIED CONFORMING: (a) the same RETURN without INTO runs first - EmitReturn emits the store before the move. (b-not-occur) the move sits INSIDE the success arm, so an unsuccessful RETURN skips it. (b-both) 'The record is available in both the record area and the data item referenced by identifier-1' - pinned by SortMergeDifferentialTests.Return_Into_MovesRecordToReceiver (AssertSpecPinned; AREA= and INTO= both print the returned record). (b-size / RECORD IS VARYING) 'The size of the current record is determined by rules specified for the RECORD clause ... the implied move is an alphanumeric group move' - 13.18.43 GR16a makes the sending operand the DEPENDING byte count. The emitter moves the WHOLE area, but EmitImageInto space-fills the area beyond the record (CobolString.Store pads with spaces), so the two are observationally identical; probe p11 (SD RECORD IS VARYING FROM 6 TO 12 DEPENDING ON WS-LEN, receiver PIC X(12) pre-filled with '*') prints LEN=12 INTO=[1AAAAAAAAAAA] and LEN=06 INTO=[2BB         ] - the 6-byte record left-justified and space-filled, exactly GR16a. (b-item-identification) 'Item identification of the data item referenced by identifier-1 is done after the record has been read and immediately before it is moved' - probe p10 writes 'RETURN SF INTO SLOT (S-K)' where S-K is a field OF the returned record, initially 0; the result T=......2TWO  3THREE...... shows SLOT(2) and SLOT(3) filled, i.e. the subscript used the JUST-READ S-K. DEFECTIVE HALF: 'according to the rules for the MOVE statement without the CORRESPONDING phrase'. The implied MOVE is SYNTHESIZED IN THE EMITTER - SortEmitter.EmitReturn:174 'move.Emit(new BoundMove(new BoundFieldOperand(rt.RecordArea), [into]))' - downstream of every binder-side MOVE check, so StatementValidation.CheckStrongMove (14.9.25.3 SR2) never sees it. REPRO probe p7: a non-strong SD record area moved into a 'TYPE TA' strongly-typed receiver compiles and runs silently, while control probe p8's explicit 'MOVE PLAIN TO WS-RECV' is rejected COBOLNET1533. EXPECTED: the implied move is subject to the MOVE statement's own syntax rules, so the same COBOLNET1533 (and, per 14.9.34.3 SR3, an SR3 diagnostic) is due at compile time. SWEEP: the same emitter-synthesized-MOVE shape is in SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRead (READ ... INTO - probe p9 confirms it also escapes) and SortEmitter.EmitRelease (RELEASE ... FROM).

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 1): 'The access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic.' CODE: BindStart -- if (file.AccessMode == FileAccessMode.Random) ctx.Edition.Error('COBOLNET0862', ... 'the access mode shall be sequential or dynamic (ISO 14.9.41 SR1)'). FileAccessMode is {Sequential, Random, Dynamic}, so the single Random test is the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair, and FileModel.AccessMode DEFAULTS to Sequential -- a SELECT with no ACCESS clause (the implicit arm a check written against an explicit clause would miss) does not false-fire. ctx.Edition.Error is unconditional, so the diagnostic fires at every strictness and every edition, right for a rule with no edition delta.
PROBED on BOTH keyed organizations, because the check sits before the organization split and a one-organization probe would not have shown that: indexed ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-sr8) and relative ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-rel) each report COBOLNET0862 SR1.
ONE EDGE NOT REACHED, and it is benign: the check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)', so a sequential-organization file never reaches SR1. 12.4.5.2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for sequential organization, so no conforming program can exercise that arm -- the hole is in the diagnostic for an already-illegal file control entry, and 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule.
TEST: NONE. grep for COBOLNET0862 across tests/ returns zero hits -- no negative fixture, no unit test -- so a green suite proves nothing about this row. conformance:2002/file_collating_seq exercises only the ACCEPT side (ACCESS DYNAMIC) and would still pass with this check deleted. Closing needs a negative fixture pinning COBOLNET0862 on ORGANIZATION INDEXED + ACCESS RANDOM + START, and its relative twin. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's own note names an unreached edge -- the SR1 check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)' at KeyedIoBinder.cs:208, so a sequential-organization file never reaches it -- and then argues the edge away with a premise I MEASURED AND BROKE: 'no conforming program can exercise that arm ... 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule'. The premise is half right and the conclusion is wrong. Half right: I read the file control entry general formats (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 12.4.5.1) rather than trusting the paraphrase, and Format 3 (sequential) does carry only '[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]' -- ACCESS RANDOM on a sequential file is indeed not conforming. Wrong: nothing in this compiler diagnoses it. ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL + ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM + START SQF FIRST compiles CLEAN -- exit 0, prb.dll written, ZERO diagnostics -- so the rule that was supposed to own the hole owns nothing, and a program that violates SR1 ('the access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic') is accepted in silence and becomes NotImplemented.Run at run time. SR1 is therefore enforced over two of the three organizations START can name and unenforced over the third; that is PARTIAL by the stated burden (an unverified edge => PARTIAL, and this one is worse than unverified -- it is verified to miss). I did NOT charge SR1 with the sequential-file rejection itself: that mechanism is already recorded as DIVERGES on SR-14.9.41.3-2, and if it is fixed the SR1 test, sitting below it, would start covering sequential files unchanged. What I charge is the CONFORMS claim, whose sole justification for the uncovered half was an escape hatch that does not exist. Everything else in the record I re-derived and it held: FileModel.cs:10 'enum FileAccessMode { Sequential, Random, Dynamic }' makes the single Random test the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair; FileModel.cs:54 'AccessMode { get; set; } = FileAccessMode.Sequential' makes the implicit arm safe; EditionContext.cs:109 'Error(...) => Diagnostics.Add($"{Prefix()}error {code}...")' is unconditional. Citation re-run and OK. Test-ref is empty, which is expected and not what moved the verdict.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 2): 'If the organization of the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequential, either the FIRST or the LAST phrase shall be specified.' The rule PERMITS START on a sequential-organization file -- it only constrains WHICH phrase. And the semantics are fully specified: 14.9.41.4 GR20/GR21 (--check, under the heading SEQUENTIAL FILES) -- 'If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to 1 if records exist in the physical file' / 'If LAST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the record number of the last existing logical record in the physical file'; with no records, or no ability to position, status '23', the invalid key condition exists, the statement is unsuccessful.
CODE: BindStart -- 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported($"START on sequential-organization file '{name}' (ISO 14.9.41 SR2 FIRST/LAST positioning - a later slice)");'. FileModel.IsSequential covers Sequential AND LineSequential. TWO defects in one line: it rejects the ONLY form SR2 permits, and it names SR2 -- the rule that MAKES it legal -- as the authority for refusing it.
AND THE REFUSAL IS NOT A DIAGNOSTIC. BoundUnsupported is a runtime loud stage: StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundUnsupported) writes LoudStmt(n.Feature). PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr2-seq): an ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL file written with two records, reopened INPUT, then 'START SQF FIRST INVALID KEY ... NOT INVALID KEY ... END-START'. Compile output: EMPTY. Run: 'Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... START on sequential-organization file SQF'. SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: the START succeeds, WS-ST = '00', the NOT INVALID KEY imperative runs, and the following READ delivers the first record ('AAAAAAAAAA').
The edition gate cannot see it either -- VersionConformancePass fires on BoundKeyedStart, a node this path never constructs, so START FIRST on a sequential file is not even edition-checked.
EDITIONS: SR2's only satisfying forms are FIRST and LAST, which are absent from the COBOL-85 START format (the compiler gates them at 2002 via ConstructRegistry 'start-first-last-2002'), hence 2002+. Annex E of the 2023 text records no 14.9.41 change from 2014, so the 2023 clause is also the 2014 requirement; the pre-2014 split is not derivable from the 2023 text alone.
TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB333; PB332. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 3): relational-operator 'is a relational operator specified in the general-relation format of 8.8.4.2, Simple relation conditions, with the exception of the relational operators IS NOT EQUAL TO or IS NOT='. The rule has TWO halves -- a positive membership test and a negative exception -- and I verified both.
THE 8.8.4.2 SET (read from the Format-1 diagram, --check on its figure note 'Each of the three brace groups requires exactly one of its enclosed alternatives; the brackets around NOT make it optional'): IS [NOT] GREATER THAN | IS [NOT] > | IS [NOT] LESS THAN | IS [NOT] < | IS [NOT] EQUAL TO | IS [NOT] = | IS <> | IS GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO | IS >= | IS LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO | IS <=. THE [NOT] BRACKET SITS ON THE FIRST SIX ONLY -- 'NOT >=' and 'NOT LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO' are NOT alternatives of the general-relation format.
HALF THAT CONFORMS: BindStart maps the operator through ConditionBinder.MapOperator and reports COBOLNET0862 when it yields '!='. Probed (out-b1/probe/sr3-ne): all three not-equal spellings -- NOT EQUAL TO, NOT =, and <> -- are rejected.
HALF THAT DIVERGES: the START KEY phrase reuses CobolExpressions.g4 comparisonOperator WHOLE, and that rule carries four alternatives outside the general-relation format -- 'IS? NOT GTEQUAL', 'IS? NOT LTEQUAL', 'IS? NOT GREATER THAN? OR EQUAL TO?', 'IS? NOT LESS THAN? OR EQUAL TO?'. Nothing narrows it for START. Probed (out-b1/probe/sr3-ops): 'START IXF KEY IS NOT >= IX-KEY' and 'START IXF KEY IS NOT LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO IX-KEY' both compile and RUN (P2-OK ST=00, P3-OK ST=00), MapOperator silently folding them to '<' and '>'. SR3 requires rejection. UNDER-REJECTS. (The operator is also grammatically OPTIONAL where the format requires it -- recorded on FMT-14.9.41.2, same phrase, different mechanism.)
OBSERVATION, deliberately NOT filed as a defect: SR3's exception list names only 'IS NOT EQUAL TO' and 'IS NOT=', so the third not-equal spelling 'IS <>' is literally outside the exception and the compiler's rejection of it is over-strict against the letter of the rule. But 14.9.41.4 GR9 a)/b) and GR17 c)/d) enumerate EQUAL, GREATER, NOT LESS, GREATER OR EQUAL and LESS, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL -- '<>' is in neither list, so the standard defines no START behaviour for it and rejecting is the defensible reading. The gap is editorial in ISO/IEC 1989:2023, not a compiler defect.
RELATED, and satisfied: Annex A.3 item 39 (--check) makes 'the relational operators LESS, NOT GREATER, or LESS OR EQUAL in the START statement' processor-dependent; docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 39 CLAIMS them, so they must be accepted -- and are.
TEST: none (zero COBOLNET0862 hits across tests/).

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 4): 'Data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses.' The rule has two operand legs (indexed and relative) and they behave differently.
INDEXED LEG -- ENFORCED, but only as a SIDE EFFECT and reported under the WRONG RULE. RecordLayout.OffsetOf bails to null when the item or any ancestor carries OCCURS ('if (p.Occurs is not null) return null;   // subject to OCCURS => no single fixed position'), so KeyIndexByPosition returns null and BindStart emits COBOLNET0862 '<name> neither names a record key nor begins at the leftmost character position of one with a length not greater than that key (ISO 14.9.41 SR6)'. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr4-occ) with '05 IX-KEY. 10 IX-ELEM PIC X(3) OCCURS 2 TIMES.' and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-ELEM (1)': rejected with exactly that message. The source IS refused, so no illegal program compiles -- but the message asserts something FALSE about this operand: IX-ELEM(1) DOES begin at IX-KEY's leftmost character position and IS shorter than it. The rule actually violated is SR4; OffsetOf's null collapses two distinct rejection reasons into one sentence, and a user reading it would look for the wrong problem.
RELATIVE LEG -- NO CHECK AT ALL. BindStart's relative arm tests only ReferenceEquals(operand.Item, file.RelativeKeyItem) (that is SR5), which is TRUE for a SUBSCRIPTED reference to the same DataItem. PROBED (same file): with '01 WS-RKT. 05 WS-RK PIC 9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.' and 'RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK', the statement 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK (2)' compiles with NO diagnostic. That shape is reachable only through a file control entry that already violates 12.4.5.13.3 SR1 (--check: 'Data-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses') -- and KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile implements 12.4.5.13's SR2 (unsigned integer, no P) and SR3 (not within a record of the file) but NOT its SR1, so nothing anywhere in the chain diagnoses it. The two missing checks cover for each other.
UNDER-REJECTS. TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB236. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 5): 'For relative files, data-name-1, if specified, shall be the data item specified in the RELATIVE KEY clause in the associated file control entry.' CODE: BindStart's relative arm -- if (operand is not null && !ReferenceEquals(operand.Item, file.RelativeKeyItem)) ctx.Edition.Error('COBOLNET0862', ... 'data-name-1 shall be the RELATIVE KEY item <rk> (ISO 14.9.41 SR5)'). The test is reference identity on the DataItem, which is the right basis: a qualified or subscripted reference to the SAME item still satisfies SR5 because it IS that data item (the OCCURS consequence of that is a different rule and is recorded on SR-14.9.41.3-4, not here). The 'if specified' half is honoured -- with no KEY phrase the code falls to 'operand ??= file.RelativeKeyItem', which is GR8's implied EQUAL, not an SR5 violation.
PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr5-excl), both directions, because a reject-only probe would not show the accept arm still works: 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-OTHER' -> COBOLNET0862 naming 'WS-RK'; 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK' accepted.
EDGE, correct by construction: when a relative file has no RELATIVE KEY clause, file.RelativeKeyItem is null, the message names '(none)' and EVERY operand is refused -- which is what SR5 requires, since the item data-name-1 would have to be does not exist.
EDGE, benign and outside this rule: an operand that fails NAME RESOLUTION short-circuits at 'if (kp is not null && operand is null) return new BoundUnsupported(...)' before SR5 runs, so an undeclared name becomes a runtime loud stage rather than a bind error. That is a name-resolution concern, not SR5.
TEST: NONE -- COBOLNET0862 has zero hits across tests/. Closing needs a negative fixture pinning the SR5 message on a relative START whose operand is not the RELATIVE KEY item. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — I attacked the ONE sentence the record leans on: 'The test is reference identity on the DataItem, which is the right basis: a qualified or subscripted reference to the SAME item still satisfies SR5 because it IS that data item.' It is the right basis for qualification -- I confirmed that -- and the wrong basis for the two reference forms that DECORATE an item, because Place.cs:31-37 defines 'PlaceDecorator.Item => Inner.Item'. Reference identity on the resolved DataItem therefore asks 'does this reference land on that storage', where SR5 asks 'is data-name-1 that data item', and the two answers part company on exactly two measured shapes. (1) REFERENCE MODIFICATION, the unambiguous one: 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK(1:2)' compiles CLEAN -- exit 0, zero diagnostics -- and emits StartRelative(..., FromAlphanumeric(RefMod(FormatImage(WS_RK), 1, 2))). 8.4.3.3.1 says 'Reference modification defines a unique data item', so data-name-1 there is NOT the data item named in the RELATIVE KEY clause and SR5 requires a diagnostic; instead the relative record number is read from the first two characters of the key's DISPLAY image, so a key of 12 starts at record 0 -- and 12.4.5.13.4 GR1 makes 1 the first relative record number, so 0 is not even a legal one. This is a silent wrong answer, not merely a missing diagnostic. (2) A LEVEL-66 RENAMES ALIAS: '66 WS-ALIAS RENAMES WS-RK.' then 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-ALIAS' also compiles clean, emitting StartRelative on WS_GRP.WS_RK. 13.18.45.4 GR1 gives the alias its own data description entry with data-name-2's attributes and storage -- a second data item over one storage -- so SR5 is violated. The compiler's own behaviour proves it does not believe otherwise: the THRU form of the SAME alias ('66 WS-SPAN RENAMES WS-RK THRU WS-TAIL') IS rejected with the SR5 message, because that one resolves to a RenamesPlace whose 'Item => AliasItem' is its own. So SR5's coverage tracks how RENAMES happens to resolve, not what the rule says. What UPHELD, and I tried hard to break each: the reject arm fires on a plainly different item and on a REDEFINES alias, at every one of 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive; the accept arm takes the relative key written plain, written qualified with OF, written qualified with IN, and written as an item defined in ANOTHER file's record (legal -- 12.4.5.13.3 SR3 bars the key only from a record subordinate to the ASSOCIATED file-name), and in each case emits a real CobolFile.StartRelative rather than swallowing it; the 'if specified' half is honoured (START with no KEY phrase raises nothing); and the no-RELATIVE-KEY-clause case refuses every operand naming '(none)'. Citation re-run and OK. The empty test-ref is expected and is not what moved the verdict. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 6 and 6) b) 1.): for indexed files data-name-1 shall reference either a) a prime or alternate record key associated with file-name-1, or b) a data item whose 'leftmost character position WITHIN A RECORD OF THE FILE corresponds to the leftmost character position of a prime or alternate record key that is associated with file-name-1 and that is defined without the SOURCE phrase in the RECORD KEY clause or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause'.
CODE: RecordLayout.KeyIndexByPosition(file, operand) -- 'if (OffsetOf(operand) is not { } off) return null; if (file.RecordKeyItem is { } pk && OffsetOf(pk) == off && operand.ImageWidth <= pk.ImageWidth) return -1;' then the same loop over file.AlternateKeys.
THE ACCEPT ARM CONFORMS and is deliberately position-based rather than name-based (12.4.5.12.4 GR4 makes the identical byte positions keys in EVERY record description of the file), so a REDEFINES of the key and a same-position item in a sibling 01 both match. It is pinned by a spec-derived test: conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition, which asserts GOT=02 directly from the rule rather than against an oracle.
THE REJECT ARM DIVERGES. OffsetOf computes the offset inside the operand's OWN 01 root ('DataItem root = item; while (root.Parent is { } parent) root = parent;') and NOTHING checks that that root is a record description of file-name-1 -- or of any FD at all. So any item at offset 0 of any 01 anywhere in the program, no wider than the key, binds as a generic key of that file. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr6-ws): '01 WS-OUTSIDE. 05 WS-PART PIC X(4). 05 WS-FILLER PIC X(20).' in WORKING-STORAGE, then 'START IXF KEY IS = WS-PART' against 'RECORD KEY IS IX-KEY' / '05 IX-KEY PIC X(6)' -- compiles CLEAN, binding keyIndex = -1 (the prime key).
And the acceptance is not merely a missing syntax check. KeyedIoEmitter.EmitStart then passes OperandText.AsString of that WORKING-STORAGE item as the comparison value, where 14.9.41.4 GR17 a) (--check) specifies 'The specified key is set up by moving the relevant parts of the RECORD AREA into a temporary data area' -- so the compiler emits a comparand the standard does not define for a statement it should have refused.
SR6 b) 1.'s 'defined without the SOURCE phrase' qualifier is vacuous in this compiler (no SOURCE surface -- see SR-14.9.41.3-7), so it is not a second defect here.
UNDER-REJECTS. TEST-REF LEFT EMPTY DELIBERATELY: the sibling-record test above covers only the accept arm and would still pass with the reject arm fixed, so naming it would misrepresent coverage.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3, printed path 6) b) 2.): 'It has the same class, category, and usage as that record key.' NOTHING CHECKS IT, and the omission is deliberate and self-documented -- RecordLayout.KeyIndexByPosition's own doc comment says '(SR6b.2's same-class/category/usage check is a pre-existing looseness kept as-is; the width-<= rule is SR6b.3.)'. The method tests OffsetOf equality and ImageWidth <= and nothing else; there is no class, category or usage comparison anywhere on the START key path.
PROBED, compile and run (out-b1/probe/l23-len and out-b1/probe/l22-run). Prime key '05 IX-KEY PIC X(6)' (class alphanumeric, category alphanumeric, usage display); sibling record '01 IX-REC3. 05 IX-NUM PIC 9(4) COMP-3.' (class numeric, category numeric, usage packed-decimal, ImageWidth 4 <= 6, offset 0 == the key's offset). 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-NUM' compiles with NO diagnostic. Run against a file holding keys '1234AA' and '9999ZZ', after MOVE 1234 TO IX-NUM, it reports 'L22-OK ST=00' and the following READ NEXT returns 1234AA. SR6 b) 2. forbids that operand outright; the compiler instead substitutes a VALUE CONVERSION (KeyedIoEmitter.EmitStart -> OperandText.AsString of the packed item) where the rule's whole premise is that the operand OVERLAYS the key's character positions. SILENT under-rejection with a wrong-answer tail: the same shape with a COMP or COMP-3 item whose rendered text does not coincide with the stored key characters compares the wrong bytes and reports no error.
ROW CONTEXT: this L-row and its sibling L2.3 are the nested-list rows kb/Work PB55 records under '14.9.41.3 L2' as scheduled for absorption into their parent rule after the defect burn-down; adjudicated here as the inventory presents them.
TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3, printed path 6) b) 3.): 'Its length is not greater than the length of that record key.' CODE: RecordLayout.KeyIndexByPosition -- 'operand.ImageWidth <= pk.ImageWidth' for the prime key and the same test over each entry of file.AlternateKeys.
VERIFIED for the alphanumeric-display case (out-b1/probe/l23-len): prime key '05 IX-KEY PIC X(6)', sibling record '01 IX-REC2. 05 IX-LONG PIC X(9).' at the same offset 0, and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-LONG' is REJECTED with COBOLNET0862 -- the longer operand does not bind. The accept side of the same threshold is covered by the shorter-operand case that KeyIndexByPosition's generic-key path serves.
PARTIAL, on two splits I could NOT verify:
(a) 14.9.41.4 GR13 distinguishes alphanumeric character positions from NATIONAL character positions for this length, and a national item cannot appear in a file record at all in this compiler -- probing '05 IX-NAT PIC N(3).' inside an FD record raises COBOLNET0899 'national data in a file record ... is recognized but not yet implemented - the record codec is single-byte and the national character is two bytes'. The national leg of the length comparison therefore has no implementation to verify, and the rule is enforced for only one of its two operand classes.
(b) ImageWidth is a DECLARED-image width (digits plus separate sign for a numeric usage, PIC length for alphanumeric), so once SR6 b) 2.'s class/category/usage identity goes unenforced (SR-14.9.41.3-L2.2) the two sides of this <= are not commensurable: a PIC 9(4) COMP-3 operand contributes 4 while occupying 3 bytes of packed storage. The rule holds soundly only where operand and key are both alphanumeric display.
ROW CONTEXT: an L-row of the kb/Work PB55 family (see SR-14.9.41.3-L2.2).
TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB358. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 7): 'Record-key-name-1 shall be specified with the SOURCE phrase in the RECORD KEY clause or in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause in the file control entry for file-name-1.'
NO SURFACE ANYWHERE. I searched rather than trusting the dossier's silence: CobolIO.g4 carries 'recordKeyClause : RECORD KEY? IS? dataReference' and 'alternateKeyClause : ALTERNATE RECORD? KEY? IS? dataReference (WITH? DUPLICATES)? alternateKeySuppressWhen?' -- neither has a SOURCE phrase, and grep for record-key-name / SourcePhrase across src/ returns only the START grammar comment and the COLLATING SEQUENCE Format-2 comment. record-key-name-1 therefore cannot be DECLARED, so START's record-key-name-1 alternative (in the 14.9.41.2 brace group) is unreachable and SR7 has nothing to constrain. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr7-source): 'RECORD KEY IS IX-COMPOSITE SOURCE IS IX-A IX-B' -> COBOL0312 'unexpected SOURCE. Unexpected token in FILE-CONTROL paragraph.'
THIS IS A SANCTIONED DECLINE, NOT A CONFORMANCE BREAK. Annex A.3 item 40 (--check): 'The capability of specifying the SOURCE phrase of the RECORD KEY clause and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 40 already records the disposition: 'SOURCE phrase of RECORD KEY / ALTERNATE RECORD KEY | 13.x | Not claimed | The record-key-name SOURCE IS key form is not provided'.
I am NOT raising NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION: the disposition already exists, so the owner owns this row; converting it to DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT is the owner's call and never mine (D13). Note the decline is an A.3 PROCESSOR-DEPENDENT element, not an A.4 optional module, so the PB260/PB261/PB281-PB283 declined-module witness notes do not cover it.
WHAT IS STILL OWED EITHER WAY: the refusal is a GENERIC parser error, not a named diagnostic saying the SOURCE phrase is not provided, and no fixture pins it -- so nothing would notice if the grammar later accepted SOURCE and silently ignored it, which is exactly the silent-miscompile the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT closing bar guards against.
EDITIONS: the SOURCE phrase is absent from the COBOL-85 RECORD KEY clause; Annex E of the 2023 text records no 14.9.41 change from 2014, so 2014 and 2023 are certain and 2002 is the conventional third. TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 8): 'If the LENGTH phrase is specified, file-name-1 shall reference a file with indexed organization.' CODE: BindStart -- 'if (length is not null && file.Organization != FileOrganization.Indexed) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET0862", ... "the LENGTH phrase requires indexed organization (ISO 14.9.41 SR8)");'. The predicate itself is right (Indexed is the only permitted organization), but the STATEMENT IS UNREACHABLE for one of the two organizations it exists to exclude.
RELATIVE LEG VERIFIED (out-b1/probe/sr1-sr8): 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK WITH LENGTH 2' on ORGANIZATION RELATIVE reports COBOLNET0862 SR8.
SEQUENTIAL LEG NOT REACHED: the check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)'. In the SAME probe run, 'START SQF KEY IS = SQ-REC WITH LENGTH 2' on an ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL file produced ZERO diagnostics -- two syntax rules violated at once (SR8 and SR2) and neither reported; the statement becomes a runtime NotImplementedCobolFeatureException instead. I flipped the axis deliberately: probing only the relative case would have shown a green check for a rule half of whose domain is unenforced.
A SECOND UNREACHED PATH: 'if (kp is not null && operand is null) return new BoundUnsupported(...)' precedes the LENGTH check, so a START whose KEY operand fails name resolution also suppresses SR8.
EDITIONS: the WITH LENGTH phrase is absent from the COBOL-85 START format (gated at 2002 by ConstructRegistry 'start-with-length-2002' / COBOLNET0900); Annex E records no 14.9.41 change from 2014, so 2014 and 2023 are certain and the pre-2014 split is not derivable from the 2023 text alone.
TEST: none.

(cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "The open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 shall be input or I-O." -> OK §14.9.41.4 1)). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR5): 'If, at the time of the execution of the START statement, the file position indicator indicates that an optional input file is not present, the invalid key condition exists and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.' The status value comes from 9.1.13.5 3b (cite.py --check 9.1.13.5 OK): 'a START or random READ statement is attempted on a file described as optional and the physical file is not present' => '23'. notes: kb/Work PB352. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR6) delegates to 9.1.14. RELATIVE + INDEXED HALF — VERIFIED against every item of 9.1.14. (a) 9.1.14 item 2 (cite.py --check 9.1.14 OK: 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is specified ... any applicable exception processing statements are not executed, and control is transferred to the imperative-statement specified in the INVALID KEY phrase'): EmitInvalid emits `if (__kstN[0] == '2') { imperative-1 }` — the '2x' family ONLY, so a '47'/'30' START does not misroute into the INVALID KEY branch. (c) 9.1.14 final-rules item 2: EmitInvalid emits the NOT INVALID KEY imperative under `[0] == '0'` only. (d) The grammar admits both phrase orders and either phrase alone (startInvalidKeyPhrase, CobolIO.g4:572), matching the choice indicators recorded in the 14.9.41.2 figure note. notes: kb/Work PB352; PB359. For indexed files, the key of reference is undefined.' FIRST SENTENCE — VERIFIED on the invalid-key paths. Both StartFail bodies set `_fpiValid = false` and `LastReadUnsuccessful = true`, which is observable through 9.1.13.7 6a (cite.py --check 9.1.13.7 OK: 'The preceding START statement referencing that file connector was unsuccessful' => '46'). subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB236. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR8): 'If the KEY phrase is omitted, the START statement behaves as though KEY IS EQUAL TO data-name-1 had been specified, where data-name-1 is the name of the key specified in the RELATIVE KEY clause associated with file-name-1.' MAIN PATH — VERIFIED. BindStart defaults the operator (`string op = kp?.comparisonOperator() is { } oc ? MapOperator(...) : "=="`) and, on the relative arm, defaults the operand (`operand ??= file.RelativeKeyItem is { } rk ? ctx.Refs.ResolveItem(rk) : null`), so an omitted KEY phrase becomes KeyedStartMode.Key with op '==' over the RELATIVE KEY item — exactly the substitution GR8 states, and consistent with GR10. OBSERVED (probe/rel-start/STPRB1 step A): RRN 2/4/6 written; MOVE 4 TO RK; bare `START RELFA` -> NOT INVALID KEY taken, FS='00', READ NEXT returns 'REC-4' (RRN 4), i.e. exactly KEY IS EQUAL TO RK. EDGE THAT DIVERGES (why PARTIAL): a relative file in ACCESS SEQUENTIAL with NO RELATIVE KEY clause — the clause is an independent bracket of the SELECT format 2 entry and 12.4.5.13 imposes no requirement to write it — makes GR8's substitution impossible. BindStart then returns BoundUnsupported('START on <f> with no resolvable RELATIVE KEY item') with NO compile-time diagnostic, and the program COMPILES CLEAN and dies at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException (probe/rel-nokey/STPRB8.cob). The standard gives such a program no meaning, so a rejection is defensible — but a silent compile followed by a run-time crash is the wrong channel; this belongs in a compile-time diagnostic. See finding M3. TEST-REF: none. The only existing case is conformance-test:KeyedIoDifferentialTests.Relative_StartKeyGreaterOrEqual_PositionsThenWalks, which routes through DifferentialGolden.Assert and is pinned to a legacy-oracle-baked .out — a characterization golden, disqualified as a closer.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR9 and GR9 b) / c)). NUMERIC COMPARISON (8.8.4.2.4): EmitStart renders the operand as `(long)(NumericRenderer.Align(num.FieldNum(sta.Operand), 0))` and calls CobolFile.StartRelative(name, op, rrn) — the RRN travels as a typed long, never a character image, so the comparison is numeric by construction. GR10 is honored because 14.9.41.3 SR5 forces data-name-1 to BE the RELATIVE KEY item (BindStart reports COBOLNET0862 otherwise) and the omitted-KEY form defaults to it. GR9 a) FORWARD SEARCH: RelativeConnector.Start walks the SortedDictionary keys ascending for '==' (ContainsKey), '>' and '>=' and breaks on the first hit. GR9 b) REVERSE SEARCH: '<' and '<=' walk the same ascending key order but KEEP the last satisfying key and break on the first non-satisfying one — which is the largest RRN satisfying the relation, i.e. the first record found searching the file in reverse. ConditionBinder.MapOperator maps NOT LESS -> '>=', NOT GREATER -> '<=', GREATER OR EQUAL -> '>=', LESS OR EQUAL -> '<='; '!=' is unreachable here (SR3 rewrite in BindStart), and no other spelling can fall through the switch, so there is no silent no-match arm. OBSERVED, file with RRN 2/4/6: probe/rel-start/STPRB1 — KEY > 4 -> REC-6; KEY < 5 -> REC-4 (the LARGEST RRN below 5, not the lowest, proving the reverse search); KEY NOT GREATER 5 -> REC-4; KEY NOT LESS 5 -> REC-6; KEY = 3 -> '23' + INVALID KEY (GR9 c). probe/rel-ops/STPRBA — EQUAL TO 4 -> REC-4; GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO 5 -> REC-6; LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO 5 -> REC-4; >= 5 -> REC-6; <= 5 -> REC-4; LESS THAN 1 -> '23'; GREATER THAN 9 -> '23'. probe/empty-start/STPRBC — KEY >= 1 on an empty relative file -> '23' (GR9 c). All six legal operators plus both boundary directions verified. EDITIONS: the reverse-search operators are A.3 item 39 processor-dependent elements (cite.py --check A.3 OK: 'the relational operators LESS, NOT GREATER, or LESS OR EQUAL in the START statement are dependent on the capabilities of the processor'); this processor supports them. NO CLOSING TEST: the only existing coverage is the legacy-baked conformance-test:KeyedIoDifferentialTests.Relative_StartKeyGreaterOrEqual_PositionsThenWalks (DifferentialGolden characterization, disqualified). CONFORMS-but-untested. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED on the record's own editions claim. The forward/reverse SEMANTICS are right and I re-derived them independently: RelativeConnector.cs:340-355 walks a SortedDictionary<long,string> (KeyedStoreTable.cs:69), so '>'/'>=' break on the first ascending hit and '<'/'<=' keep the LAST satisfying key, which is the first found searching in reverse (GR9b); ConditionBinder.MapOperator (:798-810) folds NOT LESS -> '>=' and NOT GREATER -> '<=', matching the a)/b) split exactly. I even probed an operand shape the adjudicator never tried -- ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL, which SR1 admits -- and it is correct once the 14.9.51 GR29a sequential-WRITE renumbering to RRN 1/2/3 is accounted for. What does NOT hold is editions '85,2002,2014,2023'. GR9 b)'s operator set (LESS, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL) is not COBOL-85: the standard binds it to the READ PREVIOUS phrase in ONE sentence, A.3 item 39, as a single reverse-access processor-dependent capability, and GR9 is itself split into a) (the 85 set) and b) (the added set). The compiler gates the OTHER half of that same sentence -- READ ... PREVIOUS raises COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 (VersionConformancePass.cs:254, Constructs.ReadPrevious2002) -- and gates every other post-85 element of START (start-first-last-2002, start-with-length-2002, both with constructs.json rows). The reverse START operators are gated NOWHERE: the BoundKeyedStart arm at VersionConformancePass.cs:264-271 tests only Mode and Length, tests/version-matrix/constructs.json has no row for them, and no grammar predicate covers them. So at one of the four editions the record claims, the compiler silently accepts a construct that edition does not define and executes 2002 semantics for it. One arm of the rule verified at four editions, the other at three and ungated at the fourth => PARTIAL. Owed: a start-reverse-operators-2002 construct row + a VersionConformancePass arm on BoundKeyedStart.Op in {'<','<='} + the edition-gate sweep, then a spec-derived golden to close the row.

notes: kb/Work PB357. RULE: "If arithmetic-expression-1 does not evaluate to a positive nonzero integer that is less than or equal to the length of the associated key, the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to '23', the invalid key condition exists, and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful." (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "does not evaluate to a positive nonzero integer that is less than or equal to the length of the associated key" -> OK §14.9.41.4 14)). §14.9.41.3 has NO syntax rule restricting arithmetic-expression-1 to an integer expression, so a non-integer value is legal source whose defined RUNTIME result is '23' — that is precisely why GR14 exists. CODE: the bound is checked in the connector, but on a value the EMITTER has already destroyed: `(int)(Align(expr, 0))` truncates the scale to 0 (Align passes CobolRounding.Truncation) and then narrows to a 32-bit int, so the connector's `compareLength < 1 || compareLength > keyLength` test never sees arithmetic-expression-1's real value. MEASURED (probe start-p2-b + start-p2-j; PIC X(4) prime key holding AB01): in-range legs are correct — LENGTH 0 -> FS=23, LENGTH 5 -> FS=23, LENGTH -1 (from PIC S9(4) VALUE -1) -> FS=23. DEFECTIVE legs: `WITH LENGTH 2.5` -> FS=00 and the START positions at AB01 (expected '23'); `WITH LENGTH WL` where WL is PIC 9V9 VALUE 2.5 -> FS=00; `WITH LENGTH 3 / 2` -> FS=00; `WITH LENGTH BIG` where BIG is PIC 9(12) VALUE 4294967297 -> FS=00, because the (int) narrowing wraps 4294967297 to 1 and 1 is inside the bound — a 4294967297-character partial key silently becomes a 1-character one. See finding "start-with-length-count-is-a-lossy-int-cast". || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2014 / 2023 established from the spec (Annex E lists no START change from 2014); the WITH LENGTH phrase's pre-2014 introduction is not datable from this transcription. IS? dataReference`, no SOURCE alternative), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §A.3 item 40 declares that form "Not claimed". notes: kb/Work PB358. RULE: "The key specified in the KEY phrase, or that shares a leftmost character with the data item specified in the KEY phrase, becomes the key of reference… If the execution of the START statement is successful, this key of reference is used for subsequent sequential READ statements referencing file-name-1." (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "becomes the key of reference" -> OK §14.9.41.4 16)). CODE: RecordLayout.KeyIndexByPosition matches the operand's byte OFFSET against the prime key first, then each alternate, admitting an operand no wider than that key (§14.9.41.3 SR6a and SR6b in one lookup); IndexedConnector.Start assigns `_refKey = keyIndex` only AFTER a record is found, so an unsuccessful START leaves it alone (GR7's 'undefined' is part 1/3's row), and ReadSequential walks `Ordered(_refKey)`. MEASURED — BOTH ARMS AND THE PERSISTENCE (probe start-p2-d; prime X(2), alternate IX-ALT X(4) WITH DUPLICATES SUPPRESS WHEN "ZZZZ"; records 01/DD01, 02/CC02, 03/BB03, 04/ZZZZ): (a) NAMED KEY — `START IXF KEY IS NOT LESS THAN IX-ALT` then four READ NEXTs -> 03/BB03, 02/CC02, 01/DD01, AT END: the ALTERNATE ordering, and the alternate key persisted as the key of reference across every subsequent sequential READ; (b) LEFTMOST-COINCIDENT ARM — `IX-ALT-GEN PIC X(2)` in a sibling 01 record at the alternate key's leftmost position, `START IXF KEY IS EQUAL TO IX-ALT-GEN` with "CC" -> 02/CC02 then 01/DD01, i.e. the ALTERNATE (not the prime) became the key of reference. Independently pinned by conformance:2023/altkey_suppress_when (START KEY >= on the alternate, then a full READ NEXT walk in alternate order) and conformance:2002/file_collating_seq (START KEY >= 'M' under a reversed alphabet, then the walk M,A). notes: kb/Work PB355; PB327. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "The specified key is set up by moving the relevant parts of the record area into a temporary data area" -> OK §14.9.41.4 17) a); --check 14.9.41.4 "The length of this temporary area is considered to be the length specified in the LENGTH clause" -> OK 17) b); --check 14.9.41.4 "any record identified as being suppressed by the SUPPRESS WHEN phrase of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is ignored" -> OK 17) e)). VERIFIED LEGS: c) forward search for =/>/>= and d) REVERSE search for </<= — measured in probe start-p2-d (`START … KEY IS LESS THAN` "CC02" returns 03/BB03, the last record satisfying the comparison in the reverse scan) and pinned by conformance:2002/file_collating_seq; e) the comparison under the FILE's collating sequence with the record's key on the left — pinned by conformance:2002/file_collating_seq (an ALPHABET REV prime key makes the START >= "M" walk M,A); e) SUPPRESS WHEN records ignored under an alternate key of reference — `Ordered(keyIndex)` filters IsSuppressed (which correctly returns false for keyIndex<0), pinned by conformance:2023/altkey_suppress_when and re-measured in probe start-p2-d D1 (the ZZZZ record never appears in the alternate walk); b) the 'else the length of data-name-1' branch — pinned by conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition and measured in probe start-p2-d D2. Also unverified: the national branch of e) (§8.8.4.2.9) is unreachable — a national key is refused COBOLNET0899 (probe start-p2-f), and the record-key-name-1 branch of b) is unwritable (CONFORMANCE §A.3 item 40 Not claimed). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for items a)–e) generally; the LENGTH-clause branch of b) rides on the WITH LENGTH phrase (2014/2023 established, earlier band not datable from this transcription); the SUPPRESS WHEN sentence of e) is 2023-only (Annex E.3.3 item 42, "SUPPRESS WHEN phrase … may be specified as part of the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause").

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR17 e) 1.): 'The file position indicator is set to the value of the key of reference in the first logical record whose key satisfies the comparison'. IMPLEMENTATION: IndexedConnector.Start builds `Ordered(keyIndex)` — records sorted by (key-of-reference value under KeyCompare, then Arrival) with SUPPRESS WHEN records filtered out — then iterates FORWARD for '==','>','>=' and BACKWARD for '<','<=' (GR17 c/d) and stops at the first satisfying record, setting `_fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex)` (the key VALUE, as the rule states) plus `_fpiArrival` (the duplicate-key disambiguator 9.1.8.2 needs to make arrival-order retrieval work; it adds resolution, it does not contradict the rule). GR17 e)'s operand orientation is right: `KeyCompare(part, value, keyIndex)` puts the RECORD'S extracted key on the left, matching 'with the second temporary area on the left hand side' (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK). The suppression sentence is honored by Ordered's `Where(r => !IsSuppressed(r.Image, keyIndex))`, and IsSuppressed returns false for keyIndex < 0 so the prime key is never suppressible. The partial-key truncation uses the WITH LENGTH count when present, else the operand's ImageWidth (EmitStart). OBSERVED (probe/idx-start/STPRB3, keys AAA100/BBB200/CCC300): implicit EQUAL 'BBB200' -> BBB200; '> BBB200' -> CCC300; '< BBB999' -> BBB200 (the LARGEST key below, proving the reverse search); 'NOT GREATER BBB999' -> BBB200; '>= AAA000 WITH LENGTH 3' -> AAA100. probe/idx-dup/STPRBB (alternate key WITH DUPLICATES, MM written by 05, 03, 09 in that arrival order): '>= MM' positions at 05 — the EARLIEST arrival of the duplicate set, and the walk gives 05, 03, 09; '< NN' positions at 09 — the LATEST arrival, i.e. the first satisfying record in reverse order. TESTS: conformance:2002/file_collating_seq pins START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV (expected 'START >= M UNDER REV:' then K=M, K=A, derived from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, not from any oracle); conformance:2023/altkey_suppress_when pins START KEY IS >= LOW-VALUES on a SUPPRESS-WHEN alternate key (expected 01/AA then 03/BB); conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition asserts GOT=01 for START KEY = via a sibling-record operand, reasoned from 12.4.5.12.4 GR4 + 14.9.41.3 SR6b. All three compute their expected values from the standard. EDITIONS: the GR17 e) suppression sentence depends on SUPPRESS WHEN, a COBOL-2023 addition (cite.py --check E.3.3 OK, item 42), and the WITH LENGTH count in GR17 b) is a post-85 phrase; the rule itself is present in every edition. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, on the same defect as GR9 and for the same reason: the record claims edition 85 for a branch COBOL-85 does not have and the compiler does not gate. The BEHAVIOUR survived everything I threw at it. I re-derived the ordering from source rather than from the notes: IndexedConnector.Ordered (:510-513) sorts by (key-of-reference value under KeyCompare, then Arrival) with IsSuppressed filtered out, and Start (:444-481) walks seq[i] for '=='/'>'/'>=' and seq[Count-1-i] for '<'/'<=', which is exactly 9.1.8's reverse order (descending key, reverse arrival); KeyCompare(part, value, keyIndex) puts the RECORD's extracted key on the left, matching GR17 e)'s 'second temporary area on the left hand side'; _fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex) is the key VALUE the rule names. I verified BOTH cited conformance goldens by reading them, not by trusting the note: 2002/file_collating_seq computes START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV -> 'K=M','K=A' from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, and 2023/altkey_suppress_when computes the SUPPRESS-WHEN skip from 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 -- both spec-derived, both genuinely pinning the FPI-setting branch (a mis-set FPI changes the printed walk). I then probed the edges neither test reaches. Nothing broke. What breaks is editions '85,2002,2014,2023': the record's own notes claim the BACKWARD arm for COBOL-85 ('iterates FORWARD for ==,>,>= and BACKWARD for <,<= ... < BBB999 -> BBB200, proving the reverse search'), and that operator set is A.3 item 39's other half of READ PREVIOUS, which the compiler does gate at 2002. On an indexed file the leak is starker than on a relative one: in ONE probe file the COLLATING SEQUENCE clause (2002) and SUPPRESS WHEN (2023) each correctly raise COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 while 'START IXF KEY IS LESS THAN R-KEY' beside them raises nothing. The gate exists for every neighbouring post-85 feature of this exact statement and not for this one. Forward arm verified at four editions and closed by two spec-derived tests; reverse arm verified at three editions and ungated at the fourth => PARTIAL.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB356. RULE: "If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the value of the primary key of the first existing logical record in the physical file AND THE KEY OF REFERENCE IS SET TO THE PRIMARY KEY. If no records exist in the file, the I-O status value … is set to '23' …" (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "the key of reference is set to the primary key" -> OK §14.9.41.4 18)). CODE: StartFirstLast never touches `_refKey` and orders the file by `Ordered(_refKey)` — the key of reference LEFT OVER from the previous START/random READ (IndexedConnector.cs L310 and L473 are the two sites that set it; only OpenCore L121 resets it to -1). So both halves of the rule are wrong whenever the key of reference is not already the prime key: the FPI is set to the ALTERNATE-key-first record, and the key of reference stays the alternate for every subsequent sequential READ. MEASURED (probe start-p2-a; prime X(2) / alternate X(2) WITH DUPLICATES, records 01/CC, 02/BB, 03/AA — deliberately opposite orders): `START IXF KEY IS EQUAL TO IX-ALT` (establishes the alternate) then `START IXF FIRST` then READ NEXT -> "AFTER-FIRST PRIME=03 ALT=AA". SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: the first record in the physical file under the PRIMARY key is 01, so the READ must deliver PRIME=01. The empty-file half IS correct: probe start-p2-i I4 gives INVALID KEY + FS=23. No spec-derived test exists (EditionGateDiagnosticTests L161-L180 pins only the COBOLNET0900 gate). See finding "start-first-last-indexed-does-not-reset-key-of-reference". || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2014 / 2023 established from the spec (Annex E lists no START change from 2014). The FIRST phrase is absent from COBOL-85's START and this transcription does not date its introduction. The defect is edition-invariant — one runtime method, no version predicate.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB356. RULE: "If LAST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the value of the primary key of the last existing logical record in the physical file and the key of reference is set to the primary key. If no records exist in the file, the I-O status value … is set to '23' …" (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "the key of reference is set to the primary key" -> OK §14.9.41.4 18); GR19 repeats the clause verbatim for LAST — read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §14.9.41.4 19)). Same mechanism as GR18: `Ordered(_refKey)` + `seq[^1]` with no reset of `_refKey`. MEASURED (probe start-p2-a, records 01/CC, 02/BB, 03/AA): `START IXF KEY IS EQUAL TO IX-ALT` then `START IXF LAST` then READ NEXT -> "AFTER-LAST PRIME=01 ALT=CC". SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: the LAST record in the physical file under the PRIMARY key is 03, so PRIME=03. A second consequence of ordering by an alternate: under an alternate carrying SUPPRESS WHEN, `Ordered` drops the suppressed records, so START LAST can land on a record that is not the physical last even by the alternate's own reckoning — GR18/GR19 name the PRIMARY key precisely because suppression does not apply to it. The empty-file half IS correct: probe start-p2-i I5 -> INVALID KEY, FS=23. No spec-derived covering test. See finding "start-first-last-indexed-does-not-reset-key-of-reference". || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2014 / 2023 established from the spec (Annex E lists no START change from 2014); the LAST phrase's pre-2014 introduction is not datable from this transcription. Edition-invariant defect.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352; PB353. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR20): 'If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to 1 if records exist in the physical file. If no records exist in the file, or the physical file does not support the ability to position at the first record, the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to 23, the invalid key condition exists, and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.' The construct is unambiguously legal: 14.9.41.3 SR2 (cite.py --check OK) says 'If the organization of the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequential, either the FIRST or the LAST phrase shall be specified'; 9.1.8.2 (cite.py --check OK) says 'The START statement may be used to position the file at the beginning or the end for subsequent retrievals'; and 9.1.13.5 3d (cite.py --check OK) reserves '23' for 'a START statement is attempted on a sequential file that has no records or that does not support the ability to position at the specified record'. NO IMPLEMENTATION EXISTS. I searched the tree myself rather than trusting the dossier: SequentialConnector.cs has no Start / StartFirstLast member of any kind (the only 'Start' identifiers are _lastReadBlockStart / _lastLineStart); FileRegistry.StartFirstLast's switch has arms only for RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector and throws MisroutedVerb for anything else; and KeyedIoBinder.BindStart short-circuits on `if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported("START on sequential-organization file ... (ISO 14.9.41 SR2 FIRST/LAST positioning - a later slice)")` — FileModel.IsSequential covering both SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL. OBSERVED (probe/seq-start/STPRB2.cob): the program COMPILES WITH NO DIAGNOSTIC and aborts at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException on the first START. Expected from GR20: records exist, so the FIRST form sets the file position indicator to 1, status '00', and the next sequential READ makes record 1 ('AAA-1') available. See finding M1 (and M2 for the edition-gate hole this same early return opens). EDITIONS: no Annex E entry, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; it depends on the FIRST/LAST phrases, which are absent from the COBOL-85 START format (the 2023 text alone cannot date them — this is the one edition claim here not derived purely from the transcription).

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352; PB353. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR21): 'If LAST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the record number of the last existing logical record in the physical file. If no records exist in the file, or the physical file does not support the ability to position at the last record, the I-O status value ... is set to 23, the invalid key condition exists, and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.' Same absence as GR20 and the same single site: KeyedIoBinder.BindStart rejects every sequential-organization START before the FIRST/LAST discrimination is ever reached, SequentialConnector implements no positioning entry point, and FileRegistry.StartFirstLast has no sequential arm. OBSERVED (probe/seq-start/STPRB2.cob): `START SQF LAST` compiles clean and the run unit dies on the preceding `START SQF FIRST` with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException — neither form ever executes. Expected from GR21 for that program (three records AAA-1, BBB-2, CCC-3): the file position indicator is set to record number 3, status '00', and the next sequential READ makes 'CCC-3' available. Note that GR21 also requires the '23' + invalid-key answer when the physical file cannot position at the last record — a sequential host stream is exactly the case the rule anticipates, so an implementation that cannot seek backwards is still obliged to answer '23' rather than abort. See findings M1 and M2. EDITIONS: as GR20.

subject: SUBTRACT statement

notes: RULE (two halves): 'Any record locks associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 are released by the execution of the UNLOCK statement. The presence or absence of any record locks does not affect the success of the execution of the UNLOCK statement.' - cite.py --check 14.9.47.4 (first sentence) -> OK §14.9.47.4 1). CODE: FileRegistry.Unlock calls `PhysicalFileTable.ReleaseAllForConnector(st, name)` - keyed on the CONNECTOR name, which is exactly 'associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1' - then unconditionally `c.SetStatus(FileStatusCode.Success)`, so held locks and no locks give the same 00. (a) release: conformance:2002/file_sharing has A lock record 1 (READA=00), B blocked (READB=51), then `UNLOCK F-A` and B reads 00 (AFTER=00); file_sharing_seq shows the converse - B's UNLOCK does not disturb A's own lock (UNLB=00 then REWA=00/REWB51=51). (b) presence-or-absence: p1.cob UNLOCKs an OPEN sequential file that never held a lock -> 00, and p6.cob UNLOCKs twice in a row (AUTO-UNLA=00 then AUTO-UNLA2=00 with nothing left to release). (c) ALL LOCK MODES, not just MANUAL: p6.cob uses `LOCK MODE IS AUTOMATIC` on two RELATIVE connectors - the auto-lock taken by A's READ blocks B (AUTO-READB=51) and is released by `UNLOCK F-A` (AUTO-READB2=00), matching Table A.1's UNLOCK row, cite.py --check D.2.4.3.2 '| UNLOCK | Automatic -single - multiple Manual - single - multiple | | for all lock modes: - on all locked records |' -> OK (informative corroboration; GR1 is the normative source). NOT DOWNGRADED by the unregistered-connector path of findings [unregistered-keyed-connector]/[unlock-registry-entry-is-the-one-silent-fall-through]: a connector that was never registered was never opened, so it holds no record locks and GR1 is vacuous there - the observable failure on that path is the I-O status, which is why GR2 and GR3 carry it and this row does not.

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB361. The rule has three halves. (a) 'shall immediately follow a section header' and (c) 'shall appear in a sentence by itself' ARE enforced: DeclCollectSection requires the declarative section's FIRST sentence to hold exactly one statement and that statement to be a useStatement, else COBOLNET0897 'the first sentence shall consist of a single USE statement (ISO 14.2.4 / 14.9.49 SR1)'. Probe pair.cob (`USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON F1 DISPLAY "X".`) -> COBOLNET0897, correct. (b) 'in the declaratives portion of the procedure division' is NOT enforced. `useStatement` is a plain alternative of CobolParserCore.g4#statement, so a USE sentence parses anywhere in the procedure division; nothing in the nondeclarative bind path recognises it, so it falls through StatementBinder.BindStatementCore's `_ => new BoundUnsupported(...)` arm. Probe outside.cob (a USE in nondeclarative paragraph M2) compiles clean with ZERO diagnostics and runs to completion; probe second.cob (a SECOND USE inside a declarative PARAGRAPH, after the section's legal first-sentence USE) likewise compiles and runs clean. Probe reach.cob (the same statement made reachable) does not diagnose either -- it dies at run time with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented was reached at run time: statement 'USEAFTERSTANDARDERRORPROCEDUREONF1'`, which misattributes illegal source to a missing feature. 4.2.2 requires the compile-time warning mechanism to indicate violations of the explicit syntax rules. (d) 'The remainder of the section shall consist of zero, one, or more procedural paragraphs' is satisfied: leading sentences written after the USE become an anonymous paragraph, which is exactly the 14.2.1 Format 1 declaratives shape `use-statement. [ sentence ] ... [ paragraph-name-1. [ sentence ] ... ] ...` read with 14.4.3. SCOPE LIMIT, not counted here: a DECLARATIVES portion inside a METHOD procedure division is rejected loud by StatementBinder.BindMethodRoster with DiagnosticCatalog.OoMethodDeclaratives ('DECLARATIVES inside a method are recognized but not yet implemented', anchored ISO 14.2.1) -- a declared staged loud whose primary owner is 14.2.1 Format 3, outside this clause. No test asserts COBOLNET0897 anywhere in tests/, so this row is untested even for its implemented halves.

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB364. `_declScopedFiles` (an OrdinalIgnoreCase HashSet<string>, so the 8.3.2.2 case-insensitive word rule holds) is added to per file-name of a Format-1 USE; a repeat raises COBOLNET0897 "file 'F1' already has a USE procedure in this source element (ISO 14.9.49 SR8)". Probe SR8DUP.cob (two declarative sections both `... PROCEDURE ON F1.`) -> COBOLNET0897 on the second, correct. Scope: the set is per-unit on ProcedureTableBuilder and, as for SR7, per-unit coincides with per-procedure-division here; the nest.cob contained-program probe confirms no leak across divisions. Correctly NOT extended to Format 3's file-name-2 -- SR8 speaks only of the USE AFTER EXCEPTION (Format 1) statement, and DeclBindUseF3 keeps its own SR14 pair set instead. CONFORMS-but-untested. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, downward. The rule's own prohibition is implemented correctly and I verified the half the record could NOT have verified with the probe it cited -- but the check is enforced past the rule's boundary and rejects legal source. (1) THE SCOPE HALF, re-derived: the record rests 'no leak across divisions' on nest.cob, and nest.cob names the outer file F1 and the inner file G1, so a shared _declScopedFiles could never have collided there -- the probe is incapable of detecting the defect it was cited for. I built the probe that can: RU8NEST gives the outer program and its CONTAINED program each an FD named F1 and a `USE ... ON F1.`, and RU8TWOP does the same for two NON-nested top-level programs; both compile clean, so the scope really is per procedure division. That half survives. (2) THE DEFECT: `_declScopedFiles.Add(fname)` sits INSIDE the per-operand loop of a single USE statement (ProcedureTableBuilder.cs:461-479), so a Format-1 USE that names the same file twice in ONE statement is rejected -- RU8SAME `USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON F1 F1.` draws COBOLNET0897 "file 'F1' already has a USE procedure in this source element (ISO 14.9.49 SR8)", and RU8SAME3 shows it also aborts the rest of the operand list. SR8 forbids the name appearing 'in more than one USE AFTER EXCEPTION STATEMENT'; one statement is not more than one statement. The Format-1 figure (14.9.49.2) writes `{ file-name-1 } ...` with an ellipsis and nothing restricts the repetition, and no general rule is made ambiguous by it -- GR6a associates the one procedure with the file whether the name is written once or twice. This is a hard error on source the standard permits, at ALL FOUR editions (R85SR8S, R02SR8S, R14SR8S and the 2023 default all reproduce it). CONFORMS is therefore not available: the rule is right where it speaks and wrong where it does not, which is PARTIAL. (3) SWEEP -- the same mechanism, one method away: DeclBindUseF3's AddPair is likewise called per FILE operand inside a single statement (:514-543), so RU14SAME `USE AFTER EC EC-I-O-AT-END FILE F1 FILE F1.` draws COBOLNET0716 whose own text -- 'is already specified in ANOTHER USE statement of this procedure division' -- is falsified by the program, which contains exactly one. SR14 is already DIVERGES, so the fix for both sites is one change: the duplicate set must be seeded per STATEMENT, not per operand.

subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB364. The rule's own scope IS handled correctly and was probed: SR14DUP.cob (`USE AFTER EC EC-I-O-AT-END FILE F1.` in two declarative sections) -> COBOLNET0716 citing SR14, correct; nest_ec.cob (an outer and a CONTAINED program each with the same entry) compiles clean, so 'within the same procedure division' is scoped right. THE DIVERGENCE is that the rule is applied OUTSIDE its scope. SR14 governs 'the same pair of exception-name-2 and file-name-2', and per the 14.9.49.2 Format 3 figure exception-name-2 exists ONLY in the `exception-name-2 { FILE file-name-2 } ...` alternative -- 14.9.49.4 GR3c-g confirms the split, saying 'file-name-2 is specified and exception-name-2 ...' for GR3c/d and 'file-name-2 is not specified and exception-name-1 ...' for GR3e/f/g. A bare repeated exception-name-1 is therefore NOT a pair and NOT prohibited; 14.9.49.4 GR3 defines its outcome instead ('A declarative is selected ... in the order in which they are specified. The first declarative that satisfies the selection criteria is executed and no other declaratives are executed'). DeclBindUseF3 nevertheless calls the same AddPair for the bare entry with a null file and keys DeclEcPairs on `ec + "|" + ""`, so a repeated bare name collides. Probe SR14BARE.cob (`USE AFTER EC EC-SIZE.` in two declarative sections) -> error COBOLNET0716, rejecting legal source. This is not a latent path: the existing green test ExceptionConditionConformanceTests.UseF3_DuplicatePairAcrossSections_Diagnosed asserts COBOLNET0716 for exactly that program shape -- two BARE `USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-USER-D.` declaratives with no FILE anywhere -- so a passing spec-derived-looking test currently pins the over-rejection. notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the predefined object reference EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the exception object" -> OK, GR 15). On BOTH paths that can enter a Format-4 declarative the register is set before the selector runs: EmitRaiseObject emits `ExceptionState.SetObject(<the RAISE operand>)` and then `__EcObjDispatch(ExceptionState.ExceptionObject)`; EmitPropagationPickup emits `SetObject(__po)` and then the selector. The covering case tests/conformance/2002/oo_ec_raise_object.cob enters the selected declarative and executes `SET U TO EXCEPTION-OBJECT` / `IF U NOT = NULL`, and the committed golden requires `BASE-HANDLER EXCEPTION-OBJECT` + `REGISTER-SET` - so the register is proven non-null and carrying the raised object on entry. Note the register is a run-unit-scoped single slot (ExceptionState.ExceptionObject) and a NAMED raise inside the declarative nulls it (Set sets ExceptionObject = null); that is 14.9.29.4 GR1's rule, and GR15 constrains only the state on ENTRY, which holds. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Two independent defects in the record. (1) THE TEST-REF DOES NOT PIN THE RULE. GR15 says EXCEPTION-OBJECT 'references the exception object' -- an IDENTITY claim (ISO 8.8.4.2.15: the relation is true 'if the object referenced by identifier-3 is the same object that is referenced by identifier-4'). The cited conformance:2002/oo_ec_raise_object asserts only 'IF U NOT = NULL DISPLAY "REGISTER-SET"'; its golden line 'REGISTER-SET' is satisfied by ANY non-null object, so a regression that set the register to the wrong object -- SELF, a fresh instance, the activating program -- keeps that golden green. The row is NOT closed by it and the test-ref must be emptied; the missing assertion is one line (IF U = E). I measured the identity claim myself and it HOLDS on every entry path, so the program-level half of the rule is genuinely correct -- this is a coverage correction, not a behaviour finding. (2) A HALF THAT CANNOT BE ENTERED AT ALL. 'the associated declarative' is a declarative in a procedure division, and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 permits the DECLARATIVES-bearing Format 1 (14.2.1) in a METHOD DEFINITION; StatementBinder.cs:239-242 rejects every declarative part inside a method with COBOLNET0899 'recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)' at both 2002 and 2023, so a Format-4 USE in a method -- the natural home for EC-OO handling -- is legal source the compiler refuses. Unlocated/unreachable half + verified half => PARTIAL. (Contributing, already owned by the record for GR14: the interface-name-1 arm of the associated declarative is rejected COBOLNET0859, so even in a program only the object-class arm of GR14 can ever deliver an entry for GR15 to constrain -- I confirmed that rejection. It does not by itself move GR15, because the register is written BEFORE the selector runs and is therefore arm-independent.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 4). No Annex E entry touches it.
