subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A minus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted upward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '2)'. The MIRROR of rule 1, and I read both halves separately rather than inferring them from rule 1's arm. (1) PRODUCE-THE-CHARACTER. CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 363 'char osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' writes '-' for a negative argument-4/argument-3, with the MAGNITUDE taken through Math.Abs at line 361 so the offset-hours/offset-minutes subfields carry the unsigned value the subformat wants. The negative value survives the emitter intact: IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFormattedTime / #RenderFormattedDatetime pass the offset through ArgInt -> AsInt -> RuntimeApi.IntegerArg, a raising (not wrapping) narrowing to long, not through any absolute-value or unsigned carrier. Verified by golden: conformance:2023/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'OFF-MIN=010000-2359' for FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm" 3600 -1439) -- the format's placeholder is '+' and the DATA carries '-', which is precisely the shape §15.3.3.6.1 describes. (2) HONOUR-THE-MEANING (adjust UPWARD). EmitFormatted line 328 'secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m' with a NEGATIVE offset ADDS, then lines 329-330 roll the day. Verified by golden: conformance:2023/r25_utc_roll_date_range case 3, FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ" 3067670 86399 -1439) -> '99991231T235859Z' -- local 9999-12-30 23:59:59 adjusted UPWARD by 23h59m to 9999-12-31 23:58:59 UTC. This is the direction NOTE 1 of rule 3 illustrates ('0514278124-0500' == '1014278124Z'), and CobolDate.cs#FormattedCurrentDate reproduces exactly that shape for a west-of-UTC system clock (offMin = -300 -> osign '-', oh 05, om 00, with now.TimeOfDay giving the LOCAL common time). (3) CONSUME-THE-CHARACTER. Analyze lines 513-515 accept '-' through the same single expression that accepts '+' ('if (c is not ('+' or '-')) { ... }' -- both signs take the identical no-op branch), and no downstream use is required: §15.79.4 and the §15.48.4 r1 NOTE (both --check OK, see GR-15.3.3.6.1-1) confine the returned values to the common-time / date subfields. HONEST RESIDUE: no golden feeds a '-' sign into a CONSUMING function (pb23 exercises the shared branch with '+' only); that half rests on implementation reading, of a single expression in which '+' and '-' are literally the same arm, so the two-arm-dispatch scar does not apply. Editions rationale identical to GR-15.3.3.6.1-1. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS, but TWO load-bearing claims in the note above are WRONG and the record is changed. (1) TEST-REF CORRECTED: conformance:2023/r25_utc_roll_date_range is REMOVED for the same reason as on GR-15.3.3.6.1-1 -- its format 'YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ' is a §15.3.3.5 UTC format with no offset subformat, so it emits no sign character and cannot be evidence about what a '-' in offset-subformat data MEANS. That leaves pb11's OFF-MIN=010000-2359 as the only test, and it closes only the WRITE-THE-CHARACTER half; unlike rule 1, NO golden anywhere pairs a minus-sign rendering with its UTC equivalent, so the meaning half here rests on reading alone. (2) THE NOTE'S CLAIM THAT THE NEGATIVE VALUE REACHES THE RENDERER 'not through any absolute-value or unsigned carrier' IS FALSE. Math.Abs is applied to it TWICE: CobolDate.cs EmitFormatted line 361 ('long offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes)') and CobolDate.cs OffsetOutOfRange line 446 ('if (!hasOffset || Math.Abs(offsetMinutes) <= 1439) return false'). The second one is unguarded at long.MinValue, where Math.Abs throws OverflowException, and CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg (CobolIntrinsics.cs line 139) ADMITS long.MinValue (v >= long.MinValue is inclusive), so FORMATTED-TIME('hhmmss+hhmm', 3600, W) with W = -9223372036854775808 faults a raw CLR exception out of the intrinsic where §15.3 permits only EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and the default -- the same escaping-CLR-fault shape kb/Work PB23 and R25 each closed once. IT DOES NOT CHANGE THIS VERDICT: I traced the order and the guard runs BEFORE EmitFormatted (FormattedTime line 404-407, FormattedDatetime line 458-462), and when hasOffset is false the renderer passes the literal 0 (IntrinsicRenderer RenderFormattedTime/RenderFormattedDatetime), so line 361 is unreachable with that value and no offset-subformat DATA is at stake. The defect belongs to §15.41.3 r4 / §15.40.3 r5 (rows AR-15.41.3-4, AR-15.40.3-5), not to §15.3.3.6.1, and attributing it here would be the wrong-clause error. (3) THE 'SAME offsetMinutes DRIVES BOTH' ARGUMENT IS WEAKER THAN STATED and I re-derived it rather than inheriting it: EmitFormatted line 328 runs only when isUtc, and the osign write at line 363/382 runs only when an OffSign segment exists, which a 'Z' format never has -- the two branches are DISJOINT and never co-execute, so they share an input convention, not a mechanism. The convention itself is what §15.41.3 r4 fixes ('an integer representation of offset from UTC expressed in minutes', re-checked), and r25 cases 3 and 4 pin it in BOTH directions on the UTC branch; combined with the single expression 'offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' that is a sound two-step reading, which is why the verdict survives. (4) THE CONSUME ARM WAS RE-READ CHARACTER BY CHARACTER, not inferred: in Analyze line 514 the test is 'if (c is not ('+' or '-'))', so both signs take the SAME skipped body and then the same pos++/continue -- there is no second arm to get wrong. I also measured the corpus: grepping every .cob under tests/conformance for an offset format shows NOTHING anywhere feeds a '-' or a '0' sign, or an extended '+hh:mm' subformat, into INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE / SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME / TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME (pb23 uses '+hhmm' with '+0500' only), so the row stays test-needed on the consume half.

subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically, all four normative sentences separately: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A zero to indicate that offset from UTC was not available on the system on which the information was recorded' -> OK (marker '3)'); 'If the data contains a zero in that character position, the offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of the data shall both contain zero' -> OK; 'If the values contained in offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of data in a receiving field associated with an offset subformat are both zero, the position corresponding to the plus sign in the format shall contain a plus sign' -> OK; 'The colon character in the offset subformat of an extended offset time format appears in the data associated with the format' -> OK. This is a COMPOUND rule with FOUR normative obligations plus three informative NOTEs; I located and read the implementation of every one. (a) '0' IS A PERMITTED SIGN VALUE. CobolDate.cs#Analyze lines 510-516: 'if (s.Field == Fld.OffSign) { ... char c = data[pos]; if (c is not ('+' or '-')) { if (c == '0') offZero = true; else return pos + 1; } pos++; continue; }' -- exactly the three values rules 1-3 enumerate are admitted and every other character yields the 1-based error position §15.92.4 requires. (b) A '0' SIGN FORCES BOTH SUBFIELDS TO ZERO. Analyze line 531: 'if (offZero && s.Field is Fld.OffHour or Fld.OffMinute) hi = 0;' collapses the §15.3.3.6.2 ranges (0..23 hours, 0..59 minutes) to the single value 0 for both, and the offZero flag is set before either is read because §15.3.3.6.1 puts the sign first in the subformat. Traced the per-digit narrowing at lines 543-548 by hand: sign '0' with hours '05' errors at the SECOND hours digit (the leading '0' is still consistent with the only legal '00'), which is the earliest character at which the error is determinable -- the §15.92.4 contract, not an off-by-one. (c) THE RECEIVING-FIELD REQUIREMENT ('+' when both subfields are zero). CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 363 'osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' can never produce '0' at all, and yields '+' at offsetMinutes == 0; lines 361-362 make oh/om zero only when offsetMinutes is exactly 0 (|offset| in 1..59 gives om != 0, >= 60 gives oh != 0), so the '-'-with-+0000 counterexample is unreachable. Verified by golden: conformance:2023/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'OMIT-OFF=010000+0000' for FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm" 3600) with argument-3 omitted (§15.41.3 r6 evaluates it as 0) -- literally NOTE 3's '+0000'. (d) THE COLON OF AN EXTENDED OFFSET SUBFORMAT APPEARS IN THE DATA. CobolDate.cs#Tokenize line 277 emits Seg(IsField:false, Sep:':', InData:true); EmitFormatted line 369 'if (!s.IsField) { if (s.InData) sb.Append(s.Sep); continue; }' writes it, and Analyze lines 504-508 REQUIRE it in the data ('if (pos >= data.Length || data[pos] != s.Sep) return pos + 1'). Verified by golden: pb11 'T-OFF=01:00:00+01:00'. The bind-time recognizer agrees on the subformat's two shapes -- DateTimeFormatGrammar.cs#ZoneOfWidth lines 119-122 accept the five-character '+hhmm' and six-character '+hh:mm' and require the offset's width to MATCH the common part's, so a basic/extended chimera never reaches the runtime. Also confirmed the FORMAT always carries '+' as the placeholder and never a '-': Tokenize's '-' arm (line 276) does not set afterOffSign, so a hyphen is only ever the extended-date separator -- the format/data asymmetry these three rules describe is modelled correctly rather than collapsed. HONEST RESIDUE (why this row stays test-needed even at CONFORMS): obligations (a) and (b) -- the SENDING-field permission to write '0' with zero magnitude, and its rejection when the magnitude is non-zero -- are verified by implementation reading ONLY. No golden in tests/conformance/ feeds a '0' into an offset sign position; pb23 exercises the consuming path with '+' ('19950215T05142781+0500', the D.31.5.8/D.31.5.9 examples) and pb11 pins the producing path, so the cited tests close (c) and (d) but not (a)/(b). A closing golden would be TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("hhmmss+hhmm", "01000000000") = 0 with the non-zero-magnitude mate asserting the error position. NOTE 2's cross-reference to CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED is informative and lands outside this clause: CobolDate.cs#Format21 renders §15.21.3's separate 21-character layout, whose position 17 is '0' only when the system lacks the local-time-differential facility -- .NET's DateTimeOffset always has one, so '+'/'-' is always correct there. Editions rationale identical to GR-15.3.3.6.1-1. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS after an independent re-derivation and a hand-trace of every branch; the record is changed to record what the note over-claimed and what residue remains. (1) ALL FOUR CITATIONS RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY and all return OK on §15.3.3.6.1 marker '3)'. Reading the clause whole shows FIVE normative sentences, not four: the note folds the SENDING-field permission ('For offset-time values used as sending fields, the position ... may contain a zero provided that ...' -- --check OK) into obligation (a) rather than naming it. It is nonetheless implemented by the same Analyze line 514 arm, so the omission is a labelling one. (2) OBLIGATION (b) HAND-TRACED, NOT ACCEPTED: with sign '0' Analyze line 531 forces hi = 0 while lo stays 0 for both Fld.OffHour (0,23) and Fld.OffMinute (0,59), and the per-digit narrowing at 543-548 then admits '00' and rejects everything else at the earliest determinable character -- I walked '01000000000' (accepted, returns 0), '0'+hours '01' (error at the SECOND hours digit, data position 9) and '0'+minutes '10' (error at the FIRST minute digit, position 10), all of which match §15.92.4's 'first position at which the error can be determined'. The hi=0 override is correctly scoped to OffHour/OffMinute and does NOT touch Fld.Minute, which shares the same (0,59) tuple -- the obvious way to get this wrong, checked. (3) THE FORMAT/DATA ASYMMETRY VERIFIED AT BOTH STAGES: DateTimeFormatGrammar.ZoneOfWidth lines 115-123 requires the offset subformat's width to match the common part's, and I confirmed by hand that both chimeras are rejected ('hhmmss+hh:mm' fails IsCommonTime at the extended width, 'hhmmssZ+hhmm' fails at both), and that FormatKindsAdmittedBy covers ALL SEVEN format-taking functions (IntrinsicBinder lines 382-392), so no function reaches CobolDate.Tokenize unscreened. (4) RESIDUE THE NOTE DID NOT DECLARE: obligation (d)'s CONSUMING side is also untested -- no fixture in tests/conformance feeds an extended '+hh:mm' offset into any analyzing function, so only the EMIT side of the colon rule is pinned (pb11 T-OFF); it rides the same 'if (data[pos] != s.Sep) return pos + 1' arm that the common-time colon exercises in conformance:2014/formatted_datetime, which is why the verdict holds on reading. (5) The code-location names Analyze, which houses only three of the five sentences -- the receiving-field '+' and the colon's emit half live in EmitFormatted/Tokenize; the single-path field forces the choice and Analyze is the right majority, but the row's code is genuinely three symbols in one file. (6) NOTE 2's CROSS-REFERENCE CHECKED RATHER THAN WAVED OFF: §15.21.3 position 17 does admit '0', CobolDate.Format21 line 35 never writes it, and that is correct because .NET always supplies the differential; but the SAME expression writes Math.Abs(t.Offset.Hours) into positions 18-19, and .NET admits offsets to +14:00 while §15.21.3 caps the '+' case at 'the range 00 through 13' -- an out-of-subject divergence on RV-15.21.3-1, recorded here only because this clause's NOTE 2 is what points at it.

subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: NOTE 1 item 2 - an EAE's result is implementor-defined if one or more of the ARGUMENTS are implementor-defined. Citation: cite.py --check 15.4.1 'One or more of the arguments are implementor-defined' -> OK (§15.4.1 rule 2; the near-identical L2.2 a) is disambiguated by its lettered marker, so this row is anchored on the NUMBERED item). This is a latitude/composition statement, not a behaviour requirement: nothing has to be enforced, and the only way to contradict it would be to over-define a result whose argument is implementor-defined. WHAT I READ. IntrinsicRenderer.Arg/RawArg/DecArg is the ONE argument intake for the numeric channel (every arm consumes Arg(...) or its raw/Dec twin - the class comment and the PB32/PB14 remarks on Landed make that the deliberate single seam), and it renders an argument through NumericRenderer.AsNum WITHOUT redefining its value, so an argument whose value is implementor-defined (a nested FUNCTION RANDOM - §15.75.3 r4 seed, §15.75.4 r3 domain subset; FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT - §15.80.3 r3 implementor-specified precision; FUNCTION FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE - §15.38.4 r2 accuracy) propagates its implementor-defined value into the enclosing EAE unchanged, and the compiler makes no claim to the contrary anywhere. The class of implementor-defined argument the compiler DOES take a documented position on is the floating-point carrier: docs/CONFORMANCE.md item 92 row 2 states 'when ANY argument renders as floating-point (COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-SHORT/FLOAT-LONG/FLOAT-EXTENDED), the function's equivalent arithmetic expression is evaluated in IEEE binary64', and IntrinsicRenderer.RenderNum's AnyRealArgument dispatch plus the RealMethod convention implement it. TEST-REF DELIBERATELY EMPTY - the row stays test-needed. conformance:2023/pb2_float_argument_exact_family is spec-derived and pins the float-ARGUMENT determination, but a COMP-2 item's VALUE is not implementor-defined (only its representation is), so it is corroboration, not a cover. A closing test would put a genuinely implementor-defined value in an argument position - e.g. FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT) or FUNCTION MAX(FUNCTION RANDOM(1), 0) - and assert the enclosing function's result tracks the documented determination for that argument. EDITIONS: batch default; no edition delta in the item's text. || REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. TWO INDEPENDENT COSTS, both admitted inside the record itself. (1) ZERO INSTANCES OF THE RULE WERE ACTUALLY TRACED. The record names the rule's real instances (a nested RANDOM, SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT, FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE) and then verifies NONE of them; the single class it does verify - the floating-point carrier - it disqualifies in its own words ('a COMP-2 item's VALUE is not implementor-defined ... it is corroboration, not a cover'). A CONFORMS whose only positive evidence is conceded not to be an instance of the rule is an unverified edge under rule 5, and with an empty test-ref there is nothing else holding it up. (2) THE SINGLE-SEAM PREMISE IS FALSE, AND THE FILE SAYS SO. 'IntrinsicRenderer.Arg/RawArg/DecArg is the ONE argument intake for the numeric channel' is contradicted by the same file, which carries at least five argument intakes with DIFFERENT value semantics: Arg (IntrinsicRenderer.cs:457), RawArg (:511) / DecArg (:515) / DecOf (:522), Dbl (:712) / DblOf (:525) for the binary64 lane, IntArg -> AsInt (:716, :734) which RESCALES TO 0 WITH TRUNCATION for the integer positions, and RawArgPairs (:771) for the selection family - plus Str/StrArgList for the string channel. The record read one of them. Worse, `Arg` itself is `Landed(num.AsNum(...))`, and NumericRenderer.Landed (NumericRenderer.cs:647-654) is NOT the value-preserving pass-through the note describes: for an SDIDI-carried argument it emits `DecToUnscaledIntermediate(x.Expr, ws, CobolRounding.Truncation)` at `ws = rcv.WorkingScale(NumvalScaleFloor)` (ReceiverContext.cs:61 - the floor is 6). The renderer's own PB56 remark records the consequence in the same file: 'a fixed working scale truncated sub-microscale operands to zero'. So the note's load-bearing sentence - 'it renders an argument ... WITHOUT redefining its value' - is refuted at the exact line it cites. I did NOT find an over-definition of an implementor-defined argument's value (I traced FUNCTION INTEGER-PART(FUNCTION SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT), which keeps the §15.80.3 r3 scale-7 tick carrier through Landed's identity arm for exact Int128, and FUNCTION MAX over a mixed RANDOM/fixed list, which routes to the PB65 SDIDI selection arm), which is why this is PARTIAL and not DIVERGES. Verdict PARTIAL, code-location and empty test-ref kept: the row stays test-needed, and the closing test the record itself sketches is still the right one.

subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: NOTE 1 item 3 - an EAE's result is implementor-defined if one or more of the arithmetic expressions that COMPOSE it produces implementor-defined results (--check 15.4.1 'produces implementor-defined results' -> OK at Sec.15.4.1 rule 3; the standard-mode twin at rule 2 b) reads 'produce', the singular/plural verb being the only textual difference, and both were checked so this row does not rest on the sibling's number). The composing expression this compiler meets is exponentiation with a non-integer exponent, which Sec.8.8.1.5.4 r2 e) makes implementor-defined. TWO HALVES ARE OWED AND BOTH ARE NOW MET. HALF ONE - the function arm and the `**` arm converge on ONE result: IntrinsicRenderer's standard-mode arm renders FUNCTION EXP as DecPow(DecE, DecArg(ic,0), IntermediateMode) and FUNCTION EXP10 as DecPow(DecFrom('10','0'), ...), while NumericRenderer.Power emits DecPow(DecOperand(b), DecOperand(e), IntermediateMode) under the same predicate - the same runtime entry, the same operand conversion, the same rounding mode. That half was upheld when this row was REFUTED to PARTIAL. HALF TWO - THE REFUTATION'S HALF, AND IT IS WHAT CHANGED. The refutation read: 'CobolDec.cs#Pow, non-integer-exponent branch (line 139): return FromDouble(Math.Pow(b.ToDouble(), e.ToDouble())) - both operands leave SDIDI form for binary64 before the development begins, and the development is IEEE binary64 (~17 significant digits, base 2), not the decimal128 operations Sec.8.8.1.5.3 names. So the composing expression's implementor-defined result is developed OUTSIDE the latitude this row's CONFORMS rests on.' That line no longer exists. Owner decision D-C (2026-08-30; kb/Work PB167) replaced it with ONE development carried entirely on CobolDec Add/Sub/Mul/Div - operands never leave SDIDI form and every add/sub/mul/div is a Sec.8.8.1.5.3 decimal operation - and CobolDecPowDevelopmentTests fails if any binary64 transcendental is spelled in the file. The wave that landed D-C also carried two defects of its own into this arm, both fixed before this row was re-verdicted: kb/Work PB266 (r3's reciprocal was spelled in two arms of four, so a negative non-integer exponent did not evaluate the expression r3 mandates) and kb/Work PB267 (the past-loop-bound escape rebuilt the exponent from a CLAMPED long, so an exponent past 2**63-1 was silently replaced). PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31. CLOSING TEST, and it answers the refutation's own objection ('No leg asserts FUNCTION EXP10(0.5) = 10 ** 0.5'): conformance:2023/pb167_sdidi_exponentiation now carries that leg directly, beside EXP10(0.5) = FUNCTION SQRT(10) and 10 ** 0.5 = FUNCTION SQRT(10) - so the function, the spelled-out EAE and the value Sec.15.84.4 r2 fixes exactly are pinned as one value rather than pairwise. conformance:2023/exp_standard_decimal_eae keeps the same-for-all-instances legs (P09/P17, rebaselined by D-C from the binary64 ...950 to the spec-exact ...933). BOUNDARY KEPT: the STANDARD-DEVIATION defect on RV-15.4.1-L2.1/-L2.2 is NOT an instance of this item - Sec.15.86.4 r1 composes its EAE from FUNCTION SQRT, whose standard-decimal value Sec.15.84.4 r2 specifies exactly, so no composing expression there produces an implementor-defined result. subject: Intrinsic functions
notes: TWO STATEMENTS IN ONE ROW, and both were verified (that is why this is not the PARTIAL the two-halves rule would otherwise force). Citations: --check 15.4.1 'The result is explicitly implementor-defined' -> OK (§15.4.1 rule 4); the trailing lead-in sentence checks into the same clause via --check 15.4.1 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression' (its sub-item, rule 1). HALF A - NOTE 1 item 4. The numeric/integer functions whose returned value the standard makes EXPLICITLY implementor-defined are each determined AND documented here: RANDOM's unseeded seed (§15.75.3 r4) and its distinct-sequence domain subset (§15.75.4 r3) -> CONFORMANCE.md items 144/145, measured by unit:RandomSeedSubsetTests.Seeds_0_Through_65535_YieldPairwiseDistinctSequences; SECONDS-PAST-MIDNIGHT's precision (§15.80.3 r3) -> item 171 (100 ns, scale 7, the IntrinsicRenderer 'SecondsPastMidnight' arm returns the tick count at scale 7) and its >= 86400 question (§15.80.3 r4) -> item 112; FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE's time accuracy (§15.38.4 r2) -> item 87; SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC's native usage restriction (§15.83.3 r4) -> the COBOLNET1516 refusal in IntrinsicBinder; E and PI under native (§15.27.3 r1 / §15.73.3 r1) -> the float lane. notes: THE LOAD-BEARING RULE OF THIS CLAUSE: under standard-decimal/standard-binary with an EAE specified, 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression' (--check 15.4.1 -> OK, §15.4.1 rule 1; NOTE 2 turns it into the testable relation function-identifier = EAE). VERDICT PARTIAL - most of the family is right and ONE EAE-bearing function measurably is not. WHAT IS IMPLEMENTED (read, not sampled). IntrinsicRenderer.RenderDec is the SDIDI lane: the four dividing financial/statistical functions and the NUMVAL family route there for EVERY argument shape (`alwaysDec`), the summing/selection family too, and everything else routes there as soon as a raw argument is Dec or float (AnyDecOrRealRaw). Its bodies are CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs, and each is its clause's EAE step for step - ModDec = a - b*FloorDec(a/b) (§15.64.4 r1), RemDec with TruncDec (§15.77.4 r1), MeanDec = SumDec/n (§15.60.4 r1), MidrangeDec = (max+min)/2 (§15.62.4 r1), RangeDec = max-min (§15.76.4 r1), VarianceDec = sum((x-mean)^2)/n (§15.98.4 r1), AnnuityDec = rate/(1-(1+rate)**-n) (§15.9.4), PresentValueDec = sum(a_k/(1+rate)**k) (§15.74.4 r1) - all on CobolDec with the §11.9.11 intermediate rounding threaded through as `mode`. RenderNum's own standard-mode arm holds the four constant/power rows the R18 work landed (E and PI as the exact 34-digit CobolDec.E/CobolDec.Pi of §15.27.3 r3 / §15.73.3 r3, EXP and EXP10 through the SAME CobolDec.Pow the `**` operator uses), so those EAEs agree with their spelled-out forms by construction. An all-fixed-point list for the non-dividing functions stays on the exact Int128 lane, whose steps are digit-identical on that domain (COBOLNET_NUMERIC_DESIGN.md D3; pinned by unit:CobolIntrinsicsDecTests.VariadicFamily_DecAgreesWithExact_OnFixedPointDomain). ⛔ WHAT IS NOT. FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION's EAE is '(FUNCTION SQRT (FUNCTION VARIANCE (argument-list)))' (--check 15.86.4 -> OK, rule 1), and under standard-decimal the value of FUNCTION SQRT is fixed by §15.84.4 rule 2: 'the returned value is the absolute value of the exact square root of argument-1 rounded to 34 digits according to the rules for standard-decimal arithmetic' (--check 15.84.4 -> OK). COBOL.NET has NO decimal square root: CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#StdDevDec is `CobolDec.FromDouble(Math.Sqrt(VarianceDec(mode, xs).ToDouble()))`, and FUNCTION SQRT itself is an IntrinsicCatalog Float row with no RenderDec arm, so under standard-decimal RenderNum falls to RenderFloat, whose standard-mode tail is `DecFromDouble(RealResult(call))` over CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt = Math.Sqrt. Binary64 carries ~17 significant digits where the rule requires 34, and a 31-digit receiver can see the difference: VARIANCE(1,2,3) = 2/3, whose root to 34 digits is 0.8164965809277260327324280249019..., while the shipped path yields the binary64 0.816496580927726 and zeros beyond it. The compiler's SQRT and its STANDARD-DEVIATION agree with EACH OTHER (both take the same binary64 route), so NOTE 2's relation condition is TRUE while the VALUE the rule names is still not delivered - which is why sampling could not find this and reading did. The existing goldens do not catch it because both STANDARD-DEVIATION legs choose a zero variance: pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics uses STANDARD-DEVIATION(2 2 2) = sqrt(0) = 0 and unit:CobolIntrinsicsDecTests.StdDevDec_ConstantList_IsZero the same shape. ROOT CAUSE ROW IS ELSEWHERE - RV-15.84.4-2 (not in this part; §15.84 is outside the 15.4.1 clause map) - and there is no kb/Work note for it (`grep -rn '15\.84\.4|34 digits' kb/Work/*.md` returns nothing), so it is a live gap, not a landed fix I am re-reporting. SECOND, SMALLER RESIDUE, unverified rather than refuted: FACTORIAL and the other non-dividing EAEs stay on the exact Int128 carrier under a standard mode, which keeps MORE than the SDIDI's 34 significant digits (33! is 37 digits), so above 34 digits the returned value and the SDIDI-evaluated EAE need not agree; I did not construct a program that observes it. THE STANDARD-BINARY HALF of the precondition is unreachable by design (DataBinder.BindDeclarations -> COBOLNET0806) and that is legitimate under Annex A.3 item 2 + Annex F.2, recorded in CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 2 - it is NOT part of the reason for this PARTIAL. EDITIONS 2014,2023: the rule AS WORDED names standard-decimal and standard-binary, both COBOL-2014 introductions (the 2002 predecessor is ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, which this compiler routes to the same SDIDI engine via NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal); same derivation as the adjudicated AR-15.43.3-2/-3 and RV-15.73.3-2 rows. || REFUTER - VERDICT UPHELD AT PARTIAL, and independently re-derived, but the record UNDERSTATES the gap and I am recording the additional evidence so the row is not later closed on the STANDARD-DEVIATION fix alone. Re-derivation: §15.86.4 r1's EAE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33414-33418) and §15.84.4 r2 (:33322) are verbatim as quoted; CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs:184-185 is `CobolDec.FromDouble(Math.Sqrt(VarianceDec(mode, xs).ToDouble()))`; CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:28 is `Sqrt(double x) => Math.Sqrt(x)`; RenderDec (IntrinsicRenderer.cs:649-685) has no Sqrt arm. Confirmed. ⛔ ADDITION 1 - THE 'SMALLER RESIDUE' HAS A WRONG-ANSWER HALF THE RECORD DID NOT REACH. FACTORIAL carries an EAE (§15.36.4 r1 c, --check 15.36.4 OK) and its argument rule admits every non-negative integer (§15.36.3 r1). CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#Factorial is `if (n is < 0 or > 33) return Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError(...)`, so under STANDARD-DECIMAL `FUNCTION FACTORIAL(34)` returns the §15.3 default 0 while the SDIDI value of its EAE is 2.952327990396041408476186096435E+38 - comfortably inside decimal128's ±6144 exponent range (§8.8.1.5.2 NOTE 2). MOD and REM were NOT moved: `alwaysDec` (:643-645) lists Annuity, PresentValue, Variance, StandardDeviation, the NUMVAL family, Sum, Range, Mean, Median, Midrange - not ModScaled/RemScaled. With an ALL-FIXED-POINT argument list AnyDecOrRealRaw is false, RenderDec returns null, and `FUNCTION MOD(A, B)` with A PIC 9(31) and B PIC 9V9(18) takes the switch arm at :164-171, which aligns both to scale 18 on Int128 - 49 digits, past the carrier - and raises through Align's RescaleEscape, where §15.4.1 r1 requires the §15.64.4 r1 EAE's SDIDI value. Re-derivation: the closing sentence is at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29811 exactly as quoted; §15.84.4 r2 at :33322; the clause-15 heading scan confirms the §15.97/§15.98 and §15.85/§15.86 numbering nit is CORRECT (UPPER-CASE is §15.97 at :33918, VARIANCE §15.98 at :33961, STANDARD-COMPARE §15.85 at :33332, STANDARD-DEVIATION §15.86 at :33390). ⛔ CORRECTION 1 - THE ENUMERATION OF THE EXCEPTION'S MEMBERS IS UNSOUND, AND IT MISSED A LIVE ONE. 'return d.Year * 1000L + d.DayOfYear;' places the Gregorian year in the YYYY positions and the ORDINAL day of that year in DDD — the §15.5.4 Julian date form ('The Julian date form is YYYYDDD, where YYYY represents the year and DDD represents the ordinal date within that year'). YYYY half: 1 -> 1601001 (epoch year), 3067671 -> 9999365 (terminal year), 143951 -> 1995046. DDD half, over the 62-value spec-computed sweep described in RV-15.24.4-1: the leap-day ordinal is counted (2000-02-29 -> 2000060) and 366-day years reach 366 (2000-12-31 -> 2000366), while the century non-leap years do not (1900-12-31 -> 1900365, 1700-03-01 -> 1700060 vs 2000-03-01 -> 2000061), so §15.5.1's Gregorian leap rule is honoured in the DDD positions and not merely in YYYY. Identical at --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023. Coverage note (not a test-need for this row): the cited test's only DAY-OF-INTEGER expectation is 01601001, whose DDD is 001 — no on-disk spec-derived case reaches a leap-day or a three-digit ordinal, which is why the DDD half was checked by running rather than by trusting the suite.

subject: DISPLAY-OF function
notes: UPHELD after varying the RECEIVER as well as the argument. Repertoire appends exactly one character per input character (a substitution replaces, never expands or drops), so the returned string's length is always argument-1's character count, and under D-N1 one national position is one UTF-16 char and one usage-display position. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(PIC N(5))) -> 005; the same over a PIC N(3) containing a SUBSTITUTED U+4E16 -> 003, so substitution does not change the length; the ZERO-LENGTH national literal FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N"") -> LENGTH 000 and an all-space receiver, which is correct since 15.26.3 carries no zero-length-literal prohibition (its 15.66.3 r3 twin does); a SUPPLEMENTARY-plane national literal in a PIC N(2) -> LENGTH 002 and '??', consistent with the declared D-N1 one-code-unit-per-position model; a reference-modified argument N-SRC(1:3) -> 3; a national GROUP of two PIC N(2) items -> 4. Receiver variation: STRING FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-SRC) DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO a PIC X(10) prefilled with '-' gives [HELLO-----], i.e. exactly 5 positions transferred; MOVE to a PIC X(6) gives 'HELLO '; and the length consequence in comparison is right in both directions - the result compares EQUAL to "HELLO", to "HELLO   " and to a PIC X(8) item, so the shorter operand is space-padded per 8.8.4.2.7 r2 rather than compared as a raw .NET string. There is no static width model for an intrinsic result in the compiler, so the length is purely the runtime string's and FUNCTION LENGTH reads that. conformance:2002/national_intrinsics verified on disk with its golden (LEN-D=05) and its tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json entry; the LEN-D line is computed from 15.26.4 r4, not pinned from behaviour. NOTED, and deliberately not charged here: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W)) crashes at run time with a NotImplementedCobolFeatureException naming 'ISO 15.14.3' - that is a 15.14 argument-shape gap for whoever adjudicates BYTE-LENGTH, not a 15.26.4 r4 defect.

subject: E function
notes: Verdict SURVIVES; the note is corrected and the SPEC BASIS the adjudicator missed is supplied. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 2). THE PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER, re-verified by me on the built CLI: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode with COBOLNET0806 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL' - a HARD error at --std 2002 (alongside COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), 2014 and 2023, and NOT downgradable by --permissive (2023 adds the COBOLNET0903 obsolescence warning and still errors). Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and it is F.2 ITEM 3 - not Annex E - that records the non-implementation: '3. STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' (cite.py --check F.2 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' -> OK). CITATION REPAIRED 2026-08-31, and the error was worse than a wrong annex letter: the sentence as previously quoted here ('it has not been implemented ... by any COBOL provider', singular) is F.2 ITEM 5's, which is about the VALIDATE FACILITY - a real clause answering a different question (feedback_a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question). Item 3 also carries the reevaluation note that makes the decline REVISITABLE: 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

subject: FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CONFIRMED NOT-IMPLEMENTED, independently re-verified. Citation re-validated: §15.40.3 r5 returns whole, including 'If argument-4 is specified, the magnitude of the value shall be less than or equal to 1439.' I re-ran the search rather than trusting the prior pass: `grep -rn 1439 src/ --include=*.cs | grep -v Generated/` returns NOTHING — not in the binder, not in the renderer, not in the runtime. Argument-4 flows `IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFormattedDatetime` -> `ArgInt(ic.Args[3])` -> `CobolDate.EmitFormatted`, which only ever computes `offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes); oh = (int)(offMag / 60); om = (int)(offMag % 60)`. Consequences, both silent: 2000 minutes renders offset-hours 33, violating §15.3.3.6.2 ('The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive'); 9999 minutes renders 166, so `oh.ToString("00")` emits three characters and the returned value grows past the width the format describes. §15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist for an out-of-range argument even though the VALUE is implementor-defined; it is never set. Because argument-4 may be an identifier or an expression this cannot be a compile-time check in general, but it is a one-line runtime guard beside the existing integer-date guard in `CobolDate.FormattedDatetime`. NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than DIVERGES because there is no implementation to diverge from. The identical rule text is §15.41.3 r4 for FORMATTED-TIME and is equally unimplemented (same sweep). TEST: none.

Re-read `BindIntrinsicCore`: its only FORMATTED-DATETIME-specific arm is the COBOLNET1517 literal check, and nothing correlates the argument COUNT with the SHAPE of the format literal. `EmitFormatted` does compute both predicates the rule needs — `isUtc` (a 'Z' segment) and the OffSign/OffHour/OffMinute fields — but at RUN time and only to drive emission, never to reject. `FUNCTION FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmss", 153569, 45296, 120)` compiles with zero diagnostics, prints 20210616T123456 and discards argument-4 (`hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset` is false and there is no offset field to render into). subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, and the EDITION WINDOW WAS WRONG. (1) EDITIONS. Both concepts this rule names arrive at COBOL-2014, not 2002: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.5) and the §3.166 standard binary floating-point usages ('usages float-binary-32, float-binary-64, and float-binary-128' — checked mechanically), i.e. USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-32/64/128 (§13.18.60.4 GR14–GR16). Neither exists at COBOL-2002, so the rule as worded cannot be evaluated at 2002. The adjudicator wrote 2002,2014,2023 on all six rows without deriving any of them. (2) VERDICT. By the stated rule 'code not located ⇒ NOT-IMPLEMENTED': the adjudicator's own finding is that NOTHING in BindAlgebraicFold reads ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic (the only arithmetic-mode test in IntrinsicBinder is the ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION staging arm), so there is no code for this rule and citing BindAlgebraicFold as its code-location is citing the code of a DIFFERENT rule. Today's incidental coverage comes entirely from the blanket `pic.IsFloat` ban that AR-15.43.3-1 finds DIVERGENT — a rule enforced only by a bug is not implemented. (3) ⛔ NEW — THE ONE PLACE THE CODE CITES RULE 2, IT MIS-STATES IT. The COBOLNET1516 message asserts '…under STANDARD-DECIMAL it is barred by rule 2' while the guard fires for COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-SHORT/FLOAT-LONG/FLOAT-EXTENDED — none of which is a standard binary floating-point usage under §3.166. That is a false statement of the rule shipped in a user-visible diagnostic, and it is precisely the inherited-citation failure mode. Confirmed live-and-writable: OptionsBinder#ArithmeticOf maps STANDARD-DECIMAL to ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal (only STANDARD-BINARY is rejected, at DataBinder COBOLNET0806), and FLOAT-BINARY-32/64 are LIVE usages (PicInfo#ClrType → float/double). FLOAT-BINARY-128 is out of reach (COBOLNET1564, Annex A.3 item 17). No spec-derived test.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, same two grounds as rule 2. (1) EDITIONS: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.4) and the §3.167 standard decimal floating-point usages (float-decimal-16, float-decimal-34 — USAGE per §13.18.60.4 GR17/GR18) are both COBOL-2014 additions; the rule as worded does not exist at COBOL-2002. (2) VERDICT: no code implements this rule anywhere — the prohibited combination is doubly unreachable through two INDEPENDENT non-supports that have nothing to do with §15.43, so nothing has ever evaluated the rule's condition. Both non-supports are conformance-legal and I re-derived them rather than inheriting them: DataBinder rejects STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806, and Annex A.3 item 2 reads 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (NOTE 1 adds that the mode is obsolete); FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/34 are rejected at ParseUsage with COBOLNET1564 under A.3 item 19. Worth recording for whoever revisits this: A.3 item 3 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL processor-dependent TOO, so COBOL.NET's support for it is a choice, not an obligation — which is why rule 2's combination is writable and rule 3's is not. Vacuous truth is not implementation: if either half is ever supported, nothing enforces this. No spec-derived test, and none constructible. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-binary arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014', IntroducedIn 2014, ObsoleteIn 2023), so this rule cannot apply at 2002 - confirmed empirically, the sibling STANDARD-DECIMAL clause is rejected at --std 2002 with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'. The rule's precondition can never hold: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind time with COBOLNET0806 (DataBinder.BindDeclarations), re-verified on the built CLI as a HARD error at both --std 2014 and --std 2023 and NOT downgradable by --permissive. No code computes the exact binary128 value 16312081666030376401667486162748272 / 2**112, and none can while the mode is refused. The non-support is already recorded in CONFORMANCE.md SS2 row 2 ('ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1)') and licensed by ISO Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' BARE QUESTION: should SS15.73.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by that existing Annex A.3 item-2 non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? TEST-REF STRUCK on review: the previously cited StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported exercises the MODE rejection and never references PI or any returned value, so it does not cover this rule - test-needed (a test pinning that FUNCTION PI under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover). || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

notes: DOWNGRADED FROM CONFORMS. The reversal ITSELF is exactly right - CobolIntrinsics.Reverse is a position-j <- position-(n-j+1) code-unit reversal with no length change, fed the operand's FULL fixed-width image, and re-verified live at every shape tried: X(6) VALUE "AB" -> [    BA  ] into X(8) (n = the declared width, not the trimmed value); ref-mod W-S(2:3) -> [  B     ]; A(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; N(5) -> [EDCBA   ]; numeric-edited ZZ9 VALUE 42 -> [24      ] (the EDITED image is reversed, correct); alphanumeric-edited XXBXX "AB CD" -> [DC BA   ]; an image-capable group -> [EDCBA   ]. Surrogates need no special handling - 8.5.1.4 item 2 and its closing paragraph ('Each two-octet code element of UTF-16 is treated in COBOL as though it were itself a character', cite-checked) make code-unit reversal the spec-mandated behaviour. BUT THREE LEGAL argument-1 SHAPES PRODUCE NO RETURNED VALUE AT ALL - each compiles clean at 85 and 2023 and then throws CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at RUN time, where 15.78.4 r1 requires a character string of length n: (1) an alphanumeric GROUP item containing a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - `01 G2. 05 G2-A PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC". 05 G2-N PIC S9(4) COMP-5 VALUE 5.` then `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(G2) TO W-X.` -> 'whole-group image of G2 with a float/COMP-5/INDEX leaf - the Tier-C byte island'; the argument is legal because 8.5.2.1 makes an alphanumeric group item class AND category alphanumeric, which 15.78.3 r1 admits. (2) a FIGURATIVE CONSTANT - `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(SPACE) TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundFigurative' (IntrinsicRenderer.StrArgVisitor.Visit(BoundFigurative) is a Loud arm); legal because 8.4.3.2.3 SR8 admits a literal, 8.3.3.6.4 GR1 makes SPACE an alphanumeric character value and GR3b fixes its length at one character position - exactly satisfying 15.78.3 r1. (3) `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE(ALL "AB") TO W-X.` -> 'intrinsic string argument BoundAllLiteral' (the sibling Loud arm); 8.3.3.6.4 GR3c gives it the length of literal-1. subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: A combined WEEK-date-and-time format whose argument-2 is VALID per §15.3.1.7 aborts the run unit with an unhandled .NET exception instead of returning a value. `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYWwwDThhmmss", "9999W527T235959") TO WS-F.` at --std 2014 → 'Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException … at System.Globalization.ISOWeek.ToDateTime … at CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Analyze'. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.

subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.84.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be zero or positive"` -> OK §15.84.3 2). THIS IS A VALUE CONSTRAINT, SO THE DISPOSITION THE STANDARD ASKS FOR IS A RUN-TIME EC, NOT A COMPILE-TIME REJECT — §15.3 closing paragraph, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29561: 'The rules for a function may place constraints on the permissible values for arguments... If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference.' So no COBOLNET diagnostic is owed even for the literal FUNCTION SQRT(-4). READ: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt (line 28) is `Math.Sqrt(x)`, which is NaN for every x < 0, and the NaN is screened on ALL THREE arms IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat can emit — I checked each rather than the one: (a) the fixed-receiver arm quantizes through CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble, whose first line is `if (double.IsNaN(d)) return Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError(...)`; (b) the float-receiver / receiver-less arm (line 431) returns CobolIntrinsics.cs#RealResult(call), which is `double.IsNaN(d) ? ArgumentError(...) : d`; (c) the standard-decimal arm (line 441) wraps the SAME RealResult before CobolDec.FromDouble, so the conversion never sees a NaN either. Arm (b)/(c)'s screen exists precisely because PB13 moved the raise site out from under the unquantized render and a refuter caught it. ExceptionState.cs#ArgumentError (line 248) carries BOTH dispositions the standard names: with ArgumentFunctionChecking set it does Set("EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION", fatal: true) and throws CobolFatalException (§14.6.13.1, Table 13 Fatal); with checking clear it returns 0, the §15.3 implementor-defined default. NO SPURIOUS RAISE AT THE BOUNDARY: -0.0 satisfies 'zero or positive' and Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, not NaN, so the screen does not fire on it. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb13_domain_raise_receiver_shape line 38 asserts SQRT-NEG=DEFAULT for FUNCTION SQRT(-1) written as a RECEIVER-LESS relation operand — the exact arm that had no screen before PB13 — and its header derives the disposition from §15.3/§15.4. WHAT NO TEST COVERS, verified by reading only: the checking-ENABLED throw for SQRT specifically (no fixture turns EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking on over SQRT — ExceptionState.cs#ArgumentError is the single raise site for the whole family, so this is one branch of one method, not an unaudited path), and the with-receiver COMPUTE arm for SQRT (pb13 pins that arm for ACOS, which shares FromDouble byte-for-byte). REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-derived independently, not inherited: `cite.py --check 15.84.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be zero or positive"` -> OK §15.84.3 2); the §15.3 disposition paragraph the adjudicator leans on also re-derives (`--check 15.3 "the implementor defines the result of the function reference"` -> OK §15.3 item 14), and §14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3 (read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21334ff, "An exception condition is set to exist only if checking for that condition is enabled") confirms that NOT recording the condition with checking off is correct. So the disposition MODEL is right. WHAT IS NOT RIGHT IS THE DETECTOR, and it is invisible to every arm the adjudicator checked because he checked the RENDER arms and not the ARGUMENT CHANNEL. THE CONSTRAINT IS TESTED ON A NARROWED VALUE, NOT ON argument-1. There is no domain guard on the SQRT body at all: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:28 is a bare `Math.Sqrt(x)` and the whole family's detection is the NaN artifact. That is sound only while the double the body receives has the same SIGN as argument-1 — and it does not. IntrinsicRenderer.Dbl -> NumericRenderer.Real (NumericRenderer.cs:697) converts an SDIDI operand as `(expr).ToDouble()`, and CobolDec.cs:310 is `(double)Sig * Math.Pow(10, Exp)`. For Exp <= -324 `Math.Pow(10, Exp)` underflows to +0.0, so a NEGATIVE SDIDI becomes -0.0 (verified at the IEEE level: (-1.0)*pow(10,-400) = -0.0, signbit -1), and Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 — NOT NaN. Nothing downstream can recover it: RealResult and FromDouble screen `double.IsNaN` ONLY. CONCRETE, LEGAL SOURCE: under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL with `01 A PIC S9V9(30) VALUE -0.000000000000000000000000000001` (= -1E-30, 31 digit positions, legal per §13.18.40.3 SR14), `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SQRT(A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A)` hands the function the exact SDIDI -1E-330 — comfortably inside decimal128's exponent range, so CobolDec carries it — whose value is NEGATIVE and therefore violates §15.84.3 r2. The compiler returns 0 and sets NOTHING: no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION with checking off (where §15.3's implementor-defined result would at least be defensible), and NO RAISE EVEN WITH CHECKING ON, which §14.6.13.1.1 requires. The rule's ordinary half (a plainly negative argument) IS enforced; its underflow half is not — two halves, one verified, so PARTIAL per rule 5. THE SIBLING IN THE SAME FILE IS THE PROOF THIS IS A MISS AND NOT A DESIGN: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:32-33 give LOG and LOG10 an EXPLICIT `x <= 0` guard that names §15.55.3 r2 / §15.56.3 r2 at the BODY, precisely so the domain verdict does not ride on a NaN artifact. SQRT's rule has the same shape and got no guard — and its own in-code comment misnames the clause it is honouring ("argument ≥ 0 (rule 1)"; r1 is the CLASS rule, r2 is the value rule). The fix is a body guard `x < 0 -> ArgumentError("§15.84.3 r2")` beside LOG's, which also closes the -0.0 case by construction. TEST-REF UNCHANGED BUT IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE ROW: pb13_domain_raise_receiver_shape line 38 is `IF FUNCTION SQRT(-1) = 0` — the checking-OFF receiver-less arm only. Nothing anywhere turns EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking on over SQRT (the adjudicator concedes this), and nothing exercises a standard-decimal argument at all. test-needed.

One decision settles E, PI and SQRT together. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH ITS OWN SIBLING: the standard-DECIMAL rule §15.84.4 r2 is NOT discharged by any such licence — that mode is supported and its rule is DIVERGES (see RV-15.84.4-2), so answering this question does not close §15.84.4. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.84.4 "the returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1"` -> OK §15.84.4 4). The rule leaves 'the approximation' undefined, and §15.4.1 supplies the latitude for native mode, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29777: 'When native arithmetic is in effect, the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor.' READ: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt line 28 is `Math.Sqrt(x)`; IEC 60559 requires sqrt to be correctly rounded, so this is the best binary64 approximation available, not merely a plausible one. ALL THREE RENDER ARMS CHECKED at IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat rather than the one: (a) a float receiver or a receiver-less context (line 431) returns CobolIntrinsics.cs#RealResult(call) UNQUANTIZED, so FUNCTION SQRT(2) and a COMP-2 item holding that value are the same number — the §15.4 receiver-independence PB13 restored; (b) a fixed-point receiver (line 452) quantizes through CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble at ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale (>=9, capped at the receiver's Int128 headroom so the PB5/PB13 9.2e9 saturation cannot reach a declarable receiver), rounding rather than truncating at the quantization point — an approximation landed at the receiver's own scale, which is what §15.4.1 leaves to the implementor; (c) SQRT's catalog row carries Codomain.None, and that is CORRECT rather than an omission — §15.84.4 states no bound on the returned value, so the FromDoubleBounded clamp (which exists for RANDOM's open [0,1) and ASIN/ACOS/ATAN's irrational pi bounds) must not apply here. THE 'ABSOLUTE VALUE' HALF IS VACUOUS BUT I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMED IT: §15.84.3 r2 confines argument-1 to zero-or-positive, and Math.Sqrt(x) >= 0 for every x >= 0 (Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, which is zero, not negative), so no sign correction is owed and none is missing; a negative argument is an AR-15.84.3-2 violation that takes the NaN -> EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION path instead of yielding a value at all, so it never reaches this rule. GOLDENS: conformance:2002/float_intrinsic pins SQRT=1.4142135623730951 into a COMP-2 — the correctly-rounded double of sqrt(2), whose exact value is 1.41421356237309504880… — proving the unquantized arm keeps full binary64; conformance:2023/pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage pins the quantized arm, SQRT(4)=2.00 and SQRT(NI)=2.00 into PIC 9(6)V99. EDITIONS: SQRT and its native returned-value rule are unchanged across the four editions; batch default, not read off IntrinsicCatalog's IntroducedIn. REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-derived: `cite.py --check 15.84.4 "the returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1"` -> OK §15.84.4 4), and §15.4.1's native latitude re-derives too (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29777). The APPROXIMATION half is CONFORMING and I re-verified it independently — CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:28 `Math.Sqrt(x)` is IEC 60559 correctly-rounded, and all four RenderFloat exits are accounted for (line 431 RealResult unquantized for a float/receiver-less context; line 441 the standard-decimal DecFromDouble; the Codomain arm which SQRT's Codomain.None correctly skips; line 452 FromDouble at ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale, whose cap I re-derived at ReceiverContext.cs#WorkingScale as min(max(Scale,9), 38-IntegerDigits) and which cannot fall below a legal picture's own scale). THE ABSOLUTE-VALUE HALF WAS DECLARED VACUOUS AND IS NOT, AND IT WAS DECLARED VACUOUS BY THE ONE ARGUMENT THAT FAILS. The adjudicator wrote 'Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, which is zero, not negative, so no sign correction is owed and none is missing'. The rule does not say 'made non-negative when negative'; it says the returned value IS THE ABSOLUTE VALUE of the approximation, and IEEE abs clears the sign bit: |-0.0| = +0.0 while sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 (verified: signbit -1 vs +1). IEC 60559 mandates sqrt(-0) = -0 exactly SO THAT sqrt is not the absolute value there — -0.0 is the unique input on which §15.84.4 r4's 'absolute value' phrase does work, and it is the input the code gets wrong. -0.0 is a LEGAL argument-1: §15.84.3 r2 admits zero, and a COMP-1/COMP-2 item reaches -0.0 by ordinary native underflow (e.g. a product of a negative and a positive tiny float). READ, AND THE READING IS THE FINDING: `grep Abs src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs` returns NOTHING — there is no Math.Abs anywhere on the SQRT path, in the body or in any of the four render arms, so the rule's second half is not implemented, merely unreachable-by-argument. OBSERVABILITY WAS NEVER MEASURED, WHICH IS ITSELF THE PARTIAL: the receiver-less/float arm keeps the value unquantized and the text channel renders it through CobolFloat.cs:25 `Display(double v) => v.ToString(InvariantCulture)`, which on .NET Core 3.0+ is IEEE-faithful and therefore renders a negative zero with its sign — so `DISPLAY FUNCTION SQRT(<a COMP-2 holding -0.0>)` is the candidate wrong output, and a COMP-2 receiver stores the signed zero bit-for-bit. I did not RUN it (read-only), so I report the unverified edge at its honest cost rather than claiming DIVERGES. TEST-REF WEAKENED, NOT STRUCK: conformance:2002/float_intrinsic is a D16-REVIEW golden — its header says 'D16 review', it derives no §15.84.4 clause, and it pins one positive argument — so under rule 3 it is evidence about the binary64 pipeline, not a spec-derived close of r4; pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage likewise derives §15.14.3/§15.50.3 and merely happens to contain SQRT. Both retained as the partial evidence they are. The closing test is one pinning SQRT over a negative-zero float operand. test-needed.
