subject: SUM function
notes:
Citation re-derived mechanically: `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1 (Argument rule). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Verified row `["SUM"] = Uniform('n', "§15.88.3 r1")` (line 693, in the 'statistical trio' block beside STANDARD-DEVIATION and VARIANCE); IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#Uniform builds an ArgSchema with EMPTY positional kinds and a TAIL rule, so `schema.At(i)` yields the 'n' rule for EVERY argument position — which is what §15.88.2's repeated `{ argument-1 }` needs, since every written argument IS argument-1. Enforcement: IntrinsicBinder.cs#CheckArgumentClasses (line 1652) is called on the generic path at line 587, AFTER arity and BEFORE every per-function arm; it loops all positions and calls IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation. For kind 'n', Violation reads CandidateClasses(op) and Admissible('n') = [CobolClass.Numeric] — so a numeric-EDITED item (Table 2 class alphanumeric, mapped to CobolClass.NumericEditedDeEditing) is rejected too, which the arm's comment derives from §8.8.1.1 ("an identifier referencing a NUMERIC DATA ITEM"). VERIFIED EDGES: (a) a GROUP argument — ClassOfPlace returns Alphanumeric for `Item.IsGroup` (National/Boolean for an as-if-pic group), so `FUNCTION SUM(grp)` is rejected; (b) an INDEX item — the usage-keyed arm returns CobolClass.Index before the category table, so it cannot pass as numeric; (c) a table(ALL) argument — TableAllPlace is a `PlaceDecorator(Element)` (Place.cs:158), so `p.Item` is the ELEMENT and the element's class is screened, i.e. `SUM(alphaTable(ALL))` is rejected, not failed open; (d) the figurative ZERO is admissible here by §8.3.3.6.4 GR4 (CandidateClasses gives it Numeric among four), correct behavior per the batch's rule 8. FAIL-OPEN residue, deliberate and documented at the Violation head: an operand whose class is not statically decidable (candidates empty) is not screened — that can only miss a rejection, never invent one. TESTS: tests/conformance/negative/pb58-sum-alpha.cob (`COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(N9 X3)`, header cites "ISO 15.88.3 r1", reject-at 2002 2014 2023, expected diagnostic COBOLNET1627 in the .err, registered in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json:192) and the positive twin tests/conformance/2023/pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob line 75 (`FUNCTION SUM(N9 I2 3.5)` — registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:124). Nothing missing for this rule.

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): citation re-derived independently — `cite.py --check 15.88.3 "Argument-1 shall be of class numeric"` => OK, §15.88.3 rule 1; spec text re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33501-33504. Attacked on four axes and each held. (1) TWO-ARM DISPATCH (the shape that has recurred five times in this repo): both `functionCall` alternatives that can spell SUM — the FUNCTION-keyword arm (IntrinsicBinder.cs:89) and the reserved-word keyword-omitted arm `SUM(…)` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:78, CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn) — converge on the SAME BindIntrinsicCore (line 438), whose generic path calls CheckArgumentClasses; there is no unscreened second route, and KeywordOmittedFunction cannot reach SUM at all because a reserved word never arrives in the cobolWord name slot. (2) ArgSchema.At(i) (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:172) returns the Tail rule for EVERY i when Positions is empty, so Uniform('n') genuinely screens all n positions of the repeated argument-1, not just position 1. (3) The two classifier holes I probed are closed: a ref-modified numeric item resolves through RefModPlace.Category (Place.cs:292ff), which implements §8.4.3.3.4 GR6 c) — numeric under display usage is considered class alphanumeric — so `FUNCTION SUM(N9(1:2))` is rejected; and a nested USER-DEFINED function result does NOT fall into the fail-open `BoundComputedOperand => CobolClass.Numeric` catch-all, because UdfBinder.UdfBindCall returns `new BoundNumRef(tempPlace)` over a temp cloned from the RETURNING item's description (§8.4.3.2.4 GR1), so it reaches the screen as a BoundFieldOperand carrying the real category and an alphanumeric-returning UDF is rejected. (4) EDITIONS: CheckArgumentClasses is gated only on `ctx.Edition.Permissive`, never on the edition, so the screen fires at --std 85 as well; the negative fixture's `reject-at: 2002 2014 2023` omits 85 only because that same fixture declares `01 TDEF TYPEDEF STRONG` and `01 NAT PIC N(2)`, both COBOL-2002+ constructs that would make an 85 run reject for the wrong reason — not because the rule is edition-gated. Verdict held at CONFORMS.

subject: SUM function
notes:
Citation re-derived: `cite.py --check 15.88.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"` => OK, §15.88.4 rule 1 (Returned value rule); spec lines 33507-33521 carry a/b/c, i.e. the n-ary left-to-right sum. §15.4.1 (read at spec line 29768ff) governs how an EAE is realized per arithmetic mode. ALL THREE LANES READ in IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderNum, the ONE dispatcher: (a) STANDARD-DECIMAL / STANDARD — RenderDec's `alwaysDec` list (line 645) names "SumScaled" unconditionally, so SUM ALWAYS evaluates on the SDIDI carrier under a standard mode, emitting CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec (`s = xs[0]; for i>0 s = CobolDec.Add(s, xs[i], mode)`) — the EAE evaluated left to right in the standard intermediate data item, exactly §15.4.1's "the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression". (b) NATIVE, fixed-point — `case "SumScaled" or "RangeScaled"` (line 193) takes AlignedArgs (line 756), which aligns every argument to the list's MAXIMUM scale via NumericRenderer.Align and calls CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled (`Int128 s = 0; foreach (x) s += x`) with the result NumX carried at that common scale; the alignment is escape-checked (CobolNum.RescaleEscape), so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping — §15.4.1 makes the native value an implementor-defined approximation, and the loud boundary is the documented D16/PB32 choice. (c) NATIVE with a floating argument — line 138 routes to RenderFloat(RealMethod("SumScaled")) => CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#SumReal (`double t = 0; foreach t += x`), again the same left-to-right EAE. The n=1 case falls out of every body unchanged (`(argument-1)`); the n>2 case is the same loop. The ARGUMENT COUNT for the EAE's "n occurrences" comes from the §15.3 ALL enumeration (TryBindAllArgument builds ONE TableAllPlace the backend enumerates over the fixed OCCURS count / the ODO object / the dynamic capacity), so a runtime-ranged list still sums exactly the occurrences the standard specifies. §15.88.1's companion TYPE table is also honored (not this row, but it is the same returned value): IntrinsicCatalog row Result: IntrinsicResultRule.IntegerFollowsAllArguments, resolved in IntrinsicResultType.cs#Resolve as Integer only when every argument is known integer, else Numeric. TESTS: tests/conformance/2023/pb62_standard_decimal_summing_family.cob (header cites 15.88.4; `FUNCTION SUM(10^30, 2)` under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL with ON SIZE ERROR present and not taken) whose golden reads SUM=1000000000000000000000000000002 — the exact EAE value the native Int128 alignment could not hold; tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob goldens SUM=0015000{ over an ODO ALL, MIXED=0039000{ (7+8+9+1+5+9), DYN3=0060000{ (dynamic capacity 3), ALLALL=0021000{ (two-level ALL ALL = 1..6); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob goldens SUM=        10.50 for the native mixed integer/scaled list 5+2+3.5. RESIDUE, disclosed: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY — which §15.4.1 also binds to the exact-EAE requirement — is not routed to the SDIDI lane (NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal is true only for StandardDecimal/Standard); it is not a silent divergence, because DataBinder.cs line 318 rejects the clause outright with COBOLNET0806 as a documented obsolete non-support at every edition, so no SUM can be compiled under it. That disposition belongs to §8.8.1.4.1, not to §15.88.4, and is left as an owner-level item rather than counted against this row.

REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. THE ADJUDICATOR'S EVIDENCE FOR THE NATIVE FIXED-POINT LANE IS THE RENDERER'S COMMENT, NOT THE RUNTIME BODY. IntrinsicRenderer.cs:191-192 asserts "SUM/RANGE genuinely ADD, so they keep aligned arguments — now escape-CHECKED (Align emits RescaleEscape): an alignment past the Int128 intermediate is the size-error condition, never a wrap", and the adjudicator's clause "the alignment is escape-checked … so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping" is that comment restated. The guard is real but it is on the PER-ARGUMENT RESCALE ONLY: NumericRenderer.Align (line 526) emits CobolNum.RescaleEscape, whose test is `Int128.Abs(value) > Int128.MaxValue / Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)` — it bounds each ALIGNED ARGUMENT, and says nothing about their sum. THE ACCUMULATION IS UNGUARDED: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Intrinsics/CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled is verbatim `Int128 s = 0; foreach (var x in xs) s += x; return s;` — plain Int128.op_Addition, and neither Directory.Build.props nor src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Cobol.Net.Runtime.csproj sets CheckForOverflowUnderflow, so the context is unchecked and the add WRAPS silently. The same file proves this is a two-arm miss and not a design choice: twenty lines below, MedianScaled and MidrangeScaled route every add through AddForHalving (`try { return checked(a + b); } catch (OverflowException) { throw new CobolSizeError(… "EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW"); }`) and every scale bump through ScaleForHalving, and the PB32 remark introducing them states the policy in terms that cover SUM exactly: "A wrap is never a conforming answer — §15.4.1 asks at worst for 'an implementor-defined approximation', and a value 3.2x out with its top thirty digits wrong approximates nothing." PB32's own note asserts "the ×5/×10 … costs a decimal digit of Int128 headroom that MAX/MIN/SUM/RANGE never spend" — true of the MULTIPLY, and the reason SUM was never swept; the ALIGNMENT spends that headroom just as freely, and the accumulator behind it was never guarded. REACHABLE INSIDE THE COMPILER'S OWN 31-DIGIT CAP (EditionContext.CheckDigitCapacity / MaxDigits): with `P PIC S9(31) VALUE ALL '9'` (9.999999999999999999999999999999e30) beside `Q PIC SV9(7)`, AlignedArgsEx sets the common scale to 7; Align(P,7) = 99999999999999999999999999999990000000, which PASSES RescaleEscape because the bound is Int128.MaxValue / 10^7 = 17014118346046923173168730371588 and |P| is below it. `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(P P P Q)` therefore accumulates 299999999999999999999999999999970000000, which exceeds Int128.MaxValue (170141183460469231731687303715884105727) and wraps to -40282366920938463463374607431798211456, i.e. the VALUE -4.0282366920938463e30 at scale 7. Stored into a `PIC S9(31)` receiver WITH an ON SIZE ERROR phrase: the true value 2.9999999999999999999999999999997e31 needs 32 digits and would raise the size-error condition, while the wrapped value fits the receiver — so the phrase is NOT taken and a wrong, sign-flipped answer is stored silently. That is the identical measured shape PB32 recorded for MIDRANGE ("with an ON SIZE ERROR phrase present and NOT taken") and PB65 for MIN ("a silent Int128 wrap on widening handed MIN a negative result over two positive arguments"), on the one member of the family neither sweep reached. §15.4.1's native latitude is "an implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression"; a value of the wrong sign and the wrong order of magnitude is not an approximation of it. NATIVE IS THE DEFAULT MODE (OptionsModel.cs:22, cited to §11.9.5.2 r4 — "Default ArithmeticMode.Native when absent"), so this is the lane an ordinary COMPUTE takes, and the lane structure was re-confirmed independently: RenderNum:88 `if (num.StandardDecimal)` -> RenderDec (SumScaled is in the alwaysDec list at line 645) -> SumDec; else RenderNum:107 `AnyDecRaw` -> RenderDec; else RenderNum:135 `AnyRealArgument` -> SumReal; else RenderNum:193 -> the unchecked SumScaled. The Dec lane and the float lane ARE correct as adjudicated; the fourth and default lane is not. THE EVIDENCE THAT MISSED IT WAS OUTPUT-SHAPED, exactly rule 5's warning: every golden cited sits far below the carrier boundary (SUM=15, 39, 60, 21, 10.50), and the one boundary golden, pb62_standard_decimal_summing_family, runs under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL — the single lane that is exact. SECOND HALF, INDEPENDENTLY DISQUALIFYING UNDER RULE 5: §15.4.1 binds standard-BINARY to the same requirement as standard-decimal in one sentence — "When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect and an equivalent arithmetic expression is specified: 1) the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression" — and DataBinder.cs:318 rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY outright with COBOLNET0806 at every edition. Of the two modes §15.4.1 r1 governs for this rule, one is implemented and one is refused; a rule with two halves where one was verified is PARTIAL, always, and the adjudicator's own disclosure of this residue argued it away rather than pricing it. Citations re-derived independently: `cite.py --check 15.88.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"` => OK, §15.88.4 rule 1; §15.88.4 a/b/c and §15.4.1 re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33506-33521 and :29768ff. Verdict PARTIAL; the fix is a checked accumulator in SumScaled raising CobolSizeError/EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW at the D1 escape boundary, exactly as AddForHalving already does, plus the sibling sweep (RangeScaled's `MaxScaled(xs) - MinScaled(xs)` is the same unchecked shape and belongs to §15.76.4).

subject: TAN function
notes: cite.py --check 15.89.4 "The returned value is the approximation of the tangent of argument-1." => OK §15.89.4 1) (Returned value rule). BODY: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:27 `public static double Tan(double x) => Math.Tan(x);   // §15.89`. Math.Tan takes RADIANS, which is what §15.89.1 requires ("the tangent of an angle or arc, expressed in radians, that is specified by argument-1") — the units half of the rule, checked rather than assumed. §15.89.4 states a PROSE approximation, not an equivalent arithmetic expression, so §15.4.1's last paragraph makes the value implementor-defined in every arithmetic mode and a binary64 Math.Tan satisfies it. ALL THREE RECEIVER LANES READ, NOT SAMPLED (IntrinsicRenderer.RenderFloat, lines 390–452; TAN routes here because the catalog row's Float flag is true — dispatched at line 109 `if (sig.Float) return RenderFloat(ic, sig.RuntimeMethod)`). (a) Float or receiver-less: `RealResult(Tan(…))` — stays binary64 at full precision, and RealResult is retained precisely so the NaN => EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION raise site is not skipped when the value is not quantized. (b) STANDARD-DECIMAL: `CobolDec.FromDouble(RealResult(Tan(…)))` — the approximation enters as an SDIDI operand per §8.8.1.5.1 and lands ONCE, rather than truncating at a receiver-derived working scale first (PB56). (c) Fixed receiver: `CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble(Tan(…), ws)` with ws = ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale. THE CODOMAIN COLUMN IS CORRECTLY EMPTY: the row omits Codomain, so IntrinsicCodomain.None and RenderFloat line 449 takes the unclamped FromDouble arm — right, because the tangent is UNBOUNDED and IntrinsicCodomain exists only for a §15.x.4 rule that STATES a bound (RANDOM's open [0,1), ASIN/ATAN's ±π/2, ACOS's π). Clamping TAN would be the defect here, not the fix. QUANTIZER CHECKED FOR THE SATURATION SHAPE the batch's rule 5 names: I read ReceiverContext.WorkingScale (ReceiverContext.cs:110–116, ws = clamp(max(Scale, 9)) capped at IntermediateDigits − IntegerDigits) and CobolIntrinsics.FromDouble (CobolIntrinsics.cs:211–226). The cap's stated invariant — a value that fits the receiver never saturates, and a value that does not always descales to a sentinel above the receiver's capacity — is what matters for TAN, whose values near π/2 are legitimately huge (Math.Tan(Math.PI/2) ≈ 1.633e16; at ws 9 that is 1.633e25, far inside Int128's 1.7e38, and a receiver too small for it raises the size error per §14.7.5 case 5 rather than silently storing low-order digits). No 9.2e9-class long-carrier saturation exists on this path. ARGUMENT CONVERSION CHECKED: IntrinsicRenderer.Dbl (line 712) => NumericRenderer.Real (NumericRenderer.cs:697–700), which divides the unscaled carrier by 10^scale, with Pow10D handling a NEGATIVE scale (a PICTURE-P trailing-scaled operand), so a scaled argument such as TAN(.001) reaches Math.Tan as 0.001 and not as 1. ONE EDGE NOTED, NOT A DOWNGRADE: an infinite argument (only reachable from a float item holding ±∞, which is outside the standard's data model) makes Math.Tan return NaN, which FromDouble reports as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION "argument out of domain" — arguably over-attributed, since §15.89.3 states no value restriction, but the input is unrepresentable in conforming COBOL so no conforming program can observe it. MISSING: no spec-derived test. The only exercise of TAN's value is tests/nist/programs/IF139A.cob (nist:, excluded by rule 3) and the legacy-engine unit test IntrinsicFunctionTests.Tan_Zero_ReturnsZero over CobolSharp.Runtime.Intrinsics.IntrinsicFunctions, which is not this runtime. Row stays test-needed. Editions: batch default; §15.89.4's wording is unchanged across the four editions and TAN dates from the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment. || REFUTED: CONFORMS => PARTIAL. THE STANDARD-DECIMAL HALF OF THE RETURNED-VALUE DELIVERY IS IMPLEMENTED FOR ONE RECEIVER SHAPE ONLY, AND THE ADJUDICATOR'S LANE (b) IS PRE-EMPTED FOR THE OTHERS. The three arms inside RenderFloat are tested in this order (IntrinsicRenderer.cs, RenderFloat tail): `if (num.Receiver.Real || num.Receiver.Receiverless) return RealResult(call) [Real:true];` THEN `if (num.StandardDecimal) return DecFromDouble(RealResult(call)) [Dec:true];` THEN the FromDouble/FromDoubleBounded quantizer. The receiverless/float test runs FIRST and is NOT mode-conditional, so under `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (and the obsolete plain STANDARD — NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal is `Arithmetic is StandardDecimal or Standard`, NumericRenderer.cs:394) arm (b) is unreachable for every receiverless or float-receiver TAN reference; the returned value stays a raw binary64. The adjudicator's note asserts "(b) STANDARD-DECIMAL: CobolDec.FromDouble(RealResult(Tan(…))) — the approximation enters as an SDIDI operand per §8.8.1.5.1" as if that lane covered the mode. It covers only the FIXED-POINT-RECEIVER context. SPEC BASIS, RE-DERIVED AND MECHANICALLY CHECKED, NOT INHERITED: `cite.py --check 15.4.1 "contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect"` => OK §15.4.1 — "When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the returned value for numeric and integer functions is contained in a temporary standard data item in the intermediate form defined for the arithmetic mode in effect." That sentence is UNCONDITIONAL on whether an equivalent arithmetic expression exists. The exemption the code and the adjudicator both lean on is §15.4.1's last paragraph — `cite.py --check 15.4.1 "When a numeric or integer function does not have an equivalent arithmetic expression, its returned value is implementor-defined unless otherwise specified in the function definition."` => OK §15.4.1 2) — and it exempts the VALUE, not the CONTAINER; the other clause the receiverless arm's own comment block quotes to justify itself is `cite.py --check 15.4.1 "When native arithmetic is in effect, the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor."` => OK §15.4.1, which is a NATIVE-mode sentence being used to license an arm that runs in EVERY mode. That is the a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question shape: the citation is real, and it is about a different question. OBSERVABLE, not theoretical: the text channel keeps the binary64 — OperandText.NumericExprText renders with ReceiverContext.None (Receiverless) and then `x.Real ? RuntimeApi.FloatDisplay(x.Expr)`, i.e. CobolFloat.Display => `double.ToString(InvariantCulture)` (CobolFloat.cs:25), which emits .NET shortest-round-trip form INCLUDING EXPONENTIAL NOTATION for large magnitudes, so under STANDARD-DECIMAL `DISPLAY FUNCTION TAN(1.5707963267948966)` prints 1.633123935319537E+16 where an SDIDI-carried returned value's item-92 text is plain digits. TAN is exactly the function that reaches those magnitudes (unbounded codomain, values near π/2), so this is not a corner the function cannot occupy. SCOPE OF THE GAP MEASURED, NOT GUESSED: the RELATION channel does recover — ConditionRenderer.cs:185 skips the native double compare when num.StandardDecimal and falls to `CobolDec.Compare(DecOperand(l), DecOperand(rr))`, lifting the float per §8.8.1.5.1 — so the divergence is confined to the receiverless TEXT/MOVE-source contexts and the float-receiver context; the arithmetic-receiver context is correct. NOT A KNOWN-LANDED ITEM: kb/Work greps show `Receiverless` only in PB13, PB60, PB91 and `RealResult` in none; PB13 (landed) is the working-scale cap and the receiverless-binary64 determination under NATIVE, PB56 (landed) added the StandardDecimal arm and never mentions receiverless — so the ORDERING between them is unaddressed by any landed note, and this is not a re-report of a fixed defect. (5) A THIRD UN-SWEPT CARRIER, recorded but NOT the basis of the verdict: IntrinsicRenderer.AsInt (734-743) has arms for Real, Dec and exact Int128 and NONE for the U (UInt128) carrier NumericRenderer.cs:303 emits for an unsigned 16-byte BinaryCapacity item - note the deliberate contrast with line 307, where the 8-byte unsigned item IS lifted with '(Int128)(...)' at the read site. C# defines no implicit UInt128 -> Int128 conversion, so CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg(Int128) would be handed a UInt128 and the user would see a raw Roslyn CS1503 - the same missing-carrier shape PB2 closed for float and PB32/PB14 closed for Dec. It is NOT counted against this ISO row because PicInfo.cs:269/473 make that shape reachable only through USAGE COMP-5 with a 19+ digit unsigned picture, and COMP-5 is a vendor extension with no ISO clause (PictureAnalyzer.cs:523 accepts it ungated); I could not measure it read-only, so it is logged as an observation for the AsInt landing, not as a conformance finding.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: National admission needs national data on both sides per 15.92.3 2); answers are the 15.92.4 NOTE's own 6 / 2 / 0 derived from 15.3.1.3; the two rejection fixtures cover the literal-ness and class halves separately.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: Rule 2 admits a date format, a time format OR a combined format - the widest of the seven, and the one that caught the set-not-value error: the existing corpus program 2014/formatted_datetime uses TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDD"), which the first implementation rejected. That program is spec-derived and is the covering test for the date arm.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
CITATION RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.92.4 "the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected" -> OK (§15.92.4 1)).

BOTH HALVES READ IN THE IMPLEMENTATION, NEVER SAMPLED. CobolDate#TestFormattedDatetime is a one-line pass-through (`=> Analyze(format, data, out _, out _, out _, out _, leapSecond)`), so CobolDate#Analyze IS this rule and is the code-location.
(a) ZERO. Analyze returns 0 only after every format segment has been consumed AND `pos == data.Length`; every other exit is non-zero.
(b) THE ORDINAL POSITION. Every failure arm returns `pos + 1`, the 1-BASED index of the character under examination: a separator segment whose character does not appear (`data[pos] != s.Sep`), an offset-sign character that is not '+'/'-'/'0', data exhausted mid-field, a non-digit in a digit subfield, a subfield provably out of range, and the first TRAILING character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1`).

⛔ THE LOAD-BEARING PART IS "THE FIRST ERROR ... DETECTED", AND IT IS IMPLEMENTED AS PER-DIGIT RANGE NARROWING RATHER THAN A PER-FIELD CHECK — a per-field check would have reported the START of the offending field and failed the NOTE. After consuming digit k of a width-w subfield, Analyze widens the partial value into [mn, mx] by appending the w-1-k digits still to come (`mn *= 10; mx = mx*10 + 9`) and returns pos+1 the moment `mx < lo || mn > hi`. I HAND-TRACED BOTH OF THE NOTE'S OWN EXAMPLES through that loop:
 · "yyyymmdd"/"20051314": the month subfield is [1,12]; at its first digit '1' the interval is [10,19], which straddles 12, so nothing is provable yet; at '3' it is [13,13] and 13 > 12, so the return is pos+1 = 6. That is the NOTE's 6 AND the NOTE's reason ("the character '3' occupies the first position in which it can be determined that an error has occurred").
 · "yyyymmdd"/"15990316": the year subfield is [1601,9999] (§15.3.1.3's "greater than 1600"); at '1' the interval is [1000,1999], which straddles 1601; at '5' it is [1500,1599] and 1599 < 1601, so the return is 2 — the NOTE's 2, for the NOTE's reason.
I checked the subfield bounds against the spec text rather than the comments: §15.3.3.3 verbatim gives hours "00 to 23", minutes "00 to 59", seconds "< 60" with LEAP-SECOND OFF and "< 61" with ON; Analyze uses (0,23), (0,59) and (0, leapSecond ? 60 : 59). Month is [1,12], day-of-month is bounded by DateTime.DaysInMonth of the already-parsed year/month, day-of-year by the leap year, week by LongIsoYear, weekday [1,7]. The Fraction subfield is deliberately EXEMPT from narrowing, which is right — §15.3.3.2 puts no range on it.

DELIBERATE, AND CORRECT UNDER THIS RULE: `dateRepresentable` is ignored here. "9999W526" satisfies every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule yet has no §15.5.2 integer date form; §15.92.4 can only answer with the position of a character IN ERROR and none of those characters is (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid), so 0 is the only answer the rule admits. INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE, which must PRODUCE the integer date form, raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION on the same input — the two callers of the shared analyzer diverge exactly where their rules do (kb/Work PB23, landed).

TEST EVIDENCE — six spec-derived refs that between them hit every error CLASS the narrowing implements, and I checked each is not a net. IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.TestFormattedDatetime_ErrorPosition_2014 carries both NOTE examples plus a valid value -> 0; despite the class name it is NOT a differential — I read AssertSpec at IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs:26 and it compiles, runs and compares against a WRITTEN literal, with no legacy engine in the path. conformance:2014/formatted_datetime pins the same two through the golden (TF1=+000000006, TF2=+000000002) and a valid combined round-trip (FCD=+000000000). conformance:2023/pb65_leap_second_off/_on pin the LEAP-SECOND-dependent seconds bound at DIGIT granularity and I re-derived all three from the loop: "hhmmss"/"235960" -> 5 with OFF (at the '6' the interval is [60,69] and mn 60 > hi 59) and 0 with ON; "235961" -> 6 with ON (at the '6' [60,69] straddles hi 60; at the '1' it is [61,61] > 60). conformance:2023/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form pins the 0-for-an-unrepresentable-week-date reading and week 53 in a 52-week ISO year -> 7. unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.GenuinelyInvalidData_StillReportsItsErrorPosition adds Feb 31 -> 7 and day-of-year 366 in a common year -> 7 (I re-derived both: at the leading '3' the day interval is [30,39] and mn 30 > 28, and [30,39] > 29 of a 365-day year's third digit respectively).

⚠ READ BUT NOT TESTED, named so it cannot be mistaken for coverage: a separator that does not match ("2021/06/16" against "YYYY-MM-DD"), a non-digit inside a subfield, the offset-sign arm together with §15.3.3.6.1's zero-sign-implies-zero-magnitude narrowing (`if (offZero && s.Field is Fld.OffHour or Fld.OffMinute) hi = 0;`), and a NATIONAL argument-2 (positions would be counted in UTF-16 units, one per national character position — correct by construction, but unexercised).
⚠ ONE SHAPE THE RULE DOES NOT COVER AND THE CODE ANSWERS ANYWAY: an argument-2 SHORTER than the format leaves no character in error, and Analyze returns data.Length + 1. §15.92.4 is silent on it. The standard's OWN convention for the same shape is §15.93.4 r1 c) for TEST-NUMVAL, `(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)` — cite.py --check 15.93.4 "(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)" -> OK — so this is a consistent implementor answer within the same standard, not a divergence. An argument-2 LONGER than the format is covered by the rule and is answered correctly (the first extra character's position).

EDITIONS from the standard: Annex E (2014->2023) carries no occurrence of TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME, so §15.92.4 is unchanged at 2023; the landed sibling AR-15.92.3-2 on this function records the same 2014,2023 window. NOT taken from IntrinsicCatalog's own row.

REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Three findings; the first is a two-arm bound where only one arm was checked, on the very method that IS this rule.
Citation re-derived by me: cite.py --check 15.92.4 "the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected" -> OK (§15.92.4 1)).
⛔ (1) THE OFFSET SUBFIELD BOUNDS WERE VERIFIED AGAINST THE WRONG CLAUSE. The adjudication states it checked the subfield bounds against the spec text and names §15.3.3.3 — "hours '00 to 23', minutes '00 to 59'" — then lists "Analyze uses (0,23), (0,59)". But those two switch arms are SHARED: `Fld.Hour => (0, 23)` is joined by `Fld.OffHour => (0, 23)`, and the minutes arm is written `Fld.Minute or Fld.OffMinute => (0, 59)` — ONE expression serving TWO subfields. §15.3.3.3 governs only one of them, by its own words: cite.py --check 15.3.3.3 "The minutes subfield of the data (corresponding to mm in a common time format) shall contain a value from 00 to 59 inclusive" -> OK, and the offset subformat is NOT part of the common time format — §15.3.3.6.1 defines the offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields separately (cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 "two lowercase 'h' characters representing the hours portion of the offset from UTC" -> OK). The clause that actually governs them is §15.3.3.6.2, which the adjudication never located: "The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive" / "… offset-minutes … from 00 to 59 inclusive" (specs/ISO_COBOL.md :29747, :29749). I ran that clause down expecting an invented range and the VALUES turn out right — but a bound justified by a clause that does not cover it is an unverified bound, and §15.92.4's answer is conditioned on exactly "format problems or RANGE problems". Neither `Fld.OffHour` nor `Fld.OffMinute` carries a citation in the source, while every neighbouring bound does. Rule 5: an edge unverified => PARTIAL.
⛔ (2) THE SHORT-ARGUMENT-2 ANSWER IS OUTSIDE THE RULE'S CODOMAIN, AND ITS DEFENCE IS A CLAUSE ABOUT A DIFFERENT FUNCTION. When argument-2 is shorter than the format, Analyze's `if (pos >= data.Length) return pos + 1;` yields data.Length + 1 — a position that does not exist in argument-2 — where §15.92.4 admits only "the ordinal character position at which the first error IN ARGUMENT-2 was detected". The input is REACHABLE: §15.92.3 places no size rule on argument-2 and the compiler applies none — I read the row, `Schema("§15.92.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1)`, and it carries no ArgPredicate width at either position (contrast TRIM's `.WithPredicate(1, ArgPredicate.ExactWidth(1, …))` five rows above it). The adjudication defends the answer with §15.93.4 r1 c)'s `(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)` — a real, --check-able clause that legislates TEST-NUMVAL's returned value, not this function's; that is the a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question shape, and it is the whole of the evidence offered. No test covers the shape and docs/CONFORMANCE.md carries no determination for it (its only §15.92 entry is item 112, the LEAP-SECOND one).
⛔ (3) THE "BOTH NOTE EXAMPLES" CLAIM IS NOT WHAT THE CODE DOES. §15.92.4's NOTE writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ("yyyymmdd", A-DATE)` in LOWERCASE. Both recognisers are case-SENSITIVE: CobolDate.Tokenize's switch matches 'Y'/'M'/'D' uppercase only (lowercase falls to `default` -> `return null`, and Analyze then answers 1), and DateTimeFormatGrammar.BasicDates holds the literal strings ["YYYYMMDD", "YYYYDDD", "YYYYWwwD"], so bind-time Classify returns null and the reference is rejected with DateTimeFormatKindMismatch. The NOTE's own program does not compile. That is DEFENSIBLE — §15.3.1.2 normatively requires "four uppercase 'Y' characters … two uppercase 'M' characters", and a NOTE is not normative — but the adjudication asserts "I HAND-TRACED BOTH OF THE NOTE'S OWN EXAMPLES" and every test silently substitutes uppercase (grep for "yyyymmdd" across tests/ returns nothing). The traced program is not the NOTE's program, and the substitution was never recorded.
WHAT I RE-VERIFIED AND CONFIRM, so the PARTIAL is not mistaken for a wider doubt: CobolDate#Analyze is the only body (grep of src/ for TestFormattedDatetime finds IntrinsicCatalog, IntrinsicRenderer and CobolDate alone); the RenderDec lane does NOT double-dispatch it (RenderDec's `alwaysDec` list excludes it and AnyDecOrRealRaw is false for two string arguments, so it returns null and the single native arm at IntrinsicRenderer `case "TestFormattedDatetime"` renders it at scale 0 — I checked for the two-arm shape and it is absent here); the per-digit narrowing reproduces 6 and 2 for the NOTE's DATA values under an uppercased format; §15.3.1.7's long-ISO-year condition (53 weeks iff Jan 4 is Sunday, or a leap year and Jan 4 is Saturday or Sunday) is equivalent to ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear's rule, so LongIsoYear is right; §15.3.3.6.1 rule 3's zero-sign-implies-zero-magnitude narrowing is present and correct; Tokenize's `extended` flag (a ':' or '-' anywhere in the format) is sound because no basic §15.3 format contains either character, so §15.3.3.2's phantom decimal separator is placed correctly; and a NATIONAL argument-1/argument-2 pair survives end-to-end (NationalLiteralOperand returns a BoundStringLiteral, StrArgVisitor's `Visit(BoundStringLiteral) => EmitText.CsLiteral(n.Value)` is category-blind, so positions count one per national character).

subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citation re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.93.3 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or a data item of class alphanumeric or national." -> OK (§15.93.3 rule 1). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified line 686 carries ["TEST-NUMVAL"] = Uniform('s', "§15.93.3 r1"); Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National]; Violation() intersects that set with CandidateClasses(op) and IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore calls CheckArgumentClasses(sig, args) AFTER the arity check and BEFORE every per-function arm, so the row is live for this function. Both halves of the one sentence checked. (a) A numeric literal/item, a boolean item, an index item, an object reference and a pointer are all rejected (class Numeric/Boolean/Index/Object/Pointer are absent from the 's' set); the registered negative pb58-testnumval-num compiles COMPUTE T = FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL(N9) over PIC 9(3) and is reject-at 2002 2014 2023 (manifest.json:194). (b) The admitted classes are exactly right, INCLUDING the one that looks like over-acceptance and is not: the model folds PIC A into PicCategory.Alphanumeric (PicInfo.cs:14-15 — "Alphanumeric (X) or alphabetic (A)"), so a class-alphabetic item is admitted, and §15.3 type 2 REQUIRES that — cite.py --check 15.3 "A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal shall be specified." -> OK (§15.3 rule 2), which also treats a strongly-typed group as alphanumeric and is not excluded by §15.93.3 (unlike §15.59.3/§15.71.3, which state the exclusion). Numeric-edited is admitted as class alphanumeric per §8.5.2.1 Table 2 (the NumericEditedDeEditing member, whose 'i'/'n' exclusion is a different question). POSITIVE side pinned by pb58_argument_predicates_legal line 73 (FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL("12.5") binds) and by the ten literal calls in conformance:2002/intrinsics_test_validators. EDITIONS: batch default — the rule text carries no edition delta, and neither the §15.93 clause nor Annex E/A.4 carries an in-spec attribution for TEST-NUMVAL's introduction edition (grep of specs/ISO_COBOL.md: the only Annex hit is A.4.9 item 12, which is TEST-NUMVAL-C's LOCALE keyword). The compiler's own 2002 window is IntrinsicCatalog's row, which adjudication rule 4 forbids me from using as the derivation.

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; the missing spec basis supplied and one screening claim independently re-derived): (1) The §15.3-type-2 justification for admitting a class-ALPHABETIC item was the weakest link in this row — §15.93.3 r1 names only "class alphanumeric or national", and the standard demonstrably says "alphabetic" when it means it (§15.96.3 r1 names class alphabetic explicitly), so the omission looked deliberate and the screen looked over-wide. It is not, and the decisive text is one the adjudicator never cited: Table 21, Table of functions (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 29998) gives TEST-NUMVAL's Arguments column as "Anum1 or Nat1", i.e. §15.3 argument TYPE 2 or TYPE 9, and the table's own legend (line 29885 NOTE) fixes that notation. Type 2 admits class alphabetic; type 9 admits "a national group item, a national literal, or an elementary data item of class national". Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National] is exactly type 2 ∪ type 9 under this model, so the union screen coincides with THIS function's rule and there is no over-acceptance to report. (2) I re-derived the rejection claims from the classifier rather than from the negative fixture: an INDEX item is CobolClass.Index by the USAGE-keyed arm of ClassOfPlace (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:386), which rides BEFORE the category table — the adjudicator asserted index rejection but the fail-open at Violation() line 910 (candidates.Length == 0 => return null) would have admitted it had that arm not existed. A national GROUP item resolves through Item.AsIfPic.Category => CobolClass.National (line 375-380), so type 9's group form is admitted. (3) Standing test gap, recorded, not verdict-changing (rule 3: CONFORMS with a thin test-ref is legitimate): the rule's NATIONAL alternative is exercised in NEITHER direction — no fixture binds a national literal or national item to TEST-NUMVAL — and the LITERAL half's negative (a numeric literal argument) has no fixture either, though BoundNumericLiteral => CobolClass.Numeric (ClassOf1 line 348) makes it a compile-time COBOLNET-class rejection mechanically, not the wrong-stage loud runtime value the Str() default would give. Row stays test-needed.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citations re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.4 "Otherwise, if one or more characters are in error, the position of the first character in error" -> OK (§15.93.4 rule 1, leg b) and --check 15.93.4 "argument-1 contains valid characters but is incomplete" -> OK (the rule-1 NOTE). READ, not sampled: CobolIntrinsics.TestNumval (Exact.cs:539) is a pure projection — NvScan(text, commaMode, "", false, digitCap, allowGroup:false).ErrPos — of the SAME scan the NUMVAL value path rides (Exact.cs:308), so the validator and the value function cannot disagree about what conforms. NvScan (Exact.cs:586-639) is a positional recognizer of §15.67.3 r1's TWO alternative formats, walked over the ORIGINAL string with no pre-normalization (that is what makes the reported position ordinal): leading SPACE-only run (r2's ignorable character is the space, not .NET IsWhiteSpace); format-A leading sign; spaces; digit groups with at most one decimal separator; then, only when NO leading sign was taken, a format-B trailing +/-/CR/DB in any case; then a trailing space run. ALL THREE LEGS verified. Leg a (0): every conforming shape returns new(0,...) — pinned N1 "123.45"=0, N2 " + 12 "=0 (r2's before-the-first-digit spaces), N3 "123cr"=0 (mixed-case CR), N4 "5."=0 (the 'digit [ . [digit] ]' branch), and ".5" takes the '. digit' branch. r5 (the DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA separator swap) is the commaMode parameter, fed by IntrinsicRenderer.CommaFlag (ctx.Data.DecimalPointIsComma) and unit-pinned: TestNumval("1,5", commaMode:true)=0, ("1.5", commaMode:true)=2. Leg b: the digit loop's break returns i+1 — N6 "1,234"=2 (a comma is not a NUMVAL character with allowGroup:false), N7 "1.2.3"=4 (the second decimal point). The two-formats-are-ALTERNATIVES discipline is explicit at line 630 (`if (!leadSign && ...)`), so "-12-" is position 4 rather than a sign toggle (conformance:2023/pb60_numval_one_scan). Leg c (LENGTH+1): line 621 discriminates — a digit-free scan that BROKE on a real character reports that character (r1b), one that ran off the end reports n+1; pinned N8 "    "=5, N9 " +."=4 (the NOTE's verbatim incomplete example), and unit TestNumval(" +.")=4. n is text.Length, i.e. the item's full fixed-width image, which is what FUNCTION LENGTH returns, so leg c's arithmetic is the rule's (a data-item argument does reach the scan at full width — golden N10 uses W40 PIC X(40) VALUE ALL "1"). Zero-length argument -> n+1 = 1. Digit-cap sub-notes are adjudicated on their own rows. NOT VERIFIED: a NATIONAL argument-1 (§15.67.3 r1's national CR/DB bullets) is not exercised by any golden — it is correct by construction here because the national image is UTF-16 with one char per position, so 'C'/'R' and the digits are the same code units the scan tests, but that is reasoning, not measurement.

REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Three findings, one of them a rule half that is not implemented at all.
(1) DECISIVE — LEG (a) INCORPORATES AN ARGUMENT RULE THIS COMPILER DOES NOT IMPLEMENT. Leg (a) is "conforms to the ARGUMENT RULES for the NUMVAL function", i.e. §15.67.3 rules 1-5 in full (I read the clause at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:32548-32583). Rule 4 has TWO halves — cite.py --check 15.67.3 "If standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 35. If standard-decimal arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 34." -> OK (§15.67.3 rule 4) — and the standard-binary half (35) is ABSENT FROM THE TREE: IntrinsicRenderer.DigitCapFlag (line 800) is two-valued, `num.StandardDecimal ? ", digitCap: 34" : ""`, so NvScan's digitCap is only ever 31 or 34 and the renderer's own comment at line 263 records the omission ("standard-binary's 35 rides the P12/P13 STANDARD-BINARY wave"). Rule 5 of this batch is explicit: a rule with two halves where one was verified => PARTIAL, always. The adjudicator routed the whole of §15.67.3 r4 to the L2.3 sibling row and left leg (a) clean; leg (a) cites the rule and so carries the gap too, and cannot read CONFORMS while its incorporated half is an open owner question.
(2) THE EVIDENCE FOR LEG (c) OVER A DATA ITEM IS OUTPUT-SHAPED AND CANNOT DISCRIMINATE. The note closes leg (c)'s "n is text.Length ... the item's FULL FIXED-WIDTH image" claim with "golden N10 uses W40 PIC X(40) VALUE ALL '1'". N10's verdict is 32 — the 32nd digit under the native cap — which is 32 for ANY width >= 32, so that observation is identical under the hypothesis it was cited to refute (a trimmed or short-stored image) and measures nothing about width. That is exactly the "CONFORMS whose evidence is output-shaped" failure this stage exists to catch. I re-derived the claim independently and it DOES hold, on evidence the adjudicator did not use: CobolString.Fit (src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Text/CobolString.cs:28-32) pads or truncates every alphanumeric store to exactly the declared width, so the fixed-width invariant is real; OperandText.FieldAsString line 249-250 returns PlaceRenderer.Read(p) unmodified for an Alphanumeric/NumericEdited/National leaf (no trim, no AsImage); and conformance:2023/pb33_numval_family_digit_cap TEST-31 = 0 over `S31 PIC X(44)` holding a 32-character value DOES exercise a padded 12-space tail end-to-end. The conclusion survives — the cited proof did not.
(3) TWO ARMS, ONE MEASURED, ON r5's FEED. §15.67.3 r5 (DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA) is one of the five rules leg (a) incorporates, and the note calls it "unit-pinned". The unit test CommaMode_SwapsSeparatorRoles calls CobolIntrinsics.TestNumval("1,5", commaMode: true) — the flag is a LITERAL, so it exercises the runtime scan arm and never the compiler arm (ctx.Data.DecimalPointIsComma -> IntrinsicRenderer.CommaFlag line 792 -> the emitted named argument). For TEST-NUMVAL the compiler-side half of r5 has no test of any kind; the property is proven live only through a SIBLING (conformance:2023/numvalf_decimal_comma_and_spaces compiles NUMVAL-F under the clause). Same shape for the NATIONAL edge the adjudicator itself flagged: I confirmed the leg is correct by construction (FieldAsString line 249-250 hands NvScan the UTF-16 character image, one char per national position per the D-N1 determination, so 'C'/'R', ' ' and the ASCII digits are the same code units), but it remains unmeasured in both directions.
SUSTAINED on my own read: the format recognizer itself. I hand-traced "0 1"->3, "12CR"->0, "12C"->3, "-12CR"->4 (formats are alternatives), "+12+"->4, "1. 5"->4, ".12."->4, "++"->2, "CR"->1, "+"->2, "."->2, "\t12"->1, "12 - "->0, "12--"->4 and the comma-mode swap, all against §15.67.3's two printed formats; NvScan is faithful and the leg b/c discriminator at line 621 is right. PARTIAL is for the unimplemented r4 half and the two unmeasured feeds, not for the scanner.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.4 "If argument-1 is '0 1', the returned value will be 3." -> OK (§15.93.4 rule 1, sub-note 1 under leg b). READ: NvScan (Exact.cs:603-637). The sub-note has TWO halves and both are in the code. (i) "one or more spaces following one or more digits is valid" — after the digit loop breaks, line 622 skips the space run WITHOUT reporting it, and if the string ends there (line 637, i == n) the verdict is 0; a trailing sign or CR/DB may legally follow the skipped spaces (line 630-633), so "0 " and "0 -" and "12 CR" all return 0. (ii) "the returned value is the position of the first non-space character following the spaces" — the fall-through at line 634 returns i + 1 where i is the index reached AFTER the space run was skipped, i.e. the first non-space, not the first space. Hand-traced against the standard's own example: "0 1" -> digit '0' consumed (i=0), loop breaks on the space (i=1), anyDigit true, the space run advances i to 2, text[2]='1' is neither a sign nor CR/DB, so the return is i+1 = 3 — the value the rule names verbatim. Also traced "0  1" -> 4 and "12 34" -> 4 (the first non-space after the run, not the run's start). TEST: conformance:2002/intrinsics_test_validators line 60-61 is the verbatim example, pinned N5=03 in the .out; its source comment cites the sub-note. The half (i) branch is pinned by the same golden's N2/N3 (a trailing space run and a space-then-CR both = 0).

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; one cited test observation is WRONG and is replaced, and the substituted evidence is stronger): the closing sentence claims half (i) is "pinned by the same golden's N2/N3 (a trailing space run and a space-then-CR both = 0)". N3 is FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL("123cr") — intrinsics_test_validators.cob line 54 — which contains NO SPACE AT ALL; it pins the mixed-case CR of §15.67.3 r1's alphanumeric bullet, not the space-then-CR path. subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.4 "the returned value is the position of the 32nd digit if no prior error is found" -> OK (§15.93.4 rule 1, sub-note 2); its premise re-derived too — cite.py --check 15.67.3 "If native arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in argument-1 shall not exceed 31." -> OK (§15.67.3 rule 3). READ: NvScan line 609, `if (++digits > digitCap) return new(i + 1, true, false, 0, 0)`, with digitCap defaulting to 31 on the TestNumval signature (Exact.cs:539) and IntrinsicRenderer.DigitCapFlag (line 800) emitting NOTHING under native arithmetic, so the native call takes that default. Three things checked. (1) The reported position is the 32nd DIGIT's own character position (i is the index of the digit that pushed the count past the cap), not the count and not the string end. (2) "the total number of digits" is counted across BOTH sides of the decimal separator — the counter is incremented in the single digit arm that serves the integer and fraction parts alike. (3) "if no prior error is found" holds structurally: the cap test lives inside the digit loop, so any earlier malformation has already broken the loop or returned, and any LATER malformation is at a higher position than the digit that trips the cap — so the reported position is still the FIRST character in error under leg b. The cap is tested BEFORE the accumulator multiplies, so the value projection cannot saturate into a plausible number (the PB33/PB34 defect this ordering was written for). TESTS: intrinsics_test_validators N10 = 32 over W40 (PIC X(40) VALUE ALL "1" — the 32nd digit is at position 32); pb33_numval_family_digit_cap TEST-34 = 33 over "1234567890123456789012345.678901234", where the 32nd digit sits at character position 33 because of the decimal point — I recomputed that position independently rather than trusting the fixture's prose header, which loosely says "-> 32" while the .out's overpunched "00000003C" is 33; unit DigitCap_FollowsArithmeticMode asserts TestNumval(40 x '1') == 32. Both the boundary (31 digits = 0) and the first failing case are covered.

notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.3 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or a data item of class alphanumeric or national."` -> OK, §15.95.3 rule 1. CODE READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified carries `["TEST-NUMVAL-F"] = Uniform('s', "§15.95.3 r1")` (line 687), screened by IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses, which deliberately drives off the Verified table and NOT off sig.ArgKinds ("the catalog's hint column is unaudited", line 1654), calling IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation over `Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National]` (line 874) with the §8.3.3.6.4 GR4 candidate-set intersection. WHAT r1 EXCLUDES AND WE REJECT (verified through ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfCategory): class NUMERIC (a numeric literal binds BoundNumericLiteral -> CobolClass.Numeric; a PIC 9 item -> PicCategory.Numeric -> CobolClass.Numeric), class BOOLEAN (a B"..." literal carries Category Boolean, a PIC 1 item likewise), class POINTER/OBJECT, and class INDEX (ClassOfPlace's `Usage.Index` arm, which rides BEFORE the category table). WHAT r1 ADMITS AND WE ADMIT: alphanumeric literals and items, alphanumeric GROUP items (ClassOfPlace's IsGroup arm -> Alphanumeric, and a group IS a 'data item of class alphanumeric'), national literals (N"..." carries Category National) and national items, numeric-edited display items (§8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts category numeric-edited in class ALPHANUMERIC, so r1's 'class alphanumeric' reaches it — the NumericEditedDeEditing member is that class, per its own remark), and figurative constants (SPACE/ZERO present an alphanumeric or national character value, §8.3.3.6.4 GR4/GR1; the intersection test admits them, which is PB48's landed behaviour, not a hole). notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.4 "the returned value is the position of the fifth digit of the exponent"` -> OK, §15.95.4 1) b) (list item 5). CODE READ: NvfScan's exponent scan counts exponent digits in `ed` and returns at the FIFTH one — `while (i < n && char.IsAsciiDigit(text[i])) { if (++ed > 4) return new(Pos(), false, false, 0, 0, 0); ev = ev * 10 + (text[i] - '0'); i++; }`. `Pos()` is `i + 1` and `i` has NOT yet advanced when the guard fires, so the value returned is the 1-based position OF THE FIFTH EXPONENT DIGIT ITSELF, exactly as the rule states ("1E+12345" -> 8, the ordinal of the '5'). VERIFIED ACROSS THE RULE'S TWO NAMED MODES: the arm is MODE-INDEPENDENT — the 4-digit exponent bound is hardcoded, not threaded from DigitCapFlag (which carries only the SIGNIFICAND cap) — so the standard-decimal half is satisfied, and the standard-binary half would be satisfied by the same code if the mode were admitted (it is not: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806 at every edition, the documented non-support adjudicated on RV-15.27.3-2). I do not score that as an unverified half, because the behaviour this rule names does not vary by mode in this implementation and there is no second code path to leave unread. THE 'SIGNIFICANT DIGITS' WORDING WAS ATTACKED AND DOES NOT CHANGE THE ANSWER: on a leading-zero exponent such as "1E+00005" the code returns the fifth digit's position; if 'significant' is read strictly (one significant digit, so this rule would not fire), the base argument rule still rejects the string — `cite.py --check 15.69.3 "n is one, two, three, or four digits representing the exponent"` -> OK — and §15.95.4 1) b) then asks for 'the position of the first character in error', which is that same fifth digit because the format admits only a space-string or end-of-string after the fourth. Both readings land on the same number. ORDERING ALSO CHECKED: the scan is strictly left-to-right, so a significand error or a malformed sign returns before the exponent scan is entered, satisfying the family's 'no prior error ... has been found' precedence. TEST-REF EMPTY (rule 3): nothing in tests/ writes a five-digit exponent — IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.TestNumvalF_Positions_2014's four cases and the pb60_numval_one_scan golden's ET row all stay within one exponent digit. CONFORMS-but-untested; the row stays test-needed. EDITIONS from kb/Work R28's external evidence, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The citation re-derives (`cite.py --check 15.95.4 "the returned value is the position of the fifth digit of the exponent"` -> OK, §15.95.4 1) b), list item 5) and the arithmetic the adjudicator describes is correct as far as it goes — I re-traced `if (++ed > 4) return new(Pos(), ...)` myself: `i` has not advanced past the fifth digit when the guard fires, so `Pos() = i + 1` is that digit's own 1-based ordinal ("1E+12345" -> 8, and with the figure's optional space-strings "1E+ 12345" -> 9). The verdict still costs something on TWO grounds the adjudicator argued away rather than measured. (1) THE RULE NAMES TWO ARITHMETIC MODES AND ONLY ONE CAN EVER BE IN EFFECT HERE. The rule text is 'If standard-decimal arithmetic, OR STANDARD-BINARY ARITHMETIC is in effect ...'. I read DataBinder.BindDeclarations myself: `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", ...)` — a hard error at every edition, so no program this compiler translates can ever have standard-binary in effect and the standard-binary half of this rule is never satisfied by anything. The adjudicator dismissed that with 'the behaviour this rule names does not vary by mode in this implementation', which is an argument about the CODE, not about whether the rule's stated precondition can hold. The batch has already settled the shape the other way: RV-15.27.3-2, whose SOLE condition is standard-binary, was adjudicated NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION as the documented-non-support shape and explicitly NOT CONFORMS — and this batch's own RV-15.95.4-1 note concedes sub-note b.3 (the standard-binary 35-digit cap) is ABSENT. One half verified, one half unexercisable is PARTIAL by the batch rule, always. (2) AN UNVERIFIED EDGE INSIDE THE STANDARD-DECIMAL HALF — THE DIGIT COUNT AND THE SPACE RULE. §15.69.3 r5 (`--check 15.69.3 "Embedded spaces in argument-1 are ignored except between the first numeric digit and the last digit that precedes a letter 'E'"` -> OK) makes embedded spaces IGNORED everywhere outside the significand, while r1's figure draws `n` as a contiguous one-to-four-digit run with [space-string] only before and after it. Those two readings give different answers for an exponent written with an interior space, and they land squarely on THIS rule's 'more than four significant digits' count: for `TEST-NUMVAL-F("1E+1 2345")` I traced the code to 6 — the digit loop exits at the space with ed=1, the trailing-space skip advances to '2', and `if (i != n) return new(Pos(), ...)` reports it — where the r5 reading makes the exponent 12345, five digits, and this rule requires the position of its FIFTH digit, 9. The implementation resolves a normative tension silently: nothing in NvfScan, its comments, the design docs or any test records that the choice was made, and the r5 except-clause is implemented for the SIGNIFICAND (`pendingSpace`) and nowhere else. An edge on which the rule's own answer changes, resolved without evidence, is PARTIAL under the batch's cost rule. TWO THINGS I CHECKED THAT DID **NOT** MOVE THE VERDICT, recorded so they are not re-litigated: the mode-independence of the 4-digit bound is CORRECT under native, because §15.69.3 r1's 'where' clause caps n at 'one, two, three, or four digits' with no arithmetic-mode qualification, so under native the fifth digit is the first character in error under leg b) generic and the same number comes back; and the 'significant digits' wording converges on the same number for a leading-zero exponent ("1E+012345" -> the code returns the position of the fifth DIGIT of the exponent, 8, which is exactly what the rule's words say). I also re-confirmed there is no second lane to leave unread — RenderDec's `alwaysDec` list excludes TestNumvalF, its switch ends `_ => null`, and there is no compile-time intrinsic folder anywhere in the compiler. notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'Argument-1 shall be a data item of class alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national.' -> OK (r1). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified["TRIM"] = Schema("§15.96.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1) — position 0 declares kind 's', and Admissible('s') = {Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National} (IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible), so Violation() rejects class numeric, boolean, index, object and pointer for argument-1. §8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts alphabetic and numeric-edited under alphanumeric, so 's' is exactly r1's three classes in this model (PicCategory folds PIC A into Alphanumeric — the CobolClass enum comment). The screen is REACHED on this bespoke path: IntrinsicBinder.BindTrim calls CheckArgumentClasses(sig, operands) at line 1010 before building the node (the generic path returns earlier), and CheckArgumentClasses walks schema.At(i). Positive coverage in both admitted rows: intrinsics_trim (PIC X(10) argument-1) and pb15_result_type_follows_argument (PIC N(8) and PIC X(8) argument-1, TRIM-N=[CDE] / TRIM-X=[CDE]). Figurative ZERO passes (candidate classes include alphanumeric — §8.3.3.6.4 GR4, PB48) and pb48_figurative_zero_intrinsic_argument pins it. NOT VERIFIED BY A FIXTURE: the rejection direction — no negative fixture feeds TRIM a class-numeric/pointer argument-1 (pb58-trim-arg2 tests r2's width, pb15-trim-national-result-to-an tests the §15.96.1 result table), so the row stays test-needed on that half; the code path was read instead. Deliberate latitude recorded, NOT scored as a defect: r1 says 'a DATA ITEM', and the implementation also admits an alphanumeric/national LITERAL argument-1. That is what §15.6 Table 21 types TRIM's argument-1 as (Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1) and what §15.3 type 2 admits ('A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal'), and §15.96.4's own NOTE writes TRIM("aabbcc" "c" "b") — rejecting a literal would reject the standard's own example. Editions from Annex §E.3.3 item 31 (--check OK: 'The TRIM function has been enhanced…', i.e. TRIM predates 2023) plus kb/Work R28's landed primary-source decision (WG4/J4 CD 1.2 Annex D.2 lists TRIM among the 2014 introductions); NOT derived from the IntrinsicCatalog row. REFUTED: verdict SUSTAINED — attacked on three axes and it held. (a) The load-bearing latitude citation was NOT inherited: I re-ran cite.py --check 15.3 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal shall be specified' -> OK (§15.3 2), and read §15.6's own legend in the transcription ('A digit immediately following the argument type indicates the argument's position in the list of arguments') beside the Table 21 TRIM row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md — 'Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1, Alph2 … or Anum2 … or Nat2 … or Key2 or Key2 and Alph2 …'. The literal admission is the standard's, and the Key2-then-Alph2 ordering independently corroborates the FMT-15.96.2 order finding. (b) The REJECT half was re-read rather than accepted: IntrinsicArgumentRules.CandidateClasses/ClassOf1 return a FIXED class for every operand shape that could carry a forbidden argument-1 — BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall} → ClassOfCategory(ic.ResultCategory), BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIndexRef} → Index, bare BoundComputedOperand → Numeric, BoundFigurative 'N' (NULL) → Pointer, and ClassOfPlace keys USAGE INDEX before the category table — none is in Admissible('s'), so Violation() REPORTS instead of the candidates.Length==0 fail-open. FUNCTION TRIM(FUNCTION ABS(N)) is a compile-time §15.3 rejection, not the run-time StrArgVisitor LoudValue abort (the wrong-stage family). (c) The ALL shape was checked, since FUNCTION TRIM(ALL T) puts a TableAllPlace at position 0: ClassOfPlace reads p.Item, so argument-1's class is still screened there. The editions claim was chased to its source rather than inherited — kb/Work/R28.md's 'LANDED 2026-08-08' section names the WG4/J4 CD 1.2 (2009-08-23) Annex D.2 item 4 list verbatim, and R28's earlier body explicitly warns the 2023 PDF cannot settle a 2002 window; the adjudicator used the landed half, correctly.

notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'argument-2 shall be a single character that is either class alphabetic or class alphanumeric' -> OK (r2). VERIFIED for the FIRST argument-2 only. READ: Verified["TRIM"] = Schema("§15.96.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: CrossArgRule.MatchArgument1, crossClause: "§15.96.3 r2").WithPredicate(1, ArgPredicate.ExactWidth(1, "§15.96.3 r2")). Position 1 therefore carries BOTH halves of r2: the width half (PredicateViolation ExactWidth over IntrinsicBinder.KnownWidth — a literal's Length, an item's ImageWidth, which DataItem.ImageWidth keeps in character positions and never byte-doubles for national, so a PIC N(1) argument-2 measures 1 and is not falsely rejected) and the class half (CrossViolation with MatchArgument1 intersects the candidate classes of schema.MatchedPositions(), rejecting national-argument-2-with-alphanumeric-argument-1 and the converse — r2's two sentences). negative/pb58-trim-arg2 (TRIM(X3 "AB"), expecting COBOLNET1627) pins the width half. ⛔ THE GAP: TRIM is catalogued Variadic 1..inf (IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Add "TRIM") and §15.96.2 prints '[ argument-2 ] …', so argument-2 REPEATS — but Schema()'s tail parameter defaults to '\0', so ArgSchema.Tail is null and ArgSchema.At(i) returns null for every i >= 2. Positions 3, 4, … are entirely UNSCREENED: no class kind, no ExactWidth(1), and CrossViolation cannot see them either (schema.MatchedPositions() iterates Positions only, which has length 2). BindTrim binds an unbounded operand list, so FUNCTION TRIM(X3 "A" "BC") — a two-character second argument-2 — draws no diagnostic and reaches CobolIntrinsics.Trim, whose 'c[0]' silently keeps 'B' and discards 'C'; FUNCTION TRIM(X-item "A" N"X") mixes classes r2 forbids, and a class-numeric third argument passes as well. The fix shape is one table edit (tail: 's' plus a tail predicate — the ORD/ORD-MAX rows already use WithTailPredicate), not a second check. NOT VERIFIED: any fixture with two or more argument-2s — grep of tests/conformance shows every TRIM call site has at most one. Editions: the argument-2 form is the 2023 enhancement (Annex §E.3.3 item 31, --check OK), and IntrinsicBinder.BindTrim gates operands.Count > 1 below 2023 with COBOLNET1502, so r2 has no pre-2023 reach. REFUTED: verdict SUSTAINED as PARTIAL, and CONFIRMED independently — I re-read ArgSchema.At (line 172: 'i < Positions.Length ? Positions[i] : Tail', Tail null for TRIM) and CrossViolation (line 1029: 'governed = schema.MatchedPositions()', which yields only {0,1} for a two-element Positions). But the note UNDERSTATES the hole by one whole shape, and the second shape is worse because it also punches through an EDITION gate. §15.3 rule 14 (--check OK: 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by … subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL' and 'the effect is as if each table element associated with that subscript position were specified') makes FUNCTION TRIM(ALL T) LEGAL SOURCE with no position restriction, and IntrinsicBinder.TryBindAllArgument admits it because sig.RepeatsAnArgument is true (IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 69: MaxArgs == int.MaxValue; the TRIM row is Variadic 1..inf). That ALL binds as ONE operand, so: (i) operands.Count == 1, and BindTrim's edition gate 'if (operands.Count > 1 && DialectLevel < 2023) Error(COBOLNET1502)' NEVER FIRES — at --std 2014 a 3-element table gives TRIM(T(1) T(2) T(3)), i.e. the 2023-only argument-2 form, accepted silently below its edition (IntrinsicRenderer.LeadThenTail line 576 splits the flattened array as 'method(xs[0], mode, xs[1..])', so T(2..n) ARE the argument-2s at run time); (ii) every one of those implicit argument-2s escapes BOTH halves of r2, because CheckArgumentClasses walks the OPERAND list, which has one entry — no ExactWidth(1), no MatchArgument1. A PIC X(3) table element therefore reaches c[0] and silently loses two characters. A third, smaller escape, on the plain path: PredicateViolation's ExactWidth arm is 'when knownWidth is { } w && w != p.N', so a null width falls to '_ => null' — KnownWidth returns null for {IsAnyLength: true} or {IsDynamicLength: true} items and for a computed-length ref-mod, so those argument-2s are width-unscreened too. Verdict stays PARTIAL (the first written argument-2 is genuinely screened on both halves), but the fix shape is larger than 'one table edit': the tail predicate does not reach an ALL operand, and the COBOLNET1502 count must be taken over the EXPANDED argument list (IntrinsicRenderer.StaticArgCount already computes exactly that number), not over operands.Count.

subject: TRIM function
notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'if argument-1 is class national, argument-2 is as though a national space had been specified' -> OK (r3 b). READ: CobolIntrinsics.Trim(string s, long mode, params string[] chars) opens with 'char[] set = chars.Length == 0 ? [' '] : …' — with no argument-2 the delete set is exactly one SPACE, r3's default. BOTH sub-rules land on that one line because the typed-native model stores a national item as a C# string of UTF-16 code units, one per national character position (the emitted pb15_result_type_follows_argument.g.cs shows 'private string W_NPAD = CobolString.Store("  CDE   ", 8)' for PIC N(8) and 'CobolIntrinsics.Trim(W_NPAD, 0)'), so the national space IS U+0020 and r3.b needs no separate arm — a distinct national-space constant would be the second mechanism, not a fix. Both sub-rules are exercised: r3.a by intrinsics_trim (BOTH=/LEAD=/TRAIL= over PIC X(10) "  HELLO   "), r3.b by pb15_result_type_follows_argument (MOVE FUNCTION TRIM(W-NPAD) TO W-NR over PIC N(8) N"  CDE   " → TRIM-N=[CDE]). The renderer reaches the defaulted form correctly: IntrinsicRenderer's "Trim" arm emits Intrinsic(method, Str(arg0) + ", " + TrimMode) with no chars when Args.Count == 1. Minor observation, not scored: the second guard 'if (set.Length == 0) set = [' ']' also substitutes a space when every WRITTEN argument-2 is a zero-length string — a silent fallback, but only for source r2 already forbids (a zero-length argument-2 is not 'a single character'), and it is unreachable for a static literal, which the ExactWidth(1) predicate rejects first. Editions per Annex §E.3.3 item 31 + kb/Work R28 (TRIM introduced 2014); the no-argument-2 default is the whole of 2014-era TRIM. REFUTED: CONFORMS → PARTIAL. The DEFAULT VALUE half of r3 is right and I re-confirmed the storage model in the emitted C# myself (tests/conformance/2023/pb15_result_type_follows_argument.g.cs line 15 stores PIC N(8) as an 8-char UTF-16 string padded with U+0020, line 51 calls Trim(W_NPAD, 0)) — so r3.b needing no separate national-space constant is sustained. What is NOT right is the code's test for r3's ANTECEDENT. r3 fires 'When NO argument-2 IS SPECIFIED' — a SYNTACTIC condition, decided at bind time. CobolIntrinsics.Trim decides it at RUN TIME on 'chars.Length == 0', and then a SECOND run-time test, 'if (set.Length == 0) set = [' ']', re-applies r3's default after '.Where(c => c.Length > 0)' has emptied a set built from argument-2s that WERE specified. The adjudicator's dismissal rests on a reachability claim it did not measure ('unreachable for a static literal, which the ExactWidth(1) predicate rejects first'), and that claim is only true for STATIC literals. I read PredicateViolation (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs line 939): the ExactWidth arm is guarded 'when knownWidth is { } w && w != p.N', so a NULL width falls through '_ => null' and fails OPEN; and IntrinsicBinder.KnownWidth (line 1317) returns null for 'BoundFieldOperand { Place.Item: { IsAnyLength: true } or { IsDynamicLength: true } }' and for a ref-mod whose length is not an int literal. So FUNCTION TRIM(X DYN-ITEM) over an ANY LENGTH / DYNAMIC LENGTH argument-2 currently holding the empty string binds clean, reaches the runtime with chars = [""], is filtered to an empty set, and SILENTLY TRIMS SPACES — r3's default applied where r3's antecedent is false. §15.3 rule 14 is explicit about what should happen instead (--check OK: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument … the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'); nothing here raises it. The same fallback is reached from the table(ALL) lane whenever the ALL enumerates zero elements. One half of r3 verified (the default's VALUE, by two goldens in both classes), the other half wrong on a reachable path ⇒ PARTIAL per rule 5. The fix shape is to decide r3 at BIND time — BindTrim already knows operands.Count — and let a specified-but-empty argument-2 raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION rather than fall back to a space.

notes: cite.py --check 15.96.4 'If LEADING is specified, the returned value is a character string that consists of the characters in argument-1 beginning from the leftmost character position that does not contain any argument-2' -> OK (r1). Under r1's own text ('does not contain ANY argument-2') the union reading is what the sentence says, which is why the divergence is scored on r5 and not here. REFUTED: CONFORMS → PARTIAL. The partition the note relies on does not survive: r1's own text is PLURAL-AWARE ('does not contain any argument-2'), so r1 GOVERNS the multiple-argument-2 case rather than being silent about it, and §15.96.4 r5 plus its normative NOTE fix which reading of 'any' the standard means — 'The processing of TRIM (arg-1 arg-2-1 arg-2-2) is the same as TRIM (TRIM (arg-1 arg-2-1) arg-2-2)'. Half neither verified nor correct: the ≥2 argument-2 form, for which grep over tests/conformance finds no TRIM call site at all. The DIVERGES stays attributed to RV-15.96.4-5, where the composition rule is written; this row is PARTIAL because its own returned value is only half implemented, not a second count of the same defect.

ONE DETERMINATION, BOTH ROWS: RV-15.21.3-1 and RV-15.99.3-1 share it because one formatter serves both (CobolDate.Format21) and §15.99.3 r1's table is character-for-character §15.21.3 r1's; the compile-time bake (IntrinsicBinder.CompileClock) and the run-time read (RunUnit.Current.Clock) are independent seams onto that one formatter, and the shared test asserts they agree rather than assuming it.
