(1) EMIT: IntrinsicRenderer.cs line 308 'case "DateToYyyymmdd" or "DayToYyyyddd" or "YearToYyyy"' renders string.Join over Enumerable.Range(0, ic.Args.Count) - ONLY the arguments actually written, so omission survives to C# as a missing argument rather than as a value; RuntimeApi.cs#DateFn emits 'CobolDate.YearToYyyy(...)'. (2) EXACT LANE: CobolDate.cs line 108 'public static long YearToYyyy(long yy, long off = 50)' - the one-argument reference binds this overload and off is 50. (3) FLOAT LANE: CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#YearToYyyyReal also declares 'double off = 50', so the r3 default is carried on BOTH carriers (the r5 default is NOT - see AR-15.100.3-5). (4) The catalog row is IntrinsicArity.OptionalTrailing 1..3, so the 1-argument reference is legal and reaches here. TEST DISCRIMINATES: CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_DefaultArg3_IsExecutionYear asserts YearToYyyy(76) == 2076 under a pinned 2026 clock; with off = 0 the same call would yield 1976 (max 2026, MOD 26 < 76 => r2b), so the assertion can only pass with 50, and its comment derives the value from r3 + r2a/r2b rather than from an observed output. Not a characterization or legacy-oracle test. REFUTED: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The adjudicator's own words are the defect: 'CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#YearToYyyyReal also declares double off = 50, so the r3 default is carried on BOTH carriers'. That is a claim about a SIGNATURE, and it is contradicted by the BEHAVIOUR of the very same method - the read-one-of-two-bodies shape this stage exists to catch. (1) WHICH FORM DOES r3 GOVERN? Exactly one. The §15.100.2 general format is 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY ( argument-1 [ argument-2 [ argument-3 ] ] )' with argument-3 NESTED inside argument-2's brackets, so argument-2 omitted implies argument-3 omitted: the ONLY reference r3 governs is the ONE-ARGUMENT form. The adjudicator establishes this nesting itself in FMT-15.100.2 and then never applies it here. (2) WHAT THE ONE-ARGUMENT FORM DOES ON THE FLOAT CARRIER. IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat line 404 emits 'string.Join(", ", Enumerable.Range(0, ic.Args.Count).Select(i => Dbl(ic, i)))' - only the arguments written - so 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(F)' over a COMP-2 F renders CobolIntrinsics.YearToYyyyReal(<double>). RealArgs.cs line 107 is a SINGLE method 'YearToYyyyReal(double yy, double off = 50, double baseYear = 0)', so C# fills BOTH optionals, and line 109 calls the THREE-argument 'CobolDate.YearToYyyy(y, o, b)' unconditionally. YearToYyyyAt line 123 'if (b is <= 1600 or >= 10000)' then fires on the b = 0 the program never wrote, and the reference returns the §15.3 default 0 (or aborts the run unit under >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON). MEASURED BY DERIVATION, not sampling: in 2026 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(F)' with F = 76 must be 2076 by r3 + r5 + r2a (max 2076, MOD 76 >= 76); it is 0. The 'off = 50' default is therefore present in the declaration and UNREACHABLE TO ANY RESULT on that carrier - the function is never 'evaluated as though 50 were specified for argument-2', because it is never evaluated at all. (3) THE THIRD LANE CONFIRMS WHICH BODY IS WRONG. Under --arithmetic standard, NumericRenderer.cs#Landed line 649 de-Reals the operand, AnyRealArgument answers FALSE, RenderDec has no YearToYyyy arm, and the native switch arm at IntrinsicRenderer.cs line 308 emits CobolDate.YearToYyyy(IntegerArgReal(<double>)) - the ONE-argument EXACT overload, which is correct. So the SAME source answers 2076 under --arithmetic standard and 0 under the default native mode. (4) THE TEST DOES NOT CLOSE THE RULE. CobolDateWindowingTests.cs line 41 asserts 'CobolDate.YearToYyyy(76)' - it calls the EXACT overload at the C# runtime API directly. It never compiles a COBOL one-argument reference, never reaches the renderer's lane dispatch, and cannot see YearToYyyyReal. It closes the exact carrier's half and nothing else. ONE OF TWO CARRIERS VERIFIED => PARTIAL (rule 5). Not DIVERGES: the wrong answer's mechanism is the argument-3 sentinel, already recorded in full under AR-15.100.3-5, and r3's own default value 50 is correctly written on both bodies - counting the same defect twice as DIVERGES would overstate the fan-out. code-location kept at CobolDate.cs#YearToYyyy: that is where r3's default is implemented AND correct; the residue is the second body named above.

subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.3 'Argument-3 shall be an integer greater than 1600 and less than 10000' OK (rule 4). RANGE HALF - READ CobolDate.cs line 123: 'if (b is <= 1600 or >= 10000) return ExceptionState.ArgumentError("...is not greater than 1600 and less than 10000 (§15.100.3 r4)")'. Both bounds are STRICT exactly as the rule words them: 1600 is rejected, 1601 passes, 9999 passes, 10000 is rejected. It is validated AS WRITTEN (kb/Work PB65 replaced an in-band baseYear == 0 sentinel that resolved to the clock year BEFORE the range test, so an explicit 0 silently windowed); the two-overload arity split at lines 108-111 is what makes 'written' distinguishable from 'omitted'. Tested through the shared core: tests/conformance/2023/pb65_date_windowing.cob writes 'FUNCTION DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 0)' and .out pins ZERO-A3=00000000 - the delegation at CobolDate.cs line 149 calls this same YearToYyyyAt, so the r4 branch is the one exercised, though no fixture writes the r4 violation on YEAR-TO-YYYY ITSELF and neither the 1600/1601 nor the 9999/10000 boundary is pinned. WHY NOT CONFORMS: the 'shall be an integer' half has the same unscreened sibling as r1/r2 - a floating-point argument-3 passes IntrinsicArgumentRules#IntegerViolation (Scale 0, IsFloat) and CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#TryIntegerArg truncates it toward zero instead of setting EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, so 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(4, 23, F)' with F holding 1995.9 evaluates as 1995. REFUTED: REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at PARTIAL, but the adjudicator recorded only ONE of the two reasons and missed the more harmful one. cite.py --check 15.100.3 'Argument-3 shall be an integer greater than 1600 and less than 10000' -> OK §15.100.3 4). Range half re-read at CobolDate.cs lines 123-124 - both bounds strict as worded, confirmed. Fixture re-read: pb65_date_windowing.cob line 22 writes DATE-TO-YYYYMMDD(851003, 10, 0) and the .out pins ZERO-A3=00000000; line 20 writes a direct 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(50, 10, 1900)' pinned YY-A3=1850 (r2b: 10 < 50 => 50+100x18). THE SECOND, UNRECORDED HALF - r4 FIRES SPURIOUSLY ON A FORM THAT OMITS ARGUMENT-3. r4 constrains argument-3 only when argument-3 is WRITTEN; when it is omitted, r5 supplies the execution year and there is no r4 question to ask. On the float carrier there is no arity distinction to make that determination with: RealArgs.cs line 107's single method fills baseYear = 0 for the 1- and 2-argument forms alike, so 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(F, 23)' - a reference containing no argument-3 at all - takes the line-123 r4 branch and, under EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking, aborts the run unit with 'YEAR-TO-YYYY argument-3 0 is not greater than 1600'. That is r4's REJECT disposition delivered where the rule requires no disposition, naming an argument the programmer never wrote. The exact carrier cannot do this - CobolDate.cs lines 108-111 are TWO overloads, which is exactly the PB65 'omitted-ness is the ARITY, never a value' discipline that was never propagated to the float body. So r4 has BOTH an unscreened integer-ness half (the adjudicator's finding, confirmed) AND a spurious-reject half. PARTIAL stands; the residue is larger than recorded.

subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.3 'The sum of the values of argument-2 and argument-3 shall be less than 10000 and greater than 1699' OK (rule 6). READ CobolDate.cs lines 125-127: 'long max = off + b; if (max is <= 1699 or >= 10000) return ExceptionState.ArgumentError("argument-2 + argument-3 = {max} is not greater than 1699 and less than 10000 (§15.100.3 r6)")'. Both bounds strict and on the SUM, matching the rule word for word (1699 rejected, 1700 accepted, 9999 accepted, 10000 rejected), and the test runs AFTER the r4 test so a defaulted argument-3 is already the resolved value the sum is taken over. The check is in the shared core, so the delegating pair inherits it. OVERFLOW CHECKED, not assumed: 'off + b' is long arithmetic with b constrained to 1601..9999 by r4, so a positive overflow can only wrap to a NEGATIVE value, which <= 1699 catches - no wrapped sum can land inside the legal window (an out-of-long argument is stopped earlier by the PB22 range guard). Tested: tests/conformance/2023/pb65_date_windowing.cob 'FUNCTION DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(85365, 9000, 1995)' (9000+1995 = 10995) pins R6VIOL=0000000 with the derivation written from r6 in the header, and the delegation at CobolDate.cs line 169 reaches this exact branch. The r6 violation is not written directly on YEAR-TO-YYYY in any fixture, but it is the same statement in the same method. REFUTED: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. cite.py --check 15.100.3 'The sum of the values of argument-2 and argument-3 shall be less than 10000 and greater than 1699' -> OK §15.100.3 6). The guard itself is right and I confirm the adjudicator's reading of CobolDate.cs lines 125-127 verbatim, INCLUDING the overflow argument, which I checked rather than accepted: there is no CheckForOverflowUnderflow anywhere in Directory.Build.props or any csproj, so 'off + b' is unchecked; with b in 1601..9999 only a POSITIVE overflow is reachable and it wraps to at most long.MinValue + 9998, which '<= 1699' catches - no wrapped sum can land in the legal window. WHY IT IS STILL NOT CONFORMS. r6 constrains 'the sum of the VALUES of argument-2 and argument-3' - the values AFTER r3/r5 have supplied the omitted ones. On the float carrier the value of an omitted argument-3 is the literal 0 (RealArgs.cs line 107 'double baseYear = 0', body calling the three-argument core), so for the ONE- and TWO-argument references the sum r6 governs is never formed and never tested: YearToYyyyAt returns at the r4 guard on line 123, two lines BEFORE 'long max = off + b' on line 125. Concretely, 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(F, 23)' over a COMP-2 F, evaluated in 2026, has a resolved sum of 23 + 2026 = 2049 that r6 REQUIRES to be admitted; the compiler instead answers the §15.3 default 0 and, under checking, aborts naming argument-3. r6's ACCEPT side is therefore not delivered on that carrier for two of the three arities the §15.100.2 format admits - one carrier verified, one not, which rule 5 makes PARTIAL always. The test-ref does not close it either: conformance:2023/pb65_date_windowing's R6VIOL line writes DAY-TO-YYYYDDD(85365, 9000, 1995), not YEAR-TO-YYYY, and 10995 is far outside the window - NEITHER boundary pair (1699/1700, 9999/10000) is pinned by any fixture, on any function. Kept as the test-ref because it does reach this branch, but it closes the reject side only.

subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.4 'Maximum-year is calculated as follows' OK (rule 1); the expression is '(argument-2 + argument-3)'. READ CobolDate.cs line 125: 'long max = off + b;   // r1: maximum-year' - a literal transcription of the rule, computed AFTER r4 has validated argument-3 and used by both r2 arms. The operands are the resolved arguments including the r3/r5 defaults (off = 50 from the overload default; b = the clock year on the omitted form), which is what 'the values of argument-2 and argument-3' means once r3/r5 have applied. Signed argument-2 is honoured: no abs, no clamp - conformance:2002/intrinsics_date_window T2 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(98, -15, 2008)' pins 1898, which only comes out if max = 1993 (the spec's own §15.100.4 NOTE-1 value, derived in the fixture header, not sampled). T1 (4, 23, 1995) => max 2018 => 2004 pins the positive case. There is exactly ONE site computing maximum-year and the delegating pair (§15.23.4 r1 / §15.25.4 r1) reaches it, so no second transcription can drift. REFUTED: REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL, on the adjudicator's own load-bearing sentence: 'The operands are the resolved arguments including the r3/r5 defaults (off = 50 from the overload default; b = the clock year on the omitted form)'. That is true of CobolDate.cs and FALSE of CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs, where b on the omitted form is the literal 0 - the second body the record never opened. cite.py --check 15.100.4 'Maximum-year is calculated as follows' -> OK §15.100.4 1). The transcription at CobolDate.cs line 125 ('long max = off + b;   // r1: maximum-year') is exact and I confirm it, and I also confirm the signed-argument-2 evidence: intrinsics_date_window.cob line 24 writes 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(98, -15, 2008)' with 1898 derived from §15.100.4 NOTE 1 in the fixture header, which only comes out at max = 1993. WHY PARTIAL. This rule's whole content is an arithmetic statement over the RESOLVED values of argument-2 and argument-3. On the float carrier, for the one- and two-argument references, maximum-year is not merely computed from a wrong argument-3 - it is NEVER COMPUTED AT ALL: RealArgs.cs line 107 fills baseYear = 0, line 109 calls the three-argument core, and YearToYyyyAt returns at the r4 guard on line 123, two lines before line 125 executes. In 2026 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(F, 23)' over a COMP-2 F has maximum-year 2049 by this rule; the compiler produces no maximum-year and answers the §15.3 default 0. The adjudicator's closing claim - 'There is exactly ONE site computing maximum-year ... so no second transcription can drift' - is correct about transcription and is the wrong question: the defect is not a drifted copy of the expression, it is a second path that never reaches the one copy. One carrier verified, one not => PARTIAL (rule 5). code-location unchanged: line 125 IS the rule's implementation and it is correct; the residue is the reachability on RealArgs.cs#YearToYyyyReal.

subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: cite.py --check 15.100.4 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows' OK (rule 2); --check 15.100.4 'In the year 1995, the returned value for FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY (4, 23) is 2004' OK (NOTE 1, anchored under 2) a)). READ CobolDate.cs lines 128-130: 'return max % 100 >= yy ? yy + 100 * (max / 100) : yy + 100 * (max / 100 - 1);' - arm a is 'argument-1 + 100 * (FUNCTION INTEGER (maximum-year/100))' guarded by 'FUNCTION MOD (maximum-year, 100) >= argument-1', arm b subtracts 1, both transcribed exactly. THE OPERATOR EQUIVALENCE IS EARNED, NOT ASSUMED: FUNCTION MOD is a true modulo and FUNCTION INTEGER is a FLOOR, which differ from C# '%' and '/' only for a negative dividend - and r6 (enforced two lines above) guarantees maximum-year >= 1700 > 0, so on every path that reaches this expression the two agree. The result is therefore always >= 1601, which is what makes the errored-path 0 an unambiguous sentinel for the delegating wrappers (lines 153/172). BOTH ARMS ARE TESTED against hand-derived values: conformance:2002/intrinsics_date_window T1 (r2a, 2004) and T2 (r2b, 1898) are the spec's own NOTE-1 pair, T3/T4 straddle the r2a/r2b boundary at the same maximum-year 2049 (49 => 2049, 50 => 1950), T5 pins argument-1 = 0 under r2a; unit:CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_SpecNote1_Examples re-pins the NOTE-1 pair at the runtime API. NOTE 2 is informative (a sliding vs fixed window description) and describes the implemented behavior: argument-3 omitted reads the execution-time clock (sliding), a written argument-2 + argument-3 fixes the ending year. REFUTED: REFUTED: verdict UPHELD at CONFORMS - I tried to break the operator-equivalence argument and it holds. cite.py --check 15.100.4 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows' -> OK §15.100.4 2). Both arms re-read at CobolDate.cs lines 128-130 and matched against the rendered spec text at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 34090-34106: arm a is guarded by 'FUNCTION MOD (maximum-year, 100) >= argument-1' and arm b subtracts 1, transcribed exactly. I RE-DERIVED THE EQUIVALENCE RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT: C# '%' and '/' agree with FUNCTION MOD (true modulo) and FUNCTION INTEGER (floor) only for a non-negative dividend, and r6 - enforced two lines above at line 126 - guarantees maximum-year >= 1700, so every path that reaches this expression has a positive dividend. I also re-derived the result range the delegating wrappers depend on: arm a yields [1700, 9999]; arm b fires only when MOD(max,100) < argument-1, so at the minimum max = 1700 it requires argument-1 >= 1 and yields 1600 + argument-1 in [1601, 1699]. The floor is 1601, never 1600, so the errored-path 0 really is an unambiguous sentinel for lines 153 and 172. Both arms are pinned to hand-derived spec values by conformance:2002/intrinsics_date_window (T1/T2 = the §15.100.4 NOTE-1 pair; T3/T4 straddle the arm boundary at maximum-year 2049) and re-pinned at the runtime API by CobolDateWindowingTests.YearToYyyy_SpecNote1_Examples, whose values I checked against NOTE 1 myself. A third direct YEAR-TO-YYYY arm-b line exists that the record did not cite: pb65_date_windowing.cob line 20 'FUNCTION YEAR-TO-YYYY(50, 10, 1900)' pinned YY-A3=1850. CAVEAT, deliberately NOT a downgrade: like every rule here, this expression is unreachable on the float carrier's one- and two-argument references (see AR-15.100.3-5). Unlike r6 and RV-15.100.4-1 - whose text is about the RESOLVED ARGUMENT VALUES, which that carrier corrupts - this rule is a pure function of maximum-year and argument-1 and is completely and correctly implemented wherever it executes. Downgrading it too would count one defect three times and misreport a finished transcription as partial.

subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: Read the format at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22600-22604 (no 'Figure notes' block accompanies this diagram, so the transcribed <pre> IS the authority): ALLOCATE { arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 } [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ], with ALLOCATE / CHARACTERS / INITIALIZED / RETURNING underlined and no optional noise words. Read grammar rule `allocateStatement`: two alternatives, `ALLOCATE arithmeticExpression CHARACTERS INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` and `ALLOCATE dataReference INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` — arm-for-arm identical to the diagram, both optional phrases optional in both arms, and no scope terminator / conditional phrase (matching Table 12's empty ALLOCATE row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:20867). Alternative order is safe because alt 1 requires the CHARACTERS token, so a bare data-name falls to alt 2 under ALL(*) prediction. The binder's `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` reads `al.dataReference()` (DIRECT children only, so data-names inside arithmeticExpression are not in the list) and indexes drefs[0] for data-name-1 / drefs[^1] for RETURNING — correct for all four legs, and the RETURNING()-null guard precedes the index so the no-RETURNING form cannot index an empty list. All five surface legs have goldens: `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P`, `ALLOCATE W INITIALIZED`, `ALLOCATE 6 CHARACTERS INITIALIZED RETURNING P2` (2002/allocate_initialized), `ALLOCATE B` and `ALLOCATE 5 CHARACTERS RETURNING P` (2002/pointer_alloc). Editions: ALLOCATE appears in neither the 2023 new-features list (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 1100-1130) nor Annex E, so there is no 2014->2023 delta; it cannot be COBOL-85 because SR1 requires the BASED clause and SR3 requires category data-pointer, neither of which the 1985 standard has. || UPHELD: I re-read specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22598-22604 myself — the <pre> reads exactly `ALLOCATE ┤ arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 ├ [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ]`, brackets with NO choice-indicator bars, so INITIALIZED-before-RETURNING is a fixed order and the grammar's `INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` tail matches it in both arms. I re-read `allocateStatement` at CobolParserCore.g4:1244-1247 and `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` at PtrBinder.cs:99-138: for form 1 with RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[^1] is it; for form 2 without RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[0] is it; for form 2 with RETURNING drefs is [based, returning] and both indexes are right — all four index legs re-derived, not taken on trust. I do NOT rest on the ALL(*) prediction argument: `ALLOCATE B.` and `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P.` are ENABLED goldens with byte-compared .out, which is empirical proof alt 2 is reachable. Edition re-derived independently of the code catalog: ALLOCATE is absent from Annex E (§E.2/§E.3, specs/ISO_COBOL.md 42858-44000), and §13.18.x SR16 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:15101 — 'The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section, in the working-storage section, and in the local-storage section. subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Re-read the format in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23190 and validated it mechanically (`cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK, returning the whole format line). Derived expectation BEFORE reading code, from the repaired Figure-notes block: CONTINUE is a required word (the printed missing underline is the C2 typo), the bracket makes the whole phrase optional, and AFTER / SECONDS carry underline rules so they are REQUIRED inside the phrase; the operand is arithmetic-expression-1 (a full 8.8.1 arithmetic expression, not a mere identifier/literal). READ: `continueStatement : CONTINUE (AFTER arithmeticExpression SECONDS)? ;` (CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363). Token-for-token identical to the derived shape: CONTINUE mandatory (so `AFTER 5 SECONDS` alone cannot parse as a CONTINUE, the Figure-notes' second argument), the group is `( ... )?` (bracket), AFTER and SECONDS are hard tokens inside it (not `AFTER?` / `SECONDS?`), so `CONTINUE 5` is rejected. The operand nonterminal is the SHARED `arithmeticExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4:208 -> additiveExpression -> multiplicative -> power), i.e. the same 8.8.1 rule PERFORM VARYING uses, so a parenthesized/compound expression, a literal, an identifier and a function reference are all admitted -- not a narrowed operand. The grammar's own header comment (CobolControlFlow.g4:359-360) records the same page-604-vs-page-732 contradiction the Figure notes do and resolves it the same way (the defining occurrence governs), so the transcription and the grammar agree rather than one having inherited the other's typo. Wired into the single `statement` rule at CobolParserCore.g4:719. EDITION (derived from Annex E, NOT from the registry's own IntroducedIn column): Annex E.3.3 item 14 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957 -- "Additional functionality added to the CONTINUE statement. The CONTINUE statement has been enhanced to provide the ability to pause runtime execution for a specified period of time" -- so the bracketed phrase is 2023-only while bare CONTINUE is 85-continuous. The compiler gates exactly that split: VersionConformancePass.VisitContinueStatement fires COBOLNET0900 only when `ctx.arithmeticExpression()` is present (Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs:584-589), i.e. on the PHRASE, never on the verb -- confirmed by 85/wavef_dbg_proc.cob and 85/index_name_r7_windows.cob compiling bare CONTINUE at --std 85. TESTED: 2023/continue_after exercises both operand forms (a literal `AFTER 0` and a data item `AFTER WS-N`); the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` drives VersionMatrixTests.Construct_MatchesEditionExpectation and IntroducedConstruct_IsRejectedUnderPermissive, so the below-2023 rejection is asserted at 85/2002/2014 and is not waived by --permissive. NOT exercised anywhere: a COMPOUND arithmetic-expression-1 (`CONTINUE AFTER N + 1 SECONDS`); that is a shared-nonterminal reuse rather than a private parse, so it does not cost the verdict. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-ran all three cite checks myself -- `cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK (General format), and read the format + Figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23189-23212 before opening any code. I re-read CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363 and CobolParserCore.g4:719 directly. I additionally checked the two edges the adjudicator did not: (a) `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4) admits a LEADING SIGN, so `CONTINUE AFTER -1 SECONDS` -- the literal spelling of the GR1a negative case -- parses, and `primaryExpression` admits numericLiteral / ZERO_ARITH / functionCall / dataReference / `( arithmeticExpression )`, so the operand really is the full 8.8.1 rule; (b) the SECONDS terminator cannot be swallowed by the operand, because `additiveExpression` stops at a non-addOp token and `dataReference` is single-word except for OF/IN qualification. I verified the test-refs are LIVE rather than merely present: tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json lists `continue_after` at enabled[22], and tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/VersionMatrixTests.cs:79/:124 are the two named methods; the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` carries source `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS.` with expectDiagnostic COBOLNET0900. || REFUTED (edition-basis citation, verdict unchanged): the adjudicator wrote "E.2's new-reserved-word list at :43951 adds SECONDS". That is WRONG on both counts and I did not inherit it. Line 43951 sits inside Annex **E.3.3 item 13** (heading at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43225 `E.3.3 Not affecting`), whose lead sentence is "**Context-sensitive words.** In order to provide enhanced functionality, the following words have either been added to the list of context-sensitive words or the context in which they are reserved has been expanded" -- SECONDS is in the CONTEXT-SENSITIVE list, not a reserved-word list. The 8.10 context-sensitive-words table at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:9578 confirms it: `| SECONDS | RETRY phrase, CONTINUE statement |`. The compiler agrees with the STANDARD and not with the adjudicator's note: CobolLexer.g4:562-568 comments SECONDS as "8.10 context-sensitive (user-legal at every edition)" and CobolWords.g4:89 re-admits it as a user word. This does not move the verdict -- the AFTER phrase's 2023 introduction rests on E.3.3 item 14, which I checked and which stands -- but the note's edition evidence was an uncited (and false) claim, exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 1 names, and is replaced above.

subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: READ: displayStatement : DISPLAY (dataReference | literal | functionCall)+ displayUpon? displayNoAdvancing? END_DISPLAY? ; displayUpon : UPON cobolWord ; displayNoAdvancing : WITH? NO ADVANCING (CobolParserCore.g4 lines 1300-1310). FORMAT 1 MATCHES the printed diagram element for element: the '...' operand repetition is '+', UPON is optional, WITH is an OPTIONAL word (it is NOT underlined in the format, and the grammar's 'WITH?' honours that), NO/ADVANCING are required, END-DISPLAY is optional, and a function-identifier is admitted in the identifier-1 slot per 8.4.3.1.2 (the grammar comment cites it). FORMAT 2 (screen) IS ENTIRELY ABSENT: there is no screen-name-1 arm, no AT [LINE NUMBER ...] [{COLUMN|COL} NUMBER ...] phrase, and no ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION pair. AT (CobolLexer.g4:411), LINE (:556) and EXCEPTION (:494) are dedicated lexer tokens and NONE of them is an alternative of cobolWord (CobolWords.g4 lines 9-120 -- COL and COLUMN are, AT/LINE/EXCEPTION are not), so 'DISPLAY SG AT LINE 5 COL 10 ON EXCEPTION ...' is a PARSE ERROR, not a mis-bind. The repaired Figure notes therefore have nothing to be compared against: the AT phrase's brace-enclosed choice indicators (one-or-more, any order) and the exception pair's bracket-enclosed indicators (zero-or-more, any order -- BOTH ON EXCEPTION and NOT ON EXCEPTION admissible on one statement, either order) are unimplemented along with the format. SECOND DEFECT, Format 1 side: END-DISPLAY is accepted at EVERY --std, 85 included. src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs:151 records new("END-DISPLAY", false, true, true, true, "high", "added 2002 ...") -- R85 = false -- yet tests/version-matrix/constructs.json has no end-display-* row and VersionConformancePass has no VisitDisplayStatement (grep: only VisitAcceptStatement, which gates Constructs.EndAccept2002). So the project's own reserved-word catalog says the terminator is a 2002 introduction while the gating funnel admits it at 1985 with no diagnostic -- the ACCEPT twin at least carries a registered construct. WOULD CLOSE THE ROW: (a) the Format-2 grammar + binder + a golden, (b) an end-display-2002 construct row plus the mandatory edition-gate negative fixture at --std 85. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-read specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 23402-23433 and CobolParserCore.g4:1300-1310 and CobolWords.g4:9-120 myself. Format-1 element-for-element agreement CONFIRMED, including the two things worth naming: (i) figurativeConstant is the FIRST alternative of nonNumericLiteral (CobolExpressions.g4:499-506) which is an alternative of literal, so DISPLAY SPACE / DISPLAY ZERO bind as LITERAL operands and are not lost from the operand list; (ii) ZERO/SPACE/HIGH-VALUE are NOT alternatives of cobolWord, so the dataReference alternative (listed first) cannot steal them. Format-2 absence CONFIRMED. The keyword-omitted intrinsic reference (REPOSITORY 'FUNCTION name INTRINSIC', 8.4.3.2 SR2) is NOT an extra Format-1 gap: it arrives through the dataReference alternative and ExpressionBinder.FieldOperand resolves it (ControlFlowBinder.cs:260 states this contract). || REFUTED (method, not verdict) on the END-DISPLAY leg: the adjudicator derived the EDITION of END-DISPLAY from src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs -- a catalog INSIDE the code under review, which ground rule 4 forbids as an edition source (it is the same shape as trusting a constructs.json IntroducedIn column). Re-derived independently and the CONCLUSION survives, so the verdict stands: END-DISPLAY exists in the standard only because 14.9.11.2 Format 2 gives DISPLAY the [NOT] ON EXCEPTION conditional phrases (an explicit scope terminator is meaningless for a statement with no conditional phrase), and Format 2 is the screen facility, absent from the 1985 statement; the compiler's own TWIN confirms the intended posture -- ConstructRegistry.g.cs:174 carries new("end-accept-2002", "END-ACCEPT (explicit scope terminator)", 2002, null, null, "COBOLNET0816", ...) and VersionConformancePass.cs:1362 checks it, while grep for END-DISPLAY across src/ + tests/version-matrix finds ONLY the lexer token, the grammar reference and the reserved-word row: no construct row, no Check call, no negative fixture. The DEFECT is therefore the ASYMMETRY itself (one of two twin terminators gated), which is true whatever edition number the eventual derivation assigns. Verdict PARTIAL upheld: Format 1 is implemented and spec-pinned, Format 2 is wholly absent, so neither CONFORMS nor NOT-IMPLEMENTED is available. EDITIONS held at the batch default: Annex E covers only the 2014->2023 delta and carries no DISPLAY item (grepped lines 42847-44027), and the rule text carries no edition marker, so per ground rule 4 the default stands even though Format 2 is manifestly post-1985 -- flagged here so a later edition-derivation pass narrows the Format-2 rows rather than inheriting this field.

subject: DIVIDE statement
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB134): the admit half was already pinned (all five formats bind; the 5.2.6.4 both-phrases and 5.2.3 optional-ON figure-note claims are spec-derived goldens); the REJECT half now exists - all five measured non-format shapes draw COBOLNET1689 at bind: `DIVIDE A BY B.` (every BY format prints GIVING), REMAINDER without GIVING, a multi-quotient REMAINDER (SR6's exactly-one), `DIVIDE A INTO B C GIVING D` (the silent drop of C), and `DIVIDE 2 INTO 10.` - the shape that CRASHED the compiler (ArithmeticEmitter's targets.Max on an empty receiver list, unhandled through the CLI). subject: OPEN statement
notes:
kb/Work PB316; PB236. SHAPE: correct. The printed format is OPEN { {INPUT|OUTPUT|I-O|EXTEND} [sharing-phrase] [retry-phrase] {file-name-1 [WITH NO REWIND]} … } … (cite.py --check 14.9.27.2 "sharing-phrase" OK), and the grammar is its exact image: openStatement : OPEN openClause+ / openClause : openMode (sharingPhrase)? (retryPhrase)? openFileSpec+ — outer group repeatable (openClause+), mode mandatory and single-choice (openMode), both phrases optional and in the printed order, file list one-or-more per group, NO REWIND per file. The figure notes' optional-word ruling is honoured on both sides: WITH is optional in openFileSpec (WITH? NO REWIND) and in sharingPhrase (SHARING WITH? sharingMode), and sharingMode's OTHER is optional (ALL OTHER? | NO OTHER? | READ ONLY) per the §12.4.5.15.2 figure notes, which underline ALL/NO/READ/ONLY but not WITH/OTHER. The one extra alternative, REVERSED, is the deleted '85 tape phrase and is edition-gated out at ≥2002 (VersionConformancePass#VisitOpenFileSpec → Constructs.OpenReversedRemoved2002 → COBOLNET0902), pinned by conformance:negative/open-reversed.
WHY NOT CONFORMS — two of the format's own constituents are parsed and then dropped, so the row is implemented on the syntax path and not on the meaning path.
(a) THE REPEATED GROUP'S SCOPE IS DISCARDED AT BIND. sharing-phrase and retry-phrase sit INSIDE the outer repeatable group, next to the file-names they govern; the figure note says so outright (“the OUTER braces enclose the entire group `{ open-mode } [ sharing-phrase ] [ retry-phrase ] { file-name-1 [ WITH NO REWIND ] } …`”) and §14.9.27.4 GR20 confirms the reading (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 "These separate OPEN statements would each have the same open mode specification, the sharing-phrase, retry-phrase, and REWIND phrase as specified in the OPEN statement." OK) — the mode is unambiguously per-group, so the phrases listed beside it are too. SequentialIoBinder.BindOpen declares `SharingMode? sharing` and `RetrySpec? retry` OUTSIDE `foreach (var clause in o.openClause())`, never resets them per clause, and hands the last value to ONE statement-wide BoundOpen.SharingOverride / BoundOpen.Retry, whose own doc-comment says “Applies to every file in the statement”; SequentialIoEmitter.EmitOpen then routes every file of the statement through FileOpenShared with that single override. MEASURED (probe/open-p1): leak1.cob (`OPEN INPUT FA` then `OPEN INPUT SHARING WITH NO OTHER FB`, the GR20 reference form) prints A=00 B=00; leak2.cob, the same thing written as ONE statement with two groups, prints A=00 B=61 — FA was opened with FB's sharing phrase and became an exclusive holder of the shared physical file. GR20 requires the two forms to be indistinguishable.
(b) file-name-1's OPERAND CATEGORY IS NEVER CHECKED. openFileSpec takes `dataReference`, and BindOpen resolves it only by `ctx.Data.FilesByName.TryGetValue(…)`; a miss returns BoundUnsupported, which StatementEmitter renders as a LOUD RUNTIME STAGE, not a compile error. MEASURED: und1.cob (`OPEN OUTPUT WS-X`, WS-X a WORKING-STORAGE item) compiles clean at 2023 and dies at run time with “NotImplementedCobolFeatureException … OPEN of undeclared file 'WS-X'” — illegal source accepted, and mislabelled as a compiler limitation. BindClose has the identical shape (the sibling).
The runtime consequence of (a) is adjudicated on the §14.9.27.4 GR20/GR22/GR23 rows, which are in part 3 of this subject, not here; this row records that the format's grouping is lost before those rules can be applied. Editions: OPEN is in all four; the sharing-phrase is A.4.7 item 6 and the retry-phrase §14.7.9, both absent from COBOL-85 and both gated COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 (measured on shrA.cob).
ADDENDUM FOR kb/Work PB159 (open — NOT a new finding, and deliberately not filed as one): PB159's hand-verified table lists CobolIO.g4:250 and :279 in this cluster and leaves ~84 heuristic candidates unverified. Four more in the SAME cluster are now hand-verified with cite.py, each a REAL clause naming a DIFFERENT statement (§14.9.25 = MOVE, §14.9.26 = MULTIPLY, §14.9.7 = COMMIT; OPEN is §14.9.27 and CLOSE §14.9.6): VersionConformancePass.cs:634 (“NO REWIND … survives into 2023 §14.9.26”), BoundTree.cs:855 (BoundOpenMode “ISO §14.9.25”), BoundTree.cs:858 (BoundCloseKind “ISO §14.9.7”), BoundTree.cs:887 (BoundOpen “ISO §14.9.25”) and BoundTree.cs:901 (BoundClose “ISO §14.9.7”). Findings: OPEN-P1-M1, OPEN-P1-M3.

subject: READ statement
notes:
kb/Work PB331; PB332. THE PRINTED FIGURE WAS MEASURED, NOT INHERITED. `python scripts/spec/clause_page.py 14.9.30.2` -> PDF page 722 / folio 692. `figure_geometry.py 722` reports, in printed order: Format 1 = bracket y=280.90 h=48.79 (three stacked alternatives: ADVANCING ON LOCK / IGNORING LOCK / retry-phrase), bracket y=339.26 h=31.98 (WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK), then '[ | | ]  <-- CHOICE INDICATORS (5.2.6.4)' at y=377.08 (AT END / NOT AT END); Format 2 = bracket y=507.57 (IGNORING LOCK / retry-phrase), bracket y=547.48 (WITH LOCK / WITH NO LOCK), bracket y=589.03 h=39.68 (KEY IS ...), then choice indicators at y=634.55 (INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY). `figure_extract.py 722` prints the underlining: `_ADVANCING_ ON _LOCK_`, `WITH _LOCK_`, `WITH _NO_ _LOCK_`, `_KEY_ IS`, `AT _END_`, `_INVALID_ KEY`, `RECORD` bare, `NEXT` bare, `_PREVIOUS_` underlined. Citation checked: `cite.py --check 14.9.30.2 "where retry-phrase is described in 14.7.9, RETRY phrase"` OK. FOUR CONFIRMED DEFECTS, each with a run probe.
(1) FORMAT-2 PHRASE ORDER IS INVERTED (rejects legal source). The grammar's readStatement places `readKey?` BEFORE `readAdvancingOnLock? retryPhrase? recordLockPhrase?`, but the figure places the KEY bracket AFTER both lock brackets. `READ IXF RECORD WITH NO LOCK KEY IS IX-KEY INVALID KEY ... END-READ` -> `error COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'KEY'`; identically for `IGNORING LOCK KEY IS ...` and `RETRY 3 TIMES KEY IS ...`. The reverse (non-printed) order `KEY IS IX-KEY WITH NO LOCK` compiles. Probe: out-b1/probe/keyorder/spec_{nolock,ignoring,retry}.cob vs rev.cob.
(2) THE TWO FORMAT-1 BRACKETS ARE COLLAPSED INTO ONE SLOT (rejects legal source AND under-rejects). `recordLockPhrase : IGNORING LOCK | WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK` puts bracket-1's IGNORING LOCK into bracket-2's slot. Consequence a: `READ SQF NEXT RECORD IGNORING LOCK WITH NO LOCK AT END ... END-READ` -> COBOL0001, though the figure's two INDEPENDENT plain brackets permit one alternative from each and SR3 forbids only IGNORING LOCK with 'the LOCK phrase' -- the standard names WITH NO LOCK separately as 'the NO LOCK phrase' (checked: `cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 "except when the NO LOCK phrase is specified and the record accessed was already locked by that file connector"` OK; GR11d 'the LOCK phrase' OK). Consequence b: `ADVANCING ON LOCK RETRY 3 TIMES IGNORING LOCK` on one READ COMPILES, though 5.2.6.2 (checked OK) makes a plain bracket 'the syntax element contained within the brackets OR ONE OF THE ALTERNATIVES' -- at most one of the three. Probe: out-b1/probe/lockcombo/seq.cob, seq3.cob.
(3) `ON` IS REQUIRED WHERE THE PAGE PRINTS IT UNDERLINE-FREE (rejects legal source). `readAdvancingOnLock : ADVANCING ON LOCK ;`. Measured: `_ADVANCING_ ON _LOCK_` -- ON carries no underline rule, so per 5.2.3 (checked OK: 'shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity') it is an OPTIONAL word. `READ SQF NEXT RECORD ADVANCING LOCK` -> `error COBOL0001: missing token before 'LOCK'`; `ADVANCING ON LOCK` compiles. Probe: seq5.cob/seq6.cob.
(4) FORMAT 1's `PREVIOUS` ALTERNATIVE IS PARSED AND DISCARDED ON THE SEQUENTIAL-ORGANIZATION ARM (wrong answer). SequentialIoBinder.BindRead never reads `r.readDirection()`; BoundRead carries no direction member. A record-sequential file holding AAA/BBB/CCC, OPEN INPUT, two `READ f PREVIOUS RECORD` -> observed READ1=AAA FS=00, READ2=BBB FS=00. Spec (GR21, sequential-file arm, checked OK): (b) after OPEN the first selected record is made available 'regardless of whether NEXT or PREVIOUS is specified' so READ1=AAA is right; (c) with the FPI established by a prior successful READ, PREVIOUS selects 'the first existing record ... whose relative key number is ... less than the file position indicator' -- none exists -- so READ2 shall be the at end condition with I-O status '10'. The same drop kills the edition gate: `--std 85` on that program emits NO COBOLNET0900, because VersionConformancePass's `case BoundRead sr:` gates only `sr.AdvancingOnLock` while ReadPrevious2002 fires on `BoundKeyedRead.Kind == Previous`. Probe: out-b1/probe/prevseq/prevseq.cob.
ALSO NOTED (not scored): `readStatement : READ (fileName | FILE fileName)` accepts `READ FILE f`, which no ISO format offers -- A.4.13 covers REWRITE FILE and WRITE FILE only. Verified to compile and run (probe seq8.cob). EDITIONS derivation: the 2023 text carries no edition marker on this clause and Annex E is a 2014-to-2023 delta only (E.2 22) 'READ PREVIOUS statement following an OPEN statement' is its single READ entry, which shows PREVIOUS pre-dates 2023 but dates nothing earlier). The column below is the construct's presence in the standard; the phrase-level introduction dates are NOT derivable from this document and are listed as a dossier gap.

subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB347. FORMAT (spec text read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 14.9.32.2): `RELEASE record-name-1 [ FROM { identifier-1 | literal-1 } ]`; the figure note states RELEASE and FROM are the underlined required words, the FROM phrase as a whole is optional, and exactly one of identifier-1 / literal-1 is selected when present. GRAMMAR: `releaseStatement : RELEASE dataReference releaseFrom?` and `releaseFrom : FROM (functionCall | dataReference | literal)` (CobolIO.g4:701/716). ACCEPTED SURFACE VERIFIED by probe out-b1/probe/fmt/fmt.cob (all six forms compile and run correctly): FROM omitted; FROM identifier; FROM subscripted identifier `WS-E(WS-I)`; FROM reference-modified identifier `WS-LONG(3:8)`; FROM alphanumeric literal; FROM figurative constants SPACES and ALL "X" (permitted by 8.3.3.6.3 SR1 -- `--check 8.3.3.6.3 "A figurative constant may be used whenever 'literal' appears in a format or when a rule allows it"` => OK 8.3.3.6.3 1); 14.9.32.3 states no rule prohibiting one). The `functionCall` arm is the deliberate PB10 addition and is legal (8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 makes a function-identifier an IDENTIFIER; `--check 8.4.3.1.2 "function-identifier"` => OK). ||| DIVERGENCE (over-acceptance of the record-name-1 POSITION). The format writes record-name-1, not identifier-1, and 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 confines reference modification to identifier positions -- `--check 8.4.3.3.3 "Unless otherwise specified, reference modification is allowed anywhere an identifier referencing a data item of class alphanumeric, boolean, or national is permitted."` => OK 8.4.3.3.3 5), whose closing NOTE makes it explicit: `--check 8.4.3.3.3 "where data-name-n is used in a general format or syntax rule, then reference-modification is not permitted"` => OK. REPRO out-b1/probe/neg/neg.cob line 26: `RELEASE SRT-REC(1:3).` compiles with NO diagnostic at any --std and emits `CobolSort.Release("RELNEG01::SRTF", CobolString.RefMod(SRT_REC.AsImage(), (int)(1), (int)(3)))` (verified in the generated neg.g.cs), releasing a 3-character record. EXPECTED per 14.9.32.2 + 8.4.3.3.3 SR5/NOTE, and per 4.2.2 (`--check 4.2.2 "An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate violations of the general formats and the explicit syntax rules of standard COBOL."` => OK): a compile-time indication. `dataReference` in the record-name-1 slot is the mechanism -- see finding [release-record-name-not-a-record-name]. ||| EDITION LEG: the literal-1 arm is gated 2002+ (ConstructRegistry.g.cs:191 `release-from-literal-2002` -> COBOLNET0871; probe out-b1/probe/sr4zl at --std 85 rejects, at 2002/2014/2023 accepts). The `functionCall` arm carries NO edition gate (probe out-b1/probe/sr2fn compiles clean at --std 85). Annex E of this document lists no substantive change to 14.9.32, so 2014 and 2023 are identical; the 85/2002 boundary for either arm is NOT derivable from this document (Annex E covers only the previous revision) -- recorded as a dossier gap, not as a verdict.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB350; PB351; PB320. FORMAT RE-DERIVED FROM THE PRINTED PAGE (CLAUDE.md rule 1 - the diagram is load-bearing): python scripts/render-spec-page.py 738 (printed folio 708) renders 'RETURN file-name-1 RECORD [ INTO identifier-1 ] / AT END imperative-statement-1 / [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ] / [ END-RETURN ]'. The AT END line carries NO bracket and NO choice indicators - unlike READ, whose own transcription figure note records the printed bar pair. The markdown transcription is FAITHFUL here. Therefore the AT END phrase is REQUIRED: cite.py --check 5.2.2 'They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword' -> OK, and --check 5.2.6.2 'may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted' -> OK (brackets are the ONLY thing that makes a portion omissible). RECORD and AT are un-underlined optional words: --check 8.3.2.4.3 'uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option' -> OK. CODE: CobolIO.g4:679 returnStatement writes 'returnAtEndPhrase?' - the WHOLE phrase optional - and returnAtEndPhrase's second alternative 'NOT AT? END statementBlock (AT? END statementBlock)?' makes the AT END half of the reversed pair optional too. SortBinder.BindReturn:268-273 accepts atEnd=null (PhraseBlocks.Split returns (null, first) for the NOT-led single-block form) and SortEmitter.EmitReturn:172-180 then emits an EMPTY else arm. grep over src for returnAtEndPhrase: SortBinder.cs:269 is the ONLY consumer - no later pass enforces it. REPRO A (probe p1, out-b1/probe/p1/p1.cob): a SORT OUTPUT PROCEDURE whose body is 'RETURN SF RECORD END-RETURN. DISPLAY "R=" S-TXT.' looped 4 times. EXPECTED from the format: rejected at compile time (no AT END phrase). OBSERVED: compiles clean and runs at --std 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023, printing R=ONE / R=TWO / R=TWO / R=TWO - past end-of-file the record area silently keeps the last record. REPRO B (probe p2): 'RETURN SF NOT AT END DISPLAY "R=" S-TXT END-RETURN.' - the NOT-only form, equally illegal (SR4 permits reversal only 'when specified', and AT END is unconditionally specified) - accepted at all four editions. SECOND MECHANISM ON THE SAME ROW: statementBlock (CobolParserCore.g4:793) is 'statement+', so a conditional statement NOT delimited by its explicit scope terminator is accepted where the format writes imperative-statement-1. Spec: 14.5.1 - 'An imperative statement specifies an unconditional action ... or is a conditional statement that is delimited by its explicit scope terminator' and 'Any statement with a conditional phrase that is not terminated by its explicit scope terminator is a conditional statement'. Probe p12 ('AT END IF WS-EOF = "N" MOVE "Y" TO WS-EOF NOT AT END DISPLAY ...' with no END-IF) compiles and runs. This one is cross-cutting - readAtEnd and every sibling conditional phrase share statementBlock. CONFORMING PARTS, verified: RECORD? and AT? (optional words), the INTO / NOT AT END / END-RETURN brackets, operand order, and the SR4 reversed pair. TWO INHERITED-CITATION DEFECTS in the implementing grammar file (CLAUDE.md rule 1's named failure mode): CobolIO.g4:687 justifies AT? with 'ISO 14.9.39 - "AT" is an optional reserved word', but 14.9.39 is the SET statement (--check 14.9.39.1 'The SET statement provides a means for' -> OK); the authority is 8.3.2.4.3. CobolIO.g4:698 heads the RELEASE block '// RELEASE (14.9.33)', but 14.9.33 is RESUME (--check 14.9.33.1 -> OK) and RELEASE is 14.9.32 (--check 14.9.32.1 'The RELEASE statement transfers records to the initial phase of a sort operation.' -> OK). No kb/Work note owns these rows; a register note is owed.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB332; PB320. RULE (--check 14.9.41.2, figure note): 'START, FIRST, KEY (the phrase-leading one), LAST, LENGTH, INVALID, NOT, and END-START are underlined in the printed standard (required words); file-name-1, relational-operator, WITH, and the KEY of INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY are not underlined.' I DID NOT TRUST THE OCR FOR THIS ONE: the general format is load-bearing here and the transcription's known bias is toward falsely-restrictive syntax, so I rendered the printed diagram myself at 600 dpi (PDF page 784 = printed folio 754; the figure-note's 'page 754' is the FOLIO, PDF page 754 is a SEARCH page) and read it. The render confirms: START/FIRST/KEY/LAST/LENGTH/INVALID/NOT/END-START underlined; relational-operator carries NO brackets (required inside the KEY phrase); the {data-name-1 | record-key-name-1} BRACE group; '[ WITH LENGTH arithmetic-expression-1 ]' with WITH un-underlined; a PLAIN outer bracket over FIRST/KEY/LAST; the choice-indicator bars inside the INVALID KEY brackets; '[ END-START ]'. The transcription is faithful.
CODE: startStatement : START fileName (FIRST | LAST | startKeyPhrase)? startInvalidKeyPhrase? END_START?.
WHAT CONFORMS (probed, out-b1/probe/fmt2 and /sr5-excl): at most one of FIRST/KEY/LAST -- 'START RLF FIRST KEY IS = WS-RK' draws COBOL0001 'no viable alternative at input KEY'; the INVALID group behaves as choice indicators -- both phrases with NOT INVALID FIRST ran (G1-NOTINV), neither phrase ran (G2-ST=00), INVALID alone ran; 'INVALID <imperative>' without the optional word KEY ran (G4-INV); END-START omissible; the 2002 introduction gate on FIRST fires at --std 85 (COBOLNET0900, out-b1/probe/ed85).
WHAT DIVERGES -- two words, in opposite directions:
(1) startWithLength : WITH LENGTH arithmeticExpression makes WITH REQUIRED. WITH is not underlined, i.e. an OPTIONAL word -- 5.2.3 (--check): 'Optional words are reserved words or context-sensitive words. They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats.' So 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-KEY LENGTH 3' is conforming source. Probed (out-b1/probe/fmt): rejected -- COBOL0001 'missing token before 3' plus two cascade errors. REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE.
(2) startKeyPhrase : KEY IS? comparisonOperator? dataReference makes relational-operator OPTIONAL where the rendered format requires it. Probed (out-b1/probe/ix-ops): 'START IXF KEY IS IX-KEY' compiles and RUNS (P1-OK ST=00). The grammar comment above the rule asserts 'The operator may be omitted (then EQUAL is assumed)' under an ISO 14.9.41 citation; 14.9.41.4 GR8/GR15 supply EQUAL only when the whole KEY PHRASE is omitted, never when the operator alone is -- a real clause answering a different question. UNDER-REJECTS.
(3) the record-key-name-1 arm of the brace group has no surface at all -- see SR-14.9.41.3-7 (an A.3 item 40 sanctioned decline).
TEST: none. No spec-derived test pins the format's shape; conformance:2002/file_collating_seq and conformance:2023/altkey_suppress_when each write exactly one spelling (KEY IS >= <key>) incidental to their own subjects, and both would still pass with either defect above unfixed.

subject: UNLOCK statement
notes: kb/Work PB236. RULE: the general format is `UNLOCK file-name-1 [ RECORD | RECORDS ]`. cite.py --check 14.9.47.2 (via the clause read) plus the PRINTED PAGE rendered (scripts/render-spec-page.py 798 = printed p.768): the group after file-name-1 is enclosed in SQUARE BRACKETS, and only UNLOCK is underlined. So per cite.py --check 5.2.6.2 'indicate that the syntax element contained within the brackets or one of the alternatives contained within the brackets may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted' -> OK, the whole group is omissible; and cite.py --check 5.2.3 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats.' -> OK, RECORD/RECORDS are optional words carrying no semantics (GR1's NOTE confirms: 'To unlock one particular record, use the READ statement with the NO LOCK phrase'). The transcription renders the brackets as box-drawing corners, which reads ambiguously as braces; the distinction is immaterial anyway because cite.py --check 5.2.6.3 'If one of the alternatives contains only optional words, that alternative is the default and is selected unless another alternative is explicitly specified.' -> OK. CODE: `unlockStatement : UNLOCK fileName (RECORD | RECORDS)? ;` (CobolIO.g4:528) is EXACTLY that shape. MEASURED (probe dir out-b1/probe/unlock, main-tree cobol.exe): `UNLOCK F.` / `UNLOCK F RECORD.` / `UNLOCK F RECORDS.` all accepted and behaviourally identical (p1: C/D/E all 00); `UNLOCK F RECORD RECORDS.` rejected (n1, COBOL0001); `UNLOCK F G.` rejected (n2); bare `UNLOCK.` rejected (n3); `UNLOCK "F".` rejected (n4); accepted as an imperative statement inside IF...END-IF and in a PERFORMed paragraph (p2 IN-IF/IN-PARA), which matches Table 12 (UNLOCK has no conditional phrase and no explicit scope terminator). Edition identity: recognition-gated at COBOL-2002 (VersionConformancePass.VisitUnlockStatement -> COBOLNET0900 at --std 85, measured on p1 and on n6 where the file-name is also undeclared, so the DEVLOG-724 bound-arm drop is genuinely fixed - not re-reported). ⛔ PARTIAL, NOT CONFORMS - the OPERAND half of the format is unenforced: the format writes `file-name-1`, and cite.py --check 8.4.2.1 'In order to use a resource, a statement shall contain a reference that uniquely identifies that resource.' -> OK; but `UNLOCK NOSUCH.` where NOSUCH is declared nowhere COMPILES CLEAN (n6.cob, exit 0, zero diagnostics) and aborts at run time with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented was reached at run time: UNLOCK of undeclared file 'NOSUCH'`. subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB332; PB365. The format's four figures were compared token by token with the grammar rule. CONFORMING: the {EXCEPTION|ERROR} brace (SR6), [GLOBAL] on Formats 1 and 2 only (probe GLOBF3.cob: `USE GLOBAL AFTER EC EC-SIZE.` is correctly a parse error, GLOBF1.cob compiles), `{file-name-1}...` as fileName+ (probe SR5MIX.cob `ON F1 F2`), the four mode alternatives, `{EXCEPTION CONDITION|EC}` (SR12), `exception-name-2 {FILE file-name-2}...` as useEcEntry `cobolWord (FILE fileName)*` with the outer ellipsis as useEcEntry+, `{EXCEPTION OBJECT|EO}` (SR15) and its ONE operand. The two 2002-introduction gates fire (probes F3AT85/F4AT85: COBOLNET0877 / COBOLNET0876), and the extra `USE FOR DEBUGGING` alternative is the X3.23-1985 element correctly rejected at 2023 (probe DBG23: COBOLNET0902). DIVERGENCE 1 (rejects legal source): 8.3.2.4.3 'Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format' (and 5.2.3) makes AFTER, STANDARD, PROCEDURE and ON of Format 1, and AFTER of Formats 3 and 4, OPTIONAL words -- the figure notes measured exactly that underlining. The grammar writes `USE GLOBAL? AFTER STANDARD? (EXCEPTION|ERROR) PROCEDURE ON? useOnTarget`, i.e. STANDARD and ON optional but AFTER and PROCEDURE REQUIRED, and `USE AFTER (EXCEPTION CONDITION|EC)` / `USE AFTER (EXCEPTION OBJECT|EO)` with AFTER required. Probes (cobol.exe --std 2023; the pinned worktree's CobolControlFlow.g4 and ProcedureTableBuilder.cs are byte-identical to the main tree's, so the results are attributable to the pin): `USE ERROR PROCEDURE ON F1.` -> error COBOL0001 "no viable alternative at input 'USEERROR'"; `USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR ON F1.` -> error COBOL0001 "missing token before 'ON'"; `USE EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-ALL.` -> COBOL0001; `USE EC EC-ALL.` -> COBOL0001; `USE EXCEPTION OBJECT CF4A.` -> COBOL0001. Each is legal standard COBOL that 4.2.2 requires the implementation to accept. DIVERGENCE 2: Format 4's second brace group has two alternatives, object-class-name-1 and interface-name-1; the binder resolves only the class arm (SR17 row). Recorded but NOT counted against this row: Format 2's identifier-1 is parsed by `procedureName` rather than an identifier rule -- adequate in practice (a report group's only qualifier is its report-name, one OF/IN level, which procedureName carries), but it also admits an INTEGERLIT where 8.4.3.1 admits none. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: Formats 1-2: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023. Formats 3-4: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the EC exception-condition model and the OO exception-object model). Basis: Annex E records no 2023 change to any part of 14.9.49.2 (its only USE entries, items 19a/19b, are 14.9.49.4 GR6 declarative-selection corrections), and Annex F designates no part of the USE statement obsolete or archaic.

notes: VERDICT UPHELD after an independent attack on each of the format's three obligations. `FUNCTION MAX ( { argument-1 } … )`: both words underlined (required), parentheses required, braces-plus-ellipsis = one or more with no upper bound. (1) REQUIRED WORDS AND PARENTHESES - the grammar deliberately parses the parenthesized list as a SUPERSET, `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` (read at source, both symbols exist), and the omission is caught at bind with a COBOL diagnostic rather than a parse error, which is a conforming rejection either way. (3) THE ARGUMENT SEPARATOR - `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` admits the §8.3.5 comma separator and bare juxtaposition alike. No optional phrase words exist in this format, so there is no unverified half. subject: MODULE-NAME function
notes: Verdict SUSTAINED, on re-derived grounds rather than the original ones. I read BindModuleName rather than sampling: `kind` starts at -1 and the loop errors on the FIRST non-keyword or on any argument once `kind >= 0`, then errors again if the loop saw none — so both arity bounds are structural. Two attack lines the adjudicator did not run, both of which the format rule actually reaches, come out clean. (1) THE FUNCTION-KEYWORD-OMITTED FORM. §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 and §12.3.8 SR13 make `FUNCTION` omissible for any intrinsic the REPOSITORY declares, and §15.65 carries no rule requiring the keyword — this is the exact shape of the landed PB7/PB9 defects, and MODULE-NAME is not covered by either (it is not a §8.9 reserved name and it is not zero-argument, so it takes the D2 dataReference re-route in KeywordOmittedFunction). It works, including for the reserved-word argument NESTED, under both `FUNCTION MODULE-NAME INTRINSIC` and `FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC`. (2) RESULT REFERENCE MODIFICATION (§8.4.3.3.3 SR2) and lower-case keywords both work. subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. The general format, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33307-33309, is `FUNCTION SQRT ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and SQRT both UNDERLINED — required words — and exactly one argument inside required parentheses; there is no optional phrase, no ellipsis, and no second format. READ, GRAMMAR: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 — `: FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` — so the FUNCTION keyword and the name are both required at this production, and the argument list's '(' is lexed in the dedicated FNARG mode so §8.4.3.2 SR6 ('that ( is ALWAYS the argument list') holds rather than the '(' being read as a subscript or a grouping paren. The optionality of the paren group in the grammar is deliberate (it serves the zero-argument functions) and does NOT leak into SQRT: the arity is the CATALOG's. READ, ARITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 133 — Add(new("SQRT", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "n", "Sqrt", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1, enforced at IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579: `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION SQRT takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. So a bare `FUNCTION SQRT` (given 0) and `FUNCTION SQRT(A B)` (given 2) are both rejected with the §15.3 citation. The FUNCTION-omitted spelling (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2, a REPOSITORY INTRINSIC declaration) is gated the same way — IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 301 and 339 both refuse to route a name written without an argument list unless sig.MinArgs == 0, which SQRT's is not. The row's IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.84.1's 'The type of this function is numeric'. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage writes the format both ways argument-1 can be spelled (a data item, `FUNCTION SQRT(NI)`, and a literal, `FUNCTION SQRT(4)`), each pinned to 2.00 in the .out. NOT COVERED: there is no SQRT-specific arity negative fixture; the COBOLNET1504 guard is catalog-driven and generic, so a SQRT-specific one could only re-test the shared guard. EDITIONS: the format is unchanged across the four editions (SQRT is a 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment function); batch default.
