subject: STANDARD-DEVIATION function
notes: Format read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.86.2: `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and STANDARD-DEVIATION underlined (required keywords), the parenthesised list NOT bracketed (required), and the brace-ellipsis making argument-1 one-or-more. Both halves of the format located and read. HALF 1, the keyword/name/paren shape: the grammar carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION production (grep of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend for the name returns nothing) because the form is generic — CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall is `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and CobolExpressions.g4#functionName admits IDENTIFIER. Checked the lexer for the hyphen hazard, since CobolLexer.g4 does carry STANDARD (:536), STANDARD_BINARY/STANDARD_DECIMAL (:264-265) and STANDARD_1/STANDARD_2 (:669-670) but no STANDARD_DEVIATION token: ANTLR maximal munch gives IDENTIFIER the full 18-character 'STANDARD-DEVIATION' over STANDARD's 8, which is the documented behavior at CobolLexer.g4:261-262 ('a bare STANDARD still lexes as STANDARD, and WC-COBOL still lexes as one IDENTIFIER'). The argument-list paren is retyped FNARG_LPAREN per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6, so the list is never read as a grouping or subscript paren. HALF 2, the one-or-more arity: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build:139 declares Add(new("STANDARD-DEVIATION", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "StandardDeviation", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue, matching `{ argument-1 } …` exactly; IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579 computes `given` and raises COBOLNET1504 'takes at least 1 argument(s)' when given < MinArgs, which catches both the bare `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION` and the empty-parens `()` form the grammar's optional group admits. IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.86.1 ('The type of this function is numeric'). Closing test: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 45 writes the format `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION(2, 2, 2)`, it is registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:123, and tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.out line 8 pins SD=0.0 — so the format demonstrably lexes, parses and binds. The fixture is spec-derived (its header derives every line from §15.4.1 r1 and the functions' own EAEs), not a characterization or legacy-match. Editions: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION entry and the clause has no edition-varying content, so the batch default stands; the editions field was NOT read off IntrinsicCatalog's own IntroducedIn column.

subject: SUBSTITUTE function
notes: kb/Work PB81 (2026-08-18): FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ANYCASE] [FIRST | LAST] argument-2 argument-3 } … ) — the pair repeats, so §15.3's table(ALL) is admissible among the pairs and its elements form the pairs by position at run time (the FLAT form: CobolIntrinsics.SubstituteFlat pairs the enumerated elements; a keyword before an enumeration attaches to the pair its first element opens). Written pairs pair at bind as before (SubstituteModes per pair). The ALL argument was the staged COBOLNET0899 (`substitute-all-subscript-argument`, retired).

subject: SUM function
notes:
Format read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.88.2 (line 33495-33499): `FUNCTION SUM ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and SUM underlined (required), the argument-list parentheses present, and the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis, i.e. ONE OR MORE. Both halves READ and verified. (1) THE REFERENCE SHAPE: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, with SUM present in CobolExpressions.g4#functionName (line 458) — needed because SUM is one of the §8.9 reserved words that is also a §8.11 intrinsic name. The keyword-omitted twin `SUM(…)` rides CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn (`SIGN | SUM`), and IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic lines 54-63 enforces §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 on it (COBOLNET1543 unless REPOSITORY declares SUM / FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) — so the abbreviated form is not accepted unconditionally. Arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 separator via functionArgList. §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is decided from the DEFINITION before binding (DefinitionPermitsArguments("SUM") is true since MaxArgs > 0), so `FUNCTION SUM (1:4)` draws Sr6ArgumentListError, not a bogus arity error; §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 rejects reference-modifying SUM's numeric result (ResultRefMod, COBOLNET1629). (2) THE 1..n MULTIPLICITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 152 `Add(new("SUM", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "SumScaled", …))` — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue; IntrinsicBinder.cs line 573 raises COBOLNET1504 ("takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)") for `FUNCTION SUM` written with no list or an empty one, and the unbounded max means no upper rejection. The ellipsis also licenses the §15.3 table(ALL) argument: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (MaxArgs == int.MaxValue) gates TryBindAllArgument, and its own diagnostic text names SUM as an example of a `{ argument } …` format. TESTS: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.cs re-reads §15.88.2's `<pre>` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md and asserts the catalog's unboundedness EQUALS the presence of the '…' character — spec-derived in the strict sense (the assertion's oracle is the standard's own text, not a hand list). tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob exercises the repeated-argument format over ALL (fixed, ODO, dynamic-capacity, two-level, and a mixed `SUM(F(ALL) WS-E(ALL))`); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob exercises the plain 3-argument written form. NOT covered by a dedicated fixture: a zero-argument `FUNCTION SUM` negative case — the COBOLNET1504 arm was read in source but has no SUM-specific golden; that is a test gap, not a behavior gap (the arm is shared and exercised by other MinArgs rows).

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): the format was re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33494-33499 and §8.4.3.2.3 re-read whole at :6020ff. SR2 ("If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph … the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required") and SR6 ("If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments") both check out against IntrinsicBinder.cs:57 (COBOLNET1543) and :88 (Sr6ArgumentListError, via DefinitionPermitsArguments reading MaxArgs > 0 from the catalog row). The keyword-omitted alternative `reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart*` (CobolExpressions.g4:334-346) REQUIRES the subscript group, so a bare `SUM` can never be read as a function reference — which is correct precisely because §15.88.2 has no zero-argument form, and is what keeps the report-writer `SUM OF` clause and the `SIGN` data-description clause from being swallowed. The drift test was read in full and is genuinely spec-derived: it re-scans every `#### 15.x.2 General format` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, keys on the '…' character, asserts a ≥79-row floor on BOTH the spec scan and the catalog scan so the scanner cannot silently find nothing, and asserts the equivalence in both directions — it closes the UNBOUNDED half of `{ argument-1 } …`. The at-least-one half rests on reading only (IntrinsicBinder.cs:573, MinArgs 1) with no SUM-specific fixture, which rule 3 expressly permits for CONFORMS. ONE RESIDUE FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AGAINST THIS ROW: with a runtime-ranged table(ALL) the compile-time count is `all.StaticCount ?? 1` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:572), so an OCCURS DEPENDING object of 0 satisfies MinArgs at compile time and the enumerated list reaches the runtime EMPTY — CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec would then throw IndexOutOfRangeException on `xs[0]` and CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled would return 0. §15.3 makes exactly that case undefined ("The evaluation of an ALL subscript shall result in at least one argument, otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined"), so it is not a violation of this format rule; it is worth a robustness note elsewhere, not a downgrade here. Verdict held at CONFORMS.

subject: TAN function
notes: 15.89.2 'FUNCTION TAN ( argument-1 )' written over every 15.3 type-10 argument shape (tan(0)=0 exactly by 15.89.4 r1) with the eighth-turn +1/-1 pins as the discriminator against a return-zero stub; the complement, a second argument, rejects with COBOLNET1504 at all four editions. There is no no-argument form here, unlike 15.75.2 RANDOM.

subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: cite.py --check 15.90.2 "TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD" => OK (General format, FUNCTION and TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD both underlined = required, one parenthesized argument-1, no brackets anywhere). READ: CobolExpressions.g4#functionReference `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` with `functionName : IDENTIFIER | DISPLAY | LENGTH | MERGE | NATIONAL | BIT | RANDOM | SIGN | SORT | SUM` — TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD is not a reserved word so it lexes IDENTIFIER and the format parses; the lexer's FUNCTION suppression keeps the '(' in the argument region (SR6) so 20240229 is an argument, not a subscript. READ: IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 274 `Add(new("TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "TestDateYyyymmdd", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002))` — Fixed 1..1 makes the parenthesized single argument MANDATORY: the grammar's optional arg-list and the empty-parens form both reach IntrinsicBinder.cs:573 with given=0 and raise COBOLNET1504 "takes 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)", so the no-argument shape the format does not offer is rejected. IntrinsicType.Integer matches §15.90.1 "The type of this function is integer" and Table 21 line 29995 (Int1 -> Int). EDITIONS derived from the spec, NOT from the catalog row: Annex E item 13 (line 42993) enumerates the intrinsic functions NEW in 2023 (BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE) and TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD is absent, so it predates 2023; it is not in the COBOL-85 + Amendment-1 intrinsic set, and D.31.3.8 presents it in the 2002 date-function family — hence 2002,2014,2023. The edition gate is live and pinned: conformance:negative/test_validators_below_2002 carries `reject-at: 85` and expects COBOLNET1502 (IntrinsicBinder.cs:494 "was introduced by ISO/IEC 1989:{sig.IntroducedIn}"). Positive golden intrinsics_test_validators writes the format seven times and is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json and ConformanceTests.cs:179. || REFUTED: VERDICT SURVIVES — CONFORMS confirmed, but the record's EDITIONS EVIDENCE is corrected and one over-claim in the note is withdrawn. (1) Citation re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.90.2 "TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD" => OK, §15.90.2 (General format), text `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD</u> ( argument-1 )` — both words underlined, no bracketed element, exactly one argument. (2) The grammar claim was NOT taken on trust: CobolExpressions.g4:333 is verbatim `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and the FNARG re-typing is real — CobolLexer.g4:14 `tokens { FNARG_LPAREN, FNARG_RPAREN }` and CobolLexer.g4:119 `if (PreviousIsFunctionName()) Type = FNARG_LPAREN;` — so §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is mechanically enforced, not asserted. (3) The arity gate was read at source, not quoted: IntrinsicBinder.cs `long given = args.Sum(...)` then `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET1504", ...)`, sitting AFTER BindIntrinsicArgs and BEFORE every per-function arm; and `grep TEST-DATE IntrinsicBinder.cs` returns NOTHING, so there is no bespoke arm that could divert this row past the gate. Both halves of the format (accept the one shape it offers / reject the shapes it does not) are therefore verified. (4) ⛔ EDITIONS — RULE 4 HAZARD, PARTIALLY REALIZED. Annex E item 13 is real and I re-read it (lines 42993–43001: BASECONVERT, CONCAT, CONVERT, FIND-STRING, MODULE-NAME, SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC, SUBSTITUTE), so the UPPER bound ("predates 2023") IS spec-derived. The LOWER bound is NOT. The note's two supports for 2002 do not carry it: "not in the COBOL-85 + Amendment-1 intrinsic set" is asserted with no citation and no --check, and D.31.3.8 (line 42650, re-read in full) is informative prose about the verdict codes that makes NO edition statement whatsoever — it neither says nor implies 2002. The 2023 transcription's Annex E records the delta from 2014 ONLY, so the 2002-vs-2014-vs-85 boundary is not derivable from `specs/ISO_COBOL.md` at all. The value 2002 is left standing because it is very likely correct and the rule-4 fallback ("85,2002,2014,2023") would be affirmatively WORSE — it would assert availability in an edition the function demonstrably post-dates — but it is recorded here as NOT spec-derived, and it coincides exactly with the `2002` field of the IntrinsicCatalog row under review, which is the shape rule 4 exists to catch. If the edition gate is ever challenged, the evidence must come from the 2002 or 2014 edition's own annex, not from this transcription.

subject: TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: cite.py --check 15.91.2 "FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD" -> OK, General format; the printed format is exactly 'FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD ( argument-1 )' - one REQUIRED argument, parenthesised, no optional phrase, no ellipsis, no keyword. READ: (1) src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 functionCall ('FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*') accepts the written form generically - the name needs no grammar token, which is why grep finds none in the Frontend; (2) IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build carries Add(new("TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "TestDayYyyyddd", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002)) so MinArgs==MaxArgs==1 and IntrinsicBinder.cs (the 'given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs' guard) raises COBOLNET1504 on 0 or 2 arguments - the format's arity is enforced, not merely declared; (3) the result is IntrinsicType.Integer so a refModPart on the call is rejected by IntrinsicBinder's RefModFunctionResultClass arm ('is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function', ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2) - the grammar's optional refModPart* cannot over-accept here. POSITIVE FORM EXERCISED: tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_test_validators.cob writes FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD(...) six times (J1-J6) and is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json. EDITIONS derived from the SPEC, not from the catalog's own IntroducedIn: cite.py --check D.31.3.1 "Two additional functions were added by ISO/IEC 1989:2002 as complements to these basic functions." -> OK, and D.31.3 lists exactly nine subclauses of which the last two are D.31.3.8 TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD and D.31.3.9 TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD (the other six being the COBOL-85 basic date functions), so the two additions are these; tests/conformance/negative/test_validators_below_2002.cob (reject-at: 85, registered in negative/manifest.json) pins the COBOLNET1502 window rejection below 2002. REFUTED: VERDICT UPHELD - CONFORMS survives independent re-reading, but the test-ref is TRIMMED and the evidence chain is re-grounded. (a) Citation re-derived from scratch: cite.py --check 15.91.2 "TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD" -> OK, and specs/ISO_COBOL.md 33617-33622 shows the format is one line, one bracket-free argument. (b) The grammar text was read directly rather than taken from the adjudicator: CobolExpressions.g4:332-336 is verbatim as quoted, and functionName (448-459) is IDENTIFIER plus nine reserved-word alternatives, so the hyphenated word lexes on the IDENTIFIER arm (longest-match beats any TEST prefix token). (c) The ADJACENCY question the adjudicator never asked was measured in the lexer, because the spec prints the format WITH spaces ('( argument-1 )') and a whitespace-sensitive argument-paren would REJECT legal source: CobolLexer.g4:61 PreviousIsFunctionName() tests _prevNonWsTokenType == FUNCTION, and NextToken() (143-152) advances _prev/_last only on non-WS tokens with WS itself '-> skip', so at the '(' of 'FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD ( 2024366 )' _last is the name and _prev is FUNCTION regardless of intervening spaces - OnDefaultLParen (101-120) therefore types it FNARG_LPAREN. No whitespace defect. (d) THE REJECT HALF was verified arm by arm, not inferred: arity at IntrinsicBinder.cs:573-579 (COBOLNET1504, reached because TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD matches no bespoke arm between the 493 edition gate and the 565 generic path, and ArgKinds "i" does not end in 'l'); the ALL subscript at TryBindAllArgument (2553-2587) rejects with AllSubscriptNotRepeatable because sig.RepeatsAnArgument is MaxArgs == int.MaxValue and this row's MaxArgs is 1; the result ref-mod at FinishIntrinsic (132-149) -> ResultRefMod (169-195), whose category comes from IntrinsicSig.CategoryOf (93-99) mapping IntrinsicType.Integer to PicCategory.Numeric - not one of Alphanumeric/National/Boolean, so SR2 fires. IntrinsicSig's positional record header (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) was read to confirm the row's 1,1 really are MinArgs,MaxArgs. Both halves of the format are verified by reading, so rule 5's PARTIAL cost is not owed. (e) TEST-REF CORRECTED: conformance:negative/test_validators_below_2002 was REMOVED from this row. It exercises the D8 catalog edition window (COBOLNET1502 at --std 85), which is IntrinsicBinder.cs:493's gate, not anything in the 15.91.2 general format; keeping it here would credit the format rule with coverage it does not have. The fixture is still the evidence for the `editions` field and is cited above by name. NOTE for the row's residual exposure: no fixture anywhere pins the format's REJECT half for THIS function (0 args, 2 args, ALL, ref-mod) - the pb58 negative set's nearest neighbour is pb58-testdate-frac.cob, which is TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD (15.90) and screens the argument rule, not the format.

subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
THE FORMAT READ OFF THE PRINTED CLAUSE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.92.2, lines 33665-33668): `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ( argument-1 argument-2)`. FUNCTION and the function-name are UNDERLINED, so both are required key words; the two argument operands are unbracketed and carry no ellipsis, so exactly two arguments, both required, and no repetition (feedback_underlining_not_bracketing — I measured the <u> markup, I did not infer from brackets).

GENERIC HALF — the keyword/name/parenthesised-list shape. Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | ...` and `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. The separator rule is what matters for THIS format: it admits BOTH the bare juxtaposition §15.92.2 itself prints and the §8.3.5 comma separator, and the corpus exercises both spellings (below). TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME is not a §8.9 reserved word, so it arrives through the ordinary functionName/cobolWord slot; hyphens are COBOL-word characters, so the name lexes whole.

PER-FUNCTION HALF — the name, the arity and the edition window — is the catalog row at IntrinsicCatalog#Build (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:310): Add(new("TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2, "ss", "TestFormattedDatetime", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2014)). ⚠ I READ THE IntrinsicSig RECORD DECLARATION (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) to confirm the POSITIONAL meaning of `2, 2` (MinArgs, MaxArgs) and of `2014` (IntroducedIn) instead of counting commas. The grammar's paren group is OPTIONAL, i.e. a superset parse; what actually makes both arguments REQUIRED and forbids a third is BindIntrinsicCore's arity gate — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET1504", ...)` — so a bare `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME` (0 given) and a 3-argument call are both rejected against MinArgs=MaxArgs=2.

RESULT TYPE, since the format's clause head fixes it: §15.92.1 "The type of this function is integer" — the row's IntrinsicType.Integer, and IntrinsicRenderer.cs:334 `case "TestFormattedDatetime": return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DateFn(...), 0)` renders it at SCALE 0, i.e. as an integer.

TESTS: both separator spellings of the printed format are pinned by spec-derived programs. conformance:2023/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD" "9999W526")` — the exact space juxtaposition §15.92.2 prints, which is the harder half and is easy to leave untested; conformance:2014/formatted_datetime and the AssertSpec theory write the §8.3.5 comma form. ⚠ NOT TESTED under this function's name: the arity REJECTIONS. The COBOLNET1504 gate is generic and catalog-driven (read at IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579) and is exercised elsewhere (tests/conformance/2023/pb24_length_physical_keyword pins it for FUNCTION LENGTH), but no fixture gives TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME one or three arguments.

EDITIONS from the standard: Annex E (the 2014->2023 change record) carries no occurrence of the name, so the general format is unchanged at 2023; 2014 is the introduction edition the family is gated at, and the landed sibling row AR-15.92.3-2 records the same window. Not derived from the catalog row.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:
Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.93.2 "FUNCTION" -> OK (§15.93.2 General format), the printed form being FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL ( argument-1 ) — one required argument, no optional phrase, no keyword, no repetition. READ: (1) the grammar, CobolExpressions.g4:332 functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* — functionName is the generic word slot, so TEST-NUMVAL needs no bespoke production and the written form parses; (2) IntrinsicCatalog.Build line 276, Add(new("TEST-NUMVAL", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "TestNumval", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1 matches the format's single non-optional argument, and IntrinsicType.Integer matches §15.93.1 (cite.py --check 15.93.1 "The type of this function is integer." -> OK); (3) the arity is ENFORCED, not merely declared — IntrinsicBinder.cs:573 raises COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)" for any other count. TEST-NUMVAL is NOT an OptionalTrailing/Variadic row, so no phrase the format does not print can be written. TEST: conformance:2002/intrinsics_test_validators writes the call in exactly the form §15.93.2 prints, ten times, and asserts the §15.93.4 returned values (N1..N10 in the .out). NOT VERIFIED and named honestly: no negative fixture pins the COBOLNET1504 two-argument rejection for THIS function specifically (siblings do), and the format rule itself states nothing about arity beyond the one printed operand, which the catalog row expresses. EDITIONS: batch default, same derivation limit recorded on AR-15.93.3-1 (the compiler's 2002 window and the test-numval-2002 construct row are code, not the spec).

REFUTED: (verdict SUSTAINED; the ZERO-argument path — rule 5's second famous miss, "every zero-argument intrinsic failing at run time" — probed independently and found closed at COMPILE time, which the adjudicator did not check): I traced all three routes by which a TEST-NUMVAL reference with no argument list can arrive. (a) `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL` bare: fc.functionArgList() is null, ArgsOf yields [], given = 0 < MinArgs = 1, so IntrinsicBinder.cs:573-579 issues COBOLNET1504 and returns BoundExprError — a diagnostic, never a LoudValue that survives to run time. (b) `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL ()`: the grammar's optional functionArgList is absent, same arity error. (c) `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL (1:4)`: intercepted BEFORE the bind by IntrinsicBinder.cs:87 (FNARG_LPAREN null + refModPart present + DefinitionPermitsArguments, which is MaxArgs > 0 = true here), so it draws the §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 message COBOLNET1543, not a misleading "takes 1 argument(s); 0 given" — the PB61 misroute does not reach this function. I also confirmed TEST-NUMVAL is NOT diverted to any bespoke binder (BindNumvalCFamily takes "NUMVAL-C" or "TEST-NUMVAL-C" only, line 557), so the generic arity + class path at 565-581 is the ONE path, and PB12's "bespoke binders return above CheckArgumentClasses" hazard does not apply. Test gap restated unchanged: the two-argument rejection has no fixture for this function; the row stays test-needed on that edge.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL-C function
notes:
DIAGRAM RE-DERIVED FROM THE PRINTED PAGE, not the OCR. scripts/render-spec-page.py 958 (PDF p958 = printed folio 928) shows `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C ( argument-1 [stack] [ ANYCASE ] )` where the stack glyphs are SQUARE brackets (square corners, not curly), upper leg `LOCALE [ locale-name-1 ]`, lower leg `argument-2`; underlined (required) words are FUNCTION, TEST-NUMVAL-C, LOCALE, ANYCASE. cite.py --check 15.94.2 "LOCALE</u> [ locale-name-1 ]" and --check 15.94.2 "ANYCASE" both OK; the transcription at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33756-33760 is faithful. Per §5.2.6.2 (checked: "Brackets, [ ], enclosing a portion of a general format indicate that the syntax element contained within the brackets or one of the alternatives contained within the brackets may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted") the stack is OPTIONAL and its two legs are ALTERNATIVES — so the eight legal shapes are arg1 | arg1 ANYCASE | arg1 arg2 | arg1 arg2 ANYCASE | arg1 LOCALE | arg1 LOCALE ANYCASE | arg1 LOCALE loc-name | arg1 LOCALE loc-name ANYCASE.
IMPLEMENTATION READ END TO END (not sampled). Parse: LOCALE and ANYCASE are NOT lexer tokens (grepped every .g4 — no LOCALE/ANYCASE lexer rule; CobolData.g4:367 states the choice outright), so both arrive through CobolExpressions.g4#functionArgument's arithmeticExpression->dataReference arm as bare words and are recognised BY NAME by IntrinsicBinder.cs#KeywordWordOf (fnArgPhraseWord, else a sole dataReference with no suffix). Dispatch: IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic line 557 routes NUMVAL-C/TEST-NUMVAL-C to BindNumvalCFamily BEFORE the generic MinArgs/MaxArgs screen (line 573), so the catalog row's 1..2 does not miscount the keywords — the bespoke arm owns arity. BindNumvalCFamily is a POSITIONAL walk: slot 0 always binds as argument-1 (`at > 0` guards both keyword arms, so §8.10 context-sensitivity is preserved and a leading ANYCASE/LOCALE binds as an operand and fails name resolution); ANYCASE admitted once (repeat -> COBOLNET1504) and LAST (any argument after it -> COBOLNET1504, and because that check precedes the LOCALE arm, `LOCALE` after ANYCASE is rejected too); the LOCALE arm sets LocaleWritten, runs the Constructs.NumvalCLocalePhrase2002 gate, and consumes the NEXT word as locale-name-1 only when it is not ANYCASE (line 1552 — so `arg1 LOCALE ANYCASE` does not swallow ANYCASE as a locale-name), resolving it through DataBinder.ResolveLocaleName (COBOLNET1664 when undeclared). The bracketed stack's mutual exclusion is enforced at line 1564: LocaleWritten with more than one operand -> COBOLNET1504 "argument-2 and the LOCALE keyword are alternatives" citing §15.94.2/§5.2.6.2. Operand count outside 1..2 -> COBOLNET1504 (so a bare `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C` with no argument list, which the grammar's optional FNARG_LPAREN group admits, is rejected at 0 operands). THE DEFECT IS THE >>COBOL-WORDS INTERACTION, AND IT IS BOTH DIRECTIONS OF THIS FORMAT'S TWO KEYWORDS.
Spec: cite.py --check 8.9 "ANYCASE" OK and --check 8.9 "LOCALE" OK - BOTH ARE §8.9 RESERVED WORDS (and I checked the §8.10 table mechanically: neither ANYCASE nor LOCALE appears in it). §7.3.10.3 SR3 (--check OK): "The content of literal-1, literal-3, and literal-4 shall be a reserved word, a context-sensitive word, or an intrinsic function name" - so both words are legal operands of the directive. §7.3.10.4 GR2 (--check OK): an EQUATEd literal-2 "may be used in any syntax requiring the use of the reserved word". §7.3.10.4 GR4 (--check OK): a SUBSTITUTEd literal-5 "shall be used in any syntax where the COBOL word that is the content of literal-4 is documented as required or optional", and literal-4 "shall no longer be a reserved word". §7.3.10.4 GR3 (--check OK): an UNDEFINEd literal-3 "shall no longer be reserved or restricted in any way" and its syntax "shall not be available". §15.94.2 IS such a syntax: it documents LOCALE and ANYCASE as its keywords.
MECHANISM, read end to end and NOT deduced: CobolWordsRewriter.Rewrite (src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Parsing/CobolWordsRewriter.cs:50) installs a synonym ONLY when `CobolKeywordTokens.TryTokenType(canonical, out kt)` succeeds, and DeReservedTokenTypes (:30-37) is guarded the same way; TryTokenType (CobolKeywordTokens.cs:42) is a lookup into a map built ONLY from the ANTLR lexer's literal token names (:20-37). Its own summary asserts "Every reserved word and context-sensitive word is a literal lexer token" - and that invariant is FALSE for LOCALE and ANYCASE (evidence (a) above). So no retype happens for either word. IntrinsicBinder.BindNumvalCFamily then recognises them by RAW TEXT only - KeywordWordOf (:2516) uppercases the word and lines 1527/1547 compare `== "ANYCASE"` / `== "LOCALE"` literally - and never consults `ctx.CobolWords`, although the very same file DOES consult it for the FUNCTION NAME (BindIntrinsicCore :446-448, DeReserved + Synonyms). ONE RULE, TWO PLACES.
CONSEQUENCES on legal source, both reachable because the directive is ACCEPTED: VersionConformancePass IsExistingWordCategory (:138-139) passes SR3 via the `ReservedWords.Find(w)` fallback, and tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json carries {"word":"LOCALE",r85:false,r2002:true,...} and the same row for ANYCASE - so `>>COBOL-WORDS EQUATE "LOCALE" WITH "LOCALITY"` compiles clean and is then SILENTLY INERT. (1) REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE: `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C(X LOCALITY FR)` binds LOCALITY and FR as OPERANDS, so line 1572's `operands.Count is < 1 or > 2` fires COBOLNET1504 - an arity error naming the very keyword the program legally renamed. (2) SILENT WRONG ANSWER: `>>COBOL-WORDS UNDEFINE "ANYCASE"` (GR3) or `SUBSTITUTE "ANYCASE" BY "IGNORE-CASE"` (GR4) makes ANYCASE a user-defined word and withdraws the ANYCASE syntax; `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C(X ANYCASE)` where ANYCASE is now the user's currency data item is STILL eaten as the keyword at line 1527 - the compiler turns on case-insensitive currency matching and injects the compilation-unit currency (line 1619) instead of using the named item as argument-2, with NO diagnostic. THE ASYMMETRY IS PROVABLE IN ONE COMPILER: TRIM's LEADING/TRAILING (§15.96.2) ARE lexer tokens (CobolExpressions.g4#fnArgPhraseWord; CobolLexer.cs:440/459), so >>COBOL-WORDS IS honoured for that format's phrase words and is NOT honoured for this one. Not a landed item: the only kb/Work note mentioning COBOL-WORDS is R05 (word-length ceiling), unrelated.

TWO SECONDARY CORRECTIONS TO THE ADJUDICATOR'S REASONING.
(i) "§8.10 context-sensitivity is preserved" is a REAL CLAUSE ANSWERING A DIFFERENT QUESTION. ANYCASE and LOCALE are NOT §8.10 context-sensitive words (checked the table mechanically - absent); they are §8.9 RESERVED words (--check OK on both). What justifies the `at > 0` guard is the POSITIONAL format, not §8.10; and because they are reserved, `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-C(ANYCASE)` is a §8.9 violation, yet the compiler reports only an undefined-data-name (VersionConformancePass.IsBareFunctionArgumentWord :1857-1871 EXEMPTS every bare function-argument word from the COBOLNET0901 funnel). Rejected either way, so this is diagnostic quality, not a second verdict - but the premise the CONFORMS rested on was wrong.
(ii) EDITIONS CORRECTED 85,2002,2014,2023 -> 2002,2014,2023. Batch rule 4 blesses the default only "for a rule with no edition delta", and this format HAS one, derivable without touching the code under review: §8.9 of the 2023 text reserves ANYCASE and LOCALE, and tests/version-matrix/reserved-words.json (a version-matrix artifact, not IntrinsicCatalog) records r85:false / r2002:true for BOTH with confidence "high" - a format whose two keywords are not COBOL-85 words cannot be COBOL-85 syntax (ISO 1989:1985 carries no intrinsic functions at all; the 42-function set arrived with the 1989 Intrinsic Function Module and does not contain TEST-NUMVAL-C). Annex E covers only 2014->2023 and its one related entry, E.3.3 item 1, says the NUMVAL-C ANYCASE keyword was "clarified", i.e. it pre-dates 2023 - so 2014 and 2023 are certain and 2002 is the same value the sibling FMT-15.68.2 row carries. The 2002-vs-2014 boundary for the ANYCASE keyword itself is NOT derivable from the 2023 text alone and remains an owner question if it ever matters.

notes: GAP -> CONFORMS, recorded by the LANDER, not by the implementer: cluster E wrote the §14.7.9.3 GR1 determination into docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 while its worktree was cut from a main on which an A.1 DOC row could not yet carry a verdict at all. The DOC-row mechanism (kb/Work A11 / PB280) landed afterwards, so the row is closable now and leaving it GAP would understate what is documented. The determination: the interval between the `n TIMES` re-attempts is ZERO — every lock this implementation arbitrates is held by a file connector of the EXECUTING run unit, which cannot release while another statement of that run unit runs, so no releaser can execute between two attempts and a nonzero interval could only delay an identical answer. The attempt count itself is pinned cell by cell by the drift test (RETRY n TIMES makes exactly n re-attempts, GR1's round-up applied).

notes: GAP -> CONFORMS, recorded by the LANDER (see DOC-A.1-165 for why the implementer could not). §14.7.9.3 GR2 requires the implementor to state the internal representation of the SECONDS temporary, the maximum meaningful time-out value, and the technique for determining the frequency of retries.
